papers.title: QEpy: Quantum ESPRESSO in python
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: QEpy is a Python electronic-structure software package based on Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). QEpy accomplishes two goals. First, it simplifies running and prototyping calculations with QE. Second, it targets nonstandard workflows where the electronic-structure engine is used in ways for which it was not originally designed. For example, QEpy can instruct QE to run with custom potentials in the Hamiltonian, including external, exchange-correlation, and local pseudopotentials. QEpy also exposes, at any point during an electronic-structure calculation, including between self-consistent-field cycles, quantities that would normally be accessible only through post-processing, such as the electron density and wavefunctions. QEpy’s API to the Atomic Simulation Environment gives direct access to ASE-based workflows and tools. These capabilities make QEpy a flexible platform for implementing custom workflows, interfacing QE with other simulation tools, and prototyping new electronic-structure methods. This work is written in a hybrid paper/tutorial style. Several example notebooks are presented, together with references to publications in which QEpy has already been employed. Our goal is for QEpy to serve as a versatile platform for research, teaching, and innovation in electronic-structure theory and method development.
papers.zh: QEpy：Python 中的量子 ESPRESSO

papers.title: Markov state model for the forced unfolding of a small peptide
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The mechanical unfolding of molecular complexes or biomolecules can routinely be studied using methods of single molecule force spectroscopy. In particular, the application of a force ramp with a constant pulling velocity in conjunction with stochastic modeling can be used to obtain valuable information regarding the relevant kinetics and the energy landscape. The computational counterpart of this type of experiment, using molecular dynamics simulations with atomistic resolution, allows us to gain insights into the molecular rearrangements underlying the unfolding process. However, due to the large difference in time scales, often coarse graining procedures are applied in the simulations. Most of the utilized techniques do not allow us to follow the atomistic details of the relevant conformational transitions due to the structural simplifications used to speed up the simulations. Here, we apply an earlier developed dynamic coarse graining technique based on Markov state modeling to a model peptidic system that does not unfold in a simple two-state manner. Using the donor–acceptor distances of the helical hydrogen bonds as collective variables and performing a dimension reduction allows us to construct a Markov model of the unfolding process that correctly represents the microscopic behavior of the system for not too fast pulling velocities. The chosen example shows that the method can be used to mimic the mechanical unfolding process of systems for which the end-to-end distance does not provide a sufficient order parameter and that do not unfold in a simple cooperative manner.

papers.title: Toward chemically accurate quantum simulations on quantum hardware: A quantum-HPC hybrid approach
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We report one of the most comprehensive experimental demonstrations to date of quantum-computing-based molecular simulation on IQM’s Sirius 24-qubit superconducting quantum processor, using up to 16 operational qubits. We employ Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) with the Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) Ansatz to compute ground-state energies of benchmark molecular systems, including H2, LiH, BeH2, H2O, and NH3. We further introduce the linear-CNOT unitary coupled-cluster singles and doubles Ansatz within the SQD framework, reducing the classical pre-computation overhead at the cost of increased quantum circuit depth and demonstrate its effectiveness by accurately recovering the ground-state energies of H2, LiH, and BeH2. A comparative analysis of the two Ansätze is presented, highlighting their respective merits, demerits, and practical use cases in near-term quantum simulations. In addition, we perform one-dimensional potential energy surface (1D-PES) scans for H2 and HeH+ using STO-3G and 6-31G basis sets and for LiH and BeH2 using STO-3G. We also report the first experimental generation of a full two-dimensional potential energy surface (2D-PES) map, consisting of a 32 × 32 grid in bond length and bond angle, for the water molecule in the STO-3G basis on IQM quantum hardware. Beyond small-molecule benchmarks, we integrate Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) with SQD(LUCJ) to obtain chemically accurate 4-electron-in-4-orbital active-space energies for eight ligand-like molecules, as well as for the pharmacologically relevant amantadine molecular system, representing the first of such experimental demonstrations. Across all studies, the majority of quantum-computed energies agree with reference full configuration interaction results and with DMET-complete active space CI energies for embedded systems, to within chemical accuracy for the chosen basis sets. These results demonstrate the robustness of quantum sampling-based classical diagonalization approaches while highlighting the promise of hybrid embedding strategies combined with near-term Ansätze for advancing quantum chemistry toward classically intractable molecular systems and establishing their practicality on current quantum hardware.
papers.zh: 在量子硬件上实现化学上准确的量子模拟：一种量子-HPC混合方法

papers.title: Accurate excitation energy prediction of BODIPY dyes through stacking-ensemble Δ-learning
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Accurate prediction of excitation energies is critical for the rational design of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes, but conventional time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) often suffers from pronounced functional-dependent errors for this class of chromophores. To improve TD-DFT predictions toward DLPNO-STEOM-CCSD level accuracy at a much lower computational cost, we developed a stacking ensemble Δ-learning framework that combines computationally affordable ωB97X-D3 calculations with DLPNO-STEOM-CCSD reference data to achieve accurate and transferable predictions of vertical S1 excitation energies for BODIPY derivatives. Using a dataset of 866 BODIPY derivatives containing up to 42 atoms, we first benchmarked 21 exchange–correlation functionals against DLPNO-STEOM-CCSD. ωB97X-D3 was used as a representative TD-DFT baseline for demonstrating the Δ-learning workflow. Among the 13 regression models, the stacking ensemble model achieved the best overall performance on the test set according to various metrics. This model generalized well to a size-extrapolation set of 134 BODIPY derivatives containing 43 atoms. It was further validated on an external experimental benchmark set of 15 larger BODIPYs previously reported in the literature and demonstrated transferability to nine structurally distinct near-infrared aza-BODIPYs. These results demonstrate that the proposed stacking ensemble Δ-learning framework provides an accurate, efficient, and transferable approximation to DLPNO-STEOM-CCSD level excitation energies, enabling large-scale screening and rational design of BODIPY chromophores at substantially reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Generative inverse estimation of 3D atomic coordination from near-edge spectra via equivariant diffusion models
papers.jname: npj Computational Materials
papers.abs: Extracting 3D atomic coordinates from spectroscopic data is a longstanding inverse problem. We present an equivariant diffusion model that generates the distribution of site-specific 3D structures directly from near-edge spectra (ELNES/XANES). Trained on Si–O crystals, the model achieves radial accuracy comparable to Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (EXAFS) (bond-distance MAE ~ 0.04 Å) but with superior coordination number precision (errors < 2.0% vs. EXAFS ~ 20%). Crucially, it reconstructs full 3D geometries including bond angles, overcoming the limitations of 1D radial distribution analysis. The model shows encouraging, composition-dependent transferability to amorphous systems despite being trained exclusively on crystalline lattices. Application to experimental O K -edge spectra from α -quartz, cristobalite and stishovite demonstrates feasibility for experimental spectra. This generative approach goes beyond conventional template matching, which retrieves structures from predefined references, by enabling the exploration of candidate 3D structures within a learned structural space and providing a step toward automated, quantitative, 3D local-structure inference from spectroscopic data.

papers.title: Strain-Enriched Active Sites on Anatase TiO2(001) Boost Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Artificial photosynthesis of H2O2 by TiO2-based semiconductors is a promising route for H2O2 production, but pristine TiO2 suffers from rapid charge recombination and weak O2 adsorption. Herein, we demonstrate that strain-induced active-site enrichment on the anatase TiO2(001)-(1 × 4) surface can overcome this critical bottleneck. Through facet engineering, a highly strained anatase TiO2(001)-(1 × 4) surface reconstruction is formed on {001}-dominated TiO2; this structure lowers the reduction barrier, thereby creating a high density of active sites composed of fine Ag nanoparticles and photoreduced Ti3+ species. These abundant sites facilitate efficient spatial charge separation and markedly enhance O2 activation, thereby accelerating H2O2 formation. As a result, the {001}-facet-dominated Ag/TiO2 delivers an excellent H2O2 production rate of 5360 μmol g–1 h–1, outperforming reported photocatalysts under comparable conditions and with comparable crystal facets. This work highlights strain-engineered surface reconstruction as a powerful strategy for enriching active sites in artificial H2O2 photosynthesis.

papers.title: Reconciling XPS Simulations and Experiments: New Approaches to Quantify and Minimize Core Level Binding Energy Errors in the Development of New Standards
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is a cornerstone technique for materials characterization, providing crucial insights into elemental composition and chemical states. Accurately acquiring and interpreting XPS spectra remains challenging. Theoretical predictions can be a powerful tool to address some of these issues, but their accuracy and robustness need to be well quantified. This work introduces a novel approach to tackle this need by quantifying errors in theoretical core-level binding energy predictions, enhancing the synergy between theoretical and experimental XPS analysis. By employing internal references, the effect of experimental charge referencing errors is minimized, and systematic errors and method uncertainties are differentiated. This error quantification facilitates the optimization of computational methods and opens the door to the detection of inconsistencies in experimental data, ultimately leading to more accurate signal assignments and a deeper understanding of chemical environments.
papers.zh: 协调 XPS 模拟和实验：在制定新标准的过程中量化和最小化核心能级结合能误差的新方法

papers.title: Pulsed Electrolysis Programs Relay of Adsorption Reconfiguration and OH Transfer for Neutral HMF-to-FDCA on Ru/MnO2
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMFOR) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) in neutral media avoids HMF degradation and simplifies purification, yet suffers from sluggish kinetics and low FDCA selectivity. While pulsed electrolysis coupled with a sandwich-structured Ru/MnO2 catalyst has achieved exceptional FDCA yield, its mechanistic role remains unclear. Herein, grand-canonical DFT calculations reveal that pulsed voltage drives dynamic catalyst reconstruction between Ru0/MnO2 and Ru0-RuOx/MnO2, establishing a relay of adsorption reconfiguration and *OH transfer: at low potential, Ru0/MnO2 reorients adsorbed *DFF/*FFCA from double-end to single-end adsorption; at high potential, Ru0-RuOx/MnO2 promotes *OH transfer on the aldehyde carbon. This cross-potential relay circumvents the high energy demand of either structure alone. Additionally, at high potential coadsorbed *DFF stabilizes surface *OH and suppresses overoxidation, favoring HMFOR over OER, while low-potential switching lowers *FDCA desorption and mitigates poisoning. These findings elucidate the multifunctional programming role of pulsed electrolysis and guide rational catalyst-potential design.
papers.zh: Ru/MnO2上中性HMF-至-FDCA的吸附重构和OH转移的脉冲电解程序继电器

papers.title: BN-Doped Graphene on Cu(111): Reproducible Growth and Modified π-Band Dispersion
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Extensive research has been devoted to modifying graphene’s band structure through boron nitride (h-BN) doping. The isostructural and isoelectronic nature of graphene and h-BN makes them ideal candidates for forming hybrid materials that combine the properties of both systems. However, one of the main bottlenecks in achieving this goal has been the lack of a reproducible synthesis route that consistently yields materials with comparable properties. In this work, we present a reproducible chemical vapor deposition (CVD) recipe for the synthesis of boron- and nitrogen-doped graphene (BN-graphene) on Cu(111), which has been successfully reproduced in up to four different setups. The resulting BN-graphene exhibits low BN segregation, with BN domains homogeneously incorporated within the graphene lattice. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals that BN doping modifies the band structure of pristine graphene, leading to a flattening of the π band (valence band). This modified π-band dispersion is consistent with a possible bandgap opening, although the present data do not allow an unambiguous determination of the bandgap.
papers.zh: BN掺杂石墨烯在Cu(111)上：可重现的生长和修饰的π带色散

papers.title: Asymmetric and Dynamic Binding of Suramin Attenuates CXCL3 Chemokine-Mediated Cellular Transmigration
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The growth-related oncogenic chemokine CXCL3 is an established biomarker of cervical cancer promoting metastatic cell migration and proliferation. Such activities are an outcome of the interaction of CXCL3 with its cognate GPCR receptor and ECM-associated glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) such as heparin. A heparin-analogous negatively charged polysulfonated drug, suramin, has displayed promising binding potential to chemokines on the surface overlapping with the known heparin binding site. Therefore, the flexible, symmetric, bivalent molecule─suramin─has been investigated for its binding potency against the oncogenic chemokine CXCL3. An integrated study comprising NMR, ITC, docking, consecutive molecular dynamics, PCA-free energy landscape analysis, DCCM, and correlative motion studies has been performed to understand the characteristics of CXCL3–suramin interactions and their underlying molecular mechanisms. The results suggested that the initial binding, led by the charged centers of suramin’s sulfonates and the positively charged Lys side chains from the helical interface of the dimeric CXCL3, has been found to be further stabilized by van der Waals interactions. Suramin anchors stably to the chain B helix at residues P57, Q60, I61, K64, K65, and K68 by one arm, while the other arm dynamically samples chain A residues (I61, K64, K65) and transiently accesses the interhelical groove resulting in an asymmetric, hemi-anchored, and dynamic binding pattern. Suramin binding fragments the apo three-basin energy landscape into five-basin conformationally separated bound-state minima and rewires the intersubunit dynamic coupling without disrupting the overall secondary structure of CXCL3. ITC analysis of single and triple Lys mutants corroborates the significance of K64 and reinstates the primary role of these Lys residues in the interaction, as observed from MMPBSA analysis. Considering the similar nature of suramin and heparin binding to CXCL3, suramin’s overlapping binding site with GAGs on CXCL3, and the fuzzy nature of one arm of suramin along with the redistribution of the conformational landscape upon suramin binding establishes suramin’s repurposing potential to target CXCL3-mediated cellular pathways assisting cancer cell migration.

papers.title: Interfacial Effects on Structure and Ion Dynamics in Polymer–Organic Ionic Plastic Crystal Composites
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Organic ionic plastic crystals (OIPCs) have emerged as promising solid-state electrolytes owing to their intrinsic ionic conductivity and plasticity. To further enhance their mechanical stability and transport properties, polymer–OIPC composites have been developed. However, the role of polymer–OIPC interfaces in governing ionic transport at the molecular level remains elusive. Herein, we employ atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the interfacial effects on structure and ionic transport in polymer–OIPC composites. Polymer–OIPC composites based on diethyl(methyl)(isobutyl)phosphonium hexafluorophosphate ([P1,2,2,4][PF6]) are constructed with two representative polymers, poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO). Our results reveal that both PVDF and PEO induce similar interfacial structures, yet the mobility of OIPC ions is enhanced in PEO–OIPC composites. Upon the introduction of Li+ ions as dopants, we find that Li+ ions follow distinct diffusion mechanisms in the two composites: anion-mediated diffusion in PVDF–OIPC and polymer-mediated diffusion in PEO–OIPC. The faster relaxation of Li+–PF6– coordination shells in PVDF–OIPC allows Li+ ions to exhibit normal diffusion along the interfacial plane, whereas Li+ ions in PEO–OIPC remain subdiffusive due to the slower relaxation of Li+–O(PEO) coordination shells. These findings highlight the importance of understanding ion diffusion mechanisms at the molecular level for the rational design of solid-state electrolytes.

papers.title: Modulation of the Stereoselective Transport of Brivaracetam Diastereomers in Cyclopeptide Nanotubes through Side-Chain Polarity
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Stereoselective separation is of considerable importance in pharmaceutical science because the biological activity of many drugs depends on their stereochemical configuration. Cyclopeptide nanotubes (CPNs), with their tunable structures and chiral cavities, offer promising platforms for chiral recognition and stereoisomer separation. However, the influence of side-chain polarity on the molecular recognition and discriminatory behavior of CPNs remains largely unexplored. Herein, the effect of side-chain polarity in three different CPNs on the discrimination of Brivaracetam (BVT) and its diastereomer was investigated using steered molecular dynamics (SMD) simulations. Three CPNs with distinct polarities were considered: a reference CPN with a balanced distribution of polar and nonpolar side chains, together with two analogues of higher and lower polarity. The simulations were designed in three complementary phases to examine stereoisomer transport through different regions of the nanotube. Phases 1 and 3 investigated the passage of stereoisomers along the nanotube wall, whereas phase 2 focused on their translocation through the central cavity. Interestingly, polar side-chain groups generally enhanced diastereomeric discrimination, although the extent of this effect depended on the simulation conditions and transport pathway. Along the nanotube wall, polar CPNs showed enhanced discrimination, particularly under unconstrained simulation conditions. In contrast, the CPN with balanced side-chain polarity provided the greatest discrimination during translocation through the central cavity. Overall, these findings demonstrate that subtle modifications of external side-chain functionality can markedly alter diastereomeric discrimination during stereoisomer transport through CPNs, highlighting the important role of the nanotube exterior in modulating chiral recognition.

papers.title: The Gordian Knot Enhances Ubiquitin Binding in UCH-L1
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: UCH-L1 is a monomeric deubiquitinating enzyme whose native structure embeds a shallow 52 knot near the N-terminus, placing the knotted topology in direct proximity to both the substrate-binding pocket and the catalytic site. While our previous work ( J. Chem. Inf. Model.2024, 64, 6827−6837.) established that N-terminal integrity is critical for catalytic activity, the energetic and structural consequences of removing the knot without altering the amino acid sequence remained unresolved. Here, we combine steered molecular dynamics with umbrella sampling to generate full-length, sequence-identical variants of UCH-L1 with weakened or disrupted topology and reconstruct the free-energy profile along a constrained unthreading pathway. The potential of mean force places the sampled unknotted conformations approximately 5–7 kcal/mol above the native knotted minimum, indicating a thermodynamic preference for the native topology along this pathway. Long unbiased MD simulations of fully unknotted variants in both apo and holo states show that knot removal predominantly increases local N-terminal flexibility without significantly destabilizing the global fold or disrupting the catalytic-site geometry. MM-PBSA calculations further predict less favorable ubiquitin-binding energetics upon unknotting (ca. −62 vs ca. −76 kcal/mol), suggesting that topology contributes to substrate affinity. Together, these results suggest that the 52 knot in UCH-L1 is not a passive topological feature but a functional element that constrains unfolding dynamics and contributes to substrate binding efficiency.

papers.title: Electrolyte Effects on the Elementary Steps of ESPT in Photobases–An Investigation of Dissociation and Quenching Rates in Aqueous Solutions
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Excited-state proton transfer (ESPT) in photoacids or photobases depends on several factors, such as the solvent’s pKa, temperature, or the concentration of electrolytes in solution. The latter is especially relevant for biological applications but has, to date, been explored almost exclusively for photoacids. In this contribution, we study the effect of sodium halides (NaF, NaCl, and NaI) on the ESPT reaction of 5- and 6-methoxyquinoline (5-MeOQ and 6-MeOQ). We interpret our results in the light of anion effects, i.e., quenching and enhanced recombination, competing with the effects of cations, i.e., screened recombination and an increased acidity of the solvent. Whereas for NaI, and in most solutions of NaCl, quenching effects seem to be the dominant factor, other effects are more pronounced in aqueous NaF solutions. We associate this with a charge-transfer quenching mechanism that primarily affects the (positively charged) protonated form and that is most prominent for the weak photobase 6-MeOQ and the strong quencher I–. When quenching is negligible, though, our steady-state emission experiments show an increased emission from the unprotonated form of 6-MeOQ, which we associate with an increased recombination rate. For 5-MeOQ, however, we argue that the observed results are largely attributable to Na+ effects. While these are thought to compete with quenching, UV/vis fs-TA experiments suggest an increasing contribution from the fully separated ion pair (FSIP), i.e., the product of the dissociation process in a two-step Eigen–Weller model. Lastly, we show that the dissociation rate also depends on the temperature of the solvent. We associate the observed increase in this rate with the increasing temperature of the solvents’ changed viscosity and thus a higher mobility of the OH– ions.

papers.title: Theoretical Kinetic Study on Unimolecular Decomposition of tert -Amyl Methyl Ether
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: tert-Amyl methyl ether (TAME) is not only widely used as a gasoline additive but also demonstrates significant potential as an alternative fuel. Currently, the combustion reaction mechanism of TAME remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive theoretical investigation of the unimolecular decomposition of TAME is essential for developing its combustion model. Potential-energy surfaces for the unimolecular decomposition of TAME, including CH3OH elimination and C–O/C–C/C–H bond fission reaction channels, were constructed by the high-level ab initio calculations at the QCISD(T)/CBS//B2PLYP-D3/cc-pVTZ level of theory. Conventional transition state theory (CTST) was utilized for reactions with tight transition states, and variable reaction coordinate transition state theory (VRC-TST) was used for barrierless reaction channels. In VRC-TST calculations, the interaction energies between the two adducted radical fragments were determined at the CASPT2(2e,2o)/cc-pVDZ level of theory combined with geometry relaxation and basis set energy corrections. Temperature- and pressure-dependent rate constants were obtained by solving the Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus/Master equation (RRKM/ME) at 500–2000 K and 0.01–100 atm. At 1 atm, the results demonstrate that, the elimination reaction channel of TAME ⇌ CH2═C(CH3)CH2CH3 + CH3OH is dominant at T < 1350 K, while the bond fission reaction channel TAME ⇌ ĊH3 + CH3OĊ(CH3)CH2CH3 dominates at T > 1350 K. Additionally, thermodynamic parameters (enthalpy ΔHf,298, entropy S298, and specific heat at constant pressure Cp) for all species in TAME decomposition reactions and cyclic ethers in TAME combustion models were calculated. Rate constants and thermochemical data calculated in this work are valuable for the model development of TAME combustion and greatly reduce the systematic bias of underpredicted ignition delays.

papers.title: Microwave Polarization-Enhanced Evaporation: Experiment and Theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Our previous study revealed that during microwave evaporation of water, an electric field vertical to the liquid surface facilitates water evaporation. In this work, 12 kinds of organic solvents were adopted as experimental subjects. The experiment results verify that microwave polarization-enhanced evaporation represents a universal rule. Under identical conditions, the microwave electric field vertical to the liquid surface can increase the evaporation rate by up to 20% compared with the parallel electric field. This effect is associated with intermolecular forces, dipole moment, complex permittivity, and relative molar mass. GROMACS molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that such a phenomenon originates from the reduction in surface tension and enthalpy of vaporization induced by the microwave electric field vertical to the liquid surface.

papers.title: Competition between Proton Transfer and Electron-Transfer-Mediated Decay in a Microsolvated Environment
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: We investigate the relaxation dynamics of the 1s-ionized state of the Li+ ion in microsolvated Li+(H2O)n (n = 1, 2) cluster, which decays via an intermolecular electron-transfer-mediated decay (ETMD) process. For Li+H2O, the ETMD decay rates are evaluated as a function of Li–O separation. The results reveal a pronounced distance dependence of the ETMD lifetime, reflecting the nonlocal nature of the decay. To probe solvent effects, ETMD is also examined in Li+H2S. The ETMD decay rate is computed using a highly correlated Fano equation-of-motion coupled-cluster singles and doubles (Fano-EOMCCSD) method. In Li+(H2O)2, we identify proton transfer as a highly competing relaxation pathway. By evaluating ETMD decay widths at frozen nuclear geometries sampled along the nuclear dynamics trajectories, we elucidate how changes in cluster geometry and hydrogen-bond rearrangements modulate the instantaneous propensity of the ETMD process during proton transfer.

papers.title: Grand-Canonical Path Reweighting for Constant-Potential Langevin Dynamics
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Constant-potential molecular dynamics provides an important framework for studying the structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic properties of electrochemical systems at a prescribed electrochemical potential, but independent simulations under different electrochemical conditions can be computationally demanding, particularly for rare-event kinetics. Here, we develop a trajectory reweighting framework based on extended-phase-space Langevin dynamics, in which the electron number Ne is treated as an additional dynamical degree of freedom and the nuclear and electronic degrees of freedom evolve within a unified Langevin framework. The proposed approach enables thermodynamic and kinetic properties at different electrochemical potentials to be obtained from a single ensemble of reference trajectories. We validate the method for the Volmer reaction at a Pt/water interface, where the reweighted trajectories reproduce both the thermodynamic properties and reaction rates obtained from direct dynamical simulations at the target electrochemical potential. The reweighting is performed entirely in postprocessing and introduces negligible additional computational cost. Furthermore, this dynamical reweighting approach can use well-sampled reference trajectories generated under conditions where the reaction proceeds more rapidly to estimate reaction rates under conditions where the reaction is slower.

papers.title: Local, Non-Redundant Molecular Coordinates from Disjoint Primitive Families: Symmetry-Adapted Construction and Applications
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Internal coordinates express molecular motion in chemical terms, but primitive functions are redundant, and global delocalization mixes coordinate families. We introduce extended symmetry-adapted local coordinates (ESALCs), which organize diverse chemical primitives into disjoint families and complete, nonredundant bases. The internal-coordinate form, ESALC-I, assigns general primitives to perceived chemical domains, forms local symmetry-adapted combinations, selects exact rank through the Wilson B matrix, and retains complete molecular-symmetry subspaces within a basin of fixed topology and symmetry. When bond assignments become ambiguous, the Cartesian form, ESALC-C, supplies a full-system basis with overall translations and rotations removed. Tests on covalent, fragment, and metal-contact systems establish rank, analytic derivatives, and symmetry. Stationary-Hessian comparisons for cyclobutane and norbornane show low coupling with chemically interpretable ESALC-I families. Full geometry optimizations demonstrate use with established programs.

papers.title: Regularized Frozen Natural Orbital Approach to CASPT2: Extension to Restricted Active Space Wave Functions, Different Multiplicities and Assessment of Correlation Effects
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: The frozen natural orbital (FNO) method is a well-known approximation that significantly reduces the cost of many-body perturbation theory treatments for obtaining correlation energies in a systematic and controlled manner, enabling the simulation of larger and more realistic molecular systems. Here, we implement FNO on top of restricted active-space self-consistent field (RASSCF) wave functions within second-order perturbation theory, leading to the FNO-RASPT2 method. To account for the additional approximations incurred when using RASSCF wave functions, as well as to apply it to states of different molecular charge and spin multiplicity, we introduce a regularization approach via a level-shift in the orbital deletion procedure, which helps avoid singularities resulting from vanishing denominators due to the reduced occupation of restricted (active) virtual orbitals and that we show does not significantly influence the final energies obtained. Numerical results on vertical excitation energies showcase the FNO to be up to ∼4.0 times faster than the parent computation while retaining ∼95% of the dynamic correlation energy and being within 0.1 eV of the reference calculation, with the CASPT2 equations – the main bottleneck in large molecular systems – registering over an order of magnitude speed-up. An in-depth analysis shows the regularized FNO approach to retain electron correlation appropriately for internal and semi-internal contributions, while displaying larger deviations for the external term, which originates from the initial FNO truncation based on an approximated one-electron reduced density matrix. Ongoing efforts are directed toward improving and extending our current implementation to the calculation of analytic gradients and nonadiabatic couplings to enable faster nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations in larger and more realistic molecular systems.

papers.title: A Charge-Consistent Long-Range Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Compatible with Quantum Linear System Algorithms
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Charge equilibration in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) requires repeatedly solving linear systems, providing a promising target for quantum linear-system algorithms (QLSAs). However, conventional electronegativity equalization schemes suffer from spurious fractional charges between neutral fragments at large separations. To address this limitation, we incorporate atom-condensed Kohn–Sham density functional theory approximated to second order (ACKS2) into a long-range equivariant neural-network MLIP. Across benchmark systems, the ACKS2-based model improves energy, force, and charge predictions. At a molecule–metal interface, ACKS2 restores molecular fragments to near-neutral charge states upon separation while preserving local charge redistribution near adsorption. Because ACKS2 charge equilibration reduces to solving a linear system, the classical solver can be directly replaced with the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd algorithm during inference, demonstrating compatibility with quantum linear-system solvers. These results indicate that ACKS2 provides a promising framework for charge-aware MLIPs and highlight a potential pathway toward atomistic simulations based on QLSAs.

papers.title: Multireference QM/MM Nonadiabatic Dynamics with Quantum Nuclei in Explicit Environment: Implementation in COBRAMM and Application to the Sub-100 fs Energy Transfer in NADH
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We present a mixed quantum-classical framework for simulating nonadiabatic excited-state dynamics in explicit environments. The method combines a fully quantum-mechanical treatment of both electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom in the high-level (HL) region with classical propagation of the surrounding low-level (LL) environment. The HL dynamics is described using a linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonian parametrized at the multireference (XMS-CASPT2) level of theory, while bidirectional systembath coupling is incorporated through a dynamically updated electrostatic embedding scheme. The implementation, integrated into the COBRAMM suite, interfaces Quantics, OpenMolcas, and AMBER. Benchmark tests assess the stability, energy conservation, and approximations underlying the protocol. Among those, we highlight the crude adiabatic approximation, which allows to avoid explicit QM calculations for the update of the Hamiltonian during the dynamics, making the simulation time dependent only on the size of the active space required for the initial parametrization. As a proof of concept, we investigate the sub-100 fs excitation energy transfer (EET) in solvated NADH. Compared to simulations with a frozen environment, the explicit dynamical response of the solvent enhances the charge transfer (CT)-mediated EET pathway. The results highlight the critical role of fast librational solvent modes in ultrafast nonadiabatic phenomena and establish the presented protocol as a robust approach for treating environment-driven internal conversion in rigid photoresponsive molecular systems.

papers.title: AnhDis: A Scheme for Anharmonic Nuclear Ensembles and Absorption Spectra
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: The Nuclear Ensemble Approach (NEA), typically implemented using the harmonic Wigner approximation in Cartesian normal coordinates, has shown significant limitations when applied to molecules with large-amplitude bending and torsional motions. On the one hand, rectilinear displacements fail to follow the curvature of these motions at finite amplitudes, introducing artificial bond stretching. On the other hand, harmonic potentials can inadequately describe confinement along these motions. Both limitations can lead to artificial spectral broadening and spurious transitions. In this work, the Anharmonic-Distribution (AnhDis) scheme is presented. The method is based on constructing mode-resolved potential energy surfaces through explicit scans along curvilinear paths in internal coordinates, represented in the present implementation by polynomial fits or piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation (PCHIP). By solving the resulting one-dimensional vibrational Hamiltonians, nuclear probability densities that account for anharmonic confinement and wave function asymmetry are obtained. Temperature effects are incorporated through Boltzmann weighting of the vibrational eigenstates. AnhDis thus combines curvilinear nuclear ensembles with an independent-mode treatment of anharmonicity. Comparisons with reference simulations and experimental data across atmospherically relevant molecules demonstrate that the proposed method captures absorption spectral profiles while reducing Cartesian sampling artifacts and revealing system-dependent anharmonic effects.

papers.title: FUSED: A Functional Representation for Joint Structural and Elemental Analysis of Protein–Ligand Binding Sites
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Ligand binding site representations are central to the analysis of protein–ligand interactions, with applications in functional characterization, binding-site comparison, and ligand recognition. Many descriptor-based approaches characterize ligand binding sites using a fixed distance threshold from the ligand, despite substantial variability in how such thresholds are defined and the possibility that relevant structural and compositional information changes across spatial scales. We propose Functional Unification of Structural and Elemental Descriptors (FUSED), a multivariate functional representation that jointly models structural and elemental compositional information on ligand binding sites as functions of distance from the ligand. Structural information is captured through covariance-based descriptors derived from the CDPA framework, while chemical composition is represented through isometric log-ratio coordinates to account appropriately for compositional geometry. Treating distance from the ligand as a functional domain allows structural and compositional characteristics to be examined across distance thresholds rather than at a single prespecified value. The resulting representation can be used directly or combined with dimension-reduction, statistical-learning, and/or machine-learning procedures, with the distance interval tailored to the data set, analytical task, and procedure. We evaluate FUSED on three benchmark data sets spanning complementary ligand binding-site analysis tasks: the Extended Kahraman data set for multiclass ligand discrimination, TOUGH-C1 for three-class binding-site classification, and TOUGH-M1 for pairwise matching of pockets associated with drug-like ligands. FUSED supports strong discrimination in the EK and TOUGH-C1 tasks using standard statistical-learning procedures, while a supervised Siamese neural network applied to the full FUSED representation achieves a mean ROC-AUC of 0.9375 on TOUGH-M1 under repeated sequence-cluster-disjoint evaluation. Matched evaluations against leading available methods demonstrate competitive performance, with relative advantages depending on the task and comparator. Two illustrative retrieval cases identify pockets binding identical or chemically related ligands despite low global sequence and structural similarity between the proteins. These results demonstrate that FUSED provides a flexible, alignment-free representation that supports both direct examination of threshold-dependent binding-site characteristics and competitive downstream classification and pocket matching while remaining computationally practical.

papers.title: PertiNet: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Modeling of Protein–Protein Interactions
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Protein–protein interaction (PPI) prediction requires models that combine sequence, structure and functional evidence for proteins excluded from training. We developed PertiNet, which represents these inputs as separate modality tokens, models their interactions and assigns each token a protein-pair-specific weight. On the fixed protein-disjoint Bernett benchmark, PertiNet using sequence and structure achieved AUROC, AUPRC, balanced accuracy and MCC values of 0.71, 0.72, 0.66 and 0.33, respectively. Adding Gene Ontology (GO) annotations increased these values to 0.72, 0.73, 0.67 and 0.35, compared with published TUnA values of 0.70, 0.69, 0.65, and 0.30. Within-study Bernett controls showed that complete fusion improved on concat–MLP with identical sequence and structural inputs, using either the original sequence representation or ESM-2. Matched RBP400 ablations examined the contributions of modalities and fusion components, and Dset_186_72_PDB164 provided a complementary evaluation of residue-level interface localization. These results support integrating structural and functional context with sequence representations through interactions among modality tokens.

papers.title: FamGeo-DDG: A Mutation-Centered Local Geometric-Semantic Framework for Protein–Protein ΔΔ G Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular regulation, immune recognition, and therapeutic design, making accurate prediction of mutation-induced binding free energy changes (ΔΔG) important for variant interpretation and protein engineering. However, ΔΔG prediction remains challenging because mutational effects are often localized, while benchmark performance may be inflated by residual similarity between training and validation complexes. Here, we present FamGeo-DDG, a mutation-centered local geometric-semantic framework for protein–protein ΔΔG prediction. FamGeo-DDG constructs a local residue graph around the mutation site or the union of local neighborhoods surrounding multiple mutation sites and integrates residue substitution information, DSSP-derived structural descriptors, and ESM-2-derived contextual difference features (ΔESM). A local geometric encoder and mutation-centered readout capture structural context and mutation-induced perturbations. For evaluation, we adopt three complementary 5-fold partitioning protocols, the family split, which groups complexes by complex-signature similarity, the MpbPPI split, which directly reuses the partitions provided by MpbPPI, and the structure split, which uses ECOD-guided grouping based on available structural annotations. Under matched 5-fold partitions, we compare FamGeo-DDG with 13 recent and classical baselines, including TopNetTree, GeoPPI, 3D-ΔΔG, DSSA-PPI, MutPPI+, IGMI, Prot-ΔΔG, and Pythia-PPI, and report mean ± standard deviation across folds. On the family split, FamGeo-DDG achieves PCC values of 0.5471 ± 0.1212, 0.4956 ± 0.1299, 0.5486 ± 0.1830, and 0.5168 ± 0.0792 on S645, M1101, S1131, and S4169, respectively. Across multiple data sets and partition protocols, FamGeo-DDG achieves consistent predictive performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of mutation-centered geometric and semantic representations. Ablation analysis and external validation further support the contribution of individual model components and the transferability of FamGeo-DDG across different mutation prediction scenarios.
papers.zh: FamGeo-DDG：一种以突变为中心的局部几何-语义框架，用于蛋白质-蛋白质ΔΔG预测

papers.title: Molecular Determinants of Contaminant Association with PET Nanoplastics Revealed by Atomistic Simulations
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Chemical contaminants associated with nanoplastics can form environmentally pervasive, persistent complexes with potentially toxic effects. Yet, determining which contaminants are most likely to associate with nanoplastics and which molecular determinants govern this phenomenon remains challenging. Here, we used molecular dynamics (MD) to screen and compare the surface association of small-molecule contaminants with polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic particles (PET-NPPs). Toward this aim, we developed an automated, open-source MD screening pipeline that requires only a SMILES string as input. By systematically analyzing 203 environmentally relevant contaminants in complex with a PET-NPP model, we observed widespread surface association governed by a specific set of physicochemical descriptors. Contaminant net charge defined the primary interaction regime. Among neutral contaminants, association increased strongly with molecular size at lower molecular weights. Among compounds of comparable size, the strongest binders were consistent with geometric complementarity with the PET surface, involving aromatic anchoring and, in some cases, conformational adaptability. Together, these results identify model-specific molecular determinants of contaminant association with PET-NPPs, providing a framework that enables rapid, internally consistent prioritization of contaminants for targeted experimental and mechanistic follow-up.

papers.title: Designing Efficient Asymmetric Dyes for DSSCs : A Theoretical Exploration of π‐Bridge Motifs
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: In this theoretical work, we have proposed a set of six asymmetric (D1–D6), di‐anchoring carbazole‐based dyes designed for dye‐sensitized solar cells (DSSCs), based on a previously reported symmetric reference dye (R). Departing from conventional symmetric architectures, these dyes incorporate heterocyclic π‐spacers (e.g., thiadiazole, pyrazine) asymmetrically positioned between the donor and one of the cyanoacrylic acid acceptor units, resulting in an A‐D‐π‐A configuration. We have conducted a thorough investigation into how variations in the π‐spacer and molecular asymmetry influence the key photovoltaic properties employing density functional theory (DFT) and time‐dependent DFT (TD‐DFT) for the study. The proposed dyes have comparatively smaller HOMO‐LUMO band gaps, better light‐harvesting, and show red shifted absorption spectra and other favorable properties for electron injection and dye regeneration. The spacer‐extended dyes also show longer calculated radiative lifetimes and lower intramolecular reorganization energies. Several dyes demonstrate good theoretical parameters with a balanced combination of injection thermodynamics and radiative lifetime. A comparative analysis shows that maximizing the effectiveness of DSSC sensitizers requires a balance between optical and kinetic parameters. Overall, this study provides molecular level structural‐property insights for the designing of metal‐free asymmetric sensitizers for future.
papers.zh: 为DSSCs设计高效不对称染料：对π桥基序的理论探索

papers.title: Toward Equilibrium Charges: Environment‐Consistent Atomic Charge Models for Nonpolarizable Force Fields
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: Electrostatic interactions in nonpolarizable force fields are represented by fixed atomic charges, despite their sensitivity to molecular environments. We use the self‐consistent polarization (SCP) method to derive environment‐consistent charges for seven aliphatic alcohols, from methanol to tert‐butanol, in water, methanol, pure alcohol liquids, and n ‐octanol. SCP calculations on MD‐derived solvation clusters reveal solvent‐induced polarization of hydroxyl‐group charges, dominated by direct polarization and environmental back‐polarization. Hydroxyl charges are transferable across alcohols and hydrogen‐bonding solvents, whereas aliphatic carbon and hydrogen charges depend on substitution pattern. SCP‐derived charges improve hydration free energies when transformed from bulk to vacuum values at the water–vacuum interface, achieving mean deviations of c.a. 0.3 kcal mol −1 of experiment. The reproduction of mixing enthalpies for alcohol‐water mixtures was also improved with SCP charges. These results support equilibrium‐derived charges as an intermediate description between additive and explicitly polarizable force fields.
papers.zh: 朝向平衡电荷：用于非极化力场的环境一致性原子电荷模型

papers.title: Hydrogen-bond donor–acceptor imbalance in low-frequency terahertz water spectra
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The low-frequency dielectric response of liquid water is commonly described by a dominant Debye relaxation together with additional faster contributions whose microscopic origin remains debated. Here, we show that the dielectric function of water between 0.14 and 1.21 THz can be represented by a collective Debye relaxation plus a Drude–Smith term constrained to the zero-dc-conductivity limit. The Drude–Smith spectral weight increases upon heating pure liquid water from 20 to 50 °C and decreases upon isotopic substitution (D2O at 20 °C vs H2O at 20 °C). Among several microscopic measures of electronic polarization and its fluctuations extracted from molecular-dynamics simulations, including path-integral simulations with nuclear quantum effects, the population of water molecules with unequal numbers of donated and accepted hydrogen bonds best tracks the trends of the Drude–Smith spectral weight, changing with the same sign and comparable magnitude. Because such donor–acceptor imbalance is the local condition for net intermolecular charge transfer, it points to fluctuating molecular charges, a degree of freedom that fixed-charge representations lack by construction. Consistently, ab-initio-based dielectric spectra show that the ∼0.1–1 THz response cannot be solely described within a fixed-charge representation. These results support a plausible interpretation of parts of the excess low-frequency THz response of water as electronic-polarization fluctuations associated with transient donor–acceptor imbalance within the aqueous hydrogen-bond network.

papers.title: Equation of state for hard sphere fluids across the stable and metastable regimes
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We review selected equations of state (EOSs) for three-dimensional hard-sphere fluids and revise a closed-virial construction to describe the stable and metastable disordered states. The equation preserves the prescribed coefficients B2–B11, uses a linear continuation constrained by estimates of B12–B16, and imposes a simple pole at the representative maximally random jammed packing fraction ηp=0.637. The pole is a modeling assumption for a disordered continuation and is not identified with an exact singularity of the equilibrium virial series. The remaining parameters are fitted to the high-density subset of the simulation data of Pieprzyk et al. [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 21(13), 6886 (2019)]. The overall average absolute relative deviation is 0.022 36% over their 100 data points. With unchanged parameters, the deviation is 0.005 874% over 50 points from Davidchack and Laird [J. Chem. Phys. 157(7), 074701 (2022)]. Agreement with the high-order coefficient estimates is assessed as a construction consistency check. Comparisons distinguish the information used to determine each EOS from its subsequent performance. The resulting equation combines prescribed virial inputs, a representative disordered end point, and small pressure deviations over the tested range, while retaining a phenomenological high-order continuation.

papers.title: Modeling the inner electric double layer using short-range machine learning potentials: A critical assessment
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical interfaces typically require large system sizes and long simulation times to obtain reliable thermodynamic properties. In this context, machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for computationally efficient sampling compared to density functional theory-based molecular dynamics simulations. Although conventional short-range MLIPs are recognized as inadequate for modeling the (potentially nanometer-wide) diffuse layer, they may still be capable of describing the inner electric double layer that is relevant for electrochemical reactions. Here, we evaluate the performance of common (short-ranged) MLIP architectures [the deep potential DP, the (graph) atomic cluster expansion-based models GRACE and MACE, and the pre-trained eSEN-OC25] for charged Au/electrolyte interfaces. In the evaluation, we focus on the effect of message passing and on the potentially adverse effect of data interference when training for a broad range of surface charges. Our results suggest that both local and message-passing models are able to reliably learn the interfacial structure when training on a single charge state. However, when trained on datasets that span multiple charge states, the MLIPs tested yield inconsistent predictions of interfacial water orientation and ion distributions. This behavior can be traced to the MLIPs being “blind” to the actual surface charge. Message-passing models show somewhat greater robustness to mixed-charge training data, likely due to their larger receptive field, but are still prone to artifacts and errors in the description of the interfacial structure. Overall, our results provide practical guidance on the expected accuracy and cross-charge-state transferability of short-ranged MLIPs for the description of the inner layer of electrode/electrolyte interfaces that will be relevant to their use in computational electrocatalysis.
papers.zh: 使用短程机器学习势建模内电双层：一项关键评估

papers.title: Pressure-retarded DNA translocations of nanopores reveal nanoscale stagnant fluid layers
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Although nanopore sequencing and sensing have undergone years of commercial development, accurately interpreting current signals, translating them into molecular length, position, and sequence, depends on knowing the translocation speed, which still lacks a physical model capable of predicting it from first principles. Existing models introduce adjustable parameters that can be tuned to match translocation data under a single experimental condition, but none has been tested against an independent constraint capable of distinguishing genuine nanoscale surface physics from curve-fitting. Here, we resolve this ambiguity using pressure-driven counterflow as such an independent test by measuring how the event-charge-deficit distribution of DNA translocations responds to a controlled counterpressure. Our model combining a sub-nanometer stagnant fluid layer (δ ≈ 0.18 nm, consistent across all lengths tested) with coil drag scaled by the radius of gyration reproduces the measured pressure dependence; models omitting either effect require unphysical parameter values and break down as pressure increases. These results establish the stagnant layer as a physically real departure from continuum hydrodynamics rather than a fitting artifact, and yield an analytical expression for the pressure-dependent translocation velocity that offers a route toward more accurate velocity models for nanopore sequencing and sensing.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics of a three-arm star polymer translocating through a nanopore
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: In this work, voltage-driven translocation of uniformly charged long linear and three-arm star polymers through narrow nanopores is investigated. Langevin dynamics simulation is performed using a coarse-grained model of the polymer and a semi-implicit representation of the nanopore. The mean translocation time of a linear polymer is found to be inversely proportional to the applied voltage over a wide range of voltages. In contrast, the mean translocation time of a three-arm star polymer of the same molecular weight exhibits a pronounced deviation from this scaling relation below a threshold voltage. The threshold voltage is found to be nearly independent of the molecular weight of the polymer but depends on the size of the nanopore and salt concentration. Metadynamics simulation is used to estimate the free energy landscape for the translocation of the three-arm star polymer. Below the threshold voltage, the free energy exhibits a pronounced second barrier resulting from an entropic contribution and electrostatic interactions between segments of the trailing arm inside the nanopore. A Fokker–Planck model developed using the estimated free energy accurately predicts the deviation from the scaling relation below the threshold voltage and shows a remarkable agreement with the Langevin dynamics simulation results using a voltage-independent fitting parameter. The agreement between the theory and the Langevin dynamics simulation results is seen for different nanopore radii, molecular weights of the polymer, and salt concentrations studied. A simple extension of the free energy landscape is suggested to predict translocation kinetics for higher molecular weights of the polymer without performing additional computationally expensive simulations.

papers.title: Approximating committor functions: Objective functions and enhanced sampling
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Many molecular dynamics simulations aim to study transitions between two states (from reactant to product states). In this context, the committor function (which gives, for a given molecular configuration, the probability of reaching the product state before the reactant state) is a pivotal quantity, in particular because it is the optimal importance function for rare-event simulation methods, such as importance sampling or splitting techniques. These methods are used to sample the reactive path ensemble and estimate, for example, the transition rate. However, learning such a function is generally a challenging task due to the high dimensionality of the configuration space. In this work, after reviewing existing methodologies to construct approximate committor functions, we propose a new loss function based on the application of Itō’s formula to learn the committor function with a minimization procedure on the parameters of a neural network. After comparing this novel approach to existing procedures on the Müller–Brown potential, we introduce a coupling strategy with the Adaptive Multilevel Splitting method to better approximate the committor function by improving the sampling of the reactive trajectories. This methodology, in which the committor function is iteratively learned, initially requires only knowledge of the reactant and product states.

papers.title: Determination of fundamental properties of nitrogen from first principles. III. Temperature and frequency dependence of the molecular polarizability and magnetic susceptibility
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: This work is the third part of the series of papers that focus on the theoretical determination of the properties of nitrogen that are relevant in metrology. Here, we present first-principles calculations of the temperature and frequency dependence of the molecular polarizability and magnetic susceptibility of the nitrogen molecule (N2). The purely electronic contributions to the static polarizability, Cauchy coefficients (up to sixth order), and isotropic magnetic susceptibility are computed over a range of internuclear distances using a robust composite scheme combining several electronic structure methods. The temperature dependence, evaluated from 50 to 2000 K, is determined using two independent methods: rovibrational averaging and path integral Monte Carlo. The polarizabilities obtained from theory agree with the recent high-precision thermometry measurements, wherever the latter are available, but are significantly less accurate. However, the main usefulness of the theoretical data revolves around combining it with the available experimental results to generate semi-empirical estimates of various quantities that have never been measured thus far. As an example, we determine highly accurate semi-empirical estimates of the static polarizability at key reference temperatures, α0(T) = 11.735 962 a.u. at T = 303 K and α0(T) = 11.735 585 a.u. at T = 273.16 K. Furthermore, we report theoretical values for the magnetic susceptibility, highlighting the importance of the paramagnetic contribution, and address a significant discrepancy with the experimental data for this quantity.
papers.zh: 从第一性原理确定氮气的基本性质。III. 分子极化率和磁化率的温度和频率依赖性

papers.title: Determination of fundamental properties of nitrogen from first principles. I. Atomic polarizabilities and long-range dispersion coefficients
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: This work is the first in a series of papers in which we perform theoretical calculations of various fundamental properties of nitrogen relevant for gas thermometry experiments. In this part, we focus on the properties of the nitrogen atom, namely, dynamic polarizabilities and dispersion coefficients that describe interaction between two nitrogen atoms at large internuclear separations. These quantities are calculated using a composite scheme based on coupled cluster and full configuration interaction methods and large Gaussian basis sets optimized specifically for the purposes of this work. The dispersion coefficients, Cn with n = 6, 8, 10, are obtained using Casimir–Polder formulas by numerical integration over dipole, quadrupole, and octupole polarizabilities for imaginary frequencies represented analytically by Padé approximants. Special attention is paid to careful error control and uncertainty estimation of the calculated quantities.

papers.title: External potentials for bottom-up coarse-graining of inhomogeneous fluids: On improving thermodynamic transferability
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Bottom-up coarse-grained models derived from all-atom simulations of interfacial or strongly inhomogeneous molecular fluids often suffer from limited thermodynamic transferability due to insufficient sampling of composition variations in the reference simulations, which can bias learned interactions. Rather than increasing model complexity, we show that simple, pairwise coarse-grained models can achieve improved thermodynamic transferability when trained on reference ensembles with enhanced thermodynamic information. We introduce an external ensemble methodology that employs pairwise external potentials to drive equilibrium compositional fluctuations in the all-atom reference simulations of a model inhomogeneous dodecane–water system, thereby enriching the thermodynamic information available for coarse-graining. We show that this information content can be systematically quantified and optimized using a particle fluctuation number metric directly computable in the reference ensemble that is related to the Fisher information. Coupling this approach with relative entropy minimization, we show that maximizing the compositional fluctuations according to this information metric yields substantially improved coarse-grained model predictions of the all-atom alkane–water transfer free energies. We compare different coarse-graining protocols and types of external Gaussian potentials to show that this improvement is consistently observed. Finally, we show that improved alkane–water transfer free energies enhance predictions of hydrophobically driven self-assembly behavior, with external-ensemble-derived coarse-grained models yielding an order-of-magnitude improvement in the predicted critical micelle concentration of sodium dodecyl sulfate relative to conventionally derived coarse-grained models.

papers.title: Global approximations to the error function of real argument for vectorized computation
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The error function of a real argument can be approximated to a given uniform relative accuracy by a single closed-form expression for the whole variable range, either in terms of addition, multiplication, division, and square root operations only, or also using the exponential function. Approximations to the complementary error function have also been found, including those where either only additions, multiplications, and one division, or also the exponential, are used to reach either a uniform absolute, or a uniform relative, accuracy. The coefficients have been tabulated for up to 128-bit precision. Tests of a computer code implementation using the standard single- and double-precision floating-point arithmetic show good performance and vectorizability.

papers.title: Understanding the impact of BiVO4 surface facet and termination on infrared spectroscopy and oxygen evolution reaction
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The infrared (IR) spectra of BiVO4 surfaces are sensitive to local atomic structure and can potentially provide insight into surface heterogeneity observed in recent spatially resolved nano-Fourier-transform infrared (nano-FTIR) spectroscopy measurements. However, no clear relationship has been established yet between IR spectral features and the surface atomic structures in BiVO4. Here, we used first-principles calculations to investigate the IR signatures of four low-index BiVO4 surface orientations with stoichiometric and Bi-rich terminations. We found that the most distinctive spectral feature is the symmetric stretching mode of VO43− units, which is present only on stoichiometric surfaces and exhibits facet-dependent frequency shifts and intensity variations. Analysis of the vibrational modes showed that these changes originate from differences in the magnitude and orientation of surface-induced V–O bond distortions relative to the surface normal direction. Comparison with experimental nano-FTIR spectra shows a consistent trend in the change of the symmetric stretching peak intensity across different surface facets, while discrepancies in the relative intensity ratio between asymmetric and symmetric stretching modes suggest additional contributions from experimental factors, including probe depth and tip orientation. Oxygen evolution reaction calculations further confirm the strong influence of surface orientation and termination on catalytic activity. These results establish a direct link between surface atomic structure, IR signatures, and catalytic behavior in BiVO4, providing a framework for interpreting nanoscale IR spectroscopy measurements of heterogeneous photocatalyst surfaces.

papers.title: Polarity-Resolved and Nonlinear HfZrO x Memcapacitive Dynamics for Mask-Free Reservoir Computing
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Physical reservoir computing (RC) seeks to harness intrinsic nonequilibrium device dynamics, but practical implementations often still rely on external feature extraction and random masking. Here, we exploit the polarity-resolved and nonlinear voltage-state dynamics of a solution-processed HfZrOx (HZO) memcapacitor as distinct computational functions. The polarity-dependent response maps positive and negative temporal variations of electromyography signals into separated reservoir states, enabling bipolar differential RC without conventional time- or frequency-domain feature extraction and achieving 91.67% gesture-recognition accuracy. The experimentally calibrated nonlinear voltage-state response is further reused layer by layer to diversify reservoir states without externally generated random masks, increasing the accuracy from 94.17% to 98.75%. Because both input and output are represented in the voltage domain, the device is also compatible with direct interlayer signal transfer without current-to-voltage conversion. These results show how intrinsic memcapacitive dynamics can replace externally imposed processing steps in physical RC.

papers.title: Temperature-Dependent Defect Thermodynamics and Nonradiative Recombination in Cubic CsPbBr3: The Role of Anharmonic Lattice Dynamics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: All-inorganic lead halide perovskites exhibit anomalous temperature-dependent electronic structures, yet how thermal lattice dynamics modulate defect energetics and nonadiabatic recombination remains unclear. By combining first-principles calculations and nonadiabatic coupling analysis, we investigate intrinsic defects in cubic CsPbBr3 at finite temperatures. We show that defect behavior is governed by the coupling strength between the defect and the anharmonic Pb–Br octahedral framework: strongly coupled defects undergo pronounced thermal renormalization of their levels and enhanced electron–phonon coupling, whereas weakly coupled defects exhibit smaller absolute nonadiabatic couplings. Heating renormalizes the band edges and defect levels and enhances the nonadiabatic coupling between conduction band state and defect state of strongly coupled defects. These findings establish that in strongly anharmonic halide perovskites finite-temperature lattice dynamics, rather than static 0 K defect energetics, is essential for understanding defect electronic structure and coupling relevant to carrier capture.

papers.title: Near-Field Radiative Heat Transfer in Multilayers with Thickness-Graded Transdimensional Films
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Transdimensional (TD) plasmonic materials are characterized by confinement-induced nonlocality, resulting in a thickness-dependent optical response. Multilayer structures enhance near-field radiative heat transfer through a relay mechanism, and graded structures can broaden the spectral response. We consider two multilayer structures separated by a vacuum gap, each composed of alternating TD and dielectric films, with the TD films varying in thickness along the stacking direction. The nonlocal TD response produces a redshift of approximately 13.7% and raises the peak spectral heat-transfer coefficient to 5.54 times that of the uniform Drude case. The thickness gradient broadens the high-transmission regions and raises the peak to 8.82 times that of the uniform TD case. The thickness profile controls both interfacial coupling and the optical response of individual layers. This combined control provides a potential route for enhancing and spectrally tailoring near-field radiative heat transfer.

papers.title: Nonsymmetric Vibronic Activity in the Planar Propargyl Cation Revealed by High-Resolution VUV-MATI Spectroscopy
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: High-resolution vacuum ultraviolet mass-analyzed threshold ionization spectroscopy was used to probe the low-frequency vibronic structure of the propargyl cation following threshold ionization. Rotational-contour analysis combined with zero-field extrapolation yielded a field-free adiabatic ionization energy of 70,170 ± 3 cm–1 and constrained the cationic rotational constant to A+ = 9.39(3) cm–1, both consistent with previous high-resolution measurements. Most notably, the ν8 fundamental is directly observed at 263 cm–1 together with its 82 overtone at 523 cm–1, while ν7 activity is also resolved. The ν7 and ν8 fundamentals are not reproduced by the conventional harmonic Franck–Condon (FC) treatment of the well-established planar C2V cation, whereas the totally symmetric 82 overtone is predicted with appreciable intensity and supports the ν8 assignment and progression. Displaced-geometry calculations demonstrate the strong sensitivity of the FC envelope to small structural displacements but do not establish symmetry lowering. The results therefore provide direct experimental constraints on nonsymmetric threshold-photoionization intensity and on possible vibronic, non-Condon, and anharmonic contributions.

papers.title: Multi-Barrel Nanopipets as a Model System for Quantifying Interpore Interactions and Superadditive Transport
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Developing advanced neuromorphic ionic devices requires a quantitative understanding of how neighboring nanopores interact within arrays. Crosstalk between adjacent pores is especially important because overlapping depletion zones can suppress current and cause the current through a parallel-pore array to be lower than the sum of currents through isolated pores. Here, using dual-barrel nanopipets as a model two-pore array, we show that interacting barrels connected in parallel can also produce superadditive transport, where the combined current exceeds the sum of currents through two independently measured barrels. Conductance enhancement is observed when closely spaced barrels carry opposite surface charges, with one barrel negatively charged and the other positively charged. Poisson–Nernst–Planck and Navier–Stokes continuum modeling further clarifies the role of ion concentration polarization. The models indicate that applying voltage across neighboring, oppositely charged pores creates an ion-enriched zone at the entrance of one barrel that feeds the depletion zone at the entrance of the second barrel, thereby mitigating ion concentration polarization and increasing the combined conductance. These experiments and models advance understanding of electrically and chemically addressable, interacting nanopores for future ionic circuits.

papers.title: Assessment of the Reproducibility of Experimental Results in Aqueous Alkaline Media Using Pt Electrodes
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Research in interfacial electrochemistry and electrocatalysis requires establishing standard experimental procedures and conditions that ensure reproducibility and reliability of results. While standard procedures for experimental research employing Pt electrodes in aqueous acidic solutions were established ca. 50 years ago, similar benchmarks for aqueous alkaline media do not exist. In this contribution, cyclic voltammetry (CV) experiments are performed in the 0.05–1.40 V range using polycrystalline and monocrystalline platinum electrodes (Pt(poly) and Pt(POSSC)) in 0.50 M aqueous H2SO4 (a reference electrolyte solution) and 0.10 M aqueous NaOH (a studied electrolyte solution) to verify the systems’ cleanliness and to determine the electrodes’ electrochemically active surface area (Aecsa). Afterward, chronoamperometry (CA) measurements are conducted by holding the applied potential at 0.50 V for various holding times in the 30–1,800 s range, and then Aecsa is re-evaluated by CV experiments. The results demonstrate that unavoidable contamination, present even in the highest purity chemicals and water, adsorbs on the surface of the Pt electrodes and reduces their Aecsa. The reduction in Aecsa increases with increasing the holding time in CA measurements. Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDS) spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses of the Pt(poly) and Pt(POSSC) electrodes reveal the presence of C and O-containing compounds in the case of aqueous H2SO4 solution and C, O, and Pb compounds in the case of aqueous NaOH solution. The results demonstrate the complementarity of electrochemical and surface science methods in assessing the cleanliness of electrode materials and highlight the need for rigorous experimental protocols that ensure reproducibility and reliability of experimental results.

papers.title: Probing Single Ions at Mica-Aqueous Interfaces Using Atomic Force Microscopy
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Over the last decades, atomic force microscopy (AFM) has developed into a tool capable of mapping the equilibrium 3-dimensional organization of liquid molecules at the interface with solids using a vibrating tip. While very successful for pure liquids, measurements in solutions containing dissolved ions or molecules can be more challenging due to the fact that the AFM tip can unwittingly remove single adsorbates during the measurement. This issue is particularly important for high-resolution measurements in liquid, potentially leading to adsorbed species becoming effectively invisible to the AFM despite it resolving details of the smaller liquid molecules. Here, we explore this issue systematically on a known system: the mica-water interface in aqueous solutions of 5 mM RbCl, KCl, NaCl, LiCl and 2 mM CaCl2, and pure water as a reference. The different metal cations all adsorb to the interface, but with different strengths and hydration states. We show that although atomic-level resolution of the hydrated interface can always be achieved, resolving the adsorbed ions depends on the tip vibration amplitude and imaging conditions. Measurements conducted at smaller amplitude are dominated by the equilibrium water molecular arrangement, with ionic effects becoming more prominent at larger amplitudes. This is particularly clear for ions such as Rb+ which adsorb further from the interface compared to ions with higher charge density. The results are discussed for each ion in terms of the hydration state and the measured conservative and dissipative interactions of the measuring tip.
