papers.title: Controlling Mineral Disintegration in Charged Water Microdroplets by Added Transition Metal Ions
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: In this work, we investigate the effect of electrolyte composition on mineral fragmentation in electrosprayed aqueous microdroplets. Quartz (SiO2) and corundum (α-Al2O3) suspensions containing transition-metal ions in different oxidation states (Fe2+/Fe3+, Cu+/Cu2+, and Cr2+/Cr3+), as well as representative monovalent (Na+, K+) and divalent (Mg2+, Ca2+) cations, were electrosprayed under identical conditions. Among the tested transition-metal salt formulations, the lower-oxidation-state systems were associated with fragmentation at lower applied voltages and smaller nanoparticles, whereas the higher-oxidation-state systems required higher applied voltages for comparable fragmentation. Similar trends were observed across all transition-metal cations (Fe2+/Fe3+, Cu+/Cu2+, Cr2+/Cr3+) on both mineral systems. The generality of this approach, where a foreign ion enhances disintegration efficiency, was further supported by the efficient formation of silica nanoparticles in the presence of the imidazolium-based ionic liquid, BMIM-Cl. Finite-element simulations coupling electrostatics with two-phase flow reveal that moderate volume charge densities (∼10 C·m–3) sustain asymmetric “rough” Coulombic fission with prolonged droplet–mineral contact, whereas high charge densities (50–100 C·m–3) trigger rapid “fine” fission into progeny droplets, dissipating electrostatic energy before effective mineral breakage. These results demonstrate that electrolyte composition is an experimental variable for tuning microdroplet-mediated mineral disintegration and motivate further investigation of the physicochemical factors underlying the observed trends.

papers.title: Modulating Excited-State Charge Transfer Character in 1,6,7,12-Tetrakis( p -X-phenoxy)perylene-(3,4:9,10)-bis(dicarboximide) Single Crystals
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Enhancing the excited-state charge transfer character in homogeneous organic solids provides an avenue to promote electron−hole pair generation between identical chromophores, potentially enabling higher efficiencies in organic photovoltaics. Previous studies have demonstrated that chromophore orientation has a significant effect on the propensity for complete charge separation in the solid state, but the interplay between electronic and steric effects within similar crystal packing regimes remains an open question. In this study, we compare single crystals of three 1,6,7,12-tetrakis(p-X-phenoxy)perylene-(3,4:9,10)-bis(dicarboximide)s, where X = Br, CF3, and t-butyl, Br-tpPDI, CF3-tpPDI, and tBu-tpPDI, respectively, which are found to have similar extended packing structures but sub-Å differences in slip-stacking distances between neighboring chromophores. Transient absorption microscopy shows the formation of a mixed Frenkel exciton/charge transfer (CT) excimer in all three derivatives. We find that the crystal structure of CF3-tpPDI possesses a dimer pair with a favorable geometry that accentuates the excited-state polarizability, and thus, this derivative possesses the highest degree of CT character in the mixed state. These results show that the core substituent properties of these PDI chromophores direct excited-state evolution, providing a design criterion for optimizing charge separation in solid-state organic materials.

papers.title: Collective Emission in Geometry-Aware Hierarchically Constructed LH2 Assemblies
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Collective emission in light-harvesting assemblies is governed by the local transition dipole and finite geometry of emitting units. To capture this, we develop a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian using the quantum electrodynamic dyadic Green’s tensor for a purple bacteria. We construct it for the isolated 24-bacteriochlorophyll conical frustum and its P4212 crystallographic assembly. The P4212 unit-cell symmetry is found to invert the bright-dark ordering of the single ring, placing subradiant states at the low-energy end and revealing the entire crystal to be the energy-harvesting entity. Tilt-driven switching is activated only in crystal geometries where the finite dipole-carrier (LH2) lies perpendicular to the growth plane. Vacancy and orientational disorder work only in cooperation to renormalize the switching threshold from higher polar angles to lower values.

papers.title: Large-Area Nanoporous Iron Oxide Thin Films with an Interconnected Worm-like Architecture Fabricated by Lyotropic Liquid Crystal Templating
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Large-area nanoporous metal oxide thin films with controlled morphology and high structural uniformity are of significant interest for applications in sensing, optoelectronics, catalysis, and energy conversion. Herein, we report, for the first time, a simple and scalable lyotropic liquid crystal (LLC)-templating strategy for the fabrication of large-area, uniform nanoporous Fe2O3 thin films with an interconnected worm-like nanostructure. The LLC precursor solutions were prepared from iron nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) as the iron source and the nonionic surfactant 10-lauryl ether (C12E10) as the structure-directing agent in a water–alcohol solvent mixture. Spin coating of the Fe(NO3)3–C12E10 LLC precursor solution onto solid substrates produced ordered Fe(NO3)3–C12E10 LLC films in which Fe3+ ions were confined within the hydrophilic domains of the mesophase. The structural evolution of the LLC films was systematically investigated as a function of the Fe(NO3)3/C12E10 molar ratio using low-angle X-ray diffraction and polarized optical microscopy. The results revealed the formation of well-ordered liquid-crystalline mesophases at optimized compositions, particularly at a Fe(NO3)3/C12E10 molar ratio of 3. Subsequent calcination at 450 °C removed the organic template and converted the hybrid films into crack-free, large-area (several cm2) nanoporous hematite phase of iron oxide (α-Fe2O3). The nanoporous films exhibit an interconnected worm-like morphology with structural features below 25 nm, consistent with their mesoporous nature. The films possess an indirect optical band gap of approximately 2.0 eV and a direct optical band gap of approximately 2.45 eV, consistent with the semiconducting behavior of hematite. Furthermore, the nanoporous iron oxide films are fully compatible with conventional photolithographic processing, enabling the direct fabrication of patterned microelectrodes and their integration into photodetector devices. The nanoporous iron oxide photodetectors exhibit a fast, reversible photoresponse with a responsivity of 26 nA/W under 488 nm illumination. This work establishes a versatile and scalable route for high-quality nanoporous hematite thin films and demonstrates their potential applications in optoelectronics, photocatalysis, sensing, flexible electronics, and electrochemical energy storage.

papers.title: Vacancy Dynamics Govern Selectivity in Chemical Looping Methane Oxidation over NiO
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Chemical looping methane oxidation over NiO is governed by oxygen-diffusion-controlled vacancy dynamics rather than by a single fixed reaction pathway. Density functional theory calculations show that the preferred mechanism and its rate-determining step change with the oxygen-vacancy population on NiO(100), shifting from a CH3O-mediated route on the pristine surface (101.7 kJ/mol) to dehydrogenation-dominated and oxygen-assisted routes limited by CO (82.9 kJ/mol) and CH2* (91.3 kJ/mol) oxidation as vacancies accumulate. Subsurface-to-surface oxygen migration, with barriers of 213–243 kJ/mol, dictates how rapidly consumed lattice oxygen is replenished, and a diffusion-coupled microkinetic model predicts a temperature-dependent transition from a surface-limited regime favoring incomplete oxidation to a subsurface-limited regime sustaining complete combustion. Bubbling fluidized-bed experiments on a spray-dried NiO oxygen carrier (≈85 μm particles, ≈13 wt % reversible oxygen capacity) confirm this picture: CH4 breakthrough with concurrent CO and H2 evolution occurs progressively earlier as temperature is lowered (190, 310, and 750 s at 600, 700, and 800 °C), whereas complete oxidation to CO2 is maintained throughout the run at 900 °C. These results identify lattice-oxygen diffusion as a key operando descriptor of selectivity and suggest a design principle for oxygen carriers and operating windows in chemical looping methane conversion.

papers.title: Preparation and Optimization of a CoNi Bimetallic Catalyst by a Quasi-Solid-State Mechanochemical Method for Enhanced Hydrogen Storage Performance of MgH2
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Catalysts play a critical role in improving the hydrogen storage properties in the Mg/MgH2 system. Exploring highly efficient catalysts and revealing their catalytic mechanism are hot topics but also challenging. Transition 3d metals like Ni and Co have long been established as effective catalysts for hydrogen storage materials. To maximize the synergistic effect between Ni and Co, a CoNi alloy catalyst was synthesized and optimized via a quasi-solid-state mechanochemical method. The different states of CoNi alloy catalysts were obtained by tuning the calcination temperatures to 500, 600, and 700 °C during the preparation process. The results indicated that as the calcination temperature increased, both the particle size and crystallinity of the CoNi nanoparticles increased. The catalytic results show that the Mg/MgH2 system exhibited the optimal performance when doped with 6 wt % of the catalyst synthesized at 700 °C. Specifically, this catalyzed system achieved an onset hydrogen desorption temperature of 191 °C, and the system could release 6.4 wt % H2 within 600 s at 325 °C, along with absorbing 4.9 wt % H2 within 1000 s at 150 °C. Furthermore, compared to catalysts prepared at other temperatures, the above system demonstrated superior low-temperature performance and excellent cycling stability, retaining 98% of its capacity after 20 cycles. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effect between Co and Ni, which facilitates hydrogen dissociation-diffusion and Mg–H bond cleavage-recombination. Notably, it appears that particle size and crystallinity may play opposing roles in governing the catalytic efficiency.

papers.title: Enhanced Nonlinear Optical and Time-Resolved Properties of Magic Number Iron (Fe) Nanoclusters Prepared by Egg-White Synthesis
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Protein-templated iron (EW:Fe) and gold (EW:Au) nanoclusters (NCs) were synthesized using chicken egg white as a biomolecular template and characterized with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). The synthesis yielded small EW:Fe and EW:Au nanoclusters with average diameters of 2.1 and 2.6 nm, respectively. One- and two-photon excited fluorescence measurements showed visible emission centered near 440 nm for both nanoclusters, with additional emission bands at 650 nm for EW:Au and 850 nm for EW:Fe. The fluorescence quantum yields were determined to be 0.23% for EW:Fe and 0.16% for EW:Au. Both systems displayed strong nonlinear optical responses as shown by their two-photon absorption cross sections. Time-resolved fluorescence measurements revealed multicomponent excited-state decay dynamics with characteristic lifetimes on the tens to hundreds of picoseconds time scale. The observed photophysical behavior is interpreted within a superatomic molecular orbital framework, providing new insight into the excited-state dynamics and nonlinear optical properties of novel, protein-templated Fe nanoclusters.

papers.title: Selective CO Sensing on Single-Atom W@C3N Driven by Double-Channel Orbital Coupling
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Selective detection of carbon monoxide (CO) in mixed reducing gas environments remains challenging because chemically similar molecules often produce comparable sensing responses. Here, by combining density functional theory (DFT) and nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) calculations, we identify W@C3N as a single-atom sensing platform with a preferential response toward CO among reducing gases within a series of metal-decorated C3N systems. W@C3N exhibits the strongest CO adsorption and the largest charge transfer, while the adsorbed structure remains dynamically and thermally stable. Electronic structure analysis shows that the CO selectivity originates from double-channel orbital coupling at the W site. Beyond the conventional interaction involving the W dz2 orbital, a reconstructed multi-d-orbital state provides an additional coupling channel near the Fermi level, leading to pronounced interfacial charge redistribution. As a result, CO induces much stronger orbital hybridization and transport modulation than NH3, PH3, and H2S. Especially, the calculated sensitivity toward CO reaches about 10 in a graphene/W@C3N/graphene device model. Our findings reveal that orbital regulation of single-atom centers is an effective route to enhancing CO selectivity within reducing gas environments.

papers.title: The van der Waals Heterostructures MoS2/TeGaInX (X = S, Se, Te) for Optoelectronic and Photocatalytic Applications
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Rising energy demands and environmental concerns are accelerating the shift to clean energy, with hydrogen technology emerging as one of the most promising solutions. In this study, the MoS2/TeGaInX van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) were thoroughly investigated for optoelectronic and photocatalytic applications using first-principles calculations. A significant interfacial potential drop leads to a strong internal electric field, which effectively suppresses carrier recombination and encourages the spatial separation of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. These vdWHs have favorable band edge potentials for overall water splitting at pH = 0, along with the exceptionally high carrier mobilities up to 104 cm2 V–1 s–1. The MoS2/TeGaInS, MoS2/SInGaTe, MoS2/TeGaInSe, and MoS2/TeInGaTe vdWHs exhibit remarkable solar-to-hydrogen (ηsth) efficiencies up to 30%, indicating their great potential for effective hydrogen production. Furthermore, the vdWHs show improved optical responses, such as substantial imaginary dielectric functions and high absorption coefficients up to 105 cm–1 in the visible-light spectrum, demonstrating superior light-harvesting capabilities. Overall, this work provides a deeper physical insight on Janus-based MoS2 heterostructures and offers valuable theoretical guidance for designing high-performance vdW-based photocatalytic and optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Computational Study of the Dissociation Reactions of Methyl Acrylate on the Cu(111) Surface
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to study the adsorption and dissociation of methyl acrylate (MA), with chemical formula CH2CHCOOCH3, on the Cu(111) surface. MA is a biodiesel surrogate molecule whose dissociation products may contribute to the corrosion of metallic components and engine damage. Three adsorption configurations were examined, the most stable of which is when the vinyl group (CH2═CH) covalently bonds with the Cu(111) surface with an adsorption energy of −1.38 eV and a charge transfer of −0.41|e|. The calculated reaction energies and activation barriers differ significantly from those in the gas phase, highlighting the influence of the Cu(111) surface on the reactivity. Climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) calculations gave activation barriers between 38 and 82 kcal/mol with CH2CHCOOCH3 → CH2CHCO + OCH3 as the most favorable dissociation pathway. The reaction energies fall in the range −3 to 47 kcal/mol. Further insight into the adsorption and dissociation processes via the analysis of bond lengths, charge-transfer, and partial density of states indicates that two of the adsorption configurations are characterized by strong covalent interactions whereas the third configuration has a weaker interaction with the surface. These strong interactions with the surface weaken the C═C double bond and stabilize transition states providing a catalytic effect on the different dissociation processes. Our results demonstrate that the Cu(111) surface promotes strong adsorption that lowers the reaction energies and drastically modifies the dissociation mechanisms compared with those in the gas phase, thus shedding light on the possible corrosion effects of biodiesel on copper-containing components in automotive fuel systems and engines.

papers.title: A Molecular Switch Governing Piezo1 Gating beyond Symmetry Breaking
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: A single substituent can flip a ligand from an agonist to an inhibitor, yet the underlying conformational dynamics remain elusive. Here, multiscale simulations calibrated against Yoda1 binding data resolve the ligand-dependent gating free-energy landscapes of the mechanosensitive channel Piezo1. In the unliganded state, the free-energy landscape supports a gating mechanism involving axial pore dislocation, lateral dilation, and realignment. The agonist Yoda1 stabilizes a widely dilated pore with persistent axial asymmetry, whereas the inhibitor Dooku1 arrests pore expansion after initial dislocation. This divergence reveals a geometrically selective relay between the intracellular Beam and transmembrane helical unit 9 (THU9). Productive coupling to pore dilation, rather than Beam rotation alone, dictates the pharmacological response. Guided by this mechanism, we designed Yoda1 analogs bearing an amino or nitro substitution at the same position, whose free-energy landscapes predicted contrasting functions. Intracellular calcium fluorescence assays were consistent with these predictions: the amino-substituted analog 188 elevated intracellular calcium levels, whereas the nitro-substituted analog 187 attenuated the Yoda1-evoked calcium response. These findings link single-site chemical modifications to divergent gating outcomes via symmetry breaking and pore dilation, identifying productive conformational coupling as a key molecular design parameter alongside binding affinity.

papers.title: Conformational Transition of Diphenylthiourea upon Hydrogen-Bond Formation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Unraveling the fine details of hydrogen-bond structure and conformation within catalyst-substrate complexes is key to advancing organocatalysis. By employing two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, this work provides evidence for a conformational transition of diphenylthiourea, induced by hydrogen-bond formation to 1,3-diphenyl-2-propenone in solution. Spectral shifts and coupling patterns indicate only one N–H (probed here via N–D) donor participating in hydrogen bonding. The vibrational spectra reveal a striking inhomogeneity in hydrogen-bond strength, and cross-peak analysis is consistent with single-site donor–acceptor geometry, rendering bifurcated interactions unlikely. Comparison of experimental spectral shifts upon H-bonding to harmonic frequencies from density functional theory calculations suggests a transition of diphenylthiourea from the cis–trans to the trans–trans conformation upon H-bond formation. These results highlight the interplay between molecular geometry and vibrational coupling, thereby helping to resolve the molecular structure of reactive intermediates in thiourea catalysis.

papers.title: A Hydroxyl Radical Model for the S3 State of Photosystem II
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The chemical identity of the oxygen-evolving complex (OEC) in the metastable heterogeneous S3 state that precedes water oxidation remains intensely debated. Multiple ideas regarding the oxidation states of the four constituent Mn ions, as well as the number and protonation states of oxygen ligands are being considered, entailing distinct mechanistic pathways for the subsequent O–O bond formation. Here we describe a previously unreported possibility for the OEC in the S3 state identified by quantum chemical calculations. The model contains a hydroxyl radical that is bridging a terminal Mn center and the redox-inactive Ca2+ ion. In contrast to past ligand-radical suggestions the hydroxyl radical form has a crystallographically consistent intracluster O···O distance of 2.0 Å, while its total proton count is fully aligned with experimental data. Calculations suggest that the hydroxyl radical intermediate has a low-spin or diamagnetic ground state. Importantly, its unusual excited state profile make it a rare, though not definitive, candidate for the near-infrared absorbing component of the S3 state. The hydroxyl radical model enriches our perspectives on S3 state heterogeneity and expands the map of structure–property correlations in biological water oxidation.

papers.title: pH-Resolved SAXS Analysis of the Solution Assembly of Murine Amelogenin Variants
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Amelogenin is an intrinsically disordered enamel matrix protein whose pH-dependent self-assembly is central to enamel biomineralization. Although AMELX-associated mutations and engineered variants are known to alter enamel structure, how these sequence changes affect amelogenin solution-state ensembles and assembly pathways remains unclear. Here, we combine small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) with monomeric replica exchange molecular dynamics (REMD) simulations to characterize nonphosphorylated murine amelogenin (rM179), Ser16-phosphorylated amelogenin (pS16), the amelogenin point mutants P41T and T21I, and the amelogenin deletion variants H3 (minus H67, H68, and H69) and Delta (minus A166 - D179 at C-terminal) at pH 3, 6, and 8. SAXS data shows that all variants remain disordered at pH 3 but differ in compaction and degree of self-association: H3 samples a more compact ensemble, Delta exhibits expansion or weak self-association, and T21I forms ribbon-like aggregates. REMD provides monomer-level context for these SAXS trends, predicting variant-dependent differences in conformational dimensions and transient structural propensities. At pH 6, pS16 and P41T favor smaller, more dynamic low-order assemblies, whereas T21I and Delta promote larger self-associated species; H3 occupies an intermediate regime. At pH 8, most variants form nanosphere-like assemblies with sequence-dependent size and heterogeneity, while the soluble Delta fraction lacks a well-defined nanosphere population. These results show that phosphorylation, point mutation, histidine deletion, and C-terminal truncation redistribute amelogenin among distinct pH-dependent assembly states, linking sequence variation to enamel-relevant self-assembly behavior.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Phase Partitioning and Nanoscale Mixing in Rapidly Condensed U/Al and U/Al/Fe Vapors
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Rapid cooling of multicomponent vapors produces oxide particles through coupled oxidation, nucleation, condensation, and aggregation occurring on millisecond time scales. In uranium-bearing systems, these pathways remain poorly understood when redox-active and refractory elements condense together. Here, we isolate the effect of initial composition by comparing binary uranium/aluminum (U/Al) and ternary uranium/aluminum/iron (U/Al/Fe) vapors condensed under a fixed temperature profile in a plasma flow reactor (PFR). Oxygen for oxide formation was supplied through the aqueous nitrate precursors introduced into the argon plasma. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), electron diffraction, elemental mapping, and image-based particle statistics were used to relate particle morphology, crystal structure, elemental partitioning, and projected particle size. Binary U/Al condensates formed predominantly α-UO3 and η-Al2O3 as small, weakly aggregated particles. Increasing Fe relative to Al shifted the condensates toward larger aggregates containing UO2, η-Al2O3, Fe3O4, and mixed U–Fe oxides. Correlated high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) measurements show that U and Fe are spatially associated within particle aggregates, including mixed U–Fe oxide crystallites, whereas Al preferentially partitions into spatially distinct crystalline and amorphous Al-rich regions. These results demonstrate that initial composition controls both phase selection and nanoscale chemical partitioning during rapid condensation, providing particle-scale constraints for models of nonequilibrium multicomponent oxide formation.

papers.title: Conformational Dynamics of Planar and Twisted Excited States of Methoxy-Substituted Phenylpyrrolinium Salts
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Arylpyrrolinium salts exhibit intriguing excited-state behavior that couples fluorescence with photochemical reactivity. While unsubstituted phenylpyrrolinium salts are nonfluorescent, methoxy-substituted derivatives display room-temperature fluorescence, providing an opportunity to investigate the structural and electronic factors governing their excited states. Here, we combine steady-state spectroscopy, time-resolved fluorescence measurements, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations to establish a model for the photophysics of these compounds. The observed fluorescence originates from a predominantly planar S1 excited state that is in equilibrium with a lower-energy twisted conformer. The planar conformer corresponds to the bright emissive state, whereas the twisted conformer represents a dark state that was previously implicated as the reactive intermediate in photochemical [σ2+π2]-type fragmentative addition reactions with electron-deficient olefins. The biexponential fluorescence decay observed for selected derivatives is consistent with dynamic interconversion between these excited-state conformations. Further, an N-methyl analogue is nonfluorescent because steric effects destabilize the planar geometry required for emission, supporting the proposed model. Fluorescence quantum yields are low but strongly dependent on solvent and counteranion identity, demonstrating that environmental interactions modulate the equilibrium between emissive and nonemissive pathways. These results reveal how subtle structural modifications control the balance between fluorescence and photochemical reactivity in arylpyrrolinium salts and provide a framework for understanding excited-state conformational dynamics in this class of molecules.
papers.zh: 甲氧基取代的苯基吡咯鎓盐平面和扭曲激发态的构象动力学

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into the Combined Effects of Substituent Modification, Electronegativity Modulation, Solvent Polarity, and External Electric Fields on ESIPT and Antioxidant Potential in 4′,5-Dihydroxy-7-methoxyflavone
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations were employed to systematically investigate the effects of substituent electronic characteristics, para-position heteroatom substitution, solvent polarity, and external electric fields (EEFs) on excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), emission photophysics, and antioxidant-related reactivity of 4′,5-dihydroxy-7-methoxyflavone (GKO) and its derivatives. Geometric, infrared vibrational, reduced density gradient (RDG), frontier molecular orbital (FMO), natural bond orbital (NBO), and potential energy curve (PEC) analyses reveal pronounced photoinduced reorganization of the intramolecular hydrogen-bonding environment. For GKO in dichloromethane (DCM), the H···O distance decreases from 1.670 Å in S0 to 0.987 Å in S1, accompanied by substantial elongation of the donor O–H bond, indicating pronounced proton displacement toward the acceptor upon excitation. The ground state proton transfer barrier of GKO is 6.41 kcal mol–1, decreasing to 4.57 kcal mol–1 with −CN substitution and increasing to 7.32 kcal mol–1 with −NH2 substitution. O → S substitution at the para position of the proton acceptor lowers the S0 barrier to 5.26 kcal mol–1, whereas increasing solvent polarity from DCM to DMSO produces only a minor decrease to 6.31 kcal mol–1. In the excited state, no apparent energy maximum is observed along the selected O–H proton transfer coordinate for any investigated system. Unconstrained S1 optimizations instead yield spontaneous proton migration without convergence to a stable normal excited-state (E*) minimum. The energy decrease toward the proton transferred region increases from 10.84 kcal mol–1 for GKO to 14.61 kcal mol–1 for GKO-NH2, demonstrating substantial substituent-dependent modulation of the S1 potential energy profile. EEFs induce pronounced nonlinear and direction-dependent changes in proton transfer energetics. A positive field of +0.01 au causes only minor perturbation of the S1 profile, whereas +0.02 au introduces finite barriers of 2.10 and 2.80 kcal mol–1 in DCM and DMSO, respectively. Negative fields produce substantially larger S1 barriers, reaching 10.07 kcal mol–1 in DCM and 11.79 kcal mol–1 in DMSO. Photophysical calculations show that all systems exhibit characteristic K* emission with Stokes shifts exceeding 110 nm, consistent with substantial excited-state structural relaxation associated with ESIPT. For GKO in DCM, the calculated keto emission is 482.67 nm with a Stokes shift of 148.89 nm. −CN substitution shifts the emission to 446.77 nm and increases the oscillator strength from 0.2719 to 0.4849, whereas −NH2 produces a pronounced red shift to 770.51 nm, a Stokes shift of 399.27 nm, and a reduced oscillator strength of 0.0169. EEFs further regulate emissive-state characteristics: +0.01 au increases the K* oscillator strength to 0.5691, while +0.02 au induces competition between E* and K* emission and changes the dominant emissive state. Negative fields strongly suppress the E* transition, yielding nearly zero oscillator strengths. Antioxidant-related calculations distinguish the roles of electron and hydrogen transfer descriptors. Photoexcitation decreases the IP of GKO from 7.52 to 6.71 eV, indicating enhanced electron transfer propensity, while −NH2 substitution lowers the O–H BDE from 97.662 to 78.960 kcal mol–1, favoring hydrogen atom transfer. Overall, substituent characteristics, para-position heteroatom substitution, solvent polarity, and EEFs exert distinct and state-dependent effects on ESIPT energetics, emission photophysics, and electron and hydrogen transfer-related reactivity, providing quantitative insights into the regulation of ESIPT and a theoretical basis for designing molecular systems with tunable optical and antioxidant-related properties.

papers.title: Valence Bond Insights into the Bonding Nature of N-Heterocyclic Carbenes
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The bonding characteristics of N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have long been the subject of debate, particularly regarding the relative importance of carbenic versus ylidic resonance contributions. In this work, we employ ab initio valence bond (VB) theory to systematically examine the electronic structure of a series of five-membered NHCs and closely related species. Our VB analyses reveal that carbenic and ylidic characters contribute comparably to the overall wave function, with ylidic character often more pronounced in NHCs, although their relative contributions depend sensitively on the atomic composition of the heterocyclic ring. The π framework of NHCs, arising from six electrons distributed over five pπ orbitals, exhibits substantial cyclic delocalization. In addition, our VB analysis provides insights into the bidirectional electron-delocalization processes between the carbene carbon and the adjacent atoms, namely π donation to the carbene carbon and σ donation from the carbene carbon, together with their associated energetic contributions. Taken together, these results offer a unified, quantitatively grounded description of NHC bonding, highlighting the distinctive roles of π and σ interactions in shaping the electronic structure of these chemically versatile systems.
papers.zh: 对N-杂环卡宾成键性质的价键理论洞察

papers.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Multifidelity Training Strategies for Reactive Machine Learning Potentials
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Training reactive machine learning potentials (MLPs) requires extensive quantum chemical labeling of nonequilibrium configurations along reaction pathways, motivating the use of data from lower levels of theory through pretraining and Δ-learning. However, whether combining these strategies consistently improves accuracy and downstream performance remains unclear. Here, we benchmark direct and residual training, each with and without pretraining, across DPA-2, DPA-3, MACE, and DPA4-Neo, using 17.6 million configurations labeled with GFN2-xTB and 198,622 configurations labeled at the ωB97X-D/def2-TZVP level. With the full DFT training set, pretrained Δ-learning achieves the lowest energy or force MAE averaged over three training seeds in 31 of 32 combinations of architecture, data set, and property. Learning curves for DPA4-Neo nevertheless show that direct finetuning reaches the MAE of a model trained from scratch on the full data set using no more DFT training configurations than pretrained Δ-learning in all eight combinations of data set and property, while avoiding repeated GFN2-xTB evaluations during inference. Pretrained Δ-learning also improves reaction energies and forward barriers across all four architectures on GDB-10-rxn and reduces median Hessian eigenvalue errors for the evaluated DPA4-Neo checkpoint. However, local force errors can remain incompletely corrected, and these improvements do not consistently increase the success rates of reaction search workflows initialized from specified reactant and product geometries, indicating that the preferred protocol depends on the data budget, target property, and downstream workflow.
papers.zh: 针对反应式机器学习势能的多保真度训练策略的系统性基准

papers.title: Relativistic Dirac–Coulomb–Breit Four-Component Multireference Perturbation Theory within the Small Tensor Product Distributed Active Space Framework
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We present a four-component multireference second-order perturbation theory (4C-MRPT2) within the small tensor product distributed active space (STP-DAS) framework. The formulation is compatible with the Dirac–Coulomb (DC), Dirac–Coulomb–Gaunt (DCG), and Dirac–Coulomb–Breit (DCB) Hamiltonians and inherits the memory-efficient and massively parallel STP-DAS algorithm, enabling perturbative treatments over very large external spaces. Benchmark calculations on noble-gas and group-13 atoms demonstrate that 4C-MRPT2 efficiently recovers all-electron dynamic correlation while providing new insight into relativistic correlation effects. The calculations show that the Breit contribution to the correlation energy increases rapidly with atomic number and reaches approximately 4% of the total correlation energy for Xe. The method also shows that second-order correlation energies are only weakly dependent on the choice of multiconfigurational reference orbitals and that frozen-core and frozen-virtual approximations substantially reduce computational cost with minimal loss of accuracy.
papers.zh: 小张量积分布式活性空间框架内的相对论狄拉克-库仑-布雷特四分量多重态微扰理论

papers.title: SPINKS (Spin Inversion Kinetics Suite): A Fully Automated Python–ORCA Framework for End-to-End Computation of Spin-Crossing Probabilities, Microcanonical, and Canonical Reaction Rate Constants
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We present SPINKS (Spin Inversion Kinetics Suite), a freely available, fully automated Python–ORCA computational framework for an end-to-end evaluation of spin-forbidden reaction kinetics directly from an initial molecular geometry. SPINKS automatically generates, executes, monitors, and processes the ORCA electronic-structure calculations required to determine the minimum-energy crossing point (MECP) between two potential-energy surfaces. It then extracts the spin–orbit coupling (SOC), energy gradients, and Hessians required to construct the reaction coordinate and subsequently evaluates the reduced mass, crossing velocity, and vibrational and rovibrational densities of states. These quantities are used to calculate Landau–Zener and weak coupling spin-crossing probabilities and the corresponding microcanonical and canonical reaction rate constants within the framework of nonadiabatic statistical theory. The workflow automatically generates graphical visualizations and comprehensive text-based outputs while permitting user customization of ORCA input files throughout the calculation. SPINKS shows excellent agreement during validation tests against the independently developed Nonadiabatic Statistical Theory (NAST) package. The NAST program requires manual preparation and transfer of electronic-structure quantities, whereas SPINKS integrates ORCA-based electronic-structure calculations with nonadiabatic dynamics and kinetic calculations within a single end-to-end automated workflow. SPINKS is freely distributed and operates within an accessible software ecosystem based on the free and open-source Python language and the ORCA quantum-chemistry package, which is freely available for academic use. The SPINKS framework provides a practical, reproducible, and extensible platform for routine investigation of spin-forbidden chemical reactions.
papers.zh: SPINKS（自旋反转动力学套件）：用于端到端计算自旋交叉概率、微正则和正则反应速率常数的全自动Python–ORCA框架

papers.title: Surface Evaporation Protocol for Solution-Processed Bulk-Heterojunction Films via Coarse-Grained Simulations
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We present a coarse-grained molecular dynamics protocol for simulating solvent evaporation applied to P3HT:PCBM bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) films. Prior reported protocols lacked an explicit air–film interface or resorted to monatomic solvents with heavily coarse-grained solute models to work. Our approach maintains an explicit air–film interface, handles polyatomic solvents, and is better suited for complex molecular models. The resulting films reproduce experimentally reported vertical segregation (a P3HT-enriched skin over a PCBM-enriched subsurface) and an in-plane preferential orientation of P3HT backbones and π-stacking that originates at the interface and propagates downward with the drying front. A Marcus-type charge extraction model applied to the dried films revealed faster in-plane hole transport in the P3HT domains than through the film thickness, while electron transport in PCBM domains suggested the opposite trend. The results suggest an active upper surface with a large capacity for generating free charges emerges during the film’s formation that might benefit OPVs with an inverted architecture. Both the evaporation protocol and the charge transport model are formulated in general terms with the purpose of enabling the transfer of the algorithms to other systems.
papers.zh: 通过粗粒度模拟实现溶液法制备的本体异质结薄膜的表面蒸发协议

papers.title: Transferable Machine Learning of Electronic Hamiltonians with Superposition-of-Atomic-Potentials Features
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Machine learning of electronic Hamiltonians offers a unified route to electronic wave functions and physical observables. We introduce a Hamiltonian learning framework built on electronic features derived from the superposition-of-atomic-potentials (SAP) approximation, an efficient self-consistent-field initial guess that captures essential electron–electron screening. SAP quantities define a symmetry-adapted intrinsic atomic orbital learning basis and provide physics-informed inputs to an orbital-based graph neural network that predicts converged Kohn–Sham Fock matrices. To extend the approach to larger basis sets, we further develop a downfolding scheme that predicts large-basis electronic structure from minimal-basis features. On the QM9 data set, the model accurately reproduces frontier and core orbital energies, dipole moments, and the full density of states. For organic charge-transport materials, it yields accurate intermolecular transfer integrals for benzene, tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), and tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) dimers. The model also generalizes to unseen substituted-benzene heterodimers, with a mean absolute error of 4.8 meV. These results establish SAP-based Hamiltonian learning as a transferable and scalable tool for high-throughput electronic-structure prediction.
papers.zh: 具有原子势叠加特征的电子哈密顿量可迁移机器学习

papers.title: Reduction of Finite-Size Effects for Second-Order Møller–Plesset Perturbation Theory with Singularity Subtraction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) for periodic systems suffers from finite-size errors (FSEs) that have inverse volume scaling due to the Coulomb kernel singularity in reciprocal space. This error scaling limits the routine applicability of MP2 and other methods that rely on it to real materials, requiring prohibitively dense k-point meshes for convergence toward the thermodynamic limit (TDL). We introduce MP2 singularity subtraction (MP2SS), a systematic approach that applies the singularity subtraction strategy to reduce MP2 FSEs. The method employs auxiliary functions and fitting procedures that consider both the singularities present at the origin in reciprocal space and also the discontinuities in the MP2 structure factor that arise from finite k-point sampling. We present three possible MP2SS configurations (Gaussian, exponential, and tuned) which use different combinations of decay functions and demonstrate their performance for gapped systems. Across a range of extended solids and molecular crystals at large basis sets, MP2SS reduces the prefactor in MP2 FSEs and subsequently the computational resources required to converge to the TDL. MP2SS with the Gaussian auxiliary function provides the most robust corrections. Our results establish singularity subtraction as a powerful and flexible approach for mitigating finite-size errors in periodic correlation methods and provide a foundation for extending the technique to higher-order perturbation theories and other post-Hartree–Fock (HF) methods.
papers.zh: 使用奇点消去法减少二阶Møller–Plesset微扰理论的有限尺寸效应

papers.title: A Cheminformatics Analysis of Substituents in Bioactive Molecules and Their Bioisosteric Replacement Network
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Substituents, decorating the central molecule core, play a key role in medicinal chemistry, where they are modified during lead optimization to improve biological activity, physicochemical properties, selectivity, and other drug properties. The selection of appropriate substituents, guided by the bioisosteric principle, is one of the most effective strategies for optimizing molecular properties while preserving affinity for the biological target. Despite the widespread application of bioisosteric replacement in drug discovery, systematic analyses of bioisosteric relationships among substituents derived from large collections of bioactive molecules remain limited. In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of substituents occurring in bioactive molecules and investigate their bioisosteric relationships using data extracted from medicinal chemistry literature. Bioisosteric pairs are identified from substitution patterns observed in related compounds with activity on the same target, enabling the construction of a network of frequently interchangeable substituents. Because the analysis is based on the observed co-occurrence of substituents within the same molecular environments rather than on structural similarity or physicochemical descriptors, it captures experimentally validated substitution patterns and uncovers not only well-established bioisosteric pairs but also less well-known relationships. The resulting bioisosteric substituent network is made available through a free web application at https://ertlmolecular.com/tools.html, providing a practical resource for medicinal chemists engaged in lead optimization, analog design, and library development.
papers.zh: 生物活性分子中取代基及其生物等排替代网络（BRN）的化学信息学分析

papers.title: Evaluating MSA-Derived Evolutionary Information in Enzyme Recommendation for Biocatalytic Reactions
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Reaction-conditioned enzyme recommendation ranks candidate enzymes for a query chemical transformation, but the contribution of explicit evolutionary context to this task remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we present an exploratory evaluation of multiple sequence alignment (MSA)-derived evolutionary features, integrating full-sequence and pocket-level MSA Transformer representations into EnzymeCage and a benchmark-adapted Horizyn implementation through concatenation or gated fusion. On the fixed Enzyme-405 candidate pools, the evaluated EnzymeCage Pocket-MSA model achieved a Top-1 success rate of 20.3% versus 14.6% for the baseline, while Full + Pocket MSA achieved a Top-10 success rate of 61.4% versus 55.6%; changes on Orphan-335 and in the adapted Horizyn implementation varied across configurations. Although a focused three-seed EnzymeCage baseline–Pocket comparison did not establish a consistent improvement across training runs and ranking cutoffs, analyses of MSA diversity, training-reference sequence similarity, and alignment-context removal characterize the observed effects and guide further evaluation of MSA-augmented enzyme recommendation.

papers.title: Thermodynamically Guided CRISPR Spacer Optimization: Strategy-Dependent Off-Target Trade-Offs
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Most CRISPR-Cas9 design tools select guide RNAs (gRNAs) by ranking predefined candidates rather than actively optimizing them. Here we instead formulate SpCas9 spacer refinement as a constrained search problem, in which a limited number of nucleotide substitutions may be introduced outside the PAM-proximal seed region. The search is driven by a thermodynamically grounded objective that combines CRISPRspec-based specificity with penalties for suboptimal GC content and long homopolymer runs. Within this single setting we compare five search strategies: three reinforcement-learning (RL) policies, which are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN), and Rainbow Deep Q-Network (Rainbow DQN), together with a nonlearning score-guided search and a prompt-guided large language model (LLM). All five share the same objective, mutable positions, substitution budget, and evaluation protocol, so that only the search strategy differs. On 100 held-out IGF2R guides from a gene and chromosome excluded from training, every strategy significantly reduced the predicted off-target burden (38.6–78.3%) and improved independent specificity metrics without degrading on-target scores. The strategies nevertheless differed sharply in per-guide safety: the LLM achieved the largest aggregate reduction but introduced new off-target sites into 38% of guides that were initially free of them, whereas PPO, an on-policy RL algorithm, retained a strong gain with the lowest regression rate of 15%. These results show that the thermodynamic objective supplies a robust common optimization signal, while the choice of search strategy governs the trade-off between aggregate improvement and regression of already-favorable guides.

papers.title: Leveraging Contrastive Learning for Conditional and Robust TCR Sequence Generation
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: T cell receptor (TCR) initiates T cell activation programs that are central to antiviral and antitumor immunity, and TCR-engineered T cell is a promising therapeutic approach in treating solid tumors. However, the design of TCR is time-consuming and labor-intensive, and computational TCR sequence generation remains comparatively underdeveloped with fewer dedicated models. We propose an encoder-decoder generation framework (i.e., Pep2Tcr) warm-started with pretrained peptide and TCR language models to conditionally generate TCR CDR3β sequences targeting a specific peptide. It also incorporates contrastive learning over batches to pull each TCR toward the peptide it pairs with. Through a series of progressive evaluations, Pep2Tcr outperforms other state-of-the-art methods under generation distribution, hit (independent testing sets), authenticity (third-party prediction), and generation probability (OLGA). Grafting and docking experiments of some predicted positive TCR sequences to the HLA-A*02:01-AAGIGILTV (melanoma antigen) complex showed plausible scores and potential interaction patterns for downstream experimental validation.
papers.zh: 利用对比学习进行有条件且稳健的TCR序列生成

papers.title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.
papers.zh: SynthStrategy：从有机化学中的LLMs中提取和形式化潜在的战略洞察

papers.title: Half‐Way Bayesian Calibration for Assessing Uncertainties in Quantum Chemistry Guided Catalyst Optimization
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: Developments in computational chemistry have made quantum chemical modeling an essential tool for catalyst design. However, so far theoretical predictions usually lack error bars, making them almost useless in guiding high‐stakes decisions. Commonly used accuracy metrics such as mean absolute error are ill‐defined when selectivity depends on relative energies of dozens of closely related transition states, as often happens in catalysis. The main missing ingredient is a tool for estimating errors of a computational protocol where many computed values combine into a single prediction. Here we show how Bayesian statistics can be applied to a model case of catalyst optimization, providing a framework for assessing reliability of a computational protocol as well as for telling reliable predictions from unreliable ones even for very similar compounds. We find that a modest B97‐D/TZV(2d,2p)/PCM level of theory employing a semi‐local GGA‐level density functional provides a standard deviation of only ~0.26 kcal/mol in relative energies of enantiomeric transition states for the model reaction. Thus, we provide a practical tool for assessing uncertainties in computational predictions and integrating them into catalyst optimization pipelines, bridging the gap between quantum chemistry and experimental catalysis design.
papers.zh: 用于评估量子化学引导的催化剂优化中不确定性的半贝叶斯校准

papers.title: Does the Total Energy Difference Method for Modelling Core Level Photoemission Fail for Bigger Molecules?
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: The ‐self‐consistent‐field (SCF) method permits calculations of core electron binding energies in materials and molecules at a modest computational cost. However, it has been reported that whilst this method works well for small molecules, its accuracy drops off dramatically when larger systems are considered. Particularly large errors have been reported for the anthrone molecule, which consists of 25 atoms. In this work, the gas‐phase photoelectron spectrum of anthrone is revisited both computationally and experimentally. The measured C 1s binding energies in anthrone differ markedly from previously published values, and the new experimental results are in good agreement with SCF calculations. In addition, the performance of the SCF method is evaluated for a dataset of 44 core electron binding energies from medium‐sized molecules containing between 10 and 40 atoms. Both SCAN and B3LYP yield a mean absolute error of 0.19 eV for this dataset. This level of accuracy is comparable to the results of previous computational benchmarks. Overall, these results and general theoretical considerations indicate that the SCF method is suitable for modelling localized excitations in both small and large molecules, and applications to other extended systems are also promising.
papers.zh: 用于建模核心能级光电子发射的总能量差方法是否不适用于较大的分子？

papers.title: Interactions and dynamics of metastable triplet-state helium dimer with Ne and Ar
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The helium dimer in its metastable triplet electronic state, He2(aΣu+3), is a promising candidate for direct laser cooling and precision measurements. Interactions and collisions involving He2(aΣu+3) remain unexplored in ultracold and cold energy domains. Here, we present the first theoretical investigation of intermolecular interactions and collision dynamics of He2(aΣu+3) + Ne van der Waals complex. For the lowest electronic state, X3A′, we employ a spin-restricted coupled cluster method with single, double, and noniterative triple excitations. We construct a three-dimensional vibrationally averaged potential energy surface. The resulting interaction potential exhibits an extremely shallow well with a depth of 4.612 cm−1. Using this potential energy surface, we perform full close-coupling calculations, including fine-structure levels of He2(aΣu+3), to investigate collisional excitation and quenching induced by Ne. We analyze the low-energy scattering dynamics and model resonant features associated with quasi-bound states supported by the interaction potential. A propensity rule for fine-structure conserving transitions is established. We additionally consider He2(aΣu+3)+Ar collisions and compare their energy dependence and resonance structure with those of He2 + Ne. The He2 + Ar system exhibits a richer resonance structure, highlighting the sensitivity of low-energy scattering to interaction potential and reduced mass. Calculated PES and scattering properties provide a reliable benchmark for the description of the He2 + Ne van der Waals complex and may be useful for the interpretation of future experimental spectra and collision measurements.
papers.zh: 亚稳态三重态氦二聚体与Ne和Ar的相互作用和动力学

papers.title: Quantum-classical hierarchical equations of motion
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We develop a quantum–classical hierarchical equations of motion (QC-HEOM) approach for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems. The method combines the ensemble-averaged classical path reference of the quantum–classical path integral formalism with a hierarchy of auxiliary quantum influence functionals. By incorporating thermal fluctuations through an ensemble average over reference trajectories, the hierarchy is required to represent only the residual quantum memory associated with the imaginary part of the bath response function. Consequently, unlike conventional hierarchical equations of motion, QC-HEOM does not require Matsubara or Padé expansions of the thermal kernel and exhibits only weak temperature dependence of the hierarchy size. Furthermore, because thermal fluctuations are supplied through reference classical trajectories, the framework provides a natural route toward extensions beyond harmonic baths and enables the incorporation of anharmonic and molecular environments through externally generated trajectories. We derive the QC-HEOM formalism and demonstrate its exactness for a harmonic bath. Applications to an asymmetric spin–boson model and an eight-site model of the Fenna–Matthews–Olson complex illustrate the accuracy of QC-HEOM. It reproduces benchmark exact quantum dynamics results while requiring substantially fewer auxiliary objects, particularly at low temperatures. These results establish QC-HEOM as an efficient framework for treating residual quantum memory in quantum–classical descriptions of open-system dynamics. The separation of thermal fluctuations from residual quantum memory through the use of Wigner trajectories suggests an approximate route toward hierarchical treatments of complex anharmonic environments beyond harmonic bath simulations, which shall be developed in the future.
papers.zh: 量子-经典分层运动方程

papers.title: The ndπ 1Π and ndδ 1Δ Rydberg states of CO and their interactions with 1Π valence states
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Extensive vacuum-ultraviolet Fourier-transform photoabsorption spectra of isotopic CO, recorded at the SOLEIL synchrotron, have been reanalyzed. In particular, a number of weak bands in the 100 000–109 000-cm−1 region are shown to represent transitions to the previously undocumented 3, 4dδ1Δ(v = 0, 1) and 4, 5dπ1Π(v = 0, 1) levels of Rydberg states converging on the X2Σ+ state of the CO+ ion. The analysis of their local perturbations, together with the observation of further weak transitions, leads to the spectroscopic characterization of a significant number of previously unknown 1Π valence-state levels and determination of the associated Rydberg–valence level-interaction parameters. These results will inform the optimization of future coupled-channels Schrödinger-equation models of CO 1Π-manifold spectroscopy and predissociation.

papers.title: Field-dependent effective interactions near magnetic nanodomains in solution
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: External magnetic fields (eMFs) can bias paramagnetic moments in solution, but hydration-scale structure can obscure changes in an ion–nanoparticle (NP) potential of mean force (PMF). We examine three mechanisms for eMF-induced changes in the PMF of a paramagnetic monomer near a localized magnetic NP in diamagnetic water. In the dilute limit, classical density functional theory (cDFT) provides the solvent-structured nonmagnetic reference, while magnetic contributions are treated separately. Mechanism I treats the interfacial response site by site and projects its mean and covariance through the dipolar kernel. A multilayer Ising model exhibits enhanced susceptibility, but magnetostatic cancellation suppresses the mean response, and the projected covariance remains weak. Isotropic orientational averaging yields field-induced surface PMF magnitudes below 10−4kBT across sampled couplings. Building on earlier phenomenological models used to interpret observations, Mechanism II asks what collective response, sampled through a localized finite coupling profile, would be required to reach the thermal scale: at an applied laboratory field of B0 = 1 T, thermally significant near-contact coupling requires a moment-equivalent scale of order 104 μB and a strongly localized monomer-facing profile. The required moment increases as the profile broadens or extends deeper into the NP. Therefore, Mechanism II quantifies the localization and effective collective coupling required for thermal significance. Mechanism III allows field-induced interfacial changes to modify the nonmagnetic PMF. cDFT shows that water adsorption makes the ion–NP interaction more repulsive, whereas water depletion or stronger ion–NP attraction favors association. Thus, the site-resolved direct magnetic response is strongly subthermal, while indirect interfacial-state changes can produce much larger PMF shifts.

papers.title: Self-alignment unwraps the spiraling of a chiral active Brownian polymer
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Chiral active Brownian polymers in two dimensions spontaneously fold into long-lived spirals, which profoundly reshape their conformations and dynamics. Using Brownian dynamics simulations, we show that a minimal self-alignment mechanism, namely, an aligning torque that rotates the propulsion direction toward the instantaneous monomer velocity, robustly unwraps these spirals. The same mechanism drives torque-induced swelling in both chiral and achiral active chains. We quantify the structure via the radius of gyration and the end-to-end distance as functions of the alignment torque at a fixed activity and find systematic increases with torque. Distributions of the radius of gyration broaden markedly under alignment, revealing access to a wide ensemble of open conformations consistent with spiral unwrapping. Dynamical signatures corroborate this picture: the oscillatory end-to-end time correlation and the oscillations in the monomer mean-squared displacement, hallmarks of chiral rotation, are progressively suppressed as the alignment strengthens. These effects persist across intrinsic rotation frequencies, establishing self-alignment as a simple and generic control knob to release chiral polymers from spiral states and expand their conformational and dynamical repertoire.

papers.title: Development of reactive force field for Pd–Zn system and kinetic study of diffusion-driven alloy formation
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: PdZn alloys are catalysts for many reactions, and the 1:1 tetragonal PdZn intermetallic compound has been identified as the active phase for methanol steam reforming (MSR), a crucial process in hydrogen production. Yet, the mechanism and kinetics of the formation of PdZn alloys have not been addressed theoretically. In this work, reactive force field (ReaxFF) parameters for the Pd–Zn system were developed using density functional theory (DFT) training sets generated with the aid of structure prediction and DFT calculations, and the alloying process of Pd and Zn metals was investigated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. MD simulations of Pd@Zn and Zn@Pd core–shell models revealed a two-stage, diffusion-controlled alloying process with distinct diffusion coefficients and activation energies for Pd and Zn atoms, and a kinetic model was proposed for the fast alloying stage. It is found that with the advance of alloying, the alloying activation energy of the rapid alloying stage increases, and it is also proportional to the cube root of the total atom number of the system. Simulations of a Zn/Pd(111) slab model further reproduced the experimentally observed temperature dependence of the surface alloy structure: a multilayer PdZn alloy at lower temperatures and a bilayer alloy at higher temperatures. The results provide valuable insights into the fundamental mechanisms of PdZn alloy formation and offer a robust foundation for further research in catalytic applications.

papers.title: Electron-stimulated desorption of D atoms from gibbsite [Al(OD)3] and D2O ice: Energy and temperature dependence of translational energy distributions
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The electron-stimulated desorption of neutral D atoms from gibbsite [Al(OD)3] nanoplatelets and amorphous D2O ice has been investigated using 2 + 1 resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization time-of-flight mass spectroscopy in a high vacuum chamber at temperatures of 15 and 300 K. Electron irradiation at 540, 250, and 150 eV produces similar D atom translational energy distributions at ∼300 K, with a dominant intermediate-temperature component (T ∼ 1500–2100 K). Cooling to 15 K suppresses the D atom yield by ∼50% and removes the lowest-temperature (slowest) component. This decrease in yield is consistent with diminished hole mobility and restricted diffusion at cryogenic temperatures. Under identical conditions, D2O amorphous solid water ice films produce ∼20 times greater D atom signal than bare gibbsite, with significantly hotter translational distributions, reflecting the higher deuterium surface density and distinct bonding environments of bulk ice relative to the terminal hydroxyl groups on gibbsite. These results identify hole transport to terminal hydroxyl sites as the rate-limiting step for nonthermal D atom production and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding atomic hydrogen release from aluminum hydroxide phases relevant to radioactive waste storage at the Hanford Site.

papers.title: Carrier dynamics under synergistic interfacial charge and energy transfer in Au–CsPbBr3 nanocrystal heterostructures formed by chemical deposition
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Metal–perovskite nanocrystal heterostructures (NHs) offer a useful platform for regulating excited-state dynamics, but the interplay among carrier relaxation, interfacial transfer, and competing recombination pathways remains unclear. Here, Au–CsPbBr3 NHs were constructed by depositing Au nanoparticles (NPs) onto CsPbBr3 nanocrystals, and their carrier dynamics were investigated by transient absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy combined with global analysis. The deposition of Au NPs introduces an additional interfacial relaxation channel and facilitates both charge and energy transfer, leading to ∼50% photoluminescence quenching. Global analysis further shows that the band-edge state population time decreases from 0.84 to 0.60 ps, the band-edge radiative recombination lifetime increases from 218 to 488 ps, and the defect-state radiative decay lifetime decreases from 325 to 246 ps. These results reveal that Au NPs do not merely quench photoluminescence but reconstruct interfacial relaxation and recombination pathways, thereby accelerating carrier cooling, promoting interfacial charge separation, and modulating defect-state emission. Consequently, photogenerated carriers can be transferred to the interface before band-edge recombination and defect-mediated dissipation, increasing the fraction of carriers available for extraction or surface reactions. Photoresponse and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements further support enhanced charge separation and lower interfacial charge-transfer resistance in Au–CsPbBr3 NHs. This work establishes a carrier-dynamics framework for relaxation, transfer, and recombination in Au–CsPbBr3 NHs and provides a mechanistic basis for the rational design of perovskite/metal NHs.

papers.title: Optical response of coronene in the presence of a metallic substrate
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Theoretical research on graphene quantum dots (GQDs) driven by the near-field enhancement on metallic substrates has interest in the practical realm. Here, the GQD is modeled as coronene (a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon) with its edges saturated by hydrogen atoms. A combined density functional theory, QED, and statistical formalism has been used to determine the molecular dynamics quantities, such as energy levels and transition dipole moments, and a three-level model for the coronene molecule is obtained. Furthermore, we have characterized the effects of the substrate on the molecule through the enhancement factor (or equivalently, the spectral density function), which can be decomposed into a superposition of various contributions, such as surface waves (SWs) and the quasistatic near field, also known as lossy surface waves. Both of these contributions can be excited by molecular emission in the vicinity of the substrate. Using the three-level model and the substrate enhancement factor, we obtained the population dynamics of the excited levels of coronene placed in the vicinity of the substrate, as well as the modified photonic spectrum.

papers.title: Calculation of thermodynamic properties of neon with ab initio potentials using path integral and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Path integral Monte Carlo and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations using the Feynman–Hibbs corrections to account for nuclear quantum effects were employed to calculate ten different thermodynamic properties of the noble gas neon in the isobaric-isothermal ensemble. As path integral simulations could only be carried out for small systems due to the large required computational resources, while semiclassical simulations can be performed for much larger systems, an extrapolation scheme was developed to obtain results in the quantum-mechanical and thermodynamic limits, which utilizes the similar dependence of results for thermodynamic properties on the system size in both simulation techniques. This approach yields accurate results for macroscopic thermodynamic properties and additionally allows the assessment of the validity of the Feynman–Hibbs corrections in the studied region of the phase diagram. A total of 38 state points were simulated at eight isotherms between 27.5 and 100 K, covering the liquid and supercritical regions of the phase diagram at pressures up to 90 MPa. The interactions between the neon atoms were described by highly accurate state-of-the-art ab initio potentials for both pairwise and nonadditive three-body contributions. The predicted densities and speeds of sound at the isotherms 80 and 100 K agree with the most accurate experimental data from the literature within the mutual uncertainties. At lower temperatures, our results are likely more accurate than the available experimental data for the density and speed of sound.

papers.title: Transient Carrier Transport and Extraction in Passivated Perovskite Films
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The efficiency of perovskite solar cells keeps improving owing to the development of versatile passivation strategies for defects formed during the preparation of the films. Understanding the specific role of the passivation effect is a key step toward reaching the Shockley–Queisser limit. In this report, we focus on sun-like low excitation intensities to probe the carrier dynamics with passivation, as well as the charge transfer dynamics at the interface between the perovskite and the charge transport layer (CTL). The addition of the passivation layer reduces the density of both shallow and deep defects in the perovskite film, increases the carrier lifetime, enhances the diffusion coefficient and diffusion length, and accelerates carrier extraction at the interface. The imbalance of electron and hole extraction under passivation was also analyzed. These findings have direct implications for understanding the passivation effect and improving the efficiency of perovskite solar cells.

papers.title: Photoregulated Oxidase-Mimicking and Antibacterial Activity with Cascade Catalysis Probed by Copper Nanoclusters
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The development of light-responsive metal nanoclusters (MNCs) for showcasing photoregulated biomimicking catalysis and developing light-mediated potent antibacterial agents remains a central attraction of the present research. However, strategic modulation of the electronic structure in MNCs to impart light-triggered biocatalysis and antibacterial activity is associated with formidable challenges. In this study, the multidimensionally served enzymatic features in tyramine-protected CuNCs (Cu@Tyra NCs) have been comprehensively investigated, which display efficient peroxidase-like activity and a biocatalytic cascade upon coupling with a suitable natural enzyme. Upon visible light activation, photoexcited charge carriers in the Cu@Tyra NCs promote the generation of a hydroxyl radical (•OH) as a reactive oxygen species (ROS), which significantly enhances the catalytic efficiency. The photoinduced ROS also imparts strong antibacterial effects against Gram-negative bacteria (Escherichia coli) by inducing oxidative damage to cell membranes and intracellular components, exclusively in the presence of light.

papers.title: Mode-Resolved Phonon Damping and Anharmonicity in Mo2C: Insights from Temperature-Dependent Raman Spectroscopy
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The lattice dynamics of metallic molybdenum carbide (Mo2C) is investigated through mode-resolved temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy over the range of 80–296 K. The Raman-active modes at ∼143 and ∼223 cm–1 and the high-frequency mode at ∼658 cm–1 exhibit systematic frequency softening and line width broadening with an increase in temperature. The line width evolution is adequately described by a three-phonon anharmonic decay model, with normalized residuals below 5%, indicating that anharmonic phonon–phonon interactions provide the dominant contribution to the temperature-dependent line width within the investigated range. The temperature-independent residual line width is analyzed using an Allen-type framework to obtain effective upper-bound estimates of electron–phonon coupling λeff, which may include contributions from defect scattering and other temperature-independent broadening mechanisms. The extracted values decrease from 0.081 and 0.026 for the low- and intermediate-frequency modes, respectively, to 0.0019 for the high-frequency mode. This hierarchy reflects the mode dependence of the residual line width-derived effective parameters and is qualitatively consistent with the predominantly Mo-derived electronic states near the Fermi level and reported density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) calculations. The results establish anharmonic phonon interactions as the dominant temperature-dependent contribution to the line width, while the intrinsic electron–phonon contribution cannot be uniquely separated from other sources of residual broadening.

papers.title: Breaking Water at Graphene Defects
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Water dissociation at solid surfaces underpins processes ranging from corrosion and catalysis to electrochemistry and photovoltaics. Defects often serve as reactive sites for dissociation, yet how solvation influences water dissociation at such sites remains poorly understood. Here, we use state-of-the-art machine-learned interatomic potentials to explore water dissociation at defective graphene–water interfaces. We show that solvation qualitatively changes the reaction mechanism at a graphene single vacancy (SV), opening pathways that are absent for an isolated water molecule. Whereas the gas-phase process proceeds via a single concerted channel, the solvated SV splits water through two competing pathways: a basic route forming SV–H andOH(aq)−, and an acidic route forming SV–OH and H3O(aq)+. These lower-barrier pathways produce distinct chemisorbed intermediates that enhance graphene–water adsorption. Accordingly, even a simple carbon vacancy gives rise to unexpectedly rich interfacial chemistry, coupling surface chemistry to interfacial charge and wettability, with implications for carbon functionalization and nanofluidic transport.

papers.title: Unveiling the Phase Transformation Mechanism in BN from Large-Scale Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Boron nitride (BN) exhibits rich polymorphism, including cubic, hexagonal, rhombohedral, and wurtzite phases, whose dynamic transformations govern the stability and performance of BN-based materials in modern electronics, quantum photonics, and energy devices. Despite their technological importance, the atomistic mechanisms underlying its phase evolution remain poorly understood. Here, we use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a MACE-based machine learning interatomic potential. The potential is trained on high-fidelity density functional theory data and validated against ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to investigate phase transformation pathways in crystalline BN. We identify a layer-by-layer transformation mechanism that is initiated at heterogeneous BN interfaces, where local structural reconstruction propagates into neighboring crystalline regions. We further show that the transformation propensity depends on the interfacial structure and crystallographic orientation. These results provide atomistic insight into BN phase transformations under diverse thermodynamic conditions, while the associated MACE training workflow offers a generalizable framework for studying phase transformation mechanisms in other complex materials.

papers.title: Sampling Free Energy Landscapes of Ionic Colloidal Crystal Systems Using Machine-Learned Proxy Collective Variables
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Charged colloids coated with a polymer brush can be designed to preferentially self-assemble into different crystal structures by varying easy-to-tune experimental conditions. For a given set of conditions, we have observed in experiments and simulations a distribution of thermodynamically (meta)stable self-assembled crystal structures. Properly quantifying the free energy landscape of these colloidal systems is essential for rationally choosing conditions to preferentially target particular crystal structures. For some of the structures we have formed, standard crystalline order parameters are not able to differentiate between crystals or between crystals and amorphous aggregates. We show that local environment similarity descriptors are able to distinguish the relevant metastable states but are too expensive for use in biased MD simulations. Here, we adopt an approach from machine-learned interaction potentials showing that SE(3)-equivariant transformer networks can serve as an efficient-to-evaluate machine-learned proxy. As a result, we can compute the relative free energies of accessible colloidal structures as a function of different experimentally relevant physical knobs that can steer our system between two observed crystal types. As an example application, we then show how changing surface potentials of positive and negative colloids while maintaining the same attractive energy can shift which crystal structure is favored.
