papers.title: Charge Transfer from Ammonia Neutralizes Propylene Oxide Cations: Implications for the Astrochemistry of Chiral Molecules
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Propylene oxide is the first of only two chiral species observed to date in the interstellar medium but little is known about the chemistry that leads to a detectable abundance of this molecule in Sagittarius B2. We used a glow-discharge ion source and a room-temperature ion trap to study the neutralization reactions necessary to convert propylene oxide cation (PpO+)─the assumed precursor for propylene oxide in space─into the observed astrochemical. We found that the charge-transfer reaction between PpO+ and ammonia (NH3) proceeds with a pressure-independent rate coefficient of (1.39 ± 0.03) × 10–12 cm3 s–1 to neutralize PpO+ and form the radical cation NH3+. Although this measured rate coefficient is much slower than that predicted by capture theories, the high abundance of NH3 in Sagittarius B2 motivates the inclusion of this reaction in astrochemical models. We hypothesize that the low ionization energies of many chiral molecules important to origin-of-life theories means these species may exist as cations in the interstellar medium.

papers.title: Decoding Configurational Populations and Temperature of Flexible Chiral Molecules from Chiral Optical Spectra with Machine Learning
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Quantitative determination of configurational populations in flexible chiral molecules is challenging due to spectral overlap, conformational averaging, and random noise. Here, we present a multitask residual network that integrates quantum chemical calculations, spectral simulation, and deep learning to achieve configurational inversion from spectroscopic data. As a proof-of-concept study, the neural network uses DFT-computed ultraviolet–visible absorption and electronic circular dichroism spectra as input to simultaneously predict the populations of configurational isomers and the thermodynamic temperature of the system. Demonstrated on the flexible chiral drug molecule labetalol, the method achieves high accuracy: under 10% spectral noise, the root-mean-square error for configurational populations is about 8.2%, and the temperature error is below 3.4 °C. The successful inversion demonstrates that machine learning can effectively bridge spectroscopic observables and statistical thermodynamics, providing a rapid, data-driven paradigm for resolving structural distributions in complex flexible chiral systems.

papers.title: Thermal Activation under Electrochemical Conditions: CO and N2 Bond Dissociation on Co(B5)
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: In aqueous electrocatalytic environments, the protonation of stable *CO and *N2 to *COH/*CHO and *NNH is fundamentally challenged by the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). In this context, direct dissociation of these molecules offers an alternative pathway, forming reactive *C or *N fragments that can be reduced further if surface bonding is not too strong. However, the strong C≡O and N≡N bonds make dissociation challenging under ambient electrochemical conditions, and the extent to which solvent, local field, and electrolyte ions can promote bond dissociation remains unclear. In this work, we quantify these dissociation pathways at a Co(B5) step site using density functional theory, implicit-solvent calculations, and explicit-solvent calculations using enhanced sampling with machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). Implicit-solvent calculations reveal only weak sensitivity to dielectric constant, dipole moment, and solvent radius, with barrier variations typically ≤0.1 eV. In contrast, the local H-bonding network in explicit-solvent simulations lowers the dissociation barrier by ∼0.3 eV relative to vacuum by stabilizing the dissociating atoms. Across different solvents and aqueous solutes, the barrier correlates qualitatively with hydrogen-bond donor strength, pKa, and the local H-coordination number near the transition-state region. Interfacial cations (Li+ and Cs+) modify the work function but do not significantly change the dissociation barrier compared with pure water, suggesting that solvent-mediated interactions dominate under the studied conditions.

papers.title: Experimental and Theoretical Charge Density Study of Isonicotinamide Polymorphs
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Isonicotinamide is widely studied for its strong and directional hydrogen bonds, which play a critical role in crystal engineering and polymorphism. To address the absence of a quantitative charge density comparison for the two most studied isonicotinamide polymorphs (denoted 1a and 1b), this study maps the electron density distribution and topological properties of 1a and 1b, which differ in intermolecular connectivity, linking their respective H-bonding networks, intermolecular interaction strengths and lattice energetics within a single experimental and theoretical framework. High-resolution X-ray diffraction data were analyzed using the Hansen–Coppens multipole model. Topological parameters at bond critical points were evaluated to quantify hydrogen bonding, weak interactions, and electron density redistribution across the molecule. Both polymorphs exhibit well-defined hydrogen bonding networks dominated by N–H···N interactions, with bond strengths ranging from 6.48 to 35.5 kJ mol–1. Topological analysis revealed high electron densities and negative Laplacian values for covalent bonds, whereas the hydrogen-bond critical points exhibited positive Laplacian values consistent with closed-shell interactions. Notably, 1a shows stronger lattice stabilization (−114 kJ mol–1) compared to 1b (−82 kJ mol–1), indicating more efficient packing. By mapping the electron density topology and energy framework partitioning that distinguish the more stable P21/c form 1a from its less efficiently packed polymorph 1b (also P21/c), at the atomic level, this study provides a quantitative reference framework that can be used to predict and rationalize stability and solubility differences among the growing family of isonicotinamide-based pharmaceutical cocrystals.

papers.title: Solid Solution Engineering via Zr Doping in the Pd/ZrInO x Catalyst Switches Reaction Pathways for Enhanced Methanol Production from CO2
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The Pd/In2O3 catalyst is promising for CO2-to-methanol conversion, yet it is limited by poor stability and sluggish conversion of formate intermediates. Replacing the In2O3 support in Pd/In2O3 with an In2O3-based solid solution, such as ZrInOx, is an effective strategy to balance activity and stability. However, how the Zr species regulates the Pd/In2O3 catalyst, especially its effect on the reaction pathway, remains unclear. Herein, by introducing atomically dispersed Zr on the Pd/In2O3 catalyst, we demonstrate an electronic disparity strategy to tune the reaction pathway for efficient CO2-to-methanol production. Characterizations confirm that Zr promotes oxygen vacancy formation and enhances the dispersion of Pd nanoparticles. These enhance the electronic metal–support interaction between Pd and the support to accelerate the electron transfer from Pd to the support, thereby making the In sites more electron-rich and Pd more electron-deficient, as well as enhancing CO2 adsorption and H2 dissociation. Theoretical studies show that during the reaction, the In sites at the oxygen vacancy and Pd species work in synergy to induce cleavage of the C═O bond in CO2 and switch the formate pathway to the RWGS+CO* hydrogenation pathway. Consequently, the Pd/ZrInOx catalyst achieved an 18% CO2 conversion with 710 gMeOH kgcat–1 h–1 methanol space-time yield at 300 °C and 5 MPa. This work highlights the influence of the solid solution structure on the CO2 hydrogenation process.

papers.title: Elucidation of Mg-Ion Diffusion Factors in Mg–O-Based Materials Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials and Causal Analysis
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Mg-ion batteries are promising next-generation energy-storage systems because Mg metal offers high volumetric capacity, abundant resources, and intrinsic safety. However, Mg2+ usually diffuses slowly in solids because of its strong interaction with surrounding anion frameworks and cation environments. Here, Mg–O-based candidate materials extracted from The Materials Project were investigated to clarify the compositional and structural factors governing Mg-ion diffusion. Representative materials were selected by clustering composition descriptors and structural descriptors derived from radial distribution functions (RDFs) and angular distribution functions (ADFs). High-throughput molecular dynamics simulations using an M3GNet-based machine-learning interatomic potential were then performed to construct a Mg-ion diffusion-coefficient data set. LightGBM regression, SHAP-based feature importance analysis, and nonlinear NOTEARS causal discovery were integrated to analyze the hierarchical relationships among descriptors and log D. The inferred causal structure indicates that Mg-ion diffusion is not governed by a single compositional factor. Instead, composition affects the short- and medium-range order of the oxygen framework, which regulates the local Mg environment and migration-pathway connectivity. Excessively close-packed and ordered oxygen frameworks restrict Mg-ion migration, whereas moderately disordered oxygen frameworks can promote continuous migration-accessible sites around Mg ions. These results suggest that Mg-ion-conducting oxides should be designed by controlling the oxygen framework and Mg local environment through host-cation selection, particularly using lightweight host materials containing d-block cations with sizes similar to that of Mg.

papers.title: Ion Association and Hydration in Aqueous FeSO4 and MnSO4 Solutions
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Ion association in aqueous electrolyte solutions depends critically on the interplay between ion hydration and electrostatic attraction such that different ion-pair species have been detected in aqueous 2:2 electrolytes with sulfate as the prototypical divalent anion. Dielectric relaxation (DR) spectroscopy has the potential to resolve and quantify the various ion-pair species, yet literature studies are too scarce to systematically address the effect of the nature of the cation on ion association. Here, we report a DR study of aqueous solutions of MnSO4 and FeSO4 at 25 °C, at frequencies 0.2 ≤ ν/GHz ≤ 115 and concentrations up to near-saturation (∼2.7 and ∼0.8 mol·L–1 respectively). The observed spectra were consistent with the presence of five Debye modes: two at higher frequencies (ν > ca. 10 GHz) that correspond to bulk-water processes, and three solute-related modes at lower frequencies. The slowest mode, centered at ν ≈ 0.3 GHz, was consistent with overlapping contributions from the rotation of double-solvent-separated ion pairs (2SIPs) and hydrated triple ions (M2SO42+, T+) as has been found for some other divalent metal sulfate solutions. The other lower frequency modes, centered at ν ≈ 1.5 GHz and ∼8 GHz, were assigned (respectively) to the rotation of solvent-shared (SIPs) and contact (CIPs) ion pairs, with the latter mode possibly also incorporating an unresolved contribution from “slow” bulk-water molecules. Effective total cation solvation numbers, Zt(M2+, aq), derived from the water-related modes, indicated that both Mn2+ and Fe2+ immobilize approximately 11 water molecules on the DR time scale, independent of solute concentration. Combination of the present results with literature data revealed a strong correlation between the types of ion aggregates detected by DR spectroscopy and the hydration enthalpy of the divalent metal cations (excepting Zn2+). Concentrations of the various species derived from the solute-related modes were used to calculate formation constants for each species that were, where comparisons were possible, in reasonable agreement with literature values obtained by other techniques.

papers.title: Accurate Thermodynamics of Phenol Aggregates across Concentration and Temperature
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Phenol aggregate populations in carbon tetrachloride are governed by an enthalpy–entropy balance that varies with concentration and temperature. Changes in these thermodynamic conditions redistribute the population among aggregates, which is reflected in the infrared O–H stretching band, whose position and shape provide a sensitive test for population models. Here, monomer-to-tetramer populations are determined over a concentration–temperature grid using two strategies that share the same graph-based aggregate classification: a cluster-based approach relying on partition functions from conformational-search structures, and a trajectory-derived approach extracting populations from molecular dynamics simulations. The latter reproduces the experimental attenuation and displacement of the aggregate-associated bands, especially in concentrated solutions, whereas the cluster-based model predicts an overly sharp thermal depletion of larger aggregates. Temperature-dependent data further enable van’t Hoff estimates of aggregation enthalpies and entropies. Comparison with the experiment shows that the trajectory-derived strategy captures aggregation thermodynamics across the aggregate series, supporting a better sampling of the configurational space.

papers.title: In Situ IRRAS Study of Myoglobin Binding to Metal-Chelating Nitrilotriacetate-Functionalized Binary Monolayers at the Air–Water Interface
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Molecular-level understanding of protein binding to metal-chelating nitrilotriacetate (NTA)-functionalized biological surfaces remains poorly supported by direct spectroscopic evidence. Herein, in situ infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRRAS) was employed to investigate the binding of native myoglobin (Mb, with five surface-exposed histidine residues in its native state) to binary monolayers consisting of NTA-functionalized amide-linked dioleoyl lipid (DOGS-NTA) and 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC) at the air–water interface in the presence of Cu2+ or Ni2+. No Mb binding to the DOGS-NTA monolayer occurred without divalent metal ions, nor was Mb binding observed for the pure DOPC monolayer even with Cu2+ or Ni2+. Robust Mb binding to the binary monolayers was achieved via NTA–metal–histidine ternary coordination. The amide I band intensities of specifically bound Mb at a surface pressure of 30 mN/m were approximately 4-fold higher in the Cu2+ case than those in the Ni2+ case, indicating markedly enhanced protein accumulation at the interface. The higher histidine affinity, faster ligand exchange, and Jahn–Teller geometric flexibility of Cu2+ accounted for the enhanced protein binding observed at the Cu2+-chelating interface. This molecular-level understanding of metal-ion-dependent protein binding mechanisms offers guidelines for the rational design of affinity biosensors, controlled-release delivery systems, and biomimetic interfaces.
papers.zh: 肌红蛋白在气–水界面与金属螯合三乙酸代三胺官能化二元单分子层结合的原位IRRAS研究

papers.title: Theoretical Insights into Cosolvent Effects in PET Glycolysis: A Multiscale Transport-Activation Mechanism
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Despite extensive advances in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization, the molecular-level mechanisms by which solvents and cosolvents regulate PET swelling, transport, and bond cleavage remain insufficiently understood. Herein, an integrated molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) calculation was employed to systematically elucidate the roles of eight representative cosolvents─tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (M-THF), 1,3-dioxolane (DOL), δ-valerolactone (DVL), cyclopentanone (CP), ethylene glycol (EG), anisole (AS), and benzyl alcohol (BnOH)─in PET solvation and degradation-related environments. Analyses of free-volume evolution, diffusion behavior, and electronic structure-derived descriptors capturing local polarity and orbital localization reveal pronounced solvent-dependent differences in chain relaxation, molecular mobility, and electronic activation pathways. Ether- and carbonyl-containing cosolvents primarily promote PET swelling and molecular transport by modulating local polarity and chain relaxation, whereas the protic cosolvent benzyl alcohol forms a dynamically reconfigurable, ethylene glycol-coupled hydrogen-bond network that enhances molecular mobility and stabilizes reactive oxyanion/transition-state structures. These distinct interaction modes give rise to computed differences in activation barriers, which elucidate the depolymerization mechanisms of different cosolvents. This study establishes a unified transport–activation mechanistic understanding and provides theory-guided principles for the rational design of efficient cosolvent systems for PET recycling.
papers.zh: 对PET糖酵解中助溶剂效应的理论见解：多尺度转运-活化机制

papers.title: Gas-Phase Pseudorotaxane Formation of Protonated Dibenzylamine with 21-Crown-7 and Vibrational Energy Redistribution Revealed by Cold Ion Spectroscopy
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Pseudorotaxane formation is governed by a delicate balance among host–guest interactions, steric constraints, and solvent effects. Here, we investigate the complex of protonated dibenzylamine (dBAMH+) with 21-crown-7 (21C7), hereafter denoted as dBAMH+(21C7) in this study, using cryogenic UVPD spectroscopy, IR–UV DR spectroscopy, and quantum chemical calculations in the gas phase. The results of dBAMH+(21C7) were compared with those of the complexes with 15-crown-5 (15C5), 18-crown-6 (18C6), and 24-crown-8 (24C8). Although no stable dBAMH+(21C7) complex is detected by NMR spectroscopy in methanol, the complex is readily generated and isolated in the gas phase. The UVPD spectrum of dBAMH+(21C7) exhibits a congested vibronic structure resembling that of the threaded dBAMH+(24C8) pseudorotaxane rather than the simple spectrum of the nonthreaded dBAMH+(18C6) complex. Quantum chemical calculations show that a threaded form is more stable by more than 40 kJ mol–1 than a nonthreaded one for dBAMH+(21C7) in the gas phase. These results suggest that the dBAMH+(21C7) complex can adopt a threaded pseudorotaxane form. The unusually low photodissociation efficiency of dBAMH+(21C7) is also consistent with the smaller calculated oscillator strength and a substantial barrier along the dethreading pathway, providing further support for the formation of a pseudorotaxane. The IR–UV DR spectra reveal a striking difference in the signal polarity: the 15C5 and 18C6 complexes, assigned as nonthreaded, exhibit depletion signals, whereas the 21C7 and 24C8 complexes, assigned as threaded, show gain signals despite similar vibrational band positions. Vibrational density-of-states calculations indicate that this reversal cannot be explained by the number of accepting states. These findings suggest that molecular threading can influence the vibrational response and photodissociation dynamics of isolated host–guest complexes. Differences in vibrational coupling, rather than vibrational state density alone, may contribute to the distinct relaxation behavior. In the threaded form, dissociation requires passage through the transition state (TS) associated with the unthreading process. The complexes that absorb both IR and UV photons possess additional internal energy corresponding to the absorbed IR photon compared with those excited by UV irradiation alone. This additional vibrational energy may facilitate passage through the TS, thereby significantly enhancing the UVPD efficiency of the threaded form upon IR excitation. These mechanisms provide plausible explanations for the reversal of the IR–UV DR signal polarity between the nonthreaded and threaded complexes.
papers.zh: 通过低温离子光谱揭示质子化二苯甲胺与21-冠-7的气相假轮烷形成和振动能再分配

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Oxidation of Aluminum Nanoparticles in H2O–Air Mixtures: A Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are promising high-energy-density fuels for amphibious propulsion systems. However, differences in mass transfer and chemical properties between H2O and O2 have led to uncertainty regarding the oxidation kinetics of ANPs, thereby limiting their performance regulation in water–air transmedia environments. In this work, the nonequilibrium oxidation and combustion of ANPs in mixed H2O–air atmospheres with various H2O/air ratios (i.e., 1:9, 1:4, 1:2, 1:1, 2:1, 4:1, and 9:1, namely, M1:9, M1:4, M1:2, M1:1, M2:1, M4:1, and M9:1) and temperatures (1500–3000 K) are investigated by molecular dynamics simulations. The results reveal that H2O acted as a critical promoter of ANP oxidation: it adsorbed and dissociated on Lewis acid sites of the Al surface, supplying OH– and O2– reactive oxygen species, which dramatically accelerated Al–O bond formation and enhanced energy release. The synergistic effect of high temperature and high-humidity environment accelerated H2O consumption and drove vigorous Al–water reactions, releasing substantial amounts of H2. The formation of hollow nanostructures was highly dependent on the H2O/air ratio: at M4:1, the pressure generated by internal H2 ruptured the oxide shell, destabilizing the hollow structure; at M1:1, a stable hollow shell emerged due to outward diffusion of Al3+ dominating over inward O2– diffusion; while at M1:4, a dense Al2O3 layer rapidly formed, which inhibited hollowing. Crucially, the oxidation of ANPs in humid environments proceeds via proton-coupled pathways involving hydroxyl intermediates, whereas it follows direct electron transfer in air. This investigation provides atomic-level insights into the reactive dynamics of ANPs in complex oxidizing environments, offering critical guidance for the design of high-performance and environment-adaptive metallic fuels.
papers.zh: 铝纳米颗粒在H2O–空气混合物中的非平衡氧化：一项分子动力学研究

papers.title: Vibrations Drive Ultrafast Intersystem Crossing of a Photoexcited Cr(III) Complex
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The Cr(III) coordination complex serves as an archetypical 3d transition metal system for probing ultrafast excited-state dynamics with spin conversion due to its intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) pathway, 4T2g → 2Eg, upon photoexcitation. Here, we conduct ab initio molecular dynamics simulations in the 4T2g state of a model Cr(III) coordination complex, followed by analyses of multireference electronic structure properties. Across 50 trajectories, the compound retains a persistent Jahn–Teller distortion in the excited state, while exhibiting prominent symmetric metal–ligand bond stretching vibrations with frequencies of 219 and 465 cm–1. State-averaged complete active space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations obtain two corresponding normal modes at 225 and 487 cm–1 with symmetric stretching character. The lower-frequency twisting/scissoring mode strongly modulates the 4T2g/2Eg energy gap, periodically zeroing the energy gap, whereas spin–orbit coupling is essentially invariant to vibrational motion (≈60–80 cm–1). A Landau–Zener analysis shows that every trajectory reaches its first 4T2g/2Eg crossing within 100 fs, with a transition probability at that crossing of 74% on average, in agreement with the sub-100 fs ISC inferred from experiment. Furthermore, calculations of single-point excited-state absorption from 2Eg to a higher ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) state indicate that the coherences previously observed in transient absorption spectra arise from nuclear motion on the 2Eg surface. These results provide insights into the correlation between vibrational motion and electronic transitions, which can facilitate rational molecular design of transition metal complexes with desired excited-state properties by leveraging ligand versatility.
papers.zh: 振动驱动光激发Cr(III)络合物的超快系间窜越

papers.title: Approaching Coupled Cluster Accuracy with Positive Semidefinite Vertex Corrected Self-Energies
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Hedin’s formalism of functional derivatives is a successful method for systematically constructing correlated electronic theories, largely due to the success of its lowest-order self-energy expansion, the GW approximation. Beyond GW, diagrammatic resummation schemes attempt to mix correlations simultaneously across all particle-particle and particle-hole channels. Because such a comprehensive treatment is computationally prohibitive for realistic molecular systems, a highly effective alternative is to fully account for electronic correlations in one specific channel, typically the particle-hole channel. This idea was recently implemented for molecular systems, yielding a self-energy expressed in terms of excited-state energies and transition amplitudes from the solution of the Bethe–Salpeter equation, rather than the random-phase approximation used in GW. While this approach is predictive and numerically efficient, it violates the fundamental positive-definiteness constraint on the electron spectral function in certain energy ranges. In this study, we resolve this physical flaw by deriving a positive-semidefinite (PSD) extension of the theory using a rigorous framework based on the nonequilibrium Green’s function formalism. The PSD constraint introduces new scattering channels and triplet intermediate states and restores the correct physical behavior. We demonstrate that it consistently improves quasiparticle energies across standard molecular benchmarks, with an accuracy comparable to coupled-cluster reference calculations.
papers.zh: 使用正半定顶点校正自能逼近耦合簇精度

papers.title: Equivariant Interatomic Potentials without Tensor Products
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials have emerged as powerful tools for atomistic simulations, promising near first-principles accuracy across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the cost of quantum-mechanical calculations. However, the most accurate equivariant architectures rely on Clebsch–Gordan tensor products whose computational cost scales steeply with angular resolution, creating a trade-off between model expressiveness and inference speed that ultimately limits practical applications. Here we introduce Geodite, an equivariant message-passing architecture that replaces tensor products while incorporating physical priors to ensure smooth, well-behaved potential energy surfaces. Trained on the Materials Project trajectories dataset of inorganic crystals, Geodite-MP achieves accuracy competitive with leading methods on benchmarks for materials stability prediction, thermal conductivity, phonon-derived properties, and nanosecond-scale molecular dynamics, while running 3–5× faster than models performing similarly. By combining predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and physicality, Geodite enables faster large-scale atomistic simulations and high-throughput screening that would otherwise be computationally prohibitive.
papers.zh: 不使用张量积的等变原子间势

papers.title: Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Synthesis Route Evaluation
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Selecting multistep synthetic routes remains a major bottleneck in computer-aided synthesis planning: high-quality negative data are scarce, and individual reported routes provide incomplete benchmarks for route quality. We introduce an expert-augmented framework that combines large-scale reference-based learning with expert-defined chemical feasibility assessment. Large-scale pretraining on literature-derived reference routes achieves 60.3% top 1 reference-route recovery on held-out targets. In expert assessment, the model’s top-ranked route is feasible in 88.4% of assessed cases, either matching a reference route or representing an alternative endorsed by experts. Among alternative top-ranked proposals, 75.4% are judged feasible, demonstrating that divergence from a literature reference does not necessarily indicate chemical infeasibility. The pretrained model captures a measurable expert-feasibility signal (Spearman |ρ| = 0.46), which increases to 0.78 ± 0.05 after expert fine-tuning. On an independent multi-expert dataset, agreement with the expert majority increases from 48.0% to 64.0% after fine-tuning, comparable to the 64.8% agreement between a held-out expert and the majority of their peers. Together, these results show that large-scale proxy supervision can provide scalable route prioritization, while limited expert supervision substantially improves alignment with chemical feasibility.
papers.zh: 用于合成路线评估的专家增强型深度学习方法

papers.title: Proteome-Wide Identification and Membrane Positioning of Single-Pass Membrane Proteins Using AlphaFold Models
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Single-pass (bitopic) transmembrane (TM) proteins are highly abundant and functionally diverse, yet their structures remain poorly characterized. Experimental structures of full-length bitopic proteins and their functional complexes are scarce. Although thousands of predicted protein structures from hundreds of proteomes are available, accurately identifying bitopic proteins and determining their orientations within a lipid bilayer remain challenging. Here we developed AlphaPPM, a new pipeline and web server that identifies bitopic proteins from AlphaFold (AF) models and positions them in membranes. Built on the established Positioning of Proteins in Membranes (PPM) and Folding of Membrane-Associated Peptides (FMAP) approaches, AlphaPPM automatically removes low-confidence unstructured regions and signal sequences, separates structural domains, and then reassembles and orients extracellular, intracellular, and TM domains relative to membrane boundaries. We applied and validated the method across complete sets of bitopic proteins from 18 organisms. The results are available through MembranomeX, a dedicated web resource comprising an online database and four web servers. Supplemented by manual curation and cross-validation, the database contains membrane-oriented AF models of 16,697 bitopic proteins organized into 15 functional classes, 664 superfamilies, and 2497 families and data on 7966 protein complexes. Notably, the workflow identified 1225 bitopic proteins absent from established databases. MembranomeX integrates tools for structural modeling, data retrieval, model verification, and 3D visualization, providing a comprehensive platform for evolutionary, structural, and functional analyses of bitopic proteins.
papers.zh: 使用AlphaFold模型进行蛋白质组范围的鉴定和单跨膜蛋白的膜定位

papers.title: FusioBERT: A Task-Adapted Peptide Language Modeling Framework for Anti- Fusarium Peptide Discovery
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Fusarium pathogens cause substantial crop losses, motivating targeted antifungal peptide discovery. We developed FusioBERT, a 7.52-million-parameter peptide language model incorporating fixed sinusoidal positional encoding, learnable relative position bias, RMSNorm, and SwiGLU. It was pretrained on 19.18 million short sequences and 12,616 candidates mined from 232 Trichoderma genomes. The curated benchmark comprised 210 labeled peptides; evaluation used five balanced 178-sequence subsets with three-seed 5-fold cross-validation. FusioBERT achieved an MCC of 0.948 ± 0.058 and generated continuously differentiated genome-scale rankings, whereas physicochemical classifiers exhibited score saturation. Across nine external peptide tasks, FusioBERT obtained a mean MCC of 0.685, compared with 0.666 for PepBERT-large and 0.654 for ESM2. Fixed-seed residue-order shuffling reduced MCC from 0.947 to 0.874, providing preliminary evidence of sequence-order sensitivity beyond bulk composition. Among the three evaluated prioritization strategies, FusioBERT-only ranking yielded the most favorable descriptive wet-laboratory outcomes, including the strongest broad-spectrum candidates, SR1403–2 and SR1403–3. Their Hill-logistic EC50 values ranged from 1.62 to 7.07 μM; observed MIC end points were 8–32 μM. Physicochemical fusion, docking, and molecular dynamics were treated as auxiliary analyses. FusioBERT supports model-first prioritization but does not directly establish activity probabilities, candidate safety, or universal homology-independent generalization.
papers.zh: FusioBERT：用于发现抗镰刀菌肽的任务自适应肽语言建模框架

papers.title: Deep-Learning Predictions of Biomolecular Structures: Persistent Limitations and New Horizons Extended by Explicit Ion Addition
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: The advent of deep-learning-driven tools such as AlphaFold has revolutionized the prediction of biomolecular structures, offering unprecedented accuracy and accessibility for proteins, RNA, and their complexes. While these tools have demonstrated remarkable success in benchmarking competitions and enabled experimentalists to generate models with ease, their widespread use has also highlighted persistent challenges. These include difficulties in assessing model confidence, limitations in predicting transmembrane domains, nucleic acids, conformational diversity, and interactions with ions or ligands, as well as the tendency to misfold intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). In this perspective, we critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of current AI-based structure prediction tools through illustrative examples with a particular emphasis on the impact of explicit ion modeling. We notably report that the explicit addition of a few potassium cations to the prediction of IDRs or G-quadruplexes can substantially shift AF3’s predicted conformation compared to “dry” predictions. On this basis, we suggest modeling sequences both “dry” and in the presence of explicit potassium cations as a simple, practical way to sample alternative conformations and to expose disordered regions that current predictors tend to overfold. We discuss the importance of reporting confidence metrics in publications to avoid overinterpretation. Furthermore, we address the unique challenges of RNA structure prediction, where data scarcity and structural complexity limit the performance of both classical and deep learning methods. Our analysis underscores the need for continued methodological advancements, integration of complementary computational tools, and expansion of high-quality experimental data sets.
papers.zh: 生物分子结构的深度学习预测：显式离子添加带来的持续性局限和新视野

papers.title: Surrogate Machine Learning Models for ADME Prediction: From Synthetic Labels to Experimental Data
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental data sets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate data sets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access to proprietary data sets; ML models trained on these data can be referred to as surrogate models. However, systematic strategies for developing, evaluating, and applying surrogate models remain underexplored, particularly in the context of transfer learning and validation on new experimental data. In this work, surrogate modeling strategies were investigated for ADME prediction using a data set of over 270,000 compounds with synthetic labels across 25 endpoints. ML models were built on such surrogate data set and evaluated on prospective in-house and public experimental ADME data. Surrogate models based on multitask graph neural networks were predictive under prospective in-house validation and across multiple properties on external data. Uncertainty estimates were informative and actionable, identifying predictions associated with higher or lower prediction errors. Moreover, fine-tuning on experimental data further improved performance for most property data sets. Overall, these results show that surrogate models, especially coupled with fine-tuning, provide a practically valuable approach for ADME prediction, supporting model development from consistently generated data and bringing new opportunities for ML models for property prediction.
papers.zh: 用于 ADME 预测的替代机器学习模型：从合成标签到实验数据

papers.title: Large-Scale and Systematic Prediction of ADMET Properties through Heterogeneous Network and Kernel-Based Deep Learning
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Accurately predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties remains a major challenge in accelerating drug discovery, especially for underexplored natural products (NPs). Herein, we present a unified multitask learning framework that integrated heterogeneous network (HN) embeddings and a modified kernel-based deep neural network (DNN) to simultaneously predict all ADMET properties. Our model named as hdADMET captures complex molecular interactions through HNs that incorporated compound–drug relationships, experimental validated ADMET features, and the interrelationships among ADMET properties to transform the embedding representations into a kernel-based DNN for boosting the learning ability of the prediction model. Hold-out cross-validation on benchmark data sets, including ChEMBL, BindingDB, CTRPandGDSC, and NPASS, demonstrated improved and robust accuracy through data integration. Compared with the state-of-the-art multitask models, the hdADMET model achieved competitive performance with a significantly lower computational cost. Its practical utility was further demonstrated by accurately predicting the ADMET profiles of newly identified NPs mined from the literature studies. The promising candidate with high anticancer activity, low toxicity, and favorable metabolic properties was identified for further experimental validation. The hdADMET model offered an alternative way to prioritize leading compounds for clinical translation through HN embeddings and deep learning.
papers.zh: 通过异构网络和基于核的深度学习对 ADMET 特性进行大规模和系统性预测

papers.title: Fascinated by spatiotemporal hierarchy: From soft matter to liquids and glasses
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Looking back, my research has ranged across critical phenomena, polymers, phase separation, colloids, hydrodynamics, the glass transition, crystallization, water anomalies, liquid–liquid transitions, and, more recently, the mechanics of amorphous solids. The subjects spanned diverse fields, but the question that attracted me remained remarkably persistent: how do microscopic constituents generate structures and collective dynamics on much larger spatial and temporal scales? The idea of spatiotemporal hierarchy, which first impressed me as a graduate student studying critical phenomena, later reappeared in many forms—as dynamic asymmetry and viscoelastic phase separation in soft matter, as hidden many-body structural order in liquids, and as mechanical self-organization in glasses and gels. This article is therefore not intended as a chronological catalog of results. Rather, I look back on several turning points that changed how I thought about condensed matter, the people who encouraged those changes, and the recurring physical ideas that gradually connected apparently different problems.
papers.zh: 对时空层次结构的迷恋：从软物质到液体和玻璃

papers.title: Nonzero-temperature vibronic spectra of polyatomic molecules from a zero-temperature classical trajectory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: By combining coherence thermofield dynamics with the single-Hessian approximation, we enable simulations of low- to medium-resolution vibronic spectra of weakly anharmonic systems at nonzero temperatures, at negligible additional cost relative to zero-temperature calculations. Single-Hessian coherence thermofield Gaussian wavepacket dynamics is exact in any harmonic potential, provided that the reference Hessian is that of the final surface. When applied to Morse systems of increasing anharmonicity and varying temperature, this method successfully captures excited-state anharmonicity and key temperature-dependent spectral features, including hot bands and broadening. By combining the method with on-the-fly ab initio dynamics, we demonstrate its utility by computing the absorption spectra of naphthalene, aminocoumarin C450, and phenyl radical, and the photoelectron spectrum of SeO2−. Within the ab initio single-Hessian approximation, after the zero-temperature spectrum is obtained at the cost of classical molecular dynamics (on the order of hours to days), all nonzero-temperature spectra are computed in seconds.
papers.zh: 来自零温经典轨道的多元分子非零温振动电子光谱

papers.title: Partially reactive force field for the UiO-66 metal–organic framework
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: UiO-66 is the most widely studied metal–organic framework, on account of its structural tunability given by its capacity of sustaining high amounts of point defects in its structure. Its synthesis mechanism is largely unknown, with only a few works mostly focused on the formation of the Zr-oxide cluster. In this work, a partially reactive force field to model UiO-66, nb-UiO-FF, is introduced. This force field incorporates node–ligand reactivity via a Morse potential and the introduction of dummy atoms to reproduce the anisotropic charge distribution of the Zr atoms in the node. nb-UiO-FF reproduces structural features of both UiO-66 and its isoreticular analog UiO-67 as well as framework stability with or without defects, activated or filled with N,N-dimethylformamide or ethanol. Defect generation and node–ligand binding energies are comparable with density functional theory values. The force field is further employed within a molecular dynamics scheme to study the early stages of solvothermal node–ligand binding. Species with structures corresponding to motifs present in UiO-66 are observed, along with other metastable species. This force field enables studying the self-assembly of UiO-66, as well as the formation of its point defects.
papers.zh: UiO-66金属-有机框架的部分反应力场

papers.title: The exact universal exchange-only local field factor of the uniform electron gas and its near-cancellation by parallel-spin correlation near 2kF
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: I use the microscopically derived, well-known, but underappreciated, exact universal expression for the exchange-only local field factor Gx(q,ω) at ω = 0 to gain physical intuition about the separate exchange and correlation contributions to the static quantum Monte Carlo derived “measured” density and spin local field factors G+(q) and G−(q). I use the decomposition of G+ and G− into their fundamental microscopically defined spin-resolved constituents G↑↑ and G↑↓. This decomposition is possible because both G+ and G− are available from Monte Carlo calculations. Recognizing that G↑↑ includes contributions from both exchange and correlation, G↑↑ = G↑↑x + G↑↑c with G↑↑x = Gx, allows the subtraction that reveals the parallel-spin correlation. The antiparallel-spin G↑↓ depends only on correlation. The exact Gx(q,ω) is universal, independent of density, when plotted against q/kF and ω/εF. This paper focuses on the static value at ω = 0. The density functional theory exchange and correlation kernel is directly proportional to the density local field factor through fxc = −4πe2G+/q2. The local field factors define all of the response functions of the electron gas. The static Gx, known in pieces for fifty years, is assembled here into one expression, evaluated exactly, and released as a short Python module. It has a large peak of 1.99 just below 2kF, passes through π2/6 at 2kF, and tends to 1/3. Used alone in a static linear response, it predicts a spin density wave at rs = 4.96 and a charge density wave at rs = 10.62. Quantum Monte Carlo shows the gas has neither. Near 2kF, the difference is striking. Gx has a large peak near 2kF, and G+ shows no comparable structure. Exchange enters G+ and G− identically, so their difference, which is twice the antiparallel factor G↑↓, contains no exchange at all. That difference is measured directly and is small and smooth through 2kF. Whatever removed the exchange-only peak is in the parallel-spin channel. There, everything beyond first-order exchange, that is, screening and correlation together, is large and negative and mirrors the exchange peak. In the measured G+, the net removal is 40%–48% of the peak at rs = 1–10. The stability of the metallic gas against exchange-driven density waves is, therefore, a parallel-spin effect. The decomposition points to where microscopic calculations of each channel should go.
papers.zh: 均匀电子气的精确通用交换-仅局部场因子及其在近2kF处因平行自旋关联而近乎抵消

papers.title: Onsager–Dupuis theory, old and new
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The first theory that coupled electrostatics to structural polarization has been the Onsager–Dupuis theory for ice. The basic concepts that these authors developed were rapidly transferred to water as the usual solvent in liquid electrolytes. Subsequently, the Onsager–Dupuis approach has been forgotten and reinvented several times. In this short contribution, I discuss a simplified version of the structural polarization theory that I have formulated with Rudi Podgornik. I show that a phenomenological fourth-order equation for the electrostatic potential follows strictly from the Onsager–Dupuis theory. Furthermore, I derive generalizations of the Grahame equation for a set of different boundary conditions for a charged and polarizable electrode bounding a structured solvent, paving the way for the application of the general theory to experimentally realizable systems.
papers.zh: 翁萨格-杜普伊理论，旧与新

papers.title: A chemical link between interstellar isopropanol and acetone: H atom reactions in solid para -hydrogen
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Isopropanol [2-propanol, H3CCH(OH)CH3, IPA] and acetone [H3CC(=O)CH3] have been isolated in cryogenic para-H2 matrices at 3.1 K and were exposed to in situ generated H atoms. The reaction between the precursor molecules and H atoms was followed by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy. The appearance of multiple new IR bands was attributed to products of H atom addition/abstraction processes. The experimental work was supported by quantum-chemical computations, helping in the IR spectroscopic assignments. The most important reaction product was the 2-hydroxy-2-propyl radical [CH3C•(OH)CH3] in both the acetone and IPA experiments. This radical may either form upon the abstraction of one H atom from the central C atom of the IPA molecule or when an H atom is directly added to the O atom of the acetone molecule. In addition, the formation of acetone and methane (CH4) from IPA was also observed, whereas the hydroxymethyl radical (•CH2OH) formed when acetone was exposed to H atoms. The results were further corroborated by secondary UV photolytic studies, which also resulted in the formation of photolytic products, such as methyl radical (•CH3), carbon monoxide (CO), and formaldehyde [HC(=O)H]. The main product, CH3C•(OH)CH3, was found to be sensitive to UV light and quickly decomposed to acetone. From an astrochemical perspective, the results demonstrate that there is a direct chemical relationship between acetone and IPA through H-atom reactions. Furthermore, if the radical formed in the reaction recombines with another radical in which the radical center is located on a carbon atom, a branched-carbon chain compound is produced.

papers.title: Experimental observation of mesoscopic dynamic fluctuations in water–alcohol mixtures
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We applied a dynamic fluctuation measurement method to liquid water–methanol mixtures over a wide range of compositions and temperatures. This method, which we developed in recent years, combines ultrasonic and inelastic x-ray scattering techniques to detect mesoscopic-level fluctuations—that is, the degree of heterogeneity—in liquids using sound waves. As a result, it was found that dynamic fluctuations exist across a wide range of compositions and temperatures, including pure substances (water and methanol). Furthermore, in the low-methanol composition range (∼20% mol or less), the strength of dynamic fluctuation increased toward lower compositions and lower temperatures, suggesting that the origin of the fluctuation lies in the low-temperature (supercooled) region of water alone. Conversely, this indicates that in the range below 20% methanol, fluctuations in water alone are dominant rather than the mixed effects of water and methanol. We performed similar dynamic fluctuation measurements on water–ethanol and water–glycerol mixtures at room temperature. We found that dynamic fluctuations exist universally across the entire composition range and confirmed an increase in the strength of dynamic fluctuations toward lower compositions in the regions approximately below 15% and below 20%, respectively. This revealed that the phenomenon is not unique to methanol systems but is a common behavior shared by water–alcohol mixtures. It has long been known that water–alcohol mixtures exhibit various thermodynamic anomalies, but the mechanisms behind them have not yet been fully elucidated. The present results are expected to provide a new direction for discussion on this issue.

papers.title: A minimal thermodynamically consistent chemical oscillator
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Inspired by the chemical reaction network considered the smallest system featuring a Hopf bifurcation and its reversible extension, we introduce an even more minimal reaction network that is thermodynamically consistent and exhibits autonomous oscillations under nonequilibrium driving. The model combines three features that are rarely realized simultaneously in compact oscillator networks: a chemically plausible structure restricted to uni- and bimolecular reactions, reversibility of such reactions, and analytical tractability. The system consists of three internal species coupled to two chemostatted species and still undergoes a supercritical Hopf bifurcation when a chemostat concentration is varied. To analyze the dynamics and thermodynamics near the onset of oscillations, we employ the mathematical technique of normal-form reduction, which allows obtaining a controlled irreversible approximation that preserves the leading phase-space structure of the full reversible network while enabling explicit calculations. This framework provides analytical access to the bifurcation structure and the leading contributions governing thermodynamic observables. Within this setting, we use the onset of oscillations to characterize the thermodynamic response of the system. In particular, we offer an analytical description of key thermodynamic quantities such as the semi-grand Gibbs free energy and the non-conservative work rate, which exhibit a kink-like discontinuity at the Hopf bifurcation. We thus provide an analytical description of a phenomenon previously characterized only through numerical simulations of more complex networks.

papers.title: Negative differential capacitance from composition-dependent Stern capacitance in a binary mixture
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We develop a thermodynamic theory of electric double layers in binary liquid mixtures by allowing the Stern-layer capacitance to depend on the local solvent composition. This coupling produces an additional negative contribution to the inverse differential capacitance. As a result, the surface potential can become a nonmonotonic function of the surface charge density, leading to negative differential capacitance and a voltage-induced first-order transition between two electric-double-layer states. We determine the coexistence condition using a common-tangent construction for the surface-charge-controlled grand potential and obtain phase diagrams in terms of the inverse-capacitance contrast of the Stern layer, surface charge density, bulk composition, and surface potential. We also compare the theory with capacitance data for tetrabutylammonium chloride in water/1-propanol mixtures, finding semi-quantitative agreement in the continuous-response regime. These results suggest that solvent exchange inside the Stern layer can strongly control the capacitance and interfacial phase behavior of binary mixtures.

papers.title: Conformation of microhydrated ethylimidazole isomers explored by microwave spectroscopy
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (2.0–18.5 GHz) has been employed to determine the molecular structures of isolated N-ethylimidazole and 2-ethylimidazole and to investigate the structure and intermolecular interactions within N-ethylimidazole⋯H2O, 2-ethylimidazole⋯H2O, and N-ethylimidazole⋯(H2O)2. All species probed were isolated in the cold environment of a gas sample undergoing supersonic expansion prior to recording of their pure rotational spectra. Density functional theory calculations were performed to aid spectral assignments and provide further information. Consistent with the results of the density functional theory calculations, N-ethylimidazole was observed to adopt a C1 geometry when isolated and also when subsumed into N-ethylimidazole⋯H2O and N-ethylimidazole⋯(H2O)2. The isolated 2-ethylimidazole molecule was observed to be Cs but adopts a C1 geometry within 2-ethylimidazole⋯H2O. Re-orientation of the ethyl group within 2-ethylimidazole is governed by a shallow potential energy surface. Spectroscopic parameters that include rotational constants (A0, B0, and C0), centrifugal distortion constants (DJ, DJK, and d1), and nuclear quadrupole coupling constants of nitrogen nuclei have been determined by fitting parameters in a model Hamiltonian to observed transition frequencies. Precise values of intermolecular bond lengths and angles have been determined by fitting to experimentally determined moments of inertia for a range of isotopologues. All of the hydrates observed during the present work contain a primary hydrogen bond between O–H and the pyridinic nitrogen atom of the imidazole ring and also a weaker hydrogen bond between an O atom of H2O and the substituent group on the C2 atom of the imidazole ring.

papers.title: Optical mapping of composition in nanoconfined fluids applied to the meniscus geometry of an evaporating picoliter droplet
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: In confined space, deviations from bulk structure and properties are expected due to additional thermodynamic variables. In particular, composition variations arising from surface interactions may lead to additional phases and altered phase transitions. In this paper, we introduce a non-invasive method for nanoscale composition mapping in confined liquids using the surface force balance (SFB). The method extends conventional SFB analysis from apex measurements to spatially resolved reconstruction of refractive index profiles within confined fluids. The refractive index profiles provide direct access to the position and geometry of nanoconfined fluid interfaces when multiple phases are present. We describe the interferogram analysis in detail and establish its range of validity through two model scenarios. First, measurements in air demonstrate the precision of the method and are consistent with the presence of a nanometric wetting capillary. Second, we analyze dynamic evaporation of a confined heptane droplet down to 0.1 pL volume. The method provides a time-resolved reconstruction of the meniscus geometry throughout the evaporation process, without relying on the Young–Laplace equation. Although evaporation continuously drives the system out of equilibrium, the meniscus remains well described by a catenoidal geometry down to heights of ∼30 nm. At smaller separations, systematic deviations from the catenoidal profile emerge, indicating a crossover from a surface tension-dominated regime to a confinement-dominated regime. Overall, we demonstrate composition profiling as a framework to analyze confinement-induced composition variations and to quantify interfacial thermodynamic effects at the nanoscale. The analysis may be applied to more complex interfacial films and fluids, for example in partially miscible and biomolecular liquid mixtures.

papers.title: Si magic clusters on Si(111) surfaces: Atomic structure, stability, and diffusion
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Atomic and electronic structures of Si magic clusters formed during annealing/quenching of the Si(111)-7 × 7 surface are explored by means of first-principles calculations. We propose a buckled atomic chain (BAC) model of the clusters, which, although it does not show the lowest formation energy among all candidates considered, agrees with scanning tunneling microscopy data and has the lowest number of constituent atoms, thus favoring its formation kinetics upon quenching from high temperature. The BAC model consists of a buckled Si chain with alternating sp3- and sp2-like bond configurations of atoms, with half of them coming from an external source, while the other half are adatoms from the 7 × 7 structure. According to the BAC model, the cluster is stabilized on reconstructed 5 × 5, 7 × 7, 9 × 9, … Si(111) surfaces through formation of strong covalent bonds that anchor it to the substrate. Based on analysis of cluster structures, we demonstrate that they cannot diffuse without losing their integrity, but rather disassemble into smaller mobile species, which may later reassemble at different surface sites. The picture presented sheds light on our understanding of Si transport during crystal growth.

papers.title: Polarizability of poly(ethylene oxide) enhances cooperative coupling between Li+ and segmental motion
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Ion transport in polymer-based electrolytes is governed by coupled ion–polymer dynamics, yet the role of polymer polarizability remains unresolved. While molecular dynamics simulations have provided insights into the transport mechanism, simulation studies have often neglected explicit polarizability due to a high computational cost, especially for polymeric systems that require long time trajectories to estimate the transport properties. In this study, we consider lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6) in poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) melts and perform all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the APPLE&P force field. We turn on and off the polarization term in the APPLE&P Hamiltonian as a perturbation test and investigate the effects of the polarization term systematically. We find that the polarization term of PEO chains makes the Li+ ion bind strongly to the oxygen atoms of the PEO chains. Such strong binding of the Li+ ion to oxygen atoms slows down the hopping of the Li+ ion between neighboring oxygen atoms of the PEO chains but facilitates the cooperative motion of the Li+ ion with particular PEO chain segments at intermediate time scales. The enhanced cooperativity plays a key role in the ion conductivity and the self-diffusion of the Li+ ions in PEO melts.

papers.title: Polarization competition and relaxation rotation in chiral doped ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Since the discovery of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs), these materials have attracted considerable attention owing to their inherent spontaneous polarization and rapid electric field response characteristics. Recent studies on chiral ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (CFNLC) also indicate that CFNLC has great application potential in fast electro-optical switching and phase modulation. In this study, two new FNLC topological structures were observed in different temperature ranges of CFNLC samples. With the decrease of temperature (138–210 °C), a cross-shaped structure was observed in CFNLC, which was very similar to the conformation observed in cholesteric liquid crystal. Upon further cooling (104–138 °C), the interplay between chiral elasticity and spontaneous polarization leads to the formation of cross-shaped multidomain structures. When a weak alternating current electric field is applied, driven by the cooperative competition among chiral twisting force, spontaneous polarization, and external electric field, the single domain molecular director rotates reversibly and continuously and spontaneously returns to the initial equilibrium state after removing the electric field (relaxation rotation). Afterward, the relaxation rotation behavior of CFNLC was simulated by establishing a model, and the results were in good agreement with our experimental results. Based on the mechanism of relaxation rotation, it is anticipated to realize an optical modulator with superior low driving voltage and high modulation speed. These findings suggest that CFNLC may serve as low-voltage electro-optical platforms for tunable polarization modulation and switching.

papers.title: Unbiased virial-based pressure estimator
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Pressure is a mechanical but not an atomistic concept. It follows either from continuum mechanics or thermodynamics. Statistical mechanics allows us to introduce an atomistic definition of pressure. In statistical mechanics, two equivalent definitions of pressure are possible. The first follows from Green’s approach, which relates pressure to the thermodynamic derivative of the Helmholtz free energy (the logarithm of the canonical partition function) with respect to volume, and the second from a formulation of the mechanical Clausius virial theorem for a closed—or open [J. A. Schweitz, J. Phys. A 10, 507 (1977)]—system. However, as we demonstrate in this paper, both approaches are incomplete, as they result in atomistic definitions of the pressure that are only asymptotically unbiased. Here, exploiting an idea advanced by D. H. Tsai [J. Phys. A 70, 1375 (1979)], we find a simple justification for an ingenious observation made by T. W. Lion and R. J. Allen [J. Phys. Condens. Matter 24, 284133 (2012)] based on the study of J. F. Lutsko [J. Appl. Phys. 64, 1152 (1988)] and J. Cormier et al. [J. Appl. Phys. 89, 99 (2001)]. We find that the virial by itself is not enough to properly define (if not asymptotically, in the thermodynamic limit) the atomistic estimator of the pressure. Rather, one needs a proper definition of what contributes to the pressure (the force exerted per unit area on a system in equilibrium) acting on a surface dividing the space into two parts. With that, and a properly generalized concept of additive cell virial, we provide a simple justification of an already known unbiased estimator for the pressure of an open atomistic system in a local cell in equilibrium.

papers.title: Influence of Crystal Structure and Shape Anisotropies on Valence-Band States of InP Colloidal Nanocrystals: Application of the xyz Algorithm
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: We demonstrate that traditional classification of electronic states in semiconductor nanocrystals based on the quantum numbers of angular momenta becomes inappropriate and even misleading in nanocrystals with strong crystalline anisotropy, such as InP. We propose an alternative classification based on irreducible representations of the symmetry group fully taking into account symmetry aspects of both the underlying crystal lattice and the overall nanocrystal shape. Furthermore, we present a new tool for modeling semiconductor nanocrystals within the effective mass approximation by adapting the xyz algorithm widely used to find eigenfrequencies for vibrational modes of both macroscopic elastic objects and nanoparticles and based on the Rayleigh–Ritz variational principle. We demonstrate its extreme efficiency and versatility by studying the influence of crystal structure and shape anisotropies on valence-band states of InP colloidal nanocrystals destined to replace highly toxic cadmium and lead containing quantum dots in numerous applications.

papers.title: Curvature Rebuilt d-Orbital Energy Levels of TM@g-C6N6 Nanotubes for Water-Splitting Enhancement
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Precisely constructing transition metal (TM) active sites in two-dimensional materials can enhance water splitting, whereas the role of geometric factors such as interfacial curvature remains poorly understood. Nanotubes (NTs) provide a well-defined curved architecture that can modulate electron interactions and reactivity. Here, we rationally design a series of TM@g-C6N6 NTs and use first-principles calculations assisted by machine learning to elucidate how dimensional reduction and curvature govern water-splitting activity. We find that reduced curvature radius systematically promotes water splitting. Notably, the Ir/Rh-decorated g-C6N6 NTs show remarkable electrocatalytic performance with calculated overpotentials of 0.05 eV for the hydrogen evolution reaction and 0.20 eV for the oxygen evolution reaction. Curvature-induced confinement drives reconstruction and reoccupation of the d-orbital states near the Fermi level upon transitioning from a flat plane to a tubular geometry. More importantly, for different reaction intermediates, we identify a curvature-dependent inversion of the dominant adsorption orbital transition from the dz2 to the dx2–y2, which directly correlates with enhanced catalytic activity. Our results establish interfacial curvature as a key manipulator for tuning electronic structure and water-splitting reactivity in TM@g-C6N6 NT single-atom catalysts and provide a new perspective on modulating electronic and catalytic properties in TM@g-C6N6 NT-like structures.

papers.title: Synergistic SERS Enhancement in Ag NW/WSe2 Heterostructures: Interfacial Charge Transfer and Layer-Dependent Sensitivity
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates based on metal/two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor composites offer unique advantages, yet macroscopic ensemble platforms suffer from spatial nonuniformity that obscures interfacial mechanisms. A deterministic SERS platform was constructed by precisely integrating an individual Ag NW across silica–monolayer (1L) and monolayer–bilayer (2L) WSe2 boundaries. The Ag NW–1L WSe2 hybrid exhibits Raman intensities up to 7.4 times higher than Ag NWs on silica and 4.0–4.5 times higher than Ag NWs on 2L WSe2. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Ag donates ∼0.36 e to WSe2, while 1L WSe2 confines the transferred electrons to its surface, yielding a high surface charge density. In contrast, 2L WSe2 exhibits spatial charge delocalization across the bilayer, reducing the surface electron density. This work offers a controllable strategy to eliminate ensemble averaging and clarifies layer-dependent interfacial dynamics in metal–2D semiconductor heterostructures.
papers.zh: Ag NW/WSe2异质结构中的协同SERS增强：界面电荷转移和层依赖性灵敏度

papers.title: Acid-Etched Lead Telluride with Defect-Regulated Surfaces Enables Efficient Mechanical-Energy-Driven Nitrogen Fixation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Ambient ammonia synthesis is important for carbon neutrality. Tribo-electro-catalysis, which converts mechanical friction into chemical driving force through contact electrification and charge transfer, offers a route for nitrogen (N2) fixation. However, inefficient utilization of friction-induced charges and insufficient N2 activation remain major challenges. Herein, acid-etching defect engineering regulates the surface and electronic structures of lead telluride (PbTe) for N2 fixation. The catalyst etched for 90 min exhibits the enhanced activity under dark ambient conditions, delivering ammonium (NH4+) production rates of 258.98 and 329.60 μmol L–1·g–1·h–1 without and with 10 vol % methanol, respectively. Analyses reveal that etching reconstructs the surface, generates defect sites, facilitates N2 adsorption and activation, and promotes friction-induced charge utilization. Excessive etching decreases activity. Charge-trapping and electron paramagnetic resonance measurements support the role of friction-induced negative charges, establishing defect-mediated charge regulation as an effective strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis.

papers.title: Carbon-Isotope Labeling Rules Out Covalent Sulfur Addition to Graphene
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Covalent functionalization of graphene is commonly inferred from Raman spectroscopy, photoelectron spectroscopy, microscopy, and first-principles calculations. However, these methods may not distinguish bonding to the graphene lattice from the adsorption of carbon-containing reaction products. Here, we investigate this ambiguity using the gas-phase reaction of sulfur radicals with graphene as a case study. Sulfur treatment produces new Raman bands, substantial changes in the photoemission spectra, and surface compositions consistent with sulfur addition. Density functional theory calculations further show that these observations can be reproduced by a stable graphene episulfide structure in which sulfur bridges two lattice carbon atoms. A decisive control experiment using isotopically pure 13C graphene nevertheless rules out this assignment. Although the intrinsic graphene Raman bands undergo the expected isotope shifts, the characteristic reaction–product bands near 1260 and 1450 cm–1 remain unchanged. The carbon atoms contributing to these modes therefore originate from extrinsic species rather than from the graphene lattice. Detection of similar products on hexagonal boron nitride further supports the formation of organosulfur species in the gas phase, followed by their selective deposition on hydrophobic surfaces. These results show that an extensive agreement among conventional characterization methods and theoretical predictions can still lead to an incorrect structural assignment. Isotopically labeled graphene provides a direct and broadly applicable control for establishing whether carbon atoms in proposed functional groups originate from the graphitic lattice.

papers.title: In Situ EPR Spectroscopy to Track Gas Exchange Kinetics in Porous Liquids under Variable Gas Pressure
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Porous liquids (PLs) are novel promising materials, which demand development of informative spectroscopic tools to track their functioning in situ and operando. In this work we demonstrate in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy as a versatile method to investigate variable-pressure gas exchange in PLs of the third type based on metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and sterically excluded solvents. The use of permanently encapsulated in-MOF spin probes (stable nitroxide radicals) allows tracking evolution of EPR spectral shapes under applied gas pressure, and following theoretical analysis reveals contributions of gas exchange kinetics in MOF particles, gas diffusion through the bulk sample and gas dissolution in PL. We exemplify this approach with two PLs based on MOF ZIF-8 dispersed in dibutyl phthalate or ionic liquid [Bmim]BF4. In both PL examples EPR provides unique information on gas exchange kinetics (air-to-CO2 and CO2-to-air) vs pressure in situ, which is indispensable for adjusting target functioning of PLs and their applications in future.

papers.title: Single-Ion Hydration Through the Lens of Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Single-ion hydration provides a stringent test of molecular models because local ion–water interactions, collective polarization, nuclear quantum effects, and long-range electrostatics all contribute to experimentally measurable structure, spectra, and thermodynamics. Here we discuss how data-driven many-body potentials, in particular MB-pol for water and MB-nrg for hydrated ions, provide a physically transparent route from correlated electronic structure data to predictive simulations of ion hydration from clusters to bulk water and aqueous interfaces. We emphasize how this framework transforms single-ion hydration from a parametrization problem into a hierarchy of many-body observables, and we outline opportunities for connecting simulations directly with interfacial spectroscopy, hydration free energies, and complex electrolyte environments.

papers.title: Single- and Multiexciton Dynamics in Porphyrin Nanorings
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Exciton transport in molecular assemblies is typically studied in linear chains and polydisperse aggregates, where chain ends perturb the electronic structure and structural inhomogeneity can obscure size-dependent trends. Molecular nanorings overcome both limitations. They are end-group-free macrocycles with well-defined sizes, while their dimensions can be synthetically tuned from a few to several tens of porphyrin units. Here, we use intensity-cycled femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy to disentangle single-exciton and multiexciton dynamics in a series of fully conjugated molecular nanorings containing 6–40 Zn-porphyrin units. By isolating the third-, fifth-, and seventh-order nonlinear responses, we independently track single-, two-, and three-exciton dynamics, respectively, enabling the ring-size dependence of exciton–exciton annihilation (EEA) to be determined without relying on a priori kinetic assumptions. The EEA rate decreases systematically with an increase in ring size, accompanied by a crossover from annihilation-limited to diffusion-limited EEA between 20 and 30 porphyrin units. The smallest nanoring exhibits no resolvable multiexciton dynamics, consistent with exciton delocalization across the entire ring or equivalent subinstrument response EEA, whereas larger rings exhibit increasingly diffusive exciton motion as static disorder limits delocalization. The retrieved exciton diffusion coefficients are 2–3 orders of magnitude higher than those we previously reported, indicating that the assumptions inherent to conventional intensity-dependent fitting can substantially underestimate exciton mobility.
papers.zh: 卟啉纳米环中的单激子和多激子动力学

papers.title: A-Site-Dependent Hydrogen Affinity in Ti3AlC2 Single Crystal and Ti3ZnC2-Oriented Platelet
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: MAX phases provide compositionally tunable layered structures for investigating hydrogen interactions, but the role of A-site chemistry remains insufficiently understood. Here, Ti3ZnC2-oriented platelets were prepared from Ti3AlC2 single-crystal precursors through Al-to-Zn substitution in a Lewis-acidic molten salt. Under the tested conditions, the temperature required for near-complete Al removal increased with the lateral size of the precursor platelets. Surface and cross-sectional EDS analyses were consistent with near-complete Al-to-Zn substitution in the examined regions. Density functional theory calculations of selected ideal-bulk configurations identified Ti–A layer interstitial sites as energetically favorable for H insertion in both phases. Replacing Al with Zn lowered the most favorable single-H formation energy from −0.22 to −0.61 eV and stabilized selected multi-H configurations. At 77 K and 72.2 bar, Ti3ZnC2 showed an H2 uptake of 0.303 wt %, compared with 0.145 wt % for Ti3AlC2. The Ti3ZnC2-oriented platelets reached 0.505 wt % at 100 bar, despite having slightly lower N2-accessible BET surface area and pore volume than the Ti3AlC2 precursors. These results reveal an A-site-dependent difference in ideal-bulk H-insertion energetics and total low-temperature H2 uptake. These findings identify A-site chemistry as an effective compositional variable for tuning hydrogen interactions in Ti-based MAX phases.
papers.zh: Ti3AlC2单晶和Ti3ZnC2取向薄片中A位依赖性氢亲和力

papers.title: Prolonged Exciton Survival with Enhanced Spatial Contraction in Layered WSSe Alloys
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The spatial extent of an optically detected excitation population is determined by both particle motion and spatially selective survival, so a more persistent signal need not imply greater spreading. Here, we combine broadband transient transmission spectroscopy, fluence-dependent kinetics, and transient absorption microscopy to follow the A-exciton bleach in monolayer, bilayer, and trilayer nominal WS0.9Se1.1 alloys. Increasing layer thickness produces a pronounced temporal–spatial contrast. The bleach becomes more persistent, whereas its spatial profile undergoes stronger transient contraction. Fluence-dependent kinetics further reveal that enhanced survival after the initial decay can coexist with faster depletion at later times. Joint analysis using a trapping–diffusion model with shared reaction parameters supports a picture in which traps fill more rapidly near the excitation center, suppressing further capture there, while continued capture at the periphery narrows the bleach-active population. Diffusion and density-dependent loss oppose this narrowing and contribute to the subsequent width recovery. These results show that temporal persistence and spatial spreading need not evolve together when relaxation is spatially selective.
