papers.title: Understanding the Contrasting Effects of V vs Mn Doping on the OER Activity of Co3O4(001): A DFT+ U Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Designing efficient electrocatalysts for clean energy conversion requires atomic-scale insight into the relationship between targeted surface modifications and catalytic performance. Using density functional calculations with an on-site Hubbard U term (DFT+U), we investigate the effect of Mn and V doping on the performance of Co3O4(001) as an anode material for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Our results show that Mn, which is preferentially incorporated at a surface octahedral site at both the B- and A-terminated Co3O4(001) surfaces, has a detrimental effect on the OER efficiency. In contrast, V, which also prefers a surface octahedral site at the B-layer termination, acquires a 5+ oxidation state and reduces the overpotential (η) of a Cooct reaction site from 0.48 to 0.43 V. Remarkably, at the A-termination, V is incorporated as V4+ in the subsurface layer, which reduces the overpotential at the tetrahedral Co site from 0.74 to 0.18 V. This enhancement in catalytic activity is attributed to the modification of the surface Cooct oxidation state from Co3+ (IS) to Co2+ prior to OER and its further variation during OER. This substantially reduces the binding energy of *OH and thereby the potential-determining step height by 0.56 eV. Taking into account implicit solvation increases the overpotential for both undoped and Mn-doped surfaces, whereas it marginally decreases the overpotential for the V-doped A-layer termination. The deprotonation of *OH to *O constitutes the potential-determining step for all investigated surface reaction sites, thereby positioning them on the right leg of the volcano plot, while η of the Cotet reaction site at the V-doped A-layer lies beyond the top of the volcano. These insights demonstrate how selective doping can be used as a promising strategy to tailor catalyst’s performance.
papers.zh: 了解V掺杂与Mn掺杂对Co3O4(001)的OER活性的相反影响：一项DFT+ U研究

papers.title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopic Identification of Ethylene Adsorption States on Ag + -Exchanged ZSM-5 Zeolites
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy was applied to investigate the adsorption behavior of ethylene on ZSM-5 zeolites containing Na+, Ag+, and H+ sites. Ethylene adsorbed on Na+ and Ag+ sites could be distinguished by its characteristic NIR absorption band. Further, ethylene adsorbed on Brønsted acid sites was identified by the formation of protonated ethyl species. Temperature-dependent measurements also revealed distinct desorption behaviors associated with different cation sites. The applicability of NIR spectroscopy was further demonstrated by in situ monitoring of ethanol dehydration over Ag+0.5/H+0.5/ZSM-5. Upon ethanol adsorption, ethoxy species were first formed on Brønsted acid sites. At reaction temperatures above 200 °C, ethylene was generated and subsequently adsorbed on Ag+ sites, while water was simultaneously produced. In contrast, the characteristic C–H stretching bands of ethylene were not detected in the mid-IR region under the same reaction conditions. This may lead to the misleading conclusion that ethylene produced during ethanol dehydration is not adsorbed on the catalyst surface. These results demonstrate that NIR spectroscopy provides complementary information to conventional FT-IR measurements for investigating adsorption phenomena and catalytic reactions.

papers.title: Building Metal–Oxygen Connectivity in Amorphous Iridium Oxide through Electrochemical Cycling in Acid
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The development of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts has been hindered by the high overpotential requirements, challenges in catalyst stability, and the complexity of OER mechanisms. Under water oxidation conditions, multiple concurrent processes, such as catalyst dissolution and surface reconstruction, further complicate mechanistic understandings. One factor that makes studies of water oxidation mechanisms especially difficult is the dynamic nature of the catalytic structure under reaction conditions. Herein, we report the observation of a stabilization effect of an amorphous iridium oxide (IrOx) catalyst under water oxidation conditions. The effect was revealed to be caused by improved connectivity between neighboring Ir and O atoms on the surface. The reaction was found to proceed in parallel to the oxidation of H2O and was only observed under potentials above the onset of water oxidation. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations further confirmed this understanding. The results shed light on the competing reaction pathways once an active metal center is activated and highlight the favorable outcomes by improved connectivity for water oxidation catalysis.
papers.zh: 通过酸性电化学循环在非晶铱氧化物中建立金属-氧连接

papers.title: Systematic Investigation of Superconducting Trends in Lanthanide-Substituted M C2H8 Ternary Hydrides
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The pursuit of high-temperature superconductors represents a persistent challenge in solid-state physics. Hydrogen-rich ternary materials subjected to high pressure have emerged as particularly promising candidates. Among these, the Fm3̅m-MC2H8 family exhibits remarkable stability and compositional diversity. While LaC2H8 has been investigated, other lanthanide substituted variants remain largely unexplored. This work systematically investigates the superconducting properties of lanthanide-based MC2H8 compounds over a wide range of pressures. Calculations predicted 14 unknown superconductors within this family, with critical temperatures strongly dependent on the choice of metal M. Notably, LuC2H8 achieves the highest Tc of 99.5 K (at 200 GPa), while YbC2H8 stabilizes at the lowest pressure (30 GPa). The pressure- and temperature-dependent trends governing superconductivity in these systems have been further elucidated, providing insight into the role of lanthanide substitution in enhancing superconducting properties. These findings expand the landscape of high-temperature superconductors and highlight the potential of hydrogen-rich ternary hydrides under extreme conditions.
papers.zh: 镧系元素取代的M C2H8三元氢化物中超导趋势的系统研究

papers.title: Evolution of Surface Intermediate Species in the Direct N2O-Mediated Conversion of Methane to Methanol over H+-Ferrierite
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The direct conversion of methane to methanol under mild conditions remains a central challenge in catalysis. In this study, we employ a series of ferrierite (FER) zeolite catalysts to investigate the surface species and acid-site characteristics associated with methane activation in the presence of N2O. In situ DRIFTS measurements reveal the formation of surface methoxy-related species on protonic ferrierite (H+-FER) at temperatures above 200 °C, with their spectral intensity increasing with reaction temperature. Variation of the parent NH4+-FER calcination temperature (450, 550 °C) and alkali-ion exchange (Na+, K+) demonstrates a correlation between methoxy formation and the presence and density of Brønsted acid sites. Importantly, H+-FER maintains methoxy stabilization up to 300 °C, exhibiting enhanced persistence of methoxy-related species at elevated temperatures, consistent with the influence of the confined FER pore environment on the stability of surface intermediates. Complementary solid-state NMR, NH3-TPD, XPS, and pyridine-desorption IR spectroscopy provide consistent evidence for the structural and acidic properties of the FER catalysts. Additional DRIFTS-MS experiments show that H2O exposure leads to the attenuation of surface methoxy-related bands and a transient methanol-related mass-spectrometric response, supporting the formation of methanol-related products from surface species generated during CH4 + N2O exposure. Overall, this study provides spectroscopic evidence linking the acid environment of H+-FER to the formation of surface methoxy-related species and highlights the potential role of zeolite confinement in stabilizing reactive surface intermediates during methane oxidation.
papers.zh: 甲烷在H+-沸石上直接经由N2O介导转化为甲醇过程中表面中间体物种的演变

papers.title: Disulfide Rearrangement Driven Changes in the Structure, Dynamics, and Conformational Stability of Conotoxin Pl14A
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Conotoxin Pl14A, a 25-residue peptide from the venom of the cone snail Conus planorbis, contains four cysteines that can pair in three ways, yet only the globular connectivity (Cys7–Cys22, Cys11–Cys24) is found in nature. Using classical and replica-exchange molecular dynamics, we compared it with the ribbon (Cys7–Cys24, Cys11–Cys22) and bead (Cys7–Cys11, Cys22–Cys24) isomers. The globular isomer stays compact, retaining its helix and a persistent intramolecular hydrogen-bond network and coordinated motion, and occupies a single deep free-energy basin, whereas the ribbon isomer is partially disordered and has an unstable secondary structure, with a shallow landscape. The bead isomer, which has no disulfide linking the two halves of the peptide, rearranges early into a non-native structure with a new β-bridge and a fragmented landscape. Conformational stability therefore follows the order globular > ribbon > bead, and the intramolecular free energy favors the globular isomer over both alternatives, most strongly over the bead. Simulations of the reduced peptide show that this preference is already encoded in the sequence without disulfide bonds, the peptide mostly adopts a globular-like fold, and most of its bonding-competent cysteine geometries match the globular pairing. The disulfides thus reinforce, rather than dictate, a fold the sequence already favors, and pairings that conflict with it destabilize the peptide, most strongly when no long-range disulfide remains. These results help explain connectivity selection in conotoxins and other disulfide-rich peptides, with implications for peptide engineering.
papers.zh: 二硫键重排驱动的锥蜗毒素Pl14A的结构、动力学和构象稳定性变化

papers.title: A Unified Thermodynamic and Kinetic Benchmark for the Catalytic Glucose–Fructose–Mannose Interconversion in Water
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Catalytic interconversion of glucose–fructose–mannose (GFM) in water is a fundamental reaction network central to carbohydrate chemistry and biomass valorization. Herein, using enzyme-catalyzed equilibrium data, we identified deviations in the standard molar Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔfGθ) and the standard molar entropy (Sθ) of aqueous mannose and refined these values from −910.99 to −912.77 kJ mol–1 and from 266.90 to 272.89 J mol–1 K–1, respectively. An equilibrium composition model accounting for sugar degradation was developed to quantify the GFM network, yielding temperature-dependent normalized concentrations under varying sugar mass balances. This enables quantitative determination of how far any GFM system deviates from its thermodynamic equilibrium. Kinetic modeling shows that irreversible degradation pathways convert the GFM network into a mass-loss system, while byproduct-driven autocatalysis promotes both sugar interconversion and degradation, thereby preventing the GFM system from reaching equilibrium. For chemo-catalytic systems, catalyst-accelerated degradation and catalyst self-deactivation cause irreversible sugar loss to kinetically outcompete GFM interconversion, pulling the system from equilibrium. The near-equilibrium hexose concentrations observed in pairwise interconversion represent a kinetically controlled pseudosteady state rather than true global thermodynamic equilibrium. Notably, the established benchmark applies to dilute aqueous systems, whereas concentrated and nonaqueous systems require activity coefficient correction, reparameterization, and kinetic validation.
papers.zh: 水介质中葡萄糖–果糖–甘露糖催化互变的统一热力学和动力学基准

papers.title: Multiscale Prediction of Thermodynamic Properties of Supercritical Aqueous Sodium Sulfide Using Synchrotron Experiments, Atomistic Simulations, and Artificial Neural Networks
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The increase of fossil fuel use is responsible for increased greenhouse gas emissions, which have a great impact on the environment, leading to global warming. Consequently, substantial efforts are devoted to decreasing our dependence on fossil fuels and there is a growing interest in harnessing the chemical energy from other carbon-neutral sources like biomass. Supercritical water gasification (SCWG), which is a catalyst-mediated process, provides a promising method to transform organic streams and wastes into fuels due to the utilization of water as a nontoxic green solvent. However, the process is limited by sulfur impurities that deactivate the catalysts required for efficient conversion. The optimization of SCWG remains challenging because the solvent properties of aqueous mixtures in the supercritical regime are unknown, and they have significant differences while crossing the Widom line, which separates liquid- and gas-like states. In this study, we propose a framework to determine accurate thermodynamic properties for complex systems under supercritical conditions, where experimental data are scarce. We demonstrate that a methodology combining structural characterization experiments, atomistic simulations, and machine learning enables the development of reliable equations of state for systems with previously unknown properties. This approach characterizes changes in the thermophysical properties of the aqueous solution across the Widom line, with potential implications for ion solvation and sulfur speciation in SCWG. By providing thermophysical property predictions that may inform process models aimed at improving sulfur removal and mitigating catalyst poisoning, our framework advances the SCWG method as a clean energy technology. More broadly, the methodology is generalizable and can be applied to a wide range of complex fluid systems with poorly understood thermodynamic behavior.
papers.zh: 使用同步辐射实验、原子模拟和人工神经网络对超临界硫化钠水溶液的热力学性质进行多尺度预测

papers.title: Nonparametric Analysis of Nonexponential Relaxation: Standard and Two-Dimensional Kinetics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: When a system’s relaxation is not well described by a single rate constant, the range of results is often restricted before the data are analyzed. This paper presents an alternative, “data-first” approach that avoids these restrictions. The method is nonparametric: no model or fitting function, such as a stretched exponential, is used. At the same time, it avoids the ambiguities in nonparametric approaches that are based on the inverse Laplace transform. Experimental data are initially transformed into a spectral representation, which helps to visualize their important features and limitations. These kinetic spectra are then quantified by “descriptors” that characterize the relaxation mechanism but are insensitive to the details of the data analysis. This method not only treats standard kinetics; it also extends naturally to newer, multidimensional experiments. These ideas are illustrated with one- and two-dimensional data from a recent study of solute rotation in micelles.
papers.zh: 非指数弛豫的非参数分析：标准动力学和二维动力学

papers.title: Atmospheric Chemistry of 3,3,3-Trifluoropropane-1,2-diol, CF3CH(OH)CH2OH: OH Radical and Cl Kinetics and the Products and Mechanisms of Cl Atom-Initiated Oxidation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Photochemical reactors were used to study the Cl-atom- and OH-radical-initiated oxidation of several oxygenates, including the title compound, 3,3,3-trifluoropropane-1,2-diol (CF3CH(OH)CH2OH), in 700 Torr of air or N2 diluent at 296 K. Using relative rate methods, k(Cl + CF3CH(OH)CH2OH) = (6.8 ± 1.3) × 10–12 cm3 molecule–1 s–1 and k(OH + CF3CH(OH)CH2OH) = (1.6 ± 0.3) × 10–12 cm3 molecule–1 s–1 were determined. The atmospheric lifetime with respect to reaction with OH radicals is estimated at 7.2 days for CF3CH(OH)CH2OH. The primary oxidation products were identified as α-hydroxy carbonyls with absorption bands located at 1753 and 1780 cm–1, assigned to the formation of CF3CH(OH)CHO and CF3C(O)CH2OH, respectively. Nonlinear fits were used to estimate k(Cl + CF3CH(OH)CHO) = (4 ± 1) × 10–12 cm3 molecule–1 s–1 and k(Cl + CF3C(O)CH2OH) = (9 ± 4) × 10–13 cm3 molecule–1 s–1. Major final products are CF3CHO, CF3C(O)OH, and COF2. As part of this study, the IR spectrum of CF3C(O)CHO was recorded and the rate coefficient k(Cl + CF3C(O)CHO) = (9.7 ± 1.0) × 10–13 cm3 molecule–1 s–1 was determined. The products and the oxidation mechanism are discussed in the context of the atmospheric degradation of third-generation CFC-replacement compounds.
papers.zh: 3,3,3-三氟丙烷-1,2-二醇的大气化学，CF3CH(OH)CH2OH：OH自由基和Cl动力学以及Cl原子引发氧化的产物和机理

papers.title: Reweighting Free Energy Profiles with Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Fast Consensus Building
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made density functional theory (DFT)-level molecular dynamics highly affordable. However, their rapid proliferation makes it prohibitively expensive to benchmark every new model against the potential of mean force (PMF), the bridge between microscopic atomic fluctuations and macroscopic thermodynamic and kinetic observables. Reweighting the trajectory of a single “source” MLIP onto a suite of target potentials offers a cheaper route, but it is hindered by the statistical collapse of exponential free energy perturbation when the phase-space overlap between potentials is low. We show that for system sizes of practical interest, this collapse is essentially unavoidable, and we quantify it with an information-theoretic diagnostic, the reweighting entropy, that indicates when reweighting can be trusted. To sidestep the collapse, we introduce a systematic, scalable reweighting framework spanning exponential reweighting, the Gaussian approximation, and the energy-only estimator. When applied to the intramolecular radical cyclization of hexenyl (17 atoms), all three estimators perform well and reproduce the target ωB97M-V/def2-TZVP PMF. However, when extended to Li+ transport through a water-solvated zeolite (601 atoms), only the energy-only estimator recovers the PMFs of a diverse suite of MLIPs from a single source simulation by discarding the noisy entropic contribution to the free energy correction. An independent, brute-force umbrella sampling of one of the most divergent targets (MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN) for this system confirms it: beyond the shape of the PMF, both the reaction and activation free energies are recovered within chemical accuracy. The same analysis reveals that the studied MLIPs partition into two clusters, one of plain generalized gradient approximation (GGA) models (PBE, PBE-sol) and one of meta-GGA and/or dispersion-corrected models (PBE-D3, r2SCAN, r2SCAN-D4), reflecting differences in their training data and DFT reference. The resulting protocol thus offers an affordable and reliable route to cross-model consensus on materials properties, even when exact reweighting is statistically intractable.
papers.zh: 使用通用机器学习原子间势能对自由能曲线进行重新加权，以快速达成共识

papers.title: Low-Scaling Equation-of-Motion Coupled Cluster Method for Open-Shell Systems: I. IP-EOM-DLPNO-CCSD
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We present the formulation and implementation of an unrestricted/open-shell domain-based local pair natural orbital equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method with single and double excitations for vertical ionization potentials (UHF IP-EOM-DLPNO-CCSD). The method extends the open-shell DLPNO–CCSD reference calculation to the (N – 1)-electron sector by reusing the localized occupied orbitals, pair domains, pair lists, and pair natural orbital spaces generated for the correlated ground state. Removal of an α or β electron is treated in separate spin sectors. The one-hole sector is retained in the fully localized occupied space, whereas the two-hole–one-particle sector is represented in compact, spin-resolved PNO spaces. The accuracy is controlled by the standard LoosePNO, NormalPNO, and TightPNO hierarchy. For ionized states dominated by one-hole character, canonical and local calculations performed with the same quasi-restricted-orbital (QRO) reference give typical RMSD differences of a few hundredths of an eV for the main-group radical and transition-metal benchmark sets. A representative TightPNO comparison for naphthalene further indicates that the additional local IP-EOM approximation contributes less than 0.10 eV for the ten matched states examined. Larger delocalized systems show less regular threshold dependence, and even predominantly one-hole states can exhibit changes greater than 0.1 eV between NormalPNO and TightPNO. Timing calculations for anionic acenes up to heptacene, with 1038 basis functions, show low-order effective scaling for the IP-EOM step. Applications to C70– and to the Pheophytin radical anion, the latter containing 3020 basis functions, demonstrate that the method can treat large open-shell molecular systems beyond the size range routinely accessible to canonical IP-EOM-CCSD. Finally, comparisons with available experimental data for the N-carbazolyl radical and the ovalene radical cation provide additional context for the calculated vertical ionization energies.
papers.zh: 用于开壳层系统的低标度运动方程耦合簇方法：I. IP-EOM-DLPNO-CCSD

papers.title: FermiLink: An Agent Harness for Multidomain Scientific Simulations
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Artificial intelligence (AI) agent harnesses have been developed for autonomous scientific simulations, but most current agent harnesses are tested on a single or a small set of software packages. Herein, FermiLink, an extensible open-source agent harness, is introduced for multidomain scientific simulations. Its key design principle is the separation of package knowledge bases from simulation workflows, so that simulation workflows in FermiLink, from figure-level simulations to full-paper-level research on high-performance computing clusters, operate uniformly among supported packages via a four-layer progressive disclosure mechanism. This agent harness is specifically optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling multiday, multistep scientific simulations in the absence of human intervention. Using OpenAI Codex as the agent provider, the capabilities of FermiLink are demonstrated across approximately 50 scientific software packages spanning nine research domains from chemistry to engineering. Systematic benchmarks on 132 real-world figure-level reproduction tasks with 44 packages show that FermiLink reproduces 74 (56.1%) of published figures with simulations, among which 30 (22.7%) achieve high-fidelity agreement and 35 reach qualitative agreement with the target figures. A smaller set of human expert-guided reproduction benchmarks with 10 packages in physics and chemistry further highlights the importance of expert insights for improving the simulation fidelity. Beyond reproduction, a single-blinded study demonstrates that FermiLink can produce research-grade results on unpublished polariton physics problems when provided with sufficiently detailed research objectives. Overall, FermiLink provides a scalable research infrastructure that may accelerate the path from scientific questions to computational results across diverse domains.
papers.zh: FermiLink：用于多域科学仿真的代理线束

papers.title: Can Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo with Broken Symmetry Trials Describe Iron–Sulfur Clusters?
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) has in several cases been found to perform well on strongly correlated systems, including compounds containing transition-metal elements. Here, we benchmark the method for three iron–sulfur clusters ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S], and the FeMo cofactor) using a hierarchy of systematically improved trial states derived from coupled cluster (CC) theory, including up to quadruple excitations relative to the Hartree–Fock (HF) reference, as well as multi-Slater trial states derived from unrestricted density matrix renormalization group wave functions. Our results reveal for these systems that, as the symmetry-broken trial is improved beyond the mean-field level, the phaseless AFQMC energy can become less accurate, and in some cases even less accurate than the underlying trial projected energy itself, displaying an inverted energy pattern that is only corrected once the trial fidelity is sufficiently high. For [2Fe-2S], we show that a decreased accuracy in the AFQMC energy can coincide with a simultaneous improvement in the trial state and the walker ensemble, as measured by their fidelity relative to the exact ground state, a behavior which is allowed by the nonvariational nature of the phaseless AFQMC energy estimator. We further find that this is not solely due to the use of spin-unrestricted trial states, as the inversion persists in [2Fe-2S] when we explicitly break the symmetry of the Hamiltonian by applying a fictitious local spin-Zeeman field. Instead, we find that the energy inversion is related to the choice of measurement trial in the estimator, where using a high-order CC trial state for measurements may introduce errors that are suppressed when the measurement wave function is restricted to lower excitation subspaces. In particular, measuring the energy with the mean-field reference while guiding the walkers with a CC trial removes the inverted pattern and improves the overall accuracy across the iron–sulfur clusters, with a possible exception for [4Fe-4S] where energies with a CCSDT guide may be less accurate than those guided by CCSD for some broken-symmetry families. Taken together, our findings suggest that the relatively accurate energies obtained with an HF trial state in these systems arise from favorable error cancellation, warranting significant caution about the reliability of phaseless AFQMC with such trials for strongly correlated transition-metal systems of this kind.
papers.zh: 无相辅助场量子蒙特卡洛方法结合破缺对称性试探能否描述铁-硫簇？

papers.title: Consistency, Cancellation, and Experiment in Quasi-Harmonic Thermochemistry
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: For weakly bound molecular complexes, the Gibbs energy is often limited less by the electronic interaction energy, now computed to near chemical accuracy, than by the statistical-mechanical treatment of their low-frequency intermolecular vibrations. The standard remedy, Grimme’s quasi-harmonic correction, rescales the entropy of these modes toward a free-rotor limit while leaving their energy harmonic; because both derive from the same partition function, this is thermodynamically inconsistent. Applied consistently to energy and entropy, the correction largely cancels over the dominant intermolecular modes, whereas the entropy-only form leaves a one-sided shift that grows with system size. We test this against experiments: carboxylic acid dimerization, methanol vapor association, and sulfuric acid–ammonia nucleation in the CLOUD chamber. The entropy-only correction departs from experiment in all three cases, while the plain harmonic treatment matches the dimerization data and, supplemented by a physically grounded anharmonic term, the measured alcohol vapor properties and nucleation barriers. For such complexes, thermodynamic consistency is a prerequisite that no empirical entropy correction can replace.
papers.zh: 准谐波热化学的一致性、抵消和实验

papers.title: Sequence Model-Based Prediction and QM/MM Assessment of CYP2C19 Variant Effects on Mephenytoin Oxidation
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19) genetic variation contributes to interindividual differences in drug metabolism, yet relating sequence-level variation to substrate-specific catalytic mechanisms remains challenging. Here, we combine a generative sequence model based on the maximum entropy (MaxEnt) framework for mutation scoring, published biochemical activity data, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics adaptive steered molecular dynamics (QM/MM ASMD) calculations to examine CYP2C19 variant effects on S-mephenytoin oxidation. In the primary correlation analysis, MaxEnt scores showed nonsignificant negative rank trends with Vmax and CLint, whereas Km showed no corresponding rank association. CYP2C19*1A (WT) was used as the reference system, and CYP2C19*23 and CYP2C19*26 were selected as contrasting variants for atomistic analysis. MD simulations revealed variant-dependent changes in conformational sampling, correlated motions, and substrate positioning, but the population of geometries satisfying a predefined reactive distance-angle criterion did not reproduce the experimental activity trend. At the production pulling rate, the Seed 1 QM/MM-ASMD profiles showed a lower C12 oxygen-addition barrier for CYP2C19*23 and a higher barrier for CYP2C19*26 relative to CYP2C19*1A. Additional CYP2C19*1A and CYP2C19*23 starting configurations yielded a lower three-seed mean barrier for CYP2C19*23 at that pulling rate, although the barrier ranges overlapped and starting-configuration dependence was appreciable, and a slower-pulling control showed substantial rate sensitivity. The sampled NIH-shift profiles exhibited apparent low barriers in all three systems; however, substantial discrepancies between partition-level nonequilibrium-work estimators precluded establishing quantitatively converged CV2 barrier magnitudes. Thus, the calculations support qualitative differences among the sampled reaction profiles but do not quantitatively reproduce the magnitude of the experimental kinetic differences. The combined sequence, MD, and QM/MM workflow provides a framework for prioritizing variants and developing substrate-specific mechanistic hypotheses while making the sampling limitations explicit.
papers.zh: 基于序列模型的预测以及QM/MM对CYP2C19变异对美非妥英氧化作用影响的评估

papers.title: An Antisymmetric Framework with Cross-Modal Information Decoupling for Predicting Missense Mutation-Induced Changes in Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Accurately predicting changes in protein–ligand binding affinity induced by missense mutations is important for understanding disease mechanisms, identifying drug resistance mutations, and supporting precision medicine. However, existing computational methods often directly integrate protein sequence and structure information, which may introduce background information, structural uncertainty, and redundant cross-modal information, limiting the identification of transferable mutation-related features. In addition, most existing approaches do not explicitly enforce the thermodynamic consistency of binding free energy changes upon mutation reversal. Here, we present MutBindPred, a cross-modal deep learning framework for predicting missense mutation-induced changes in protein–ligand binding affinity. MutBindPred jointly models wild-type and mutant protein–ligand complexes and introduces a cross-modal information decoupling module to separate modality-shared background information from modality-specific mutation-related signals. The framework further captures directional differences between wild-type and mutant states and incorporates an antisymmetric constraint to improve the thermodynamic consistency of predicted ΔΔG values. Under rigorous protein and ligand cold-start settings, MutBindPred achieves improved generalization performance compared with existing baseline methods. Further analyses show that sequence-derived heterogeneous representations provide the strongest transferable predictive signals. Structural representations show limited standalone predictive utility but contribute as an auxiliary modality for guiding cross-modal representation learning. Overall, MutBindPred provides a thermodynamically consistent and generalizable framework for predicting missense mutation-induced changes in protein–ligand binding affinity.
papers.zh: 一种具有跨模态信息解耦的反对称框架，用于预测错义突变诱导的蛋白质-配体结合亲和力变化

papers.title: BFEE3: An AI-Assisted, Feature-Rich, and Streamlined Platform for Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations for protein–ligand and protein–protein complexes, based on molecular simulations, are now established as essential tools in drug design and protein engineering. Nevertheless, both geometrical and alchemical routes require multistage simulation campaigns involving input preparation, postprocessing, and bookkeeping. These complex procedures can introduce preventable errors and limit accessibility for nonexpert practitioners. Therefore, there is a clear need for user-friendly and automated software environments to address these challenges. The Binding Free Energy Estimator (BFEE) is one such tool that has been widely adopted for estimating binding free energies. In this work, we present BFEE3, a release that delivers two major advances. First, it integrates an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant that enables the configuration of binding free energy protocols through natural language and provides on-demand explanations of methodological differences and the roles of individual options. Second, it incorporates recently developed protein–ligand ABFE protocols based on the double-decoupling method (DDM), including lucid DDM (LDDM) and well-tempered metadynamics-λ adaptive biasing force-accelerated DDM (WTM-λABF-DDM). Additional enhancements include support for protein–protein ABFE calculations, GROMACS compatibility for geometrical protein–ligand workflows, one-click simulation setup, and other usability improvements. We demonstrate the main advances of BFEE3 on three representative protein–ligand systems, focusing on natural-language-driven setup, automated input generation, postprocessing, and convergence analysis. We anticipate the use of BFEE3 by both expert and nonexpert users across physical chemistry, biochemistry, and medicinal chemistry.
papers.zh: BFEE3：一个基于AI、功能丰富且流程简化的平台，用于计算绝对结合自由能

papers.title: Structural Insights into the Coaggregation Mechanism of TTR and TDP
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: The self-aggregation of TTR and TDP proteins is closely associated with the treatment of TDP-43 proteinopathies. Recent experimental evidence suggests that TTR and TDP-43 can coaggregate in the cytoplasm of Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) patients and disease models. However, their coaggregation molecular mechanisms are unknown. Herein, we investigated the conformational ensembles of TTR, TDP, and TTR-TDP systems, respectively, employing all-atom replica exchange molecular dynamics (REMD), molecular dynamics (MD), and coarse grain (CG) MD simulation methods. Analyses reveal that TTR-TDP heterohexamer can assemble into closed/open β-barrel structures, but TTR/TDP homohexamer can form bilayer structures, implying the distinct coaggregation property of the TTR-TDP heterohexamer. Compared to TTR/TDP systems, the TTR-TDP system has a higher β-sheet content, longer β-strands and larger β-sheets, suggesting the stronger coaggregation ability of the TTR-TDP heterohexamer. Further analyses reveal that the hydrophobic interactions play the pivotal role in driving the coaggregation of TTR and TDP. These findings may provide a deeper understanding of the pathogenesis of related amyloid diseases and prove the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
papers.zh: 对TTR和TDP共聚集机制的结构性见解

papers.title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR–FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.
papers.zh: 膜脂质组成和不对称性调节模型两亲性肽MAP的易位与渗漏

papers.title: In Silico Design of Dimerization Interfaces in Drosophila melanogaster Glutathione Transferase
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Understanding the molecular determinants of protein–protein interface stability remains a central challenge for the rational engineering of oligomeric enzymes. Here, the glutathione transferase GSTE3 from Drosophila melanogaster is used as a model system to decipher the factors governing dimer stability through an integrated structural, computational, and experimental approach. The X–ray crystal structure reveals a canonical homodimeric organization with a conserved Epsilon-class dimerization motif at the subunit interface. Molecular dynamics simulations combined with inter-residue contact network analysis provide a quantitative description of the interface, identifying persistent and transient interactions that contribute to dimer stability. Building on this framework, sequence-space exploration by Monte Carlo simulations is employed to design the dimerization interface and enhance stability. Distinct modeling strategies, differing in mutation schemes and energy evaluation methods, yield multiple classes of variants with diverse interfacial properties. Their stability and interaction patterns are further assessed using molecular dynamics simulations, enabling comparative analysis of structural robustness and contact network organization. Selected variants are subsequently produced in vitro to evaluate their experimental feasibility. Altogether, this study establishes a multiscale framework for the rational engineering of protein–protein interfaces and highlights both the potential and limitations of sequence–based optimization strategies for stabilizing enzyme dimers.

papers.title: Strain Induced Optoelectronic, Thermal, and Photocatalytic Activity of the Double Perovskite Oxide Sr 2 InOsO 6 With Os‐5d Transition Metal Oxides for Spintronic Devices: A GGA and GGA + mBJ First‐Principles Comparative Analysis
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: The increasing global energy demand and the inherent nature of conventional electronic devices and power conversion systems point to the need for the development of advanced energy materials with a clear focus on sustainability. In this work we examine the structural, electronic, optical, thermal and photocatalytic properties of double perovskite oxide Sr 2 InOsO 6 strongly correlated Os‐5d electrons using the GGA, GGA+mBJ, GGA+U, GGA+U+mBJ correlation method with and without spin orbital coupling (SOC) and applying strain engineering these are implemented within DFT based WIEN2K code. GGA without SOC show metallic or semiconducting behavior underestimate band gap 0.24–0 eV with biaxial strain −1%, 5%. GGA+mBJ show semiconductor behavior band gap 2.31–1.38 eV with biaxial strain 1%, −5%. Exchange interactions in the Os‐5d orbitals, indicating intrinsic magnetic ordering in Sr 2 InOsO 6 . Additionally optical and transport properties including dielectric function, refractive index, absorption coefficient, extinction coefficient, reflectivity, electrical conductivity, Seebeck coefficient, power factor, specific heat capacity, thermal conductivity have been evaluated. Observing the photocatalytic properties CB −5.27 eV which is below the H + /H 2 potential −4.44 eV, Sr 2 InOsO 6 is suitable for OER photocatalyst. These results highlight Sr 2 InOsO 6 as a viable option for advanced optoelectronics, and sustainable OER Z‐scheme photocatalytic systems.

papers.title: Tuning the Thermoelectric Performance of Two‐Dimensional GeIBr via External Electric Field and Layer Number: A First‐Principles Study
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: Thermoelectric materials with high energy conversion efficiency are of considerable interest for addressing the energy crisis and environmental issues. In this work, first‐principles calculations were performed to systematically investigate the effects of an external electric field and variation in layer number on the electronic structure and thermoelectric performance of the GeIBr monolayer. GeIBr is identified as an indirect‐band‐gap semiconductor with a band gap of 2.15 eV, and its mechanics and dynamical stabilities are confirmed by the elastic constant and phonon spectrum calculations. The external electric field has only a limited influence on the band gap. A weak electric field of 0.3 V/Å induces little change in the thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ), whereas a strong electric field of 0.6 V/Å significantly enhances the thermoelectric performance, increasing the ZT value from 2.06 to 5.52 at 900 K. Moreover, increasing the layer number reduces the band gap to 1.83 eV. Although the bilayer structure lowers the ZT value of the n ‐type system, it markedly enhances the thermoelectric performance of the p ‐type system, with the ZT value increasing from 2.06 to 3.60 at 900 K. These findings demonstrate that GeIBr is a promising thermoelectric material, whose thermoelectric performance can be effectively improved by external electric‐field tuning and changes in layer number.

papers.title: Curvature‐Induced Kinetic Trapping in Chemical Reactions
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: Crossing an activation energy barrier in a chemical reaction needs time because enough kinetic energy needs to redistribute into the barrier‐crossing mode. Kinetic energy redistribution is also needed to get across regions with strong reaction path curvature. This latter fact is frequently overlooked, possibly because barriers and curvature peaks often coincide, and curvature is invisible in the usual, pseudo‐one‐dimensional reaction energy profiles. For a set of related stepwise Diels–Alder reactions, we examine reaction paths, energy profiles and molecular dynamics trajectories, demonstrating three different cases: (1) One with a traditional IUPAC‐conforming potential energy intermediate, in which the surrounding energy barriers coincide with curvature peaks; (2) another case in which the second C–C bond closure is associated with small curvature and no clearly visible energy barrier, accordingly the dynamics towards full ring closure is comparatively fast; and (3) a final case also without an energy barrier for the second C–C bond closure but with a large curvature peak there, leading to exceptionally long kinetic trapping between the two C–C bond formations in the downhill‐energy region. Hence, we advocate for calculating reaction path curvature as simple add‐on to reaction paths, to identify cases warranting a full molecular dynamics study. Besides reaction path curvature, further features are analyzed that contribute to dynamic delays, opening up unconventional reaction control possibilities.

papers.title: T-pentagraphene: A New Carbon Network with Enriched Properties
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The discovery of novel two-dimensional (2D) semiconducting carbon networks is crucial for advancing next-generation all-carbon electronics. We are proposing a novel two-dimensional semiconducting carbon allotrope, termed as T-pentagraphene, which may be consider as a blend of pentagraphene and T-graphene. This structure is energetically more favorable than other graphyne family members, including experimentally synthesized graphyne and graphdiyne monolayers. Density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations confirm that this new carbon allotrope is dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable; capable of withstanding temperatures up to 2000 K. T-pentagraphene exhibits an intrinsic semiconducting nature, band gap as large as 3.07 eV, close to TTH-carbon (3.23 eV), penta-graphene (3.25 eV), tetrahexcarbon (3.70 eV), TO-C10 (3.97 eV). Additionally, it demonstrates an ultrahigh hole carrier mobility of 1.619 × 105 cm2·V–1·s–1 (HSE06) and outstanding optical properties, covering entire the UV region. Due its ultrahigh hole carrier mobility alongside superior optical performance, makes T-pentagraphene a promising candidate for next-generation electronics and optoelectronic devices. We also investigate the mechanical properties of T-pentagraphene, including its Young’s modulus, in-plane stiffness, Poisson’s ratio, bulk modulus, and shear stiffness under applied mechanical strain. Owing to its exceptional multifunctional properties including electronic, optical and mechanical, T-pentagraphene suggest its strong potential for influencing various scientific and nanotechnology applications.

papers.title: Au8 Kernel Packing and Ring Shell Contact Redistribution in Thiolate and Selenolate Au24 Nanoclusters
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The thiolate/selenolate pair [Au25(XR)18]− (X = S or Se) provides a useful reference for ligand substitution around a comparatively compact Au13-centered framework because the two derivatives retain closely related structures. Here, density functional theory calculations and reciprocal methyl models with S/Se exchange are used to examine how local geometry controlled by S or Se is accommodated by alternative Au24X20 kernel-shell topologies. The experimentally derived Au24(SR)20-A* framework contains a face-to-face Au4/Au4 Au8 kernel wrapped by four Au6(SR)5 rings, whereas the experimentally derived Au24(SeR)20-B* framework adopts a perpendicular-edge Au8 kernel and interlocked Au5(SeR)4/Au7(SeR)6 rings. Reciprocal ligand-exchange models separate the direct structural response to S/Se substitution within a fixed topology from that associated with A/B topology reorganization. Within either topology, S-to-Se replacement produces only modest changes in the kernel–motif d3 and inter-ring d5 Au···Au contacts. In contrast, A-to-B topology reorganization changes the Au8 kernel from face-to-face to perpendicular-edge Au4/Au4 packing and produces a substantially larger shortening of d5. This structural separation is retained across PBE-D3, PBE0-D3, and TPSS-D3 optimized structures, for which fixed-topology S-to-Se replacement changes d5 by only 0.01–0.05 Å whereas A-to-B topology reorganization shortens d5 by 0.24–0.32 Å. Complementary Au(I) dimer scans show that replacing S by Se shifts the local Au(I)···Au(I) potential toward a shorter minimum-energy separation and a deeper interaction well under a common coordination model. Together, these results support a structural picture in which S/Se identity shifts the local interaction landscape, while Au8 packing and the ring shell determine how this preference appears across the Au24X20 framework.

papers.title: Endohedral Sodium in NaPb12 Clusters: Charge-State-Dependent Stabilization and Electron Counting
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Endohedral plumbaspherenes are a growing family of closo lead cages whose known members are typically characterized by transition-metal guests. Herein, we examine sodium as an s-block guest in a Pb12 cage and evaluate how its endohedral stabilization depends on cluster charge. Global structure searches, DFT refinements, and correlated single-point calculations reveal a clear charge-dependent structural response across the NaPb12 series, whereas the neutral charge state favors a crown-like structure, the monoanion selectively stabilizes an endohedral [Na@Pb12]− configuration, and the dianion favors an exohedral sodium arrangement. This preference is consistent with a Wade–Mingos picture in which the Na valence electron contributes to the Pb12 skeletal framework, making the monoanion the 26-electron closo member of the series in a similar fashion to Ca@Pb12. QTAIM and spin-density analyses show distinct charge accommodation across the three charge states, while continuous shape measures and magnetic-response calculations characterize the structural and aromatic response of the Pb12 framework. These results identify [Na@Pb12]− as a charge-state-selected endohedral sodium plumbaspherene, and they show that sodium can participate directly in skeletal electron counting without adopting transition-metal-like bonding. Overall, charge-state control emerges as a simple strategy for tuning guest location and electron counting in endohedral main-group clusters.

papers.title: Alchemical Transfer Free Energy Perturbation Simulations Reveal Entropic Mechanism Governing the Binding of a Charged Peptide to a Protein Target
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We combined alchemical transfer free energy perturbation (FEP) and replica exchange with solute tempering (REST) molecular dynamics to probe the energetics of the binding of a charged peptide to a protein target. For this purpose, we have selected the coreNLS peptide KKPKKE, the conserved fragment from the nuclear localization signal (NLS) sequence in viral capsid protein binding to nuclear transporter importin-α (impα). This peptide binds to impα, natively forming a specific pose similar to that resolved experimentally. The two main outcomes of our work are as follows. First, we further develop the FEP methodology. Alchemical transfer is a rarely used version of FEP, in which an unbound peptide is gradually decoupled, while the bound peptide is coupled. Because the net charge of the system remains unchanged, no charge-related corrections within FEP are necessary. Additionally, our FEP protocol utilizes a “laissez faire” soft-walled flat-bottom spherical restraint, which does not affect a ligand as long as it occupies the major NLS binding site in impα. We showed that combining FEP with REST molecular dynamics affords exhaustive sampling of the binding process and reduces the free energy error down to 0.4 kcal/mol. Second, we found that the coreNLS binds impα with moderate affinity of ΔGb0 = −4.6 kcal/mol. We analyzed the factors contributing to binding energetics. Direct interactions between the peptide and impα favor binding and are likely to be responsible for largely native binding pose of the coreNLS. These direct binding interactions are supplemented by the gains in water–water, ion–ion, and water–ion interactions. Both, direct and indirect, enthalpic gains are about equally important, but cannot compete with severe enthalpic losses stemming from the expulsion of water and ions from the binding interface. As a result, the net binding enthalpy is unfavorable. The factor, which ultimately “saves” coreNLS binding to impα, is a strong entropic gain occurring upon water and ion release from the binding interface. Based on our investigation, we classify the mechanism governing coreNLS binding to impα as entropic. Our isothermal titration calorimetry measurements confirm the estimates of ΔGb0 provided by FEP. By connecting with our prior studies and other reports, we propose that such binding mechanism may be applicable to other charged peptides reflecting complex interplay between binding enthalpy and entropy. Interestingly, our data suggest that the ligands binding diffusively or by adopting specific poses may utilize an entropic binding mechanism.

papers.title: Property-Defining Feature Extraction in Porous Crystalline Materials Using Attention-Guided Cooperative Game Theory
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Porous crystalline materials assembled from molecular building blocks offer vast potential across applications such as gas storage, separation, and catalysis, yet their structural tunability creates an expansive design space that demands the systematic identification of their property-defining features. To help researchers identify these features rapidly and inform next generation design, we introduce the Explainable Crystal Transformer (ExCT); an attention-guided cooperative game-theoretic workflow for extracting property-defining structural features in porous crystalline materials by combining attention-based representation learning, Shapley-style attribution, and local surrogate-fidelity screening. Designed for broader use across reticular frameworks, ExCT is demonstrated here with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as a representative case study of H2, CH4, and CO2 adsorption: cooperative game-theoretic attributions highlight chemically plausible local regions in selected hypothetical MOFs and qualitatively correspond to reported adsorption environments in experimentally studied cases, whereas attention identifies broader property-associated regions. Strict held-out surrogate-fidelity screening retains only a subset of high-fidelity explanations, more frequently for H2 than CH4 and less frequently for CO2.

papers.title: Distinct Plasmonic and Electronically Mediated Pathways for Vibrational Excitation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Understanding how plasmonic energy is transferred into molecular vibrations at metal–molecule interfaces is essential for controlling plasmon-driven chemistry and surface-enhanced spectroscopies. However, distinguishing vibrational excitation mediated by electronic transitions and vibronic coupling (VC) from plasmon-enhanced Raman vibrational pumping (PERVP) remains challenging because both mechanisms generate nonequilibrium vibrational populations. Here, we combine cryogenic surface-enhanced Raman scattering with controlled surface chemistry to investigate these competing excitation pathways using thionine adsorbed on gold nanostructures. Citrate-stabilized gold nanoparticles exhibit two distinct excitation regimes. The first is characterized by unusually intense anti-Stokes scattering despite weak Stokes emission, with laser-power dependences inconsistent with conventional vibrational pumping. This behavior is attributed to VC facilitated by molecular adsorption geometries that favor metal–molecule electronic coupling and transient charge transfer. The second regime exhibits strong Stokes scattering and superlinear anti-Stokes intensity, consistent with PERVP and molecular optomechanics. In contrast, bromide-containing gold nanorods exhibit a single excitation regime with laser-power dependences closely matching theoretical predictions for PERVP, suggesting preferential molecular dipole alignment with the localized plasmonic field. At cryogenic temperatures, pronounced anti-Stokes blinking and the transient activation of weak or Raman-inactive vibrational modes further reveal dynamic interfacial restructuring associated with bromide adsorption. These findings demonstrate how molecular orientation, interfacial electronic coupling, and surface chemistry influence the dominant vibrational excitation pathway, providing a framework for controlling plasmonic energy transfer at metal–molecule interfaces.

papers.title: Divergent Ultrafast Carrier-Density and Photoconductivity Dynamics in Antimony-Doped Halide Perovskite Thin Films
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Heterovalent ion substitution can tune the optoelectronic properties of metal halide perovskites, but its impact on charge-carrier recombination and transport remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate antimony incorporation in methylammonium lead iodide (MAPI) thin films using complementary ultrafast spectroscopy techniques. Optical absorption shows that the bandgap remains approximately 1.61 eV across substitution levels up to 10%, whereas photoluminescence and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveal increasing nonradiative recombination rates with increasing antimony content. Optical pump–terahertz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy further uncovers fluence-dependent dynamics distinct from TA that are absent in pristine MAPI. After considering alternative mechanisms, we interpret this behavior as consistent with partially heterogeneous transport, in which Sb3+ incorporation may introduce low-mobility, defect-rich regions within a higher-mobility crystalline network. Thus, heterovalent substitution can introduce hidden transport losses without changing optical bandgap, highlighting the importance of mobility-sensitive measurements to probe doped perovskite films.

papers.title: Electron-Induced Formation of C 2 on Si(100) from Acetylene and Ethylene
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Hydrogen Desorption Lithography on Si(100) demonstrates the ability of the Scanning Tunneling Microscope (STM) to create functional atomic-scale structures and devices. The dehydrogenation of adsorbed molecules represents a potential complementary technique that has received little attention. For example, formation of C2 could introduce local strain or act as a center for subsequent reactions and would inform positionally controlled mechanosynthesis, an approach with vast potential in surface patterning and functionalization. Here, we studied the electron-induced dehydrogenation of acetylene and ethylene on Si(100) at 4 K using STM. Excitation of acetylene at ≥+3.2 V induces configurational switching, including to a new sublayer-bonded geometry previously predicted to be an adsorption precursor, as well as migration and desorption. Excitation also induces dehydrogenation to C2. Switching between three observed C2 configurations can be induced by excitation at ≥+4.2 V. Simulations using density functional theory reproduced the experimental images based on the choice of functional, dimer-buckling averaging, and the inclusion of diffuse basis functions. In addition, dehydrogenation could be induced using field-emitted electrons on a scale ranging from a single molecule to a radius of >10 nm. These observations highlight the potential of carbon dehydrogenation as an additional tool in Atomically Precise Fabrication (APF).

papers.title: Interplay of Janus Polarization and Interfacial Electric Fields Governing Carrier Dynamics in MoS2/MoSSe Heterostructures
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: It is crucial to understand the role of polarization and the built-in electric field in heterostructures of two-dimensional materials, as these factors significantly affect carrier dynamics, interfacial properties, and device performance. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the electronic structure and excited-state carrier dynamics of MoS2/MoSSe heterostructures. We show that the interplay between the intrinsic polarization of Janus MoSSe and the interface-induced electric field strongly modulates interlayer charge transfer. This dual-field coupling drives a transition between type-I and type-II band alignments and switches the dominant carrier relaxation pathways from intralayer recombination to interlayer charge separation. Carrier relaxation is further governed by the interplay between nonadiabatic coupling and phonon-assisted transitions. These results identify polarity reversal as an effective strategy for tuning charge-transfer pathways and excited-state dynamics in van der Waals heterostructures, and provide guidance for designing two-dimensional optoelectronic and photocatalytic materials.

papers.title: Temperature Driven Evolution of Alumina Nanowhiskers in Aluminum Intercalated Layered Graphene Oxide
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Layered graphene oxide (GO) has attracted considerable attention for a wide range of applications, from optoelectronic devices to solar cells, where performance can be significantly enhanced through elemental intercalation. In this work, we demonstrate the temperature-dependent hydrothermal growth of Al-intercalated GO (Al@GO), achieved through the chemical reaction of GO and aluminum acetylacetonate, resulting the formation of Al–O–C bonds, as confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction measurements reveal the transformation of GO to reduced GO (rGO) at 180 °C, while scanning electron microscopy indicates the formation of layered GO with tortuous porous morphology. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy, along with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, further confirms the discrete evolution of alumina nanowhiskers, predominantly in the γ-phase, as evidenced by selected area electron diffraction. Density functional theory calculations support the formation of Al–O–C bonds in Al@GO, while Al intercalation induces an indirect-to-direct bandgap transition in GO.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanism of Proline-Mediated Regulation of Graphene–Bacterial Membrane Interactions: A Balance between Dispersion Stabilization and Membrane Disruption
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Graphene nanosheets have attracted considerable attention as antibacterial nanomaterials due to their ability to directly damage bacterial membranes. However, the poor dispersion of graphene in aqueous environments limits its practical applications. Recently, natural amino acids [Mao, T.; et al.Nature2025, 645, 915–921].have been proposed as biocompatible stabilizers for nanomaterials. Nevertheless, how amino acid concentration affects graphene-membrane interactions remains unclear. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the regulation of monomeric proline on graphene insertion into bacterial membranes. Three systems containing 0, 1, and 2 M proline were constructed to reveal the influence of proline on graphene transport behavior, membrane perturbation, and molecular interactions. The results show that graphene can spontaneously insert into bacterial membranes under all investigated conditions, indicating that proline cannot completely eliminate graphene-membrane interactions. However, introducing proline significantly delays graphene penetration by enhancing graphene stabilization in the aqueous environment. The average insertion time increases from 22.3 ± 6.8 ns without proline to 95.3 ± 22.4 ns and 102.7 ± 29.1 ns under 2 and 1 M proline conditions, respectively. After insertion, graphene still induces membrane deformation, alters lipid ordering, and changes lipid mobility, suggesting that its membrane-disruptive activity is maintained. Energetic analyses reveal that the regulation mechanism originates from the competition between graphene-proline stabilization and graphene-membrane attraction. Proline strengthens graphene interactions with surrounding solution molecules, while graphene-lipid interactions remain sufficiently strong to drive membrane insertion. These findings provide molecular insights into the balance between graphene stabilization and antibacterial activity and offer guidance for designing amino acid-assisted graphene-based antibacterial materials.

papers.title: Deciphering the Role of Glycine Betaine in Modulating the Kinetics and Thermodynamics of Iron-Binding and Release by Human Serum Transferrin at Physiological, Endosomal, and Acidic pH Levels
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Human serum transferrin (hSTf) reversibly binds to Fe3+ ions and delivers them to cells in the presence of physiological anions (chloride, ATP, citrate). In humans, glycine betaine (GB) serves as a metabolic methyl donor in the liver. As the liver is the primary site of hSTf synthesis, GB’s influence on hSTf is crucial for maintaining the protein’s structural integrity and regulating iron metabolism. This study deciphers how GB affects the kinetics and thermodynamics of iron binding and release by hSTf, both in the absence and in the presence of chloride anions, at physiological pH 7.4, endosomal pH 5.5, and acidic pH levels below 5.0. Analysis of the effects of GB on equilibrium and kinetic parameters for iron release of hSTf and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of hSTf with GB yielded significant results: (i) at pH 7.4 and 5.5, the experimental and MD simulation studies suggest that the preferential exclusion of GB from the protein enhances the stability of the Fe3+-hSTf complex in diferric-hSTf (Fe2hSTf); (ii) at pH 7.4 and 5.5, the enthalpic stabilization effects of GB retard the rate of iron release from monoferric-N-lobe of Fe2hSTf (FeNhSTf); (iii) at acidic pH (<5), the preferential binding of GB to Fe2hSTf reduces the stability of the Fe3+-hSTf complex and accelerates the rate of iron release from Fe2hSTf; (iv) GB reduces the conformational flexibility and backbone fluctuation to stabilize Fe2hSTf conformation at pH 7.4 and 5.5, while it induces conformational changes that lead to higher protein fluctuations and flexibility at pH 4.5; (v) under acidic pH conditions (<5), nonsynergistic chloride anion reduces the stability of the Fe3+-hSTf complex, and the addition of GB exhibits an additive impact on chloride effect to reduce the stability of the Fe3+-hSTf complex in Fe2hSTf. Thermodynamic analysis of isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) profiles revealed that GB enhances the binding affinity of Fe3+ to apo-hSTf at physiological pH 7.4. Additionally, the investigation of GB’s effects on the average fluorescence lifetime of Fe2hSTf (τavg) at pH 7.4 and pH 5.5 reveals that GB forms ground-state interactions with Fe2hSTf at physiological pH 7.4 while engaging in excited-state interactions at endosomal pH 5.5.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Contacts of Lipases at PEGMA/SBMA Brush Interfaces
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Enzyme performance on polymer brush supports depends on brush composition, and the optimum composition differs by enzyme. The design rules governing this specificity have been difficult to resolve due to the complexity of the enzyme’s surface chemistry. In particular, it remains unclear which enzyme residues contact the interface and how those contacts change with the chemical composition of the surface. We used atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) to simulate four lipases across a five-point composition series of poly(ethylene glycol) methacrylate (PEGMA) and zwitterionic sulfobetaine methacrylate (SBMA) brushes. From pure PEGMA to pure SBMA, median residue contacts decrease by 53–63% for all four enzymes, and the polar fraction of contacting residues is higher on pure SBMA than on pure PEGMA. At each enzyme’s experimentally optimal composition, the within-enzyme fits suggest that median contacts increase and polar fraction decreases with enzyme surface solvation free energy per area, consistent with the experimental hydrophobic intensity framework but requiring validation with additional enzymes. The composition trends keep their direction when replica 1, 2, or 3 is left out of every composition, and enzyme size and shape differ little between bound and not-bound frames. These simulations provide residue-level interfacial detail that is difficult to obtain experimentally and offer a starting point for physics-based design of polymer brush supports.

papers.title: Site-Dependent Structural Effects of R1 Spin Labeling in an Aβ42 Protofilament Characterized by Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Site-directed spin labeling coupled with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) is used to characterize structural features in amyloid fibrils, but whether the nitroxide spin label R1 perturbs the structure it reports remains unclear. Molecular dynamics simulations compared wild-type Aβ42 with ten R1-labeled variants in a five-layer protofilament derived from the type I human-brain fibril structure. We quantified nitroxide proximity, regional interlayer packing, backbone hydrogen bonding, R1–protein contacts, and R1 side-chain rotamer sampling. Simulated nitroxide contacts reproduced the experimental distinction between sites with strong and weak spin–spin interactions, although some sites deviated from the trend. Regional interlayer organization and backbone hydrogen bonding were preserved relative to wild-type. However, structural responses were site-dependent and sometimes extended beyond the labeling site. The 32R1 system produced the largest rearrangement of the C-terminal tail. Comparison with the corresponding unlabeled cysteine control showed smaller perturbation, indicating that the response at position 32 arose primarily from the R1 label rather than the cysteine substitution itself. Thus, R1 generally preserved the protofilament architecture and reflected the local packing environment while producing label-specific structural adjustments. These results support R1 as a reporter of local packing in Aβ42 fibrils and demonstrate the value of site-resolved comparisons for identifying label-induced effects.

papers.title: Evaluation of Homogeneous Arrhenius Reaction Kinetics for Energetic Materials in the High Explosive Initiation Time Experiment
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The Arrhenius kinetics for the onset of exothermic reactions in energetic materials control many facets of their handling safety and performance. We report new measurements of the kinetics of thermal explosion at temperatures up to 700 K for the secondary explosives pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN), cyclotetramethylene tetranitramine (HMX), and hexanitrohexaazaisowurtzitane (CL-20). These data are obtained from the high explosive initiation time (HEIT) experiment, which rapidly heats small samples confined in hollow steel needles by the discharge of a high voltage fireset. The ignition and growth of deflagrations in the HEIT experiment are analyzed theoretically, which identify a high temperature regime that is associated with a small effective activation energy where the time-to-explosion is controlled by the deflagration velocity, and a low temperature regime with a large activation energy that is controlled by the induction time for the onset of reactions at the interface with the hot needle. Our theoretical model shows why the reaction rates obtained in the low temperature regime are consistent with predictions from independent reactive molecular dynamics simulations and experimental measurements for uniformly heated samples, despite the very inhomogeneous temperature profiles generated in the HEIT experiment prior to ignition. Since the HEIT experiment provides time-to-explosion data that is relevant to ignition in accident scenarios in the temperature interval between existing methods, including the one-dimensional time-to-explosion tests and reactive molecular dynamics simulations, we have derived and report improved estimates for the effective single-step Arrhenius kinetics of PETN, CL-20, and HMX.

papers.title: Nucleophilicity from a Conceptual DFT Viewpoint: A Four-State Ensemble-Inspired Model
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: By taking advantage of the fundamental convexity of the exact energy as a function of the number of electrons, we extrapolate the straight-line segments connecting the N and N + 1 states and N – 2 and N – 1 states in a four-state ensemble-inspired model. These segments intersect at a unique point that determines a fractional charge transfer condition,ΔNint−=−λ, which naturally contemplates the reactivity of the cation and neutral forms in terms of their hardness. The energy evaluated at the intersection point, Ni, and the energy evaluated at −λ in the ensemble segment,Nl, give rise to our proposed descriptors that contribute to the electronic panorama of the donation process and describe the reactivity of a set of molecules in specific conditions. The performance of the indicators as nucleophilic indices was evaluated in five chemical reactions: the oxidation of metals, the proton affinity of amines, the stability of coordinated metals that follow the Irving–Williams series, and the kinetic substitution of indoles and alkenes. The nucleophilicity indices proposed are an important complement to the electrophilicity index because they are based on a different response that, although they may lead to similar results with respect to the correlation with a given property, they may be used to recognize dominant aspects of the electronic structure in a chemical interaction. The results obtained support their use as complementary descriptors of the intrinsic electronic contribution to nucleophilic reactivity within specified reaction families.

papers.title: Exploring Chemical Concepts and Reactivity from Conceptual Density Functional Theory in Excited States via the ΔSCF Approach
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Along with the recent development of the ΔSCF approach for excited state electronic structure description using density functional theory (DFT), we extend and develop conceptual density functional theory (CDFT) for evaluating chemical concepts and reactivity descriptors for both ground and excited states. Thereby, the fundamental energy functionalEJ[{npσ},v(r)] based on the generalized adiabatic connection Kohn–Sham (GAC-KS) theorem is introduced. Offering a straightforward interpretation of the reactivity of excited states analogous to that of the ground state. In this framework, ground state CDFT naturally emerges as a special case when the derivative with respect to the number of electrons is taken at the frontier orbital occupation, i.e., dN = dnf. Starting from the ground state system, the spin-polarized analytical linear response function (LRF) is tested to examine the atomic shell structure for alkali atoms as well as the reactive region upon electron addition and removal processes using the Fukui kernel. The behavior of the LRF is then illustrated for ground, singly excited, and doubly excited states of a set of molecular systems, revealing the expected trends and nature of bond polarizability and bonding character. The analytical Fukui function is also presented here for its ability to describe local electrophilicity and nucleophilicity for ground and excited states. An inverse relationship for the condensed electrophilic and nucleophilic Fukui functions is observed between the ground and excited states for a set of small molecules, including substituted benzenes. The dual descriptor obtained from the analytical Fukui function via a finite difference approximation is applied to interpret the Woodward–Hoffmann (WH) rules for pericyclic reactions. For both thermally driven and photoinduced ring cyclization processes at the ground and excited states, respectively, the dual descriptor successfully translates the WH rules from molecular orbital context into a purely density-based language.

papers.title: A Computational Framework for the Determination of the Binding Affinity of Peripheral Proteins to Homogeneous Membranes
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Peripheral membrane-binding proteins (PMPs) are essential to immunological and neurological processes, and disruptions in their membrane interactions are implicated in cancer, neurodegeneration, and autoimmune diseases. Their functional diversity arises from the wide range of mechanisms by which they associate with lipid surfaces, motivating atomistic computational frameworks capable of quantifying binding energetics. We present such a methodology and demonstrate it using Bacillus thuringiensis phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C (BtPI–PLC), a 296-residue virulence factor that preferentially associates with phosphatidylcholine (PC) membranes. Experimental studies report dissociation constants near 24 μM for wild-type BtPI–PLC binding to PC vesicles, corresponding to a standard free energy of −6.6 kcal/mol. BtPI–PLC associates with membranes through cation−π interactions involving Y88 and Y246, hydrophobic contacts from helix B, and other noncovalent interactions, making comprehensive sampling challenging. Here, we present a statistical mechanical geometrical route formulation based on the potential of mean force for the quantitative characterization of dilute PMP binding to homogeneous membranes. Using enhanced sampling via well-tempered metadynamics and extended adaptive biasing force, we obtain a computational estimate of the standard binding free energy, −6.2 ± 0.3 kcal/mol, consistent with experimental estimates for BtPI–PLC membrane association.

papers.title: MERIT: Mechanism-Driven Model Predicts Drug Outcomes and Nominates Indications for Failed Drugs
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Drug development depends on efficacy and safety, but many trial-outcome prediction models incorporate trial design, prior development history, or compound identity, enabling compound memorization and inflating apparent performance. We developed MEchanism-Resolved Inference of Trial outcomes (MERIT), a model that predicts trial outcomes from molecular and disease features without using information on similar-compound success. MERIT integrates the disease and drug of interest with large-scale drug–protein, protein–metabolite, and immune interaction maps to link a drug’s intended and potential off-target effects to tissue-specific efficacy and safety. Across 753 small-molecule drugs and 3,133 trials, MERIT achieved an overall AUROC of 0.770 (0.765 for efficacy and 0.784 for safety) under structure-holdout evaluation, outperforming two published methods retrained on the same trials and folds. Scored by a mechanism-fit profiling, MERIT ranked the approved indication above the failed one for 83% (50 of 60) of a preselected set of 60 cohort compounds that failed one indication but are approved for another. Finally, we registered locked, outcome-blind predictions for 55 drug-indication pairs in ongoing phase III trials for prospective evaluation.
