papers.title: Correlation-Driven Orbital Optimization in One-Dimensional Hubbard Systems
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The flexibility afforded by molecular orbitals plays a central role in the development of quantum-chemical methods. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure of delocalized half-filled one-dimensional symmetric AA and asymmetric AB systems described by the Hubbard Hamiltonian through a bottom-up strategy designed to assess the performance of a two-step procedure. The proposed framework aims at constructing a correlated wave function, thereby providing a complementary perspective to conventional band-structure descriptions. In a first step, Rayleigh–Schrödinger perturbation theory is applied to a zeroth-order local valence-bond ground state in order to incorporate charge-transfer configurations and account for short-range delocalization effects. In a second step, the resulting second-order energy is minimized with respect to orbital rotations. Starting from the canonical molecular orbitals obtained from the one-electron part of the Hubbard Hamiltonian, the method is benchmarked against exact cluster calculations for both symmetric AA and asymmetric AB systems. Although the second-order energy correction in symmetric systems is insensitive to the choice of the molecular orbitals, electron–electron interactions in asymmetric systems drive departures from the canonical orbital representation, emphasizing the role of local electronic correlations in determining the optimal orbital framework. Beyond its quantitative performance, the present approach complements the conventional Bloch-function picture and offers a chemically intuitive interpretation for extended systems.

papers.title: Formation, Spatial Distribution, and Dynamics of Lewis and Brønsted Acid Sites on α-MoO3(010): A Density Functional Theory Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The catalytic performance of α-MoO3 in lignin hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) depends on Lewis (oxygen vacancy) and Brønsted (hydroxyl) acid sites generated during H2 reduction. We present a density functional theory study of the α-MoO3(010) surface, addressing oxygen vacancy formation, hydrogen adsorption on all three surface oxygen types, coverage-dependent effects, hydrogen diffusion, and H2 dissociative adsorption. Hydrogen adsorption is thermodynamically preferred on the asymmetric bridging oxygen and kinetically reinforced by a low barrier to surface migration. Coverage-dependent calculations at HDO-relevant temperatures reveal that oxygen vacancies promote Brønsted site formation. H2 reduction proceeds with a substantial dissociation barrier to form an adsorbed water intermediate, branching into Lewis acid site formation via water desorption or Brønsted acid site formation via hydroxyl generation. Partial reduction of Mo6+ toward Mo5+ accompanies both vacancy creation and hydroxylation. These results provide a unified atomic-level framework connecting gas-phase reduction to a more realistic representation of the catalytically active surface.

papers.title: Counterion Ordering at Ionized Carboxylate Self-Assembled Monolayers on Au(111) and Its Influence on the Potential of Zero Charge
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The electrostatic properties of the Au(111)/self-assembled monolayer (SAM)/electrolyte interface were investigated using density functional theory combined with the effective screening medium and reference interaction site model (DFT-ESM-RISM) with explicit counterions. Calculations for deprotonated carboxyl-terminated SAMs show that Na+, K+, and Cs+ counterions localize within the SAM termination region, occupying interstitial positions between COO– groups rather than forming a diffuse layer governed by electrolyte concentration. The resulting interfacial structure can be described as a quasi-two-dimensional carboxylate–counterion ionic crystal. The calculated potential of zero charge (PZC) shifts exhibit weak dependence on bulk electrolyte concentration and are consistent with available experimental data for Na+ systems. To clarify the microscopic origin of the PZC shifts, the electrostatic potential profiles were decomposed into contributions arising from the SAM dipole, the carboxylate–counterion ionic layer, and polarized interfacial water. The analysis reveals that the water contribution dominates for Na+, whereas the ionic contribution becomes increasingly important for K+ and Cs+. The results indicate that the electrostatic response of the interface is governed primarily by local counterion–carboxylate organization within the SAM termination region and the resulting polarization of interfacial water. These findings provide a molecular-level explanation of experimentally observed PZC shifts and establish the electrostatic consequences of local counterion–carboxylate organization and the resulting polarization of interfacial water.

papers.title: Vapor Condensation on Bioinspired Cylindrical Array-Coupled Wedge Surfaces with Wettability Gradients: A Molecular Dynamics Simulation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Efficient steam condensation is pivotal for industrial applications such as thermal management and water harvesting. With the advancement of micronano fabrication, the precise regulation of droplet dynamics and efficient liquid drainage at the microscale have emerged as a key pathway to transcend the limits of traditional condensation heat transfer. Inspired by the directional liquid transport of the Nepenthes peristome, this study employs molecular dynamics simulations to establish a model of interactions between droplets and surfaces under condensation conditions. This approach investigates how coupling biomimetic copper microstructures with wettability influences autonomous droplet propulsion, surface renewal, and phase transition dynamics. This paper proposes a surface structure coupling cylindrical microarrays with wedge-shaped wettability patterns, which exhibits favorable comprehensive performance regarding nucleation and liquid drainage under the conditions investigated. Furthermore, the mechanisms by which different wedge angles influence droplet growth and the autonomous transport process toward the collection region are analyzed. It is revealed that introducing a wettability gradient within the wedge patterns significantly enhances the driving force. Finally, the regulatory effects of varying system pressures on condensation and droplet propulsion are discussed. This study elucidates the synergistic influence of structure and wettability on droplet behavior, providing a theoretical basis and structural optimization strategies for designing bioinspired surfaces for efficient condensation heat transfer and autonomous microscale droplet manipulation.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Predicting Magnetization from X-ray Diffraction of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles Using Simple Physics-Based Data Generation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Automation and high-throughput characterization and synthesis for material development are becoming increasingly common; these approaches require machine-learning (ML) tools to assess material properties, ideally based on a single measurement. Here, ML models are developed to predict magnetization from X-ray diffraction (XRD) for iron oxide nanoparticles. Our approach is to first develop a set of simulated data that links modulated XRD, based on a crystallographic information file (CIF), to a simple magnetic model to determine magnetization at a given magnetic field, thereby enabling us to train random forest (RF) and gradient boosting (GB) regression models on a large amount of simulated data. The models are validated by synthesizing iron oxide nanoparticles and measuring their crystal structure via XRD and room temperature magnetization curves. In doing so, we can fine-tune both the training hyperparameters and the optimal size of the simulated data sets used to train the models. Through this optimization, the best models can achieve an R2 greater than 0.8 across seven distinct sets of XRD and magnetization curve data sets used for tuning, for predicting the max magnetization (at 2.8 T) of the measurement. Lastly, we demonstrate reasonable predictions on the full magnetization vs magnetic field curve, showing that the RF model excels at predicting the high magnetic field values, which is key for determining the success of an iron oxide nanoparticle synthesis for applications like magnetic particle imaging (MPI), thermal magnetic particle imaging (T-MPI), and hyperthermia.

papers.title: Polymer Assembly Mediated by Attractive Crowding Agents: Good-Solvent vs Poor-Solvent Polymers
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Polymer assembly dictates the functional performance of soft materials and is fundamentally associated with intracellular liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), a ubiquitous process in living cells. Macromolecular crowding exerts dramatic regulatory effects on both assembly dynamics and condensate morphologies. Although extensive studies concerning macromolecular crowding effects have long focused on repulsive interactions, a systematic mechanistic picture describing how attractive crowders tune the structural and dynamic features of polymer assemblies and LLPS remains elusive. Herein, we construct a coarse-grained Langevin model to simulate polymer-crowder aggregation of good-solvent and poor-solvent chains by adjusting intercrowder attraction, crowder size and crowder concentration. Our results demonstrate a series of novel structural and kinetic features. Intercrowder interaction strength serves as a key switch governing condensate morphology: good-solvent polymers evolve sequentially from crowder-bridged clusters to homogeneous mixed droplets and core–shell assemblies, whereas poor-solvent chains form compact self-aggregates, cage-confined multiclusters or patchy core–shell structures. Crowders with large sizes impose dominant geometric packing restrictions, generating distinctive porous and layered condensates. Increasing crowder concentration can fully dissociate good-solvent polymer aggregates while merely breaking poor-solvent polymer clusters into small separated domains. Moreover, a prevailing three-step assembly mechanism involving nucleation, diffusion-limited lag and cluster coalescence is identified for all polymer systems. This work establishes an integrated framework interpreting the competition between crowding-mediated bridging and intrinsic assembly of poor-solvent polymers. The new insights yielded in this study enrich our understanding of intracellular condensates and provide useful guidance for functional polymer design.

papers.title: Small-Molecule-Mediated Molecular Recognition Controls Tryptophan Self-Assembly and Programs Tunable Emission
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Engineering fluorescence from natural biomolecules without covalent modification offers a sustainable route to functional optical materials, yet biomolecule-based optical materials remain relatively unexplored, and the molecular principles governing their emergent photophysics remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that small-molecule-directed self-assembly can redirect tryptophan (Trp) from uncontrolled fibrillar aggregation toward well-defined supramolecular architectures while tuning its intrinsic fluorescence through distinct molecular- and solvent-mediated pathways. Co-assembly with l-ascorbic acid (Asc, pH ∼ 3) suppresses the native Trp emission (∼350 nm) and generates a band at 470 nm (λex = 380 nm), showing a remarkable 120 nm red-shift, with a fluorescence quantum yield (ϕ) of 0.13. This process produces spherical assemblies (∼12.5 μm) through first-order kinetics, driven by π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and CH−π interactions. These stable assemblies exhibit reversible pH-responsive emission and reduced cytotoxicity compared to conventional dyes. In contrast, hydrazine (Hyd, pH 10) accelerates assembly formation by ∼2.5-fold, yielding larger spheres (∼18 μm) with emission centered at 430 nm (λex = 345 nm), exhibiting a 40 nm blue shift relative to Trp-Asc assemblies. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal distinct molecular mechanisms: Asc directly associates with Trp, whereas Hyd preferentially reorganizes the surrounding water network, indicating a predominantly solvent-controlled pathway for reorganization and association. Metadynamics further reveals that Hyd reshapes the Trp–Trp association landscape, favoring a specific geometry over tighter packing. Thus, small-molecule-mediated control over molecular recognition, solvation, and intermolecular organization can redirect uncontrolled biomolecular aggregation into defined supramolecular architectures while programming emergent fluorescence, establishing a noncovalent strategy for engineering supramolecular fluorophores from native biomolecules.

papers.title: Compressibility of Water and Organic Liquids from Monte Carlo Simulations: Support for the Lennard-Jones 12–6 Potential
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Densities of organic liquids and water have been computed at pressures from −250 atm to 10,000 atm using Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in the NPT ensemble with the OPLS and TIPnP force fields. Comparisons with experimental data show average discrepancies of ca. 1%. It is demonstrated that the fluctuation formula for compressibility from statistical mechanics yields results in close accord with the slope of the density versus pressure results from the present long MC simulations. Definitive results for the isothermal compressibility of the TIP3P, TIP4P, and TIP5P water models at 25 °C are reported as 53, 50, and 58 ± 1 in units of 10–6 atm–1, respectively, while the experimental value is 45.8. A straightforward, versatile procedure is provided for computing a fundamental property of fluids with applications for fuel science, hydraulic systems, acoustics, and force-field evaluation. The results also support the validity of the use of the Lennard-Jones 12–6 potential for describing interatomic nonbonded interactions by reproducing experimental density data through the full fluid range up to ca. 40% compressions.

papers.title: Exploring the Proton Conductivity across the C-Dots Doped Cellulose Nanocrystal Biopolymer
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Biopolymers have gained significant attention across the energy, fuel, bioelectronics, and biomedical applications owing to their intrinsic protonic conductivity. Among them, polysaccharides represent a class of low-cost and abundant biomacromolecules suitable for constructing functional biopolymers. In this work, we present a novel strategy to enhance proton conduction in biopolymer systems by integrating varying concentrations of carbon dot (C-Dot)-derived surface functional groups into a cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) biopolymer. Blue-, green-, and red-emitting C-Dots, with varying degrees of oxygen-rich surface functional groups and heterocyclic nitrogen-enriched core states, were incorporated as dopants into the CNC biopolymer. Notably, the inclusion of B-, G-, and R-C-Dots led to ∼2-, 4-, and 10-fold enhancements in protonic conductivity, respectively, compared to pristine CNC biopolymer. This approach provides an effective pathway for designing advanced self-assembled biopolymer proton-conducting materials for next-generation bioprotonic applications.

papers.title: Electroosmotic Flow Enhancement in Subnanometer Carbon Nanotubes Triggered by Water Ordering Cooperatively Induced by an Electric Field and Ion
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Ion and water transport through subnanometer carbon nanotubes (CNTs) exhibits numerous anomalies absent in bulk solutions, yet the interplay among the confined water structure, external electric fields, and ion transport remains poorly understood. Here, we use systematic nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to study single-file water confined in a CNT of radius 0.37 nm, both in the absence and presence of a single Na+ ion, under applied electric fields ranging from 0 to 0.2 V Å–1. In the Na+–water–CNT system, the electroosmotic flow (EOF) velocity increases nonlinearly with the field. Such nonlinear enhancement is attributed to water ordering that is exclusive to the ion-containing system. This enhanced ordering is evidenced by a larger average number of hydrogen bonds per water molecule, longer hydrogen-bond lifetimes, a reduced interoxygen distance with a higher first peak in the oxygen–oxygen radial distribution function, and a decrease in free energy. Further relative permittivity calculations reveal that the effective permittivity decreases with increasing electric field, leading to a monotonic rise in the Born energy difference between the Na+–water–CNT and water–CNT systems. This increase in Born energy likely drives the observed water ordering in Na+–water–CNT. Our findings uncover a previously unrecognized coupling mechanism among ions, electric fields, and water structure under extreme confinement.
papers.zh: 电场和离子协同诱导的水有序化引发的亚纳米碳纳米管中电渗流增强

papers.title: Selective Separation of H2S and CO2 from Natural Gas Using Low-Viscosity, Highly Basic Protic Ionic Liquids: Absorption Characteristics and Molecular Mechanisms
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: To achieve efficient removal of CO2 and H2S from natural gas, four protic ionic liquids (PILs) were designed and systematically investigated in this work. Structural characterization and physicochemical property measurements were carried out. Among the four PILs, the cation and anion of [DBNH][PhO] exhibit planar structures that confer the lowest viscosity (20.30 cP at 313.2 K). At 313.15 K, its H2S solubility reaches 2.61 and 4.68 mol·kg–1 at H2S partial pressures of 0.1 and 1 bar, respectively. The solubility-based H2S/CO2 selectivity is 4.83 when defined as the ratio of H2S solubility at 0.1 bar to CO2 solubility at 1 bar, whereas the equal-pressure solubility ratio at 1 bar is 8.67. The experimentally determined gas solubility data are correlated using the reaction equilibrium thermodynamic model (RETM), from which key thermodynamic parameters, including the apparent equilibrium constant, Henry’s law constant, enthalpy, and entropy, are obtained. Furthermore, quantum chemistry calculations, including electrostatic potential (ESP) analysis, Atoms in Molecules (AIM) topological analysis, and energy decomposition analysis, are performed to elucidate the origin of the high H2S/CO2 selectivity of [DBNH][PhO]. The strong basicity of [PhO]− significantly enhances H2S solubility, whereas steric hindrance and π-conjugation effects hinder the effective insertion of CO2.
papers.zh: 使用低粘度、高碱性质子离子液体从天然气中选择性分离H2S和CO2：吸收特性和分子机制

papers.title: Field Cycling NMR Relaxometry as a Tool for Detecting the Quality of Biotechnological Drugs
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Biotechnological drugs mostly contain proteins or peptides; therefore, any change in ambient conditions during their storage and administration to patients may cause structural modifications, which, in turn, lower the drug quality/effectiveness. Among different drug quality issues hampering drug stability and pharmacokinetics, the commonly observed ones are aggregation and glycation. Both processes include changes at a molecular level that can indeed be probed by field cycling NMR relaxometry as an alternative to traditional techniques used in the detection of drug quality issues. In this study, as a forthcoming problem in diabetes pharmaceuticals, aggregation effects on a commercially available insulin drug (Humulin-R) and glucose-mediated glycation of bovine serum albumin (BSA, as a model serum protein for in vitro tests) were investigated by means of FFC NMR relaxometry experiments. 1H spin–lattice relaxation rate dispersion (NMRD) profiles obtained on insulin samples treated under three different stress conditions showed that, for a sample agitated at a high temperature (T = 50 °C), one observes a significant low-frequency dispersion that can be associated with rotational/reorientational motion of aggregates formed under this condition. Regarding the glycation experiments on the BSA solution, the low-frequency proton relaxation rate, R1, increases with glycation temperature and glycation time, which is related to the aggregation induced by advanced glycation end-product (AGEs) formation on the surface of BSA. Overall, for the detection of drug quality issues, FFC NMR relaxometry is promising as a noninvasive and relatively low-cost technique that does not involve any additional sample preparation procedures or use of chemicals.
papers.zh: 场循环NMR弛豫测定法作为检测生物技术药物质量的工具

papers.title: Analytical Potential Energy Surface and Variational Transition-State Theory Kinetics of the NH3 + Br → NH2 + HBr Hydrogen-Abstraction Reaction
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The hydrogen-abstraction reaction NH3 + Br → NH2 + HBr is strongly endothermic and has no measured rate coefficient. We report a full-dimensional analytical potential energy surface (PES) for it and variational transition-state theory (VTST) rate coefficients in both directions over 200 to 2000 K. CCSD(T)/CBS benchmarks, with a −3.51 kcal/mol spin–orbit correction on the reactant asymptote, place a very late saddle point 17.6 kcal/mol above the reactants but 2.1 kcal/mol below the NH2 + HBr asymptote once zero-point and spin–orbit corrections are included. A valence-bond/molecular-mechanics PES calibrated against that benchmark reproduces the stationary-point energies to 0.5 kcal/mol and the adiabatic barrier to 0.25 kcal/mol. The submerged barrier has two consequences. In the forward direction, it empties the ground-state tunneling window and makes the variational rate an upper bound, because flux is counted at energies from which products are inaccessible; quasi-classical trajectories on the same surface, once their zero-point leakage is removed, agree with the corrected variational rate within a factor of 3 over 1000 to 2000 K. In the reverse direction, a two-step treatment with long-range capture agrees with conventional transition-state theory above 400 K but falls by a factor of 3.4 below it at 200 K, and the activation energy is negative below 1000 K (−2.8 kcal/mol at 298 K), as measured for CH3 + HBr. The rate coefficients are predictions.
papers.zh: NH3 + Br → NH2 + HBr夺氢反应的解析势能面和变分过渡态理论动力学

papers.title: Extending AIMNet2 to Macrocyclic Peptides through Data-Efficient Continual Training
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Macrocyclic peptides are among the most promising therapeutic modalities, yet no general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) has been systematically benchmarked for their conformational analysis. We show that on the MPCONF196 macrocyclic benchmark, the four-model AIMNet2 ensemble outperforms MACE-OFF23(S), despite macrocycles being entirely absent from its training data. A single AIMNet2 model is 3- to 5-fold faster and needs 5- to 63-fold less GPU memory than the MACE-OFF23 models at their default float64-precision. The four-model ensemble is about as fast as MACE-OFF23 but retains a 3- to 32-fold memory advantage even against MACE-OFF23 in float32. The larger MACE-OFF23(M) and MACE-OFF23(L) models remain more accurate. To narrow this gap, we introduce a continual training protocol that requires new quantum-chemical labels for fewer than 25,000 domain-specific conformers (<0.13% of the training corpus) while preserving conformational-energy accuracy on nonmacrocyclic molecules. On a sequence-disjoint holdout of unseen CREMP macrocyclic peptides, the resulting model, AIMNet2-macro, reduces conformational energy RMSE by 25 to 27% and DFT force RMSE by 20% (25% on backbone atoms) and improves lowest-energy conformer recovery relative to the original AIMNet2. It retains the conformational-energy accuracy of the original model on the nonmacrocyclic drug-like molecules of CONFORGE and also improves accuracy on the structurally distinct macrocycles of MPCONF196, although this smaller improvement is not statistically significant. Among the ten training strategies compared, only continual training on the combined corpus (AIMNet2-macro) achieves this improvement without degrading small-molecule accuracy. AIMNet2-macro is therefore the best balanced, though not the most accurate, of the models tested. As an independent case study, AIMNet2-macro reproduces DFT conformational energies of six cyclosporine A conformers with an RMSE of 0.78 kcal mol–1 and the correct rank ordering, the lowest error among the MLIPs and semiempirical methods evaluated on this system. The continual training strategy has been adopted in the AIMNet2 (2025) release, which unifies small-molecule, macrocyclic, and intermolecular-interaction treatment in a single production potential.
papers.zh: 通过数据高效的持续训练将 AIMNet2 扩展到大环肽

papers.title: A High-Fidelity Reactive Force Field ReaxFFCHON-S25 for C/H/O/N Systems via Successive Partition Optimization: Unraveling Mechanistic Insights into Hydrocarbon and Ammonia Combustion
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Accurate reactive molecular dynamics (RMD) simulations of hydrocarbon and ammonia combustion are often hindered by obsolete quantum mechanical (QM) training data and the large computational cost of conventional ReaxFF parametrization. To address these challenges, we develop ReaxFFCHON-S25, a high-fidelity reactive force field for C/H/O/N systems, parametrized via Successive Partition Optimization (SuPO), an efficient and scalable strategy for force field refinement. Parameters were trained against a comprehensive QM data set computed at the M06–2X/6–311++G** level within the meta-GGA framework. The reference library comprises 30,267 configurations (>29,256 data points) spanning 356 representative systems (C0–C8, including nitrogenous species). The training subset (2570 configurations, >2497 data points) covers 171 systems and incorporates exhaustive scans of bond lengths, angles, torsions, transition states, and elementary reactions. The benchmarking reveals that ReaxFFCHON-S25 significantly outperforms the legacy ReaxFF-lg models, reducing RMSEs by 21.0% (C/H/O) and 13.1% (C/H/O/N) for the C0–C4 training sets, and by 34.4%–46.2% for the out-of-sample C5–C8 test sets. The RMD simulations further validate the force field’s robustness: the simulated apparent activation energy for ammonia oxidation aligns closely with the reported experimental measurements, and the resolved reaction network accurately captures critical intermediates (e.g., NH2, HNO) and pathways consistent with both the experimental observations and high-level theoretical benchmarks. Crucially, ReaxFFCHON-S25 elucidates the mechanistic intricacies of NOx formation and elimination, establishing a powerful computational microscope for unraveling nitrogen combustion chemistry. This work provides a validated computational tool for gas-phase hydrocarbon and ammonia combustion, offering a foundation for future extension to more complex carbon-neutral fuel systems.
papers.zh: 通过连续分区优化实现的C/H/O/N体系高保真反应力场ReaxFFCHON-S25：揭示烃类和氨燃烧的机理见解

papers.title: Theoretical Characterization of Hydroxyfuranones Related to Biomass Burning and Their Tautomers
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The formation of hydroxyfuranones has been observed in biomass plumes and suggested as an indicator of their temporal evolution. This work focuses on the characterization of three different hydroxyfuranones and their open-chain tautomers. The relationship between the thermal stability and structures is studied using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Furthermore, harmonic and anharmonic IR vibrational frequencies calculated using generalized second-order perturbation theory (GVPT2) are compared with several experimental IR spectra. We find good agreement for the most important vibrational modes. It is also shown that the thermodynamic stability depends on substituent positioning and structural features like intramolecular hydrogen bonding. The DFT + GVPT2 approach was successfully used to distinguish between different tautomers.
papers.zh: 与生物质燃烧相关的羟基呋喃酮及其互变异构体的理论表征

papers.title: Systematic Improvement of Trial States in Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We extend the use of coupled cluster (CC) trial states in the phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) method beyond single and double excitations to include both triple and quadruple excitations. With this AFQMC/CC hierarchy, we are able to systematically benchmark the method’s performance on molecular systems as the quality of the trial is improved. Our results show that the phaseless AFQMC energy improves systematically and is typically significantly more accurate than the energy of the underlying trial state. However, the relative improvement compared to the trial CC energy decreases as we ascend the CC hierarchy. As the CC wave function is usually further approximated when used as an AFQMC trial, we also explore the relationship between the components of the CC wave function and the resulting AFQMC/CC error. Our results suggest that improving the representation of the CC wave function in the AFQMC trial does not always lower the bias even when it increases the fidelity of the trial with the exact ground state.
papers.zh: 无相辅助场量子蒙特卡洛中试探态的系统性改进

papers.title: A Three-Level Noise Floor for Cyclodextrin Binding Constants and What It Permits for Descriptor-Based Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Regression and machine-learning models for cyclodextrin inclusion constants are often reported with cross-validated Q2 near 0.9, yet the reproducibility of the compiled data on which they are trained has not been quantified. This work quantifies it at three levels, each defined by the uncertainty it captures. The within-experiment fitting precision of a single calorimetric study, 0.008 log units, is a lower bound on repeatability; head-to-head comparisons between laboratories and methods give 0.115 log units (95% CI: 0.079–0.210); and 128 replicated host–guest pairs in a verified extraction of the standard thermodynamic compilation give 0.157 log units (95% CI: 0.115–0.220, from a pair-level bootstrap), with a heavy tail in which 7.3% of pairwise comparisons, and an estimated 3–5% of single determinations, deviate by more than 1 log unit. Propagated through the replication structure of a 44-pair modeling set under three error models, this noise implies an out-of-sample R2 ceiling of about 0.70–0.78, and response noise accounts for roughly two-thirds to nine-tenths of the leave-one-out error of the adopted model, an error statistically compatible with a model limited by the data alone. Against this bound, a size descriptor derived from measured limiting diffusion coefficients through the Edward-corrected Stokes–Einstein relation was compared with McGowan volume, each paired with log P. The two are statistically indistinguishable (95% CI of the difference in mean squared error, −0.024 to +0.042) under leave-one-out and leave-one-guest-out validation, and both lose accuracy when whole chemical families are withheld. No packing optimum is detectable, and normalizing guest size by cavity volume degrades performance by aliasing the size term onto the host intercepts. The durable result is the bound, which should accompany any accuracy reported on compiled data.

papers.title: Multiscale Molecular Simulations Reveal the Structural Pathway of Histatin 1 Self-Association
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Histatins are a family of human saliva peptides; the three main members consist of Histatin 1 (Hst1), Histatin 3 (Hst3), and Histatin 5 (Hst5). Despite their high primary-structure similarity, the peptides display varied functions and behaviors. Experimental evidence supports concentration-dependent self-association of Hst1, but the molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This property is of interest because it is not observed in Hst5. Here, we combine atomistic and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with a decomposition-based trajectory analysis to investigate the structural origins of Hst1 self-association across multiple length and time scales. Atomistic simulations reveal dimers that remain associated over the simulated time scales, together with transient higher-order oligomers. Analysis of intermolecular residue contacts highlights aromatic residues as prominent contributors to peptide association, consistent with a multivalent interaction network. Coarse-grained simulations extend these observations to larger systems and longer time scales, demonstrating a progressive assembly into dynamic peptide clusters. By discretizing the resulting conformational landscape, we extracted representative structures to reconstruct the self-association pathway from dispersed monomers to higher-order assemblies. The simulations provide a multiscale description of Hst1 self-association and support a model in which weak, multivalent peptide–peptide contacts contribute to the formation of dynamic peptide-rich assemblies. Although the present work does not directly demonstrate liquid–liquid phase separation, it identifies molecular features associated with biomolecular assembly.
papers.zh: 多尺度分子模拟揭示组蛋白1自缔合的结构途径

papers.title: XTQSPRKinetic: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Reaction-Space Clustering and Property Learning from SMILES
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Chemical heterogeneity can limit the ability of a single global structure–property model to represent modified Arrhenius parameters across a reaction network. XTQSPRKinetic combines learned reaction grouping with specialist regression in a configurable mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture evaluated on a Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG)-derived n-hexane pyrolysis/steam-cracking network containing 1215 elementary reactions. Using 23 Boruta-confirmed descriptors, a seven-family gate combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation with fuzzy C-means clustering and hard routing to Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) specialists yielded fitted-network root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 7.904, 0.985, and 4.855 for ln A, n, and Ea (kcal mol–1), respectively. Under the same descriptor basis, the learned-family configuration achieved lower reconstruction errors than both the unpartitioned global baseline (corresponding RMSEs of 14.394, 1.819, and 8.946) and size-matched random partitions (mean RMSEs of 10.746, 1.329, and 5.932). RMG-label specialists achieved still lower RMSEs of 5.629, 0.681, and 3.935. This comparison uses 15 RMG classes versus seven learned groups and differs in class composition, partition resolution, and specialist support; the performance gap cannot therefore be attributed to label semantics alone. Learned grouping provides a complementary organization without requiring RMG labels for gate fitting or routing. Residual diagnostics identified rare 1,3-sigmatropic rearrangements among the largest errors, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) revealed family dependent use of the shared descriptors. These metrics characterize fitted-network reconstruction; predictive performance on unseen reactions requires separate held-out evaluation.
papers.zh: XTQSPRKinetic：用于反应空间聚类和从SMILES学习性质的混合专家框架

papers.title: The effects of the substrate and graphene on the interfacial structures of DMSO revealed by heterodyne-detected sum frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics analysis
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Understanding molecular structures at electrode/electrolyte interfaces is essential for optimizing high-performance electrochemical reactions. Here, we investigated the interfacial structures of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), a widely used aprotic solvent, at the air/DMSO, SiO2/DMSO, and air/graphene/DMSO interfaces by heterodyne-detected sum frequency generation (HD-SFG) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. HD-SFG spectroscopy is an interface-selective nonlinear spectroscopic technique capable of determining the absolute orientation of interfacial molecules. To enable HD-SFG measurements at the buried SiO2/DMSO interface, where precise optical phase control is challenging, an octadecyltrichlorosilane self-assembled monolayer was introduced on the SiO2 substrate as a phase reference for accurate determination of the interfacial complex susceptibility. The obtained spectra revealed that the hydrogen atoms of the methyl group preferentially orient toward the air side (CH3-up configuration) at the air/DMSO interface, whereas they orient toward the bulk DMSO side (CH3-down configuration) at the SiO2/DMSO interface. Furthermore, introducing graphene, an optically transparent two-dimensional carbon material relevant to practical carbon electrodes, shifts the most probable configuration at the interface: the S=O bond points toward the liquid phase, while the methyl groups orient nearly perpendicular to the surface normal. MD simulations with polarizable models well reproduced the spectral band shapes and signs, revealing the physical meaning of the signs of imaginary amplitudes in terms of orientation and local solvation effects. These results provide molecular-level insights into how the substrate and graphene affect the interfacial structures and demonstrate HD-SFG spectroscopy, combined with polarizable MD simulations, as a powerful approach for elucidating molecular-level structures at buried electrochemical interfaces for energy storage systems.
papers.zh: 通过外差检测的和频产生(HD-SFG)光谱和分子动力学分析揭示的衬底和石墨烯对DMSO界面结构的影响

papers.title: A propagator theory of non-Gaussian diffusion and power-law relaxation in multidimensional disordered media
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Disordered energy environments generate spatially heterogeneous mobility and persistent deviations from Gaussian diffusion. Such systems are common, and dynamics often provide a route to understand the heterogeneity, as in solution spectroscopy. We develop a propagator theory of tagged-particle motion in multidimensional media described by spatially correlated, quenched Gaussian site-energy disorder and detailed-balance hopping dynamics. The disorder-averaged self-propagator is formulated for a specified initial ensemble, and its Fourier transform, the self-dynamic structure factor, is analyzed through a small-wavevector cumulant expansion. To describe the approach to Gaussian diffusion, we introduce a coarse-grained local-mobility field and relate the non-Gaussian parameter to the time correlation of the mobility sampled along the particle trajectory. In the homogenized diffusive regime, convolution of the spatial mobility correlation with the long-time propagator produces an algebraically decaying mobility memory. Consequently, the non-Gaussian parameter exhibits dimension-dependent long-time relaxation: (t−1/2) in one dimension, [(ln t)/t] in two dimensions, and (t−1) for (d > 2). The amplitudes retain information about energetic disorder, spatial correlations, dimensionality, and initial preparation. The theory thus connects microscopic site-energy disorder, propagator dynamics, mobility memory, and experimentally measurable non-Gaussian corrections to the self-dynamic structure factor.
papers.zh: 多维无序介质中非高斯扩散和幂律弛豫的传播子理论

papers.title: Percolation of sheared suspensions of attractive hard spheres
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We have simulated suspensions of colloidal spheres under shear flow to study the formation of clusters, the percolation transition, and the conductivity of the suspensions. The spheres interact via a steep repulsive core and an optional attractive tail of varying strength. In the steady state, we observe transient clusters in the plane orthogonal to the flow direction, which lead to a decreased percolation threshold. These anisotropic clusters are strongly aligned. They affect the conductivity under shear and occur independently of the geometric connectivity criterion and the attractive strength of the spheres. Attractions lower the percolation threshold, but shear flow counteracts this effect. The alignment of clusters and the anisotropy of the conductivity become non-monotonic for the strongest attraction we studied. The flow-aligned orientation of clusters controls the behavior at weaker shear in that case.

papers.title: New aspect of hydrogen sulfide dimer: CCSD(T)/CBS potential surface of antiparallel interactions
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The potential energy surface of the hydrogen sulfide dimer with antiparallel S–H⋯H–S orientations was investigated by high-level very accurate CCSD(T)/CBS quantum chemical calculations. More than 1300 geometries were calculated to characterize the potential energy surface. The antiparallel dimer that is minimum on the potential surface has an interaction energy of −1.57 kcal/mol, only slightly less strong than that of the classical hydrogen-bonded dimer (−1.71 kcal/mol). These data demonstrate that antiparallel interaction represents an important stabilization motif in hydrogen sulfide aggregates. Symmetry-adapted perturbation theory reveals that the interaction is governed by comparable electrostatic (47%) and dispersion (43%) contributions, in contrast to the antiparallel water dimer, where electrostatic interactions dominate. The present study provides the first detailed characterization of the antiparallel interaction in the hydrogen sulfide dimer and extends the understanding of the shallow potential energy surface of this system.

papers.title: High-resolution photoelectron spectroscopy of vibrationally excited TiO2 anions
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: High-resolution photoelectron spectra of TiO2− excited to its v3=1 state were obtained via slow electron velocity-map imaging of cryogenically cooled anions (cryo-SEVI). To determine the ν3 (antisymmetric stretch) anion frequency, growth and depletion of various features in the cryo-SEVI spectrum were monitored over a range of infrared (IR) excitation energies. Photoelectron scans were taken at an IR pre-excitation energy of 918 cm−1 and yielded a ∼6% depletion of features in the ground state cryo-SEVI spectra as well as new hot and sequence bands based on the 310 and 311 transitions, respectively. By monitoring hot band intensities as a function of IR laser frequency, the rotational profile of the v3=0–1 transition was mapped out and found to be centered at 914(7) cm−1. The observed hot bands are Franck–Condon forbidden and arise from Herzberg–Teller coupling with the Ã1B2 neutral excited state, similar to what was observed in the cryo-SEVI spectra of TiO2−. The results from this IR cryo-SEVI experiment lay the groundwork for future investigations of larger bare and complexed transition metal–oxide clusters.

papers.title: Cancer-associated histone tail mutations reshape conformational ensembles and DNA-contact states in nucleosomes
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Cancer-associated histone mutations can perturb chromatin regulation, yet how many noncanonical mutations in intrinsically disordered histone tails alter nucleosome dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we combine pan-cancer histone mutation profiling with 31.5 μs of all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of complete nucleosomes to investigate recurrent mutations in the H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 tails. We identify recurrent and understudied mutation sites beyond canonical H3 oncohistones and characterize how selected substitutions perturb histone-tail conformational ensembles and DNA contacts in their nucleosomal context. The simulations reveal mutation-specific redistribution of tail–DNA contacts across the nucleosomal DNA surface, accompanied by changes in MM/GBSA-derived relative interaction-energy estimates. For selected systems, Markov state modeling further resolves metastable tail–DNA contact states and shows that mutations alter their structural characteristics and population distributions. These perturbations are not confined to the substituted residues but extend to neighboring interaction networks. Together, our results provide a molecular-level physical picture of how cancer-associated histone-tail mutations reshape conformational and interaction-state landscapes in nucleosomes.
papers.zh: 与癌症相关的组蛋白尾部突变重塑了核小体的构象集合和DNA接触状态

papers.title: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer dynamics with neural network potentials and nuclear quantum effects
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ∼11.5 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.
papers.zh: 基于神经网络势能和核量子效应的激发态分子内质子转移动力学

papers.title: Electronic excited states and photodissociation pathways of iso-propylamine: Experimental and theoretical investigations
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We report for the first time absorption cross sections of iso-propylamine in the energy range of 40 000 to 80 000 cm−1 using synchrotron radiation. Quantum chemical calculations based on time-dependent density functional theory are used to conduct a detailed spectral analysis. The observed intensity profile of the room temperature absorption spectrum is well reproduced by a theoretical simulation that includes vertical excitation energies and oscillator strengths of its two stable conformers, gauche (G) and anti (A). Rydberg series that converge to the first ionization limit of iso-propylamine are assigned via quantum defect analysis. Several vibronic progressions are observed along with the Rydberg series. The dominance of progressions involving the NH2 wagging mode observed along with the 3s Rydberg transition implies a molecular geometry change involving the NH2 group in the excited state. This is confirmed by geometry optimization calculations, which predict a planar geometry in the excited state vis-à-vis pyramidal geometry in the ground state. The measured absorption cross sections are used to estimate the lower limit of the UV photolysis lifetime of iso-propylamine in the upper atmosphere. In addition, the photodissociation dynamics of iso-propylamine probed using potential energy scans of S1, T1, and T2 excited states along each of the possible direct bond cleavage channels show that direct dissociation via S1 is unlikely, and intersystem crossings may play an important role. Molecular channels involving H atom migration leading to CH4 and NH3 formation in both iso-propylamine and n-propylamine are investigated and compared using intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations.
papers.zh: 异丙胺的电子激发态和光解离途径：实验和理论研究

papers.title: Confinement-force scaling of flexible polymers: From Gaussian chains to self-avoiding walks
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The confinement of flexible polymers between parallel walls generates entropic forces whose magnitude and scaling depend on excluded-volume strength. While ideal Gaussian and fully self-avoiding walk (SAW) chains represent well-characterized limits, a unified description of confinement forces across the crossover between them has remained incomplete. We develop such a description by expressing confinement free energies and forces in terms of the dimensionless ratio L/Rg, where L is the slit width and Rg is the unconfined radius of gyration. Using the exactly solvable Gaussian chain as an analytic benchmark, validated with sub-percent accuracy by a Brownian-bridge-corrected Rosenbluth estimator, we establish the asymptotic force law f·Rg∼L/Rg−3 and deploy the same framework across the full Gaussian–SAW crossover. For the absorbing-wall calculations, confinement is defined through the survival of the tethered chain within the slit. Monte Carlo simulations of self-avoiding walks yield an approximate collapse, without adjustable parameters, of f·Rg vs L/Rg across chain lengths, with measurable residual chain-length dependence and an effective exponent broadly consistent with the theoretical SAW limit −1/ν+1≈−2.70. Using the Domb–Joyce model to interpolate continuously between the two limits, we test whether the confinement response at fixed w becomes approximately organized across chain lengths when expressed in terms of the independently measured L/Rg, and quantify the remaining finite-chain deviations. Systematic tests across boundary conditions and spatial dimensions show that ideal Gaussian chains have a strictly vanishing confinement force under the discrete fold-back reflecting ensemble used here, whereas finite excluded-volume interactions generate a measurable force under the same ensemble. These results demonstrate the sensitivity of the confinement response to both polymer interactions and the statistical definition of the boundary condition. Across all conditions examined, the boundary condition produces a systematic change in the force amplitude and detailed scaling response, while the leading organization by Rg is retained as a leading-order description. However, the reflecting-to-absorbing force ratio varies with the reduced slit width and the residuals are systematic, so the boundary condition is not a purely multiplicative renormalization of the force amplitude, and the data do not establish an exact universal master curve. These results show that the diversity of confinement responses across polymer models, interaction strengths, and boundary conditions is organized at leading order by size scaling via Rg, providing a useful scaling description of flexible-polymer confinement, with measurable finite-size, interaction-dependent, and boundary-dependent corrections, relevant to soft-matter and biophysical systems.

papers.title: From 4D to 2D: Efficient computation of the electron correlation energies of atoms in molecular systems
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The accurate modeling of (bio)molecular systems remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. In recent years, machine learning potentials (MLPs) have emerged as a promising approach, combining the efficiency of classical force fields with near quantum-mechanical accuracy. Among these, the physics-informed MLP FFLUX employs the Interacting Quantum Atoms (IQA) energy partitioning scheme to decompose molecular energies into atomic contributions derived from quantum mechanics for machine learning. However, incorporating two-electron correlation energies into IQA, and consequently into FFLUX, is currently unfeasible for larger systems en masse, due to the steep computational scaling associated with the necessary storage and evaluation of the two-particle density matrix (2PDM). In this work, we introduce a proof-of-concept workflow that employs density fitting (DF) to compress the 2PDM into a two-index representation, thereby accelerating the IQA partitioning of two-electron correlation energies. By expressing traditionally four-center electron repulsion integrals in terms of auxiliary basis functions, the DF approximation enables a size reduction of the 2PDM from O(N4) to O(NDF2), where N is the number of basis functions and NDF is the size of the auxiliary basis set. The method proposed here is demonstrated using coupled cluster singles and doubles densities. The resulting reduction in computational cost and memory requirements enables correlated IQA analyses for significantly larger systems than previously accessible. Thus, this development provides an important step toward incorporating explicit electron correlation and hence dispersion directly into FFLUX atomic ML models, thereby improving both their physical robustness and transferability. This advance will eliminate the need to artificially add empirical potentials, or a posteriori dispersion correction.

papers.title: Neutral-to-zwitterionic transition in protonated glycine clusters drives magic number stability
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Molecular clusters in the gas phase often exhibit “magic numbers,” corresponding to enhanced abundances at specific cluster sizes, typically attributed to particularly stable geometric arrangements. Here, we combine electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) with quantum chemical calculations to investigate the structure and stability of protonated glycine clusters. The experimental mass spectrum reveals pronounced magic numbers at cluster sizes n = 3 and n = 6. To elucidate their origin, we performed a systematic computational investigation of glycine clusters up to n = 7, including global structure searches, high-level electronic structure calculations, and thermal stability simulations. Our calculations show that clusters with n = 2, 4, and 5 are predominantly composed of canonical glycine molecules; the n = 7 clusters are composed of both neutral and zwitterionic glycine molecules, whereas the hexamer is the first cluster size for which fully zwitterionic structures become thermodynamically preferred. This neutral-to-zwitterionic transition gives rise to a highly cooperative hydrogen-bonding network and is accompanied by a pronounced increase in thermal stability, providing a natural explanation for the exceptional abundance of the hexamer. In contrast, the enhanced abundance of the trimer is consistent with kinetic stabilization under electrospray ion-source conditions rather than with the thermodynamic stability of its global free-energy minimum. These findings provide molecular-level insight into the emergence of magic numbers in glycine clusters and the onset of zwitterionic stabilization in finite molecular assemblies.

papers.title: EmbASI: An extensible Pythonic framework for DFT-in-DFT and WF-in-DFT embedding
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: High-level quantum mechanical (QM) simulations are important for understanding chemical and physical systems, but these methods scale unfavorably with system size, and this limits calculations to model representations of the real systems. To simulate realistic systems, approaches such as hierarchical quantum mechanics in quantum mechanics embedding (QM/QM) can be used to localize the accurate electronic structure methods to a region of chemical interest, with the wider environment represented using a less expensive embedding potential. However, implementing embedding procedures into established QM software packages is often challenging due to their monolithic design and complex software structure. Here, we present a modular and open-source approach that enables QM/QM embedding using established electronic structure codes with reduced development overhead. We demonstrate the new software, EmbASI, using the projection-based embedding theory scheme. Calculations performed for pentanol and organic dimers demonstrate the efficacy of the hierarchical density functional theory (DFT) embedding approach with the charge localization and partitioning procedures implemented in the wrapper environment; when using a truncated local atomic orbital basis, wavefunction-in-DFT embedding calculations demonstrate speed-ups of 32× for a 70 atom system, evaluated with RPA@PBE-in-PBE relative to a full RPA@PBE calculation, while introducing minimal errors to the total energies of the embedding simulations (<1 kJ mol−1). We then demonstrate capabilities for realistic extended zeolite models, achieving similar minimal errors with significant compute speed-up and memory reductions. The results demonstrate the capabilities of EmbASI for immediate applied QM/QM modeling and provide a broader foundation for multiscale QM simulations using established electronic structure infrastructure.

papers.title: Bayesian sampling of structural ensembles: The role of ensemble-counting measures
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Structural ensemble refinement is widely used to integrate molecular simulations with experimental measurements. While most applications focus on the maximum-a-posteriori ensemble, Bayesian sampling of the posterior distribution can provide uncertainty estimates and posterior averages for arbitrary observables. A notable step in this direction was introduced by the Bayesian Energy Landscape Tilting (BELT) framework, where sampling is performed on a family of maximum-entropy ensembles parameterized by Lagrange multipliers. Here, we show that Bayesian sampling in this setting requires an explicit choice of ensemble-counting measure. In particular, the flat measure in Lagrange-multiplier space used in the original BELT formulation leads to a posterior distribution that is formally non-normalizable for finite reference trajectories. We propose the Jeffreys measure as an invariant ensemble-counting prescription, restoring normalizability in the finite-sample situations considered here, and providing a consistent definition of posterior averages. Using both an analytically tractable Gaussian model and maximum-entropy refinement of RNA oligomer simulations, we compare different ensemble-counting measures and show that they can significantly affect Bayesian estimates. The resulting methodology has been implemented in the MDRefine software package.

papers.title: Critical point search and linear response theory for computing electronic excitation energies of molecular systems. II. CASSCF
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The computation of excited states within the Complete Active Space Self-Consistent Field (CASSCF) framework remains a significant challenge in quantum chemistry, both theoretically and algorithmically. In this work, we extend the Kähler manifold formalism introduced in Paper I Grazioli et al. [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 064101 (2026)] of this series to the CASSCF theory and draw a geometrical connection from the time-dependent CASSCF equations to state-specific and linear response methodologies for excited states. This is achieved by first investigating the underlying CASSCF manifold and identifying its Kähler structure, which is complicated by the nontrivial coupling of CI and orbital degrees of freedom. Building on these theoretical findings, we derive the CASSCF linear response equations in a straightforward manner and develop a robust state-specific method that relies solely on first-order derivatives of the CASSCF energy functional. Numerical results on representative molecular systems—water, formaldehyde, and ethylene—demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed state-specific method, while revealing the difficulty of reliable identification of excited states due to nonlinearity induced by the CASSCF theory.

papers.title: OptiMat Alloys: a FAIR-aligned living database of multi-principal element alloys enabled by a conversational agent
papers.jname: npj Computational Materials
papers.abs: Existing FAIR materials repositories can only serve pre-computed entries, so broad coverage is perpetually incomplete and cannot adapt to new questions on demand. We present OptiMat Alloys, a large language model-powered conversational agent for multi-principal element alloy exploration. Its central contribution is LLM-based workflow orchestration coupled to a living database : every calculation is performed on demand and persisted automatically with provenance in a local database, so asking a question produces provenance-rich, FAIR-aligned records without a separate deposition step. The agent is accessible through a web interface that requires no programming expertise ( low-barrier accessibility ) and reports uncertainty through cross-potential and cross-configuration validation ( built-in uncertainty quantification ). By coupling foundational machine learning interatomic potentials that cover nearly the entire periodic table with natural-language interaction, OptiMat Alloys enables targeted, on-demand computation guided by the user’s domain knowledge and brings computational alloy screening within reach of any materials scientist.

papers.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization for quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy
papers.jname: npj Computational Materials
papers.abs: Quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) provides an indispensable means to understand structure-property relationships in atomic dimensions. Successful quantification requires reliable retrieval of essential atomic structural information despite artifacts arising from practically unavoidable imaging imperfections. Experimental observation combined with model-based iterative image simulation has enabled broad applications in quantitative structural and chemical determination of objects spanning zero to three dimensions. However, the large number of parameters involved makes the current multi-step, user-supervised iterative approach highly time-consuming, restricting its use to small sample areas and experienced users. In this work, we implement and apply a physics-informed Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to advance HRTEM quantification toward full automation and large-field-of-view analysis. Unlike conventional optimization methods, our approach adopts a stepwise strategy that fully leverages BO’s strength in handling high-dimensional parameter spaces, while its probabilistic engine efficiently refines the parameter space for rapid quantification. Using a BaTiO 3 single crystal that contains heavy, medium, and light elements as a model system, we demonstrate that the three-dimensional crystal structure can be determined from a single HRTEM image with a three- to four-order-of-magnitude improvement in time efficiency. This approach opens new avenues for fast, automated quantification over larger sample volumes and, promisingly, for in-situ applications.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Electronic Bands and Phonon Renormalization Modulate Thermoelectric Transport in ZrSnPt and ZrInAu
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Finite-temperature thermoelectric calculations typically introduce temperature through carrier occupations and scattering rates while retaining zero-temperature electronic and vibrational states. Here, using ZrSnPt and ZrInAu as model systems, we retain first-principles-derived band- and k-resolved electronic energy shifts induced by thermal expansion and lattice vibrations and incorporate them directly into Boltzmann transport calculations. These nonuniform shifts modify band dispersion and valley alignment and lead to strongly material-, carrier-, and temperature-dependent transport responses. On the lattice side, we combine finite-temperature phonon renormalization and thermal expansion with three- and four-phonon scattering. The combined electronic and lattice effects produce relative changes in the thermoelectric figure of merit ZT ranging from −9.04% to +42.29% relative to the static reference treatment. These results highlight the importance of treating temperature-induced changes in transport-relevant electronic and vibrational states on a consistent footing for predictive thermoelectric transport calculations.

papers.title: Ultrafast Radiative Recombination of Singlet Excitons in Conjugated Polymer Aggregates Modulated by the Intrachain Dissociation–Interchain Delocalization Competition
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: We readily modulated relaxation pathways of singlet (S1) excitons in push–pull conjugated polymer (CP, D18) aggregates by controlling the spin-coating process. Transient absorption spectroscopy results reveal that intrachain (localized) S1 excitons are efficiently converted into emissive interchain-delocalized excitons in an H-type excitonic coupling-dominant film. Conversely, a notable stimulated emission band emerges and red-shifts toward the steady-state photoluminescence peak within 1 ps in a film with enhanced J-type excitonic coupling (intrachain ordering). This indicates that the weakened interchain S1 delocalization leads to ultrafast intrachain S1 radiative recombination during relaxation. The competitive interplay between this weakened interchain delocalization and the intrachain ordering-driven S1 dissociation limits efficient progression into any of the dominant exciton deactivation pathways at early times. Thus, a kinetic bottleneck is induced, consequently increasing the probability of subpicosecond S1 radiative recombination. Our findings provide a molecular design strategy to minimize exciton energy dissipation in CP aggregates.

papers.title: Coordination Domain Overlap Governs Anomalous Mobility Recovery in InO x /PAA Thin-Film Transistors
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Polymer blending in oxide semiconductors is widely used but typically degrades mobility, either monotonically or after a peak. Here we report anomalous mobility recovery in InOx/PAA thin-film transistors: increasing PAA from 1 to 3 wt % collapses the mobility from 5.27 to 1.58 cm2 V–1 s–1, yet increasing to 5 wt % rebounds it to 4.05 cm2 V–1 s–1, 2.4 times the pristine value. XPS indicates decoupling from chemical defects, while TEM and C-AFM reveal a threshold evolution of the transport network from connected to fragmented to partially reconnected, consistent with the mobility trend. We propose a coordination-domain-overlap mechanism: PAA-In3+ domains evolve from isolated to partially and then pervasively overlapping, altering the condensation pathway and connectivity of the inorganic network. This work establishes network connectivity as a key design parameter for oxide/polymer semiconductors, providing a route to high-mobility composite films at high polymer contents.

papers.title: Sulfur Dioxide Sulfide (SSO2): The Elusive Isovalent Analogue of Sulfur Trioxide (SO3)
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Sulfur dioxide sulfide (SSO2) has remained experimentally undetected despite repeated theoretical predictions of its stability. As a missing sulfur oxide isovalent to sulfur trioxide (SO3), SSO2 occupies a distinctive position at the boundary of formally hypervalent bonding, where replacing oxygen with sulfur perturbs a delocalized chalcogen-oxide framework. Here, we close this long-standing gap by identifying SSO2 in cryogenic SO2 ices processed by energetic electrons using tunable vacuum ultraviolet photoionization reflectron time-of-flight mass spectrometry and high-level quantum chemical computations. These studies reveal a broader sulfur oxide network including sulfur oxide peroxide (OSOO), 1,2,3-dioxathiirane 3-oxide (cyclic-S(O)OO), and disulfur monoxide (S2O). Our results establish sulfur-atom incorporation into SO2 as a viable condensed-phase route to a previously elusive sulfur oxide─SSO2─and highlight its unique molecular structure in sulfur-rich planetary and astrochemical environments.

papers.title: Flexible Electrochromic Infrared Modulators with Integrated Conductive Composite Electrodes for Dynamic Thermal Management
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Electrochromic infrared modulators (EIMs), which enable dynamic control of infrared (IR) emissivity, hold significant promise for applications in green buildings, dynamic thermal camouflage, and intelligent thermal management. However, their practical development has been constrained by limited IR tunability and slow switching speeds, primarily arising from the inadequate performance of IR-transparent conductive and electrochromic electrodes. In this work, we present a flexible EIM with high IR emissivity modulation and fast response speed through the use of an integrated conductive MoO3/MXene electrode, which serves simultaneously as both the conductive electrode and the electrochromic electrode, eliminating the need for conventional IR transparent conductive electrodes. As a benefit from the nanorod structure of MoO3 and high conductivity of MXene, the integrated composite electrode exhibits high flexibility, high electron conductivity, and low initial IR emissivity. As a result, the assembled flexible EIMs based on the MoO3/MXene electrode and quasi-solid-state zinc-based gel electrolyte deliver exceptional electrochromic performance, including high IR modulation (Δε8–14 μm = 0.42), rapid response speed (0.50/0.54 s), and long cycling stability. The design of flexible integrated electrodes opens new pathways for developing high-performance dynamic thermal management devices.

papers.title: Halogen-Tuned Band Gaps and Net-Dipole Polarization in 0D Hybrid Ferroelectrics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: While halogen substitution routinely tunes hybrid metal halides, its influence on the microscopic origin of ferroelectricity remains underexplored. Here, we synthesize two zero-dimensional (0D) bismuth-based hybrids (3FEA)3BiX6 (X = I, Br), denoted 1-I and 2-Br, and show that the polarization mechanism shifts from one jointly governed by the organic and inorganic components to a displacive process dominated by the inorganic lattice. 2-Br exhibits an enhanced spontaneous polarization (∼4.35 μC/cm2), which originates mainly from the uncompensated net dipole of the strongly distorted [BiBr6]3– sublattices. This structural locking corresponds to a massive kinetic barrier (∼464 kJ/mol) during its anomalous phase transition. Furthermore, the inherent interoctahedral charge-transfer architecture in 1-I fosters broadband self-trapped exciton emission, which undergoes abrupt thermal quenching precisely synchronized with its macroscopic structural phase transition. These results establish halogen engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously tailoring polarization mechanisms, phase-transition behavior, and optoelectronic responses in 0D hybrid ferroelectrics, providing design principles for multifunctional ferroic semiconductors.

papers.title: Analysis of ALD-Applied Passivation Coatings on Ni-Rich Cathode Sheets for Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Applying a surface coating is among the most promising and fundamental approaches in improving the performance of existing electrode materials. This work examines four ultrathin coating materials (Al2O3, alucone, TiO2, and titanicone) applied on single-crystal LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2 electrode sheets by atomic layer deposition (ALD). Although this approach has been repeatedly demonstrated in the literature to enhance cycle stability, the mechanism of the coating remains ambiguous. Surface-sensitive analysis suggests that the coating is concentrated near the outer regions of the electrode due to the limited penetration of the gaseous ALD coating precursors. Despite this, the coatings improved the cycle stability of the cathode, particularly at low C-rate, where active material loss from HF corrosion is predominant. Thus, the improvement mechanism cannot be ascribed to the passivating nature of the coating itself. Analysis of the chemical composition of the early formed cathode-electrolyte interface (CEI) layer reveals that the coatings accelerate the decomposition of LiPF6, forming a thin inorganic-rich layer comprising LiF, LixPFyOz, and Li3PO4. This rapidly passivates the cathode surface from HF corrosion, electrolyte solvent decomposition, and lattice oxygen release, suppressing both active material loss and impedance growth. The results indicate that (1) metal oxide or metalcone coatings can behave in a similar manner to electrolyte additives and (2) complete coverage of the active particle surface is not required. To support these conclusions, LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2 was loosely “coated” with TiO2 nanoparticles either by mixing them in the electrode slurry or adding them to the electrolyte as a suspension. Both cases also resulted in an improvement in cycle retention, due to the favorable side reactions generated between TiO2 and F–/PF6–. Preliminary work was also conducted in analyzing the combined effect of passivating LiNi0.83Mn0.06Co0.11O2 both with a coating and common electrolyte additive (fluoroethylene carbonate, FEC). Adding FEC can further enhance the production of fluoride species on the CEI layer, resulting in the strongest cycle retention tested in this work.

papers.title: Femtosecond Pulsed Laser Effect on Mechanical Stability and Photoelectrocatalytic Activity of Au–Pt Nanorods
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Harnessing solar energy for chemical transformations has gained increasing attention as a pathway toward cleaner and more modular chemical synthesis, with the potential to reduce reliance on conventional thermocatalytic processes. Here, we employ femtosecond (fs) laser irradiation to induce morphological restructuring of bimetallic Au–Pt nanorods (NRs) through processes associated with curvature-driven surface diffusion, surface smoothing, and localized interparticle coalescence. We systematically investigate the influence of fs-laser treatment on the structural, optical, mechanical, and photoelectrochemical properties of Au90Pt10NRs. Irradiation with 800 nm femtosecond laser pulses decreased the average nanorod length from 47.1 ± 5.6 to 37.7 ± 3.9 nm and the average aspect ratio from 3.7 ± 2.8 to 2.5 ± 2.2 (n = 150), while increasing the average width from 12.8 ± 2.0 to 14.6 ± 1.8 nm, with particular emphasis on the trade-off between mechanical robustness and photoelectrochemical performance. The laser-treated nanorods also exhibited an increase in average contact stiffness from 7.7 ± 1.1 to 10.6 ± 1.6 μN/nm, corresponding to an approximately 38% increase. In contrast, laser treatment attenuated the longitudinal localized surface plasmon resonance response and reduced the photoelectrochemical response, including an approximately 10% decrease in photocurrent density after the first 1000 s of illumination relative to the untreated nanorods. These findings reveal a structure–property trade-off in which femtosecond laser processing enhances mechanical robustness while attenuating plasmonic and photoelectrochemical performance, providing a framework for balancing structural durability and functional activity in plasmon-enhanced photoelectrocatalysts for solar-hydrogen production.

papers.title: Stacking-Controlled Reactivity and Friction of Water in Atomic-Scale hBN Channels from First Principles
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Understanding the behavior of water confined in atomic-scale channels is a cornerstone of nanoscience and nanofluidics. Unlike graphene, isostructural hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spontaneously acquires electric charges in liquid water due to hydroxide ion (OH–) adsorption. Yet, whether this reactivity persists under monolayer and bilayer confinement remains an open question. Here, we use first-principles modeling to uncover the role of stacking symmetry (AA vs AA’) between hBN walls─a factor that has so far received little attention in boron nitride systems─on the structural and dynamical properties of Å-scale water. We systematically probe neutral, alkaline, and acidic environments to elucidate how water self-ions (H3O+ and OH–) interact with hBN interfaces. Combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) for extended time scales, we obtain a consistent description, at the revPBE-D3 level of theory, of water’s structural and transport properties under extreme confinement. Our results demonstrate that stacking symmetry critically impacts monolayer water systems and modulates the energetics of chemisorbed hydroxide and interfacial friction. In alkaline conditions, chemisorbed hydroxide doubles friction, yet its effect on water diffusion is minimal. Strikingly, monolayer water exhibits a twofold diffusion enhancement compared to bilayer water, reaching bulk-like values─revealing that diffusion is an intrinsic property of the water layer, independent of wall chemistry. This work delivers quantitative estimates of friction and diffusion coefficients, conditional on the chosen functional and water loadings, that provide a reference for future experiments on Å-scale water transport.

papers.title: Spatially Differentiated Solid – Liquid Interfaces in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Adsorption
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Selective adsorption of small molecules from complex aqueous matrices is often limited by macromolecular fouling and inefficient mass transfer at hydrophobic particle surfaces. Here, we report a covalent organic framework (COF) adsorbent designed to create spatially differentiated solid–liquid interfaces through polyacrylamide (polyAM) grafting onto an alkyne-containing COF. Improved aqueous dispersibility, suppressed nonspecific protein adsorption, and retained pore accessibility are consistent with a hydrophilic exterior and accessible internal adsorption domains. Adsorption kinetic studies showed that COF-polyAM14k increased the apparent pseudo-second-order rate constant for rhodamine B adsorption from 0.027 to 0.626 g mg–1 min–1 and enabled efficient bisphenol A recovery from 10-fold-diluted milk. Subsequent amination of accessible residual alkyne sites via a thiol–yne click reaction with cysteamine hydrochloride shifted the zeta potential of COF-polyAM16k from approximately −32.0 to +8.4 mV and enhanced potassium indoxyl sulfate removal, consistent with a contribution from electrostatic interactions. These results support a spatially differentiated interfacial design strategy combining hydrophilic polymer modification with tunable adsorption functionality in COF adsorbents.
