papers.title: Interfacial Charge Rearrangement-Driven Sliding Ferroelectricity with Ultralow Switching Barriers and Strain-Reversible Polarization in HfXY (X, Y = S, Se) Janus and Homogeneous Bilayers
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Two-dimensional sliding ferroelectrics have emerged as a research frontier for post-Moore information devices, owing to their low energy barriers, reversible polarization switching, and potential compatibility with flexible electronics. Based on first-principles calculations, we systematically investigate the sliding ferroelectric properties and strain-tunable behavior of HfXY (X, Y = S, Se) homobilayer and Janus bilayer systems. Through structural optimization, elastic constant analysis, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we confirm the equivalent thermodynamic and mechanical stability of the AB and BA stacking configurations. Using Berry-phase polarization theory, we find that these bilayer systems exhibit degenerate bistability during the AB ↔ BA stacking transition, with out-of-plane polarization magnitudes ranging from 0.19 to 0.82 pC/m, and the polarization reversal predominantly originates from charge redistribution driven by interfacial chalcogen atoms. This charge redistribution mechanism endows the systems with extremely low polarization switching barriers (approximately 12–15 meV per unit cell). Further biaxial strain engineering reveals that compressive strain enhances interlayer coupling and interfacial charge transfer, thereby increasing polarization magnitude, whereas tensile strain weakens the interfacial interaction, leading to reduced polarization and, in some cases, even reversal of the polarization direction. This work reveals the sliding ferroelectric properties of Hf-based bilayer systems, provides a theoretical basis for their microscopic origin, and demonstrates the potential of strain engineering in the polarization manipulation of two-dimensional van der Waals materials.

papers.title: Mechanistic Origins of Atomic-Scale Control in Plasma-Thermal Atomic-Layer Etching of Nickel
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: We present a mechanistic density functional theory (DFT) investigation of atomic-layer etching of nickel previously modified by surface nitride formation. Etching is performed via gas-phase formic acid, and we focus on the influence of nitrogen coverage on reaction energetics and mechanisms. Using two models for the etching process, removing a partial or full surface Ni atomic layer, we examine formic acid adsorption and reaction by dehydrogenation and hydrogen transfer to nitrogen. We show that the mechanism for Ni etching initiates with the formation of metastable nickel-formate surface complexes, partially decoordinated from other Ni on the surface, and their desorption with accompanying ammonia release. Product stability calculations reveal that polynuclear nickel-formate-ammonia complexes are thermodynamically favored over mononuclear species, with meta-generalized gradient approximation (GGA) functionals (SCAN, R2SCAN, R2SCAN-rVV10) providing consistently lower (more favorable) reaction energies than Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) and better in line with experimental observations. Mechanistic pathways on the stepped Ni(843) surface demonstrate a strong dependence on nitrogen coverage: low coverage preserves surface crystallinity but limits the thermodynamic driving force for product desorption, whereas high coverage populates terrace and subsurface sites, weakens Ni–Ni bonds, and facilitates surface rearrangements, forming nickel-formate surface complexes that render early desorption steps accessible. These findings underscore the critical role of nitrogen content in enabling controlled and efficient etching and provide atomistic insight into surface complex formation, hydrogen stabilization, and nickel removal. This work establishes a computational framework to optimize atomic-layer etching of nickel nitride surfaces.

papers.title: Solvation-Mediated Effects of Contact Mutations on p53-DNA Binding Dynamics and Energetics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The tumor suppressor protein p53 is a sequence-specific transcription factor whose DNA-binding domain (DBD) is essential for maintaining genomic stability. Mutations at residues that directly contact DNA frequently impair DNA recognition and are strongly associated with tumorigenesis. In this study, we performed atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the impact of frequent contact mutations (R248Q, R248W, R273C, and R273H) on the dynamics, energetics, and hydration properties of the p53-DNA complex. Comparative analysis of wild-type (WT) and mutant complexes reveals that these mutations perturb hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interaction networks and alter the solvation environment at the DNA-binding interface, leading to less favorable binding free energies, as quantified by alchemical free energy calculations. Analysis of interfacial water dynamics shows that water molecules in the WT complex are more ordered and long-lived, forming stable water bridges that reinforce protein–DNA contacts. The mutations are accompanied by changes in the interfacial hydration network, including mutation-dependent variations in water-bridge occupancy, water mobility, rotational dynamics, and H-bond relaxation lifetimes. These molecular changes are associated with altered solvation contributions and reduced binding affinity in the mutant systems.
papers.zh: 接触突变对p53-DNA结合动力学和能量学的溶剂化介导效应

papers.title: Probing Rigidity and Fluidity of the Hydrophobic Region of Liposomes Using FTIR and 2D IR Spectroscopies
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Rigidity and fluidity of a lipid bilayer’s hydrophobic interior in unilamellar liposomes were evaluated using alkyl-azide-type probes for linear infrared (FTIR) and two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopies. When embedded into a bilayer of DPPC liposomes, the probes, azido-(CH2)n-COOH with n = 6, 8, 10, 13, 15 (denoted as aznAC), position their azido moieties at specific depths in the bilayer, defined by the alkyl tether length (n). The N3 moiety’s asymmetric stretching mode, νas, at ca. 2100 cm–1 shows abrupt changes in its peak width when the DPPC bilayer undergoes an Lβ–Lα phase transition, thus demonstrating probe sensitivity to the rigidity of the bilayer. Temperature dependences for the νas peak width show a sharp change at the phase transition temperature, Tph, for every depth (n), except for n = 6, although the magnitude of the sharp change at Tph differs for different depths, indicating that the packing order depends greatly on the depth in the bilayer. The range of the νas peak width change for az10AC is remarkable, with widths of 9.5 cm–1 at 25 °C and 22.7 cm–1 at 45 °C, which is a 2.4-fold change. A detailed DFT computational analysis was performed to understand the origin of the high sensitivity of the probes to the rigidity of the environment. It was established that the softness of the CNN angle (θ) and the presence of the θ-dependent multiple strong Fermi resonances with interaction energy exceeding 20 cm–1 result in severe broadening of νas. Furthermore, we showed that specific restrictions in the θ-angle distribution, occurring, for example, in bilayers in the gel phase reduce the νas peak width greatly. Spectral diffusion 2D IR measurements revealed the time scales of the conformational relaxation of the bilayer for az10AC in liposomes, which were found to be ca. 6 ps with a significant static component in the gel phase (25 °C) and ca. 2 ps in the liquid-crystal phase (45 °C). Such a large difference in decay times between the two limiting phases makes the aznAC probes sensitive reporters of bilayer fluidity. An isotopically edited compound, 15(N3)-(CH2)10-COOH (15az10AC), was also tested as a probe for the rigidity of the environment. While the width of the νas,15 peak at 2028 cm–1 is narrower than that of 14az10AC in the same environment, it still shows high sensitivity to the rigidity of the environment. DFT-based modeling revealed that a smaller number of Fermi resonances in 15aznAC is the reason for its narrower peak width. Simultaneous use of the two probes, 14aznAC and 15aznAC, was shown to be practical for simultaneously probing two different membrane regions.
papers.zh: 使用FTIR和2D IR光谱法探究脂质体疏水区域的刚性和流动性

papers.title: Hydration Effects on Ion Solvation Shell Structure and Cation Associations in ssDNA/ssRNA-Ionic Liquid Electrolytes
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The effect of hydration on the solvation shell structure and ion association was investigated in biopolymer-based ionic liquid electrolytes composed of single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) or RNA (ssRNA) and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hexafluorophosphate ([BMIM][PF6]). All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed using the OL15/OL3 nucleic acid force fields, an optimized OPLS-AA model for [BMIM][PF6], and the TIP3P water model. Radial distribution functions g(r) and coordination numbers CN(r) reveal that BMIM+ and PF6– ions form compact and symmetric coordination shells with CN(r) ≈ 5.0 at the lowest hydration levels. Increasing water concentration weakens this association, reducing CN(r) to ∼4.16 at 25 wt % water, indicative of water-mediated screening and the disruption of extended ion–ion correlations. In contrast, BMIM+-phosphate (PO4–) interactions remain weak (CN(r) < 1.1) across all hydration levels, as Na+ counterions preferentially neutralize phosphate sites. Analysis of ion-association probability distributions P(n) further shows that the broad, high-n tails observed at low hydration collapse into narrow peaks centered near n = 0–1 as water content increases, signifying the breakdown of multi-ion clusters into isolated ion pairs and free ions. Although modest sequence-dependent variations in coordination are observed, the overall hydration-dependent trends in solvation-shell structure and ion association remain qualitatively consistent across the nucleic-acid sequences. Collectively, these results elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which hydration modulates local ion-polymer correlations and dynamic clustering in hybrid biopolymer-ionic liquid electrolytes, providing microscopic insights relevant to ionic conductivity and charge transport in hydrated soft materials.
papers.zh: 水化对ssDNA/ssRNA-离子液体电解质中离子溶剂化壳结构和阳离子缔合的影响

papers.title: Protonation-Coupled Rewiring of the Hydrogen-Bond Network Underlies Allosteric Dysfunction in the ALS-Linked K76E Mutant of Cyclophilin A
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The recently discovered K76E mutation in cyclophilin A (PPIA) is associated with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet the atomic-level mechanism driving its dysfunction remains elusive. Using constant pH molecular dynamics (CpHMD) simulations, we find that the distal K76E substitution is accompanied by changes in the protonation states of key histidine residues and in their local conformational environment. Because these protonation populations derive from a single 100 ns CpHMD trajectory per system, they may be sensitive to limited conformational sampling, and we treat them as provisional assignments rather than as converged equilibrium properties. In microsecond-scale fixed-charge simulations with these assignments, the hydrogen-bonding network around the active site is reorganized and the occupancy of contacts near the catalytic site is altered. The catalytic gatekeeper loops become more flexible and the correlation-based communication pathway linking the mutation site to the catalytic center is altered, without large-scale structural change. Our results suggest that coupled protonation–conformational changes, rather than direct active-site disruption, may contribute to the reduced activity of the K76E variant, underscoring the often-overlooked role of variable protonation states in disease-associated mutations; establishing this mechanism will require more extensive CpHMD sampling.
papers.zh: 氢键网络的质子化偶联重连是环孢霉素A的ALS-连接K76E突变体的变构功能障碍的基础

papers.title: Accurate Ionization Energies for MF and Characterization of the Low-Energy States of MF+ (M = Sc, Y, La)
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: A subset of monovalent metal fluorides have been identified as promising candidates for precision spectroscopic measurements that probe physics beyond the standard model. The interpretation of the precision data will require parameters that can only be derived from validated high-level electronic structure models. Recent calculations have focused on the use of ionization energies (IEs) as a means to evaluate the quality of the computational predictions. However, validation depends on the availability of accurate experimental data. In this study we report IE values for ScF, YF, and LaF. These were previously known with errors of ±0.3 eV. The present measurements yielded IEs of 6.6121(12), 6.6937(12), and 5.6104(12) eV, respectively. The two-photon ionization technique used for these measurements also permits the observation of the low-energy states of the MF+ cations. The vibronic structures established that the ground states were ScF+ X2Δ, YF+ X2Σ+, and LaF+ X2Δ. The IEs for ScF and LaF predicted by a recent computational study were significantly higher than the measured values. This discrepancy was traced to the fact that MF+ 2Σ+ ground states had been assumed. The computed IE for YF, where the cation does have a 2Σ+ ground state, was in good agreement with experiment.
papers.zh: MF的精确电离能和MF+（M = Sc、Y、La）低能态的表征

papers.title: DEGAUSS-3p: A Three-Site Water Model from Soft Gaussian-Charge Electrostatics and a Rare-Gas-Informed Double-Exponential Potential
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Classical fixed-charge water models combine point-charge Coulomb interactions, which diverge at short distances and neglect charge penetration, with a Lennard–Jones 12–6 repulsion whose r–12 dependence does not reflect the near-exponential decay of quantum-mechanical exchange repulsion. The DEGAUSS force field replaces both with finite, Gaussian-smeared charge densities and a double-exponential van der Waals potential, with adjustable short-range softness and rare-gas-informed starting values for the double-exponential exponents. DEGAUSS-3p is parametrized directly for liquid water using these interaction forms. The resulting rigid three-site model captures the density anomaly and tetrahedral organization of liquid water, with a balanced description of structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic properties. Gaussian electrostatics and double-exponential repulsion thus provide an effective basis for modeling liquid water with finite interactions at short distances.
papers.zh: DEGAUSS-3p：基于软高斯电荷静电学和稀有气体信息双指数势的叁位点水模型

papers.title: Free Energy Landscape Perturbation for Estimating Mutation-Induced Population Shifts from Reference Molecular Dynamics Ensembles
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Mutations can alter protein function by redistributing probability among conformational states, even when structural changes are modest. Directly estimating a perturbed conformational free energy landscape with molecular dynamics is expensive because each mutation requires a new converged simulation. Here, we introduce Free Energy Landscape Perturbation (FELP), a state-local reweighting framework that estimates mutation-induced population shifts from a reference ensemble. FELP partitions a reference trajectory into discrete microstates, evaluates restrained reference-to-perturbed energy differences for configurations sampled within each state, and combines spatially regularized state-local Zwanzig factors with the reference state probabilities to estimate the perturbed state distribution. FELP estimates how a perturbation changes the relative probabilities of conformational basins and reports effective-sample and overlap diagnostics that identify when the predicted shift lacks support in the sampled reference ensemble. We describe the FELP estimator, its implementation, and its performance on capped dipeptides, chignolin, T4 lysozyme, and the EGFR kinase domain. FELP is intended for perturbations that reshape populations within a sufficiently sampled reference landscape, providing a practical bridge between local alchemical energy evaluation and ensemble-level mechanistic interpretation.
papers.zh: 用于从参考分子动力学系综估计突变诱导的种群变化的自由能景观扰动

papers.title: How Molecular Packing Controls Electronic Structure in π-Stacked Radical Dimers: A DFT and Descriptor-Based Machine-Learning Study
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: π-Stacked radicals exhibit electronic properties that are highly sensitive to subtle changes in molecular packing, yet identifying which structural features control these interactions remains challenging. Here, we combine density functional theory calculations with chemically defined structural descriptors to quantify geometry−electronic structure relationships across 2,582 π-radical dimer configurations of five different polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) radical dimers. Extremely randomized trees and multilayer perceptron models predict fragment-orbital SOMO coupling, interaction energy, frontier-orbital separation, and the SOMO−SOMO interaction energy with test-set R2 values of 0.94−0.98 for radical families represented in training. Feature-importance analysis separates two structural regimes: global π-surface descriptors are most strongly associated with frontier-orbital variation and contribute to the interaction-energy scale, whereas local stacking registry and short C···C contact networks are most strongly associated with radical−radical coupling and corrected spin-dependent interaction energy. Comparison with a baseline that uses no structural descriptors shows that the frontier-orbital separation is largely set by the identity of the parent radical, whereas the two pancake-bonding properties are predicted from packing geometry alone and transfer to radical families absent from training. Y-randomization and geometry-clustered validation support the robustness of these relationships. This framework provides an interpretable, geometry-based route for evaluating and prioritizing packing arrangements in π-stacked radical dimers.
papers.zh: 分子堆积如何控制π堆积自由基二聚体的电子结构：基于DFT和描述符的机器学习研究

papers.title: Computational Mapping of Cholesterol-Binding Landscapes in TRPV6
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Cholesterol is an important regulator of membrane protein function, yet the molecular basis of its interaction with ion channels remains incompletely understood. This is particularly relevant for TRPV6, a highly Ca2+-selective epithelial ion channel essential for systemic calcium homeostasis, whose activity is influenced by membrane lipids. Here, a multiscale computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG-MD) simulations, molecular docking, and site identification by ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) was used to investigate cholesterol-interaction landscapes in TRPV6 across distinct conformational states. The three complementary approaches consistently identified recurrent cholesterol-interaction regions distributed throughout the transmembrane domain of TRPV6, particularly near the S1/S2 helices, the S4–S5 interface, and adjacent transmembrane segments. Although these interaction regions were largely conserved between open and closed conformations, cholesterol occupancy and interaction persistence differed between channel states. CG-MD simulations revealed spontaneous cholesterol-enriched regions within the membrane, SILCS identified energetically favorable interaction hotspots, and molecular docking defined preferred sterol docking sites. Together, these approaches provide a coherent description of cholesterol recognition across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Several computationally predicted interaction regions spatially overlapped with sterol-associated regions observed in cryo-EM structures of TRPV6, supporting their potential physiological relevance. Collectively, these findings indicate that cholesterol interaction with TRPV6 is distributed across multiple membrane-facing regions rather than a single dominant interaction site and is influenced by channel conformation. More broadly, this work demonstrates the value of integrating complementary computational approaches to investigate lipid–protein interactions and provides a molecular framework for understanding sterol regulation of TRPV6 and related TRP channels.
papers.zh: TRPV6中胆固醇结合位点的计算性绘图

papers.title: PriMPT: Prior-Informed Multiscale Paired-Token Representation Learning for CRISPR/Cas9 Off-Target Cleavage Activity Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Accurate prediction of CRISPR/Cas9 off-target cleavage activity requires molecular representations that explicitly capture the interaction compatibility between guide RNA and target DNA. This study presents PriMPT, a prior-informed multiscale paired-token representation learning framework that redesigns guide-target tokenization using 1-, 2-, and 3-gram paired tokens and injects mechanism-informed pair-prior descriptors into the corresponding embeddings through scale-specific gated injection, thereby incorporating RNA–DNA interaction information before contextual modeling and facilitating interaction-aware learning of guide-target compatibility. Across guide-disjoint cross-validation on six public data sets and a cross-data set external test, PriMPT achieved the numerically highest mean area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) among the evaluated models in each of the seven scenarios, with ablation studies identifying input-level pair-prior injection as the most consistent contributor and Integrated Gradients analysis yielding attribution patterns consistent with established aspects of Cas9 target recognition. These results suggest that PriMPT captures mechanism-relevant sequence-pair patterns and offers a mechanism-informed representation learning strategy for CRISPR/Cas9 off-target risk assessment.
papers.zh: PriMPT：用于预测 CRISPR/Cas9 脱靶切割活性的先验多尺度配对标记表示学习

papers.title: Long-Timescale Molecular Dynamics Reveal a Coordination-Biased Conformational Selection Mechanism for Sorcin Activation
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Sorcin is a dimeric penta-EF-hand Ca2+-binding protein that regulates intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis through Ca2+-dependent conformational activation and target recognition, and it has also been implicated in multidrug resistance in cancer. Although crystal structures have defined the apo inactive and Ca2+-bound active states of Sorcin, the transition pathways connecting these states and the conformational ensembles populated under each condition remain poorly understood. Here, we performed nine 10-μs all-atom molecular dynamics simulations (∼90 μs in total) on the special-purpose supercomputer Anton 3 to define the Ca2+-coupled conformational dynamics of dimeric human Sorcin. Starting from the Ca2+-bound structure, we directly observed the transition from the active to the inactive state following Ca2+ removal, indicating that loss of Ca2+ coordination is sufficient to drive inactivation on the microsecond timescale. Simulations initiated from the Ca2+-bound crystal structure with retained ions revealed ultrafast Ca2+ dissociation and rebinding at all EF-hand sites, indicating weak intrinsic Ca2+ affinity and highly dynamic ion exchange. In complementary simulations initiated from the apo structure, Sorcin spontaneously sampled active-like conformations even in the absence of stable Ca2+ binding, supporting a conformational selection mechanism in which Ca2+ shifts the population toward preexisting active states rather than inducing the transition de novo. Across all conditions, we observed pronounced and persistent structural asymmetry between the two protomers, revealing that the Sorcin homodimer is dynamically heterogeneous. Together, these results support a coordination–biased conformational selection model for Sorcin activation, in which weak and rapidly exchanging Ca2+ binding stabilizes, rather than induces, the active state. This work provides a dynamic framework for understanding Sorcin function as a fast Ca2+ sensor and offers broader mechanistic insight into activation principles of EF-hand Ca2+-binding proteins.
papers.zh: 长时间尺度分子动力学揭示了索辛活化的配位偏向构象选择机制

papers.title: HyperDFI: Cross-View Hypergraph-Graph Contrastive Learning for Drug-Food Interaction Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Drug-food interactions (DFIs) are one of the major factors that trigger adverse drug events and have important research and clinical application value. However, experimental identification of DFIs remains costly and limited in scalability, leading to insufficient coverage of known interactions. Existing computational methods often treat DFI prediction as a variant of drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction and primarily focus on drug-food constituent relationships, which restrict their ability to directly model drug-food interactions. In this study, we propose a cross-view hypergraph-graph contrastive learning framework named HyperDFI for predicting interactions between drug and food (food constituents). We first construct four benchmark data sets by integrating information from DrugBank and PubMed, covering both drug-food and drug-food constituent interactions. Based on these data sets, heterogeneous bipartite graphs were established. HyperDFI jointly captures local topological structures and global high-order semantic relationships by combining graph neural networks (GNNs) and dynamic hypergraph neural networks (HGNNs). Furthermore, a cross-view contrastive learning strategy is introduced to align representations at different structural scales, thereby enhancing their consistency and discriminability. Extensive experiments on four benchmark data sets demonstrate that HyperDFI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In addition, case studies on grapefruit further validate its ability to uncover novel DFIs.
papers.zh: HyperDFI：用于药物-食物相互作用预测的交叉视图超图-图对比学习

papers.title: A new generation of effective core potentials: Selected heavy 5 d and 6 p elements
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We expand the correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) library by developing semi-local pseudopotentials and matching basis sets for heavy elements from 5d (Hf, Os, Hg) and 6p (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. To accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin–orbit coupling, and electron correlation effects, we implement a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy across three distinct resolutions. This includes a small 60-core (Hf, Os, Hg) that explicitly correlates subvalence shells, a large 78-core definition for the main-group elements that rigorously accounts for core polarization and relaxation effects in sparse valence environments, and an intermediate 68-core partition for Hg and Tl. This 68-core architecture represents a unique development in the ccECP library, optimizing the balance between accuracy and computational efficiency in a manner unexplored for lighter elements. Optimized against relativistic all-electron coupled-cluster theory with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples references, the ccECPs deliver outstanding atomic precision, achieving a global average atomic low-lying states deviation of just 0.045 eV. This accuracy translates directly to robust molecular transferability, systematically restricting dissociation energy discrepancies to under 0.03 eV and equilibrium bond lengths to within 0.005 Å. By enforcing a regularized, finite potential at the origin for enhanced numerical stability in stochastic quantum Monte Carlo methods, this library removes a critical methodological bottleneck for predictive many-body simulations of heavy-element systems and materials.
papers.zh: 新一代有效核心电势：选定的重5 d和6 p元素

papers.title: Adsorption of patchy colloids on a patchy surface: A combined thermodynamic perturbation theory and Henderson–Abraham–Barker approach
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Reversible binding of ligands to their substrates is a common refrain in physics, chemistry, and other disciplines that features prominently in problems as diverse as the binding of proteins to membranes or passivating ligands depositing onto quantum dots. Here, we introduce a theoretical formalism to describe this phenomenon analytically with the help of very basic physical concepts. We assume that the ligands can be modeled as spherical particles that interact with each other via an attractive patch placed rigidly on their surface. The ligands are located above an infinite impenetrable surface with which they also interact via attractive patches. Therefore, the proposed model captures excluded volume of ligands, confinement in space, and adsorption to planes mediated by attractive forces—the three basic properties common to all complexation processes near surfaces. The Wertheim thermodynamic perturbation theory for associating fluids is extended to the proposed model utilizing the Henderson–Abraham–Barker-type approach. Analytical expressions are derived for the surface coverage as a function of various parameters such as temperature, ligand density, and others. Computer simulations are performed to test and confirm the accuracy of the theoretical predictions. Increasing ligand density is seen to enhance the surface coverage, while ligand–ligand interactions always lead to surface destabilization. Similarly, sticky patches on a surface in close proximity to each other negatively affect its ligand coverage. Our findings add new insight to the basic understanding of ligand–surface interactions, suggesting that the proposed model can be used as a powerful tool with which to design and analyze new surface-based materials.
papers.zh: 不均匀胶体在不均匀表面上的吸附：结合热力学微扰理论和Henderson–Abraham–Barker方法

papers.title: Combining exponential expansion theory with Bayesian inference for the analysis of inelastic scattering spectra
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Over the past decade, advances in inelastic x-ray and neutron scattering instrumentation have created a demand for probabilistically grounded data analysis. To address this, we proposed a Bayesian method that uses Monte Carlo techniques and a reversible jump routine to support the determination of the number of modes that contribute to the spectrum of density fluctuations S(Q, ω). So far, a similar approach has been applied to models that fail to satisfy the proper sum rules governing the moments of the distribution S(Q, ω), typically consisting of multiple damped harmonic oscillator modes, along with additional central peaks. We show that applying Bayesian inference to an exponential expansion theory-based model, which explicitly enforces the relevant sum rules, provides a rigorous and physically constrained framework for the analysis and interpretation of experimental spectra. In particular, this result enables analysis of the complex and relatively unstructured shape of terahertz inelastic spectra of disordered systems.
papers.zh: 将指数展开理论与贝叶斯推断相结合，用于分析非弹性散射谱

papers.title: Dilute-regime polymer thermophoresis from coil to globule via molecular dynamics simulations
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Particles (molecules, colloids, polymers, etc.) in solution migrate along a temperature gradient in a process called thermophoresis, thermodiffusion, or the Soret effect. Experiments have revealed many striking behaviors in dilute polymer solutions, including sign changes and extrema in the Soret coefficient ST as a function of solvent quality. We investigate the phenomenology of dilute-regime polymer thermophoresis using a minimal particle-based model that interpolates between a swollen coil and a compact globule, simulating various chain lengths. Our model exhibits sign changes in ST as a function of solvent quality, from thermophilic (ST < 0) to thermophobic (ST > 0) behavior, in both the good-solvent and poor-solvent regimes. To our knowledge, the latter has not been previously reported and occurs when increasing the monomer–monomer attraction. We correlate the increase/decrease of ST with that of the negative solvation entropy. Furthermore, our results highlight that the difference between the thermophoretic and drift velocities can be large, even for relatively large polymers approaching the long-polymer limit. We observe the counter-intuitive situation of a net drift against the direction of particle accumulation for portions of the good-, Θ-, and poor-solvent regimes.
papers.zh: 通过分子动力学模拟实现的从线团到小球的稀溶液体系聚合物热泳

papers.title: Vibrational spectra and anharmonic coupling of the O–H stretch in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline: Insights from constrained nuclear–electronic orbital theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Hydrogen bonds can exhibit pronounced nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) that strongly influence proton-transfer dynamics. 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ) is a prototypical excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) system with a strong intramolecular hydrogen bond, and its vibrational spectra and anharmonic mode couplings have recently attracted considerable interest. Here, we use constrained nuclear–electronic orbital density functional theory (CNEO-DFT) and molecular dynamics (CNEO-MD), which account for NQEs, particularly nuclear quantum delocalization effects, to investigate the O–H stretching vibration (νOH) of HBQ and its anharmonic coupling with other modes in the ground state. The νOH frequency calculated by CNEO-DFT agrees closely with the experiment, and CNEO-MD reproduces the characteristic finger-like structure of the infrared spectrum. Normal mode frequency shift analysis and CNEO-MD simulations with resonant νOH excitation consistently identify several low-frequency in-plane backbone bending modes that are strongly coupled to the νOH. Taken together, this work establishes a detailed understanding of the ground-state vibrational spectrum and νOH mode couplings in HBQ, providing a basis for further investigation of their roles in ESIPT dynamics.
papers.zh: 10-羟基苯并[h]喹啉中O–H伸缩振动的振动谱和非谐耦合：受限核-电子轨道理论的见解

papers.title: In quest of reaching minimum enthalpy
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The formation of glasses is inherently a non-equilibrium process in which the final state depends on the thermal history. In variable-cooling-rate glass annealing, where identifying the precise moment of glass transition becomes ambiguous, the concept of a glass transition interval has been put forward. By formulating glass formation during non-steady cooling from the liquid to the glassy state as a time-constrained enthalpy minimization, we derive a simple explicit solution for the optimal cooling rate within the framework of a single-relaxation-time model. By exploiting a one-to-one correspondence between enthalpy and fictive temperature, we demonstrate that minimizing the final enthalpy is equivalent to minimizing the limiting fictive temperature, independent of the cooling path. The optimal solution acquires a physical interpretation via the phenomenological glass transition criteria, normalized using a conventional standard cooling rate. The glass formation criterion standardization highlights the constant-cooling-rate dependence of the glass transition temperature as experimental evidence for an Arrhenius-type structural relaxation time in the glass transition region. Our theoretical results, including suboptimal cooling protocols and a universal scaling of the differential scanning calorimetry heat capacity curve, establish a basis for the rational design and optimization of glass annealing and suggest a reinterpretation of experimental measurements of the glass transition region.
papers.zh: 力求达到最小焓值

papers.title: Tilt control of coverage heterogeneity for hard spherocylinders locked on a sphere
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We study hard spherocylinders on a sphere with axes rigidly locked to a tangential director field at fixed angle ω to the meridian, necessarily singular at the poles. Three lengths set the problem: the rod length ℓ, the diameter D, and the host radius Rs. Monte Carlo simulations across 15 geometries and four coverages give two main results for the polar marginal, the azimuthal average of rod-center density. First, the tilt is a continuous handle on the width of the depleted region that packing induces around each singularity. Under meridian locking it is set principally by the rod length; turning the director toward the latitude contracts it substantially, the contraction being spent well before latitude locking. Second, how uniform the polar marginal can be made is limited by geometry, not tilt. The smallest variance on the sampled grid follows an empirical power law in ℓ2/(RsD), which measures how far a straight rod’s ends stand off the curved surface in rod diameters, with an effective exponent between 1.10 and 1.31. Long rods on small hosts cannot be made uniform at any sampled tilt; the remedy is geometric, not orientational. The polar marginal is equator-heavy almost everywhere, inverting only at high coverage and tilt; meridian locking is the least uniform choice, and the variance-minimizing tilt usually lies in a sampled band from 31.7° to 55°. Both results describe the infinitely locked athermal ensemble.
papers.zh: 锁定在球体上的硬球柱覆盖异质性的倾斜控制

papers.title: Pressure and temperature dependence of hydrogen-induced volume in fcc nickel hydride
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: In transition-metal hydrides, hydrogen occupies interstitial sites in the metal lattice, resulting in significant volume expansion. The difference in unit-cell volume between the metal and its hydride is denoted as hydrogen-induced volume (vH), and this value has been determined for various metal hydrides. However, systematic investigations of its effects on thermoelastic properties under pressure (P) and temperature (T) are scarce, and the P–T-dependence of vH is poorly constrained. Here, we report the P–V–T relations of nickel hydride (H/Ni ∼ 1) with a face-centered cubic structure, which is frequently observed in 3d transition metals and their hydrides. We collected x-ray diffraction data on nickel hydride at 7–16 GPa and 300–1000 K and determined its equations of state. We also conducted a melting experiment at 15 GPa and observed melting at 1450 K. The results show that nickel hydride is more compressible than pure Ni and exhibits a large thermal expansion, resulting in a negative dependence on pressure and a positive dependence on temperature of vH. This behavior originates from the reduction in bulk modulus and Debye temperature by hydrogenation, suggesting that interstitial H atoms weaken the Ni–Ni bonds through lattice expansion and possibly also through phonon softening, as evidenced by comparison at equivalent volumes.
papers.zh: 面心立方镍氢化物中氢致体积的压力和温度依赖性

papers.title: Slowing down of carrier dynamics via temperature-controlled phase transition in two-dimensional ferroelectric CuInP2S6
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The relaxation and recombination of photoexcited carriers directly determine the performance of optoelectronic devices and photocatalysts, and ferroelectric materials with spontaneous polarization may offer a unique route for modulating carrier lifetimes. Two-dimensional CuInP2S6 (CIPS) exhibits ferroelectricity at room temperature. However, the mechanism by which the temperature-induced ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition modulates the carrier dynamics in CIPS remains unclear. Herein, second-harmonic generation measurements are combined with broadband ultrafast spectroscopy to directly resolve temperature-induced phase transition in CIPS, clarifying how carrier dynamics evolve in the ferroelectric phase vs the paraelectric phase. Near the phase-transition region, the carrier lifetime exhibits a sudden and nearly twofold increase when transitioning from the paraelectric phase to the ferroelectric phase. By contrast, the carrier lifetime is only weakly affected by temperature outside this region. Electronic structure calculations and Raman spectroscopy indicate that the change in carrier lifetime is related not only to the intrinsic polarization field in the ferroelectric phase but is also closely associated with phase transition-induced modifications in the electron and phonon structures. The findings of this study provide a mechanistic basis for developing temperature-tunable and polarization-controlled behaviors for a broad range of light-related applications.

papers.title: Asynchronous structural rearrangements govern constriction of the human nuclear pore complex
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) is responsible for transport between the cytoplasm and nucleus. Cryogenic electron tomography experiments have resolved multiple conformations of the pore, in which it is dilated or constricted. Since the dilation state will impact transport properties, there is much interest in understanding the energetic factors that regulate dilation/constriction. To this end, we applied a structure-based (Go¯-like) model to study the mechanistic properties of large-scale constriction (∼100 Å) in the human NPC. Even though the structures are symmetric, the simulations implicate asynchronous rearrangements during constriction. By considering variants of the model, we further characterize the relative contributions of individual proteins to this collective process. We show that constriction is largely driven by a small subset of the NPC components. This provides an energetic/structural foundation that can guide development of precise physical approaches for studying this elusive motion.

papers.title: Atomic softness: The inherent empirical parameter calculated analytically for an atom-in-molecule by the conceptual DFT method
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: By exploring our previously published gradient theorem [P. Ordon and L. Komorowski, in Chemical Reactivity: Volume 1: Theories and Principles, edited by S. Kaya, L. von Szentpaly, G. Serdaroglu, and L. Guo (Elsevier, 2023), Chap. 9], that provides a relationship of the gradient of the electron density function and the electric field with the softness kernel as the response function, we introduce the method for analytical calculation of the local softness as the trace of the electronic softness tensor and the global softness index of a molecule is obtained by its integration. The atomic contributions to the global softness have also been calculated analytically. These softness parameters for bonded atoms have been tested as the potential indicators of site reactivity in a collection of linear molecules. The analysis has been extended to the rational hypersoftness parameter dsr/dNv, the leading factor for calculations of the local hypersoftness s2r as well as the atomic contributions thereof.

papers.title: Vibrationally assisted dissociative ionization of H2+ in orthogonal laser fields
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We present full-dimensional quantum simulations of H2+ dissociative ionization driven by strong orthogonal laser fields. We consider equal-frequency orthogonal components, which generate elliptical or circular polarization, depending on their relative phase and amplitude, as well as orthogonal 800 and 400 nm two-color fields. These two-dimensional fields strongly modify the fragmentation dynamics. Most notably, a secondary proton kinetic-energy-release (KER) peak at approximately 4–5 eV, generally negligible in height relative to the main peak in the single-color, linearly polarized reference, is strongly enhanced by the orthogonal fields studied here and becomes pronounced and comparable in height with the main peak. The yield of this peak can be coherently controlled by varying the relative carrier-envelope phase of the perpendicular field component. The perpendicular field also disrupts the clear electron–proton energy-sharing pattern observed in the main 3–3.5 eV dissociation channel, indicating more complex multichannel dynamics. Time-dependent state projections and calculations initiated from individual excited states attribute the additional peak to laser-induced vibrational excitation of H2+. The added high-KER yield provides a concrete microscopic mechanism that may contribute to the broader, flatter proton KER distribution observed experimentally under circular polarization, even when the secondary peak is not individually resolved. Furthermore, the perpendicular field rotates the fragment angular distributions, causing the most probable proton and electron emission directions to deviate substantially from the principal z axis. These findings demonstrate that the spatial and temporal geometry of orthogonal laser fields provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling ultrafast electron–nuclear dynamics.

papers.title: Water layers on ice submerged in antifreeze liquid: Nano-forcemetry
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Ice is an important material on Earth. However, despite the extensive research conducted on ice surfaces exposed to vacuum or vapor, studies of liquid–ice interfaces are limited. In this study, we used an atomic force microscope cooled to −10 °C to observe force–distance curves at the interfaces of ice and four antifreeze liquids: decane, octane, octanol, and saltwater (an aqueous solution of NaCl). The approach force curves recorded in decane and octane indicated the presence of liquid water layers on the ice wafers. Based on our accumulated knowledge of vacuum–ice interfaces, we hypothesized that the free OH groups on the ice exposed to the liquid alkanes would induce surface disordering of the ice and form a water layer. Force–distance curves observed in octanol and saltwater suggested that the ice wafers were directly exposed to these liquids without a water layer in between. The surface disordering of the ice may have been prevented in these liquids because they can form hydrogen bonds with the OH groups on the ice.

papers.title: Electrowetting: Contact angle saturation induced by non-local surface excess free energy
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Contact-angle saturation limits the high-voltage response of electrowetting-on-dielectric systems, but it is not captured by the classical Young–Lippmann relation. Here, we develop a composition-dependent interfacial energy-landscape model in which the liquid-covered and gas-covered parts of the substrate are described by adsorption-layer states with composition-dependent free energies and capacitive responses. The Young–Lippmann behavior is recovered at low voltage, while saturation emerges when the gas-covered adsorption layer becomes liquid-rich and the electrical contributions to the solid–liquid and solid–gas interfacial free energies decrease synchronously. The model provides analytical expressions for the onset voltage, saturation voltage, and saturated contact angle and separates the voltage scale from the terminal interfacial-energy contrast. Comparison with experimental data shows that the normalized electrowetting response is consistent with the proposed interfacial transition pathway. The resulting energy landscape can also contain metastable states, giving rise to path-dependent behavior during voltage withdrawal. Together, these results indicate that variations in the underlying interfacial parameters can regulate both the terminal wetting state and the overall electrowetting response.

papers.title: Next generation of ultra-coarse-graining: Self-consistent inference of critical internal states
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Bottom-up coarse-graining systematically expands the length and effective timescales accessible to molecular dynamics simulations, but the information loss during coarse-graining can prevent an accurate incorporation of the multistate phenomena common in complex biomolecular dynamics. The Ultra-Coarse-Graining (UCG) method projects the influence of discrete “quantum-like” extended degrees of freedom, “internal states,” onto the coarse-grained (CG) mapped molecules, significantly extending the expressiveness of the CG model. The previous rapid-local-equilibrium (RLE) approximation in UCG depends on user-defined collective variables (CVs, e.g., local density) and does not incorporate correlations between internal states within and between CG molecules. We present Self-Consistent UCG (SC-UCG), an integrated methodology that utilizes the underlying UCG interactions directly for internal state designation, without designing collective variables in the CG ensemble. For simulations, the internal state probabilities are self-consistently determined via graph message-passing in simulation time. We also enhance the RLE Hamiltonian with the Bethe approximation plus AI-based inference to allow explicit internal state correlations between UCG beads. For forcefield training, we develop Multilayer Internal State Consistency, a machine-learning-based method derived from the relative entropy minimization principle that does not require iterative sampling of the intermediate forcefields. We then apply SC-UCG to a model tetramer system with a second-order symmetry-breaking phase transition from the supercritical racemic fluid into subcritical D-rich and L-rich fluids. We show that SC-UCG can capture collective switching events of internal UCG states in the subcritical region, and it exhibits temperature transferability by recapitulating the phase transition, even if trained from a single-temperature dataset.

papers.title: GW reduced density matrix from iterated linearized Dyson equation
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Iterating the Dyson equation with the static part of the self-energy leads to a concise and possibly improved expression of the one-body reduced density matrix from any self-energy approximation. Here, we apply the procedure to Hedin’s GW approximation. The non-iterated GW-based density matrix was already known to yield accurate density matrices for molecular systems. We show that the Dyson-equation-based procedure is equivalent to the so-called variational Z-vector approach applied to the random-phase approximation energy functional, but only in the case of a Hartree–Fock mean-field starting point. When a generalized Kohn–Sham scheme is employed instead, the two approaches differ. By comparing the density matrix for a benchmark set of 34 small molecules to coupled-cluster reference values, we conclude that the iterated Dyson equation indeed produces improved density matrices for molecular systems. Interestingly, we observe that the excitation rank of the reference coupled-cluster matters much and that the inclusion of triple excitations quantitatively changes the conclusions of the benchmark compared to single and double excitations coupled-cluster.

papers.title: Disorder-induced dark states line shape in pump-probe spectroscopy of polaritons
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The formation of hybrid light–matter states called polaritons provides a route to shape the photophysics and photochemistry of molecules. Accordingly, the dynamics of polaritons following photoexcitation is extensively studied. In particular, the role of the dark state manifold in such processes remains unclear. Here, we investigate the line shape of pump–probe spectra of polaritons emerging at the dark states energy under the influence of disorder. Previously, we already investigated the pump–probe line shapes of polaritons in a disorder-free model and identified distinct signatures of relaxation into dark states, thus providing an indirect probe of this relaxation. Since the transition dipole moment of dark states vanishes in a disorder-free model, they cannot be directly probed. However, dark states acquire small transition dipole moments as soon as disorder is explicitly included in the model, enabling them to be directly probed. In this work, we demonstrate that the inclusion of the relaxation to dark states and disorder leads to the evolution of the spectral shape at the dark states energy from a derivative-like into an absorptive line shape. Furthermore, we investigate the dependence of the line shape on the disorder strength and its asymptotic scaling for a large number of coupled molecules. Our results demonstrate that probing dark states can help to single out the polaritonic response from the total signal.

papers.title: Water–ice coexistence under nanoscale confinement revealed by magnetization-transfer NMR
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Low-temperature ice–liquid phase coexistence and nuclear magnetization exchange dynamics of water confined in the ordered mesoporous silica material KIT-5 were investigated by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The temporal evolution of the magnetization following the preparation of non-equilibrium spin states was measured over a range of temperatures to quantify magnetization exchange between the coexisting ice and liquid phases. The analysis of the NMR spectra yielded the phase fractions, spectral linewidths, and magnetization dynamics of both phases. The equilibrium phase fractions were used to determine the temperature dependence of the non-frozen layer thickness separating the silica surface from the ice core, which was found to be in good agreement with theoretical predictions. The magnetization exchange kinetics were quantitatively described by a diffusion model, yielding an effective diffusion coefficient in the order of 10−16 m2/s for magnetization transport within the confined ice phase. Spin diffusion rates were estimated independently using several complementary approaches to assess the relative contributions of spin diffusion and molecular diffusion. While these estimates constrain the possible mechanisms of magnetization exchange, they do not permit an unambiguous separation of the spin diffusion and molecular diffusion contributions, suggesting that confinement-induced structural disorder may play an important role in magnetization transport in nanoconfined ice.

papers.title: Run-and-tumble particles in a harmonic external field: Constructing the solution of the Fokker–Planck equation from the equations of motion
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: A method for integrating the Langevin equations of motion for run-and-tumble particles is introduced to compute the joint distribution of their position and active velocity, with and without a harmonic external force field. The key step is the construction of the moments of the distribution and the correlation functions, conditional on the particles being in a specific state at the final time. For one-dimensional run-and-tumble particles in a harmonic external potential, the exact steady-state distributions for the tumble state, as well as for the run state conditional on a specified velocity direction, are obtained. This enables us to demonstrate their equivalence to the exact solutions of the corresponding Fokker–Planck equations.

papers.title: Unveiling structural bottlenecks of dynamic disorder in a density-tunable glass former: From strong to fragile regimes
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Fragility characterizes how rapidly a glass-forming liquid slows down upon supercooling, but whether strong and fragile behaviors arise from the same microscopic relaxation mechanism remains unclear. Here, we address this question using a density-tunable soft-repulsive binary mixture spanning distinct fragility regimes and analyze particle jump dynamics within the framework of dynamic disorder. Across these regimes, we show that increasing fragility is accompanied by progressively broader cage-lifetime distributions and increasingly non-exponential survival probabilities, revealing non-Poisson cage-to-jump statistics governed by fluctuating jump rates and slowly evolving structural variables. To characterize their structural origin, we first identify the neighbor ranks most strongly coupled to jump motion using Kullback–Leibler divergence and Pearson correlation analyses. We then introduce a structural slowness parameter that combines these neighbor-distance fluctuations into a reduced slow coordinate for constructing the slow-fluctuation survival probability. A comparison with the actual survival probability shows that localized neighbor-distance fluctuations control the jump rate in the strong regime, whereas extended neighbor rearrangements become relevant in the intermediate and fragile regimes, increasing the effective dimensionality of the slow-variable space. In the fragile regime, distance-based descriptors alone become insufficient at the lowest temperature, where the Voronoi free volume captures additional cage-volume fluctuations in the rate-controlling slow variable. Point-to-set correlations (PTS) grow with fragility, but the spatial extent of the slow variables exceeds the PTS length. These results reveal how the structural bottleneck for microscopic rate fluctuations evolves across density-tuned fragility regimes, linking dynamic disorder, multidimensional slow variables, and static correlations in glass-forming liquids.

papers.title: A self-consistent model for phase separation and active processes in biomolecular condensates
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Biomolecular condensates are thought to play a pivotal role in cellular organization by regulating biochemical reactants in space and time. Sustained molecular fluxes across condensate boundaries, together with the participation of phase-separating molecules in active chemical reactions such as ATP hydrolysis, call for a non-equilibrium description. Here, we propose a self-consistent framework in which diffusion–drift dynamics and chemical reactions are coupled through a conditional free energy, defined as the excess contribution to the chemical potential. Self-consistency is achieved by deriving this quantity from the same free-energy functional that governs molecular interactions and phase separation. We apply the framework to a minimal client–scaffold system and investigate how active chemical processes and phase separation interact at steady state. In doing so, our approach recovers the fundamental rules previously identified for the emergence of non-equilibrium steady-state fluxes. The model shows that active reactions involving the scaffold molecules can regulate the phase behavior of the condensate. Moreover, non-equilibrium steady-state fluxes are maximal near the boundary between the phase-separated and homogeneous regimes, suggesting that condensates sustaining molecular transport may operate close to their stability threshold. In the same region, client fluxes are also enhanced, revealing an indirect coupling between scaffold activity and client transport. These results provide a baseline for developing more detailed theories of chemically active condensates.

papers.title: Molecular rotor in copper borozene Cu4B8: A freely rotating σ-aromatic tetrahedral Cu4 core atop a boron wheel
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We identify two-layered Cu4B8 clusters featuring tetrahedral Cu4 units anchored on B8 boron wheels as global minima. A substantial charge transfer from Cu4 to the B8 wheel is observed, resulting in a charge distribution close to the idealized [Cu42+] [B82−] electron-counting scheme. AdNDP analysis reveals two delocalized σ-electrons within the quasi-tetrahedral Cu4 unit, identifying it as one of the simplest σ-aromatic motifs. The B82− wheels exhibit dual (6π + 6σ) aromaticity, serving as boron analogs of benzene (“borozene”). Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulations show pronounced fluxionality, with nearly barrierless Cu4 rotation (∼0.01 kcal/mol) enabled by an ultrasoft vibrational mode. The delocalized electronic structure of the B8 wheel contributes to the facile Cu4 rotation, while electrostatic and dative interactions stabilize the two-layer framework. These results identify electroneutral Cu4B8 as a prototypical copper–borozene cluster combining aromatic stabilization and dynamic fluxionality, offering a promising model for molecular rotor.

papers.title: Anchored Brownian motion and Bayesian methods for the analysis of single particle tracking data
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We present a novel statistical method and a prototype computational implementation for estimating the diffusion coefficient from single particle tracking (SPT) data. Our method is based on anchored Brownian motion, which is a novel representation that relaxes the restrictions of conventional Brownian motion. In particular, rather than forcing the trajectories under analysis to pass through a fixed spatiotemporal origin that can bias SPT inference, our model introduces an explicit anchoring time and position that are uncertain and estimated simultaneously with the other quantities of SPT interest, avoiding the introduction of bias. Our method is fully developed in Bayesian terms and allows for robust estimation of the diffusion coefficient and quantification of the uncertainty propagated from limited data quantity and quality as appropriate for the analysis of live-cell SPT data. We compare our methods with conventional Brownian motion and demonstrate superior performance in estimating the correct value of the diffusion coefficient. Finally, we benchmark our methods with SPT data from in cellulo and in silico experiments.

papers.title: Different paths, same purpose: How antifreeze proteins stop ice crystals from growing
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: To survive in freezing environments, different organisms have evolved a remarkable class of proteins, known as antifreeze proteins (AFPs), which inhibit the growth of internal ice crystals. Due to their ability to function at trace concentrations, AFPs are being explored for wide-ranging applications, from cryopreservation to food storage. However, AFP structure–activity relationships are incredibly complex and remain poorly understood, constituting a bottleneck in our efforts to translate the vast untapped potential of these evolutionary marvels. Complicating things further, AFPs derived from insects and fish perform the exact same function—inhibiting ice growth—using two fundamentally different mechanisms. This mechanistic dichotomy results in different failure modes and, correspondingly, in different structure–function relationships. This perspective seeks to shed light on how different AFPs use different mechanisms to achieve the same objective while highlighting gaps that remain in our understanding of how AFPs function.

papers.title: Tunable electron and spin transfer from ionized polythiophene oligomers encapsulated in cycling hydrocarbons: A combined DFT and EPR approach
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of thiophene oligomer ions, which possess polarons excited on their main axis and are encapsulated within polyaromatic cyclic hydrocarbons, were investigated using density functional theory and electron paramagnetic resonance methods. Charge and spin densities, analyzed using Mulliken and Löwdin population analyses, reveal how cyclic rings locally affect the effective parameters of the dual organic π-systems. The energy gap of these composites depends on their structure and the reorientation of the polaron spin in a magnetic field and was identified as a key feature to tune electronic and magnetic properties. The appearance of equidistant peaks in population and energy dependencies was explained in terms of the concept of magic numbers, which are linked to symmetrical and conjugated clusters. Anisotropic hyperfine coupling and g-factor eigenvalues were shown to depend on the ionic charge and spin orientation in a magnetic field, as well as on the structural properties of the surrounding cyclic belt. Separate intermolecular transfer of electronic and spin clouds to the surrounding subsystem could potentially be used for independent control of the corresponding processes in all-organic molecular devices. This could provide a foundation for designing electronic and spintronic components with independently controlled charge and spin parameters.

papers.title: Concerted mass transport governs anomalous diffusion in dynamically-stabilized bcc metals
papers.jname: npj Computational Materials
papers.abs: Understanding the microscopic origin of anomalous self-diffusion near melting remains a central challenge in bcc metals. Here we combine ab initio and machine-learning interatomic-potential molecular dynamics (AIMD, MLIP-MD) to elucidate high-temperature mass transport in group-3–6 metals. Comparative AIMD simulations near melting at ambient pressure reveal a marked difference in mass-transport behavior between dynamically-stabilized group-3 and group-4 bcc metals and group-5 and group-6 metals; for which bcc is the intrinsically stable structure. In the former, characterized by strongly anharmonic energy landscapes, sufficiently large thermal displacements of individual atoms trigger cascades of cooperative transport, including ring exchanges and spontaneous formation and migration of vacancy–crowdion-like Frenkel pairs. In contrast, diffusion in group-5 and group-6 metals remains dominated by conventional vacancy mechanisms. Temperature-dependent MLIP-MD simulations of bcc Ti further show Arrhenius-like migration of isolated point defects upon cooling toward dynamical instability. Near melting, collective reactions in nominally pristine lattice regions provide an additional transport channel contributing to non-Arrhenius self-diffusion. Structural analysis reveals transient ω-like local environments as fingerprints of lattice softening accompanying these correlated dynamics. These results identify strong lattice anharmonicity as a key factor promoting collective transport in bcc metals and suggest a broader framework for high-temperature transport in crystalline solids.

papers.title: Surface Leaky Transverse-Magnetic (TM)-Mode Resonance and Photonic-Enhanced Photoluminescence in Shallow Subwavelength Silicon Gratings
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: All-dielectric shallow silicon subwavelength gratings (SWGs) are demonstrated as a powerful platform for overcoming the fundamental waveguiding cutoffs of conventional bound transverse-magnetic (TM) modes, enabling strong light-matter interactions directly at the SWG-ambient interface. By leveraging laser interference lithography to fabricate ultrashallow silicon profiles, this work uncovers a unique regime where angle-dependent resonant anomalies emerge not from core-confined guided modes, but from the deliberate excitation of polarization-sensitive surface leaky modes operating strictly at the Wood–Rayleigh diffraction threshold. Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations validate that this threshold configuration can act as a giant electromagnetic energy concentrator at the interface, driving asymmetric Fano resonances and producing an exceptional enhancement of the local density of optical states along the grating ridges. Under p-polarized ultraviolet excitation, this localized field distribution triggers a dramatic Purcell acceleration of radiative decay pathways, enabling the detection of intense room-temperature photoluminescence from submonolayer organic residues with a giant ∼2 eV Stokes shift, resulting in an emission that is entirely quenched on unpatterned bulk silicon. These findings elucidate the physical mechanism of threshold-driven field localization in open dielectric nanostructures and highlight their transformative potential for ultrasensitive, label-free biomolecular optical detection.

papers.title: Interfacial and Diffusive Electronic Energy Transfer from Molecular Monomers to Aggregates
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Understanding microscopic mechanisms of electronic energy transfer and transport in organic semiconductors is crucial to their optoelectronic and photochemical applications. Yet the mechanisms are often strongly complicated by the entangled factors such as intermolecular coupling, structural fluctuations, energetic disorder and molecular aggregation. In particular, molecular aggregates reorganize the excitonic energy landscape and introduce additional pathways for energy relaxation. Here we identify a system where optically dark, H-like aggregates of boron dipyrromethene spontaneously formed in polymer films can function as energy sink for photoexcited monomers. By combining concentration-dependent and polarization-resolved ultrafast measurements, we identify two sequential energy migration processes: a relatively slow diffusive energy transport occurring through intermonomer exciton hopping, and a rapid (subps) interfacial monomer-to-aggregate energy transfer. Temperature-dependent measurements down to 1.7 K reveal that while intermonomer hopping is suppressed with decreasing temperature, interfacial energy transfer is instead accelerated.

papers.title: Pump-Guided Directional Amplification of Spontaneous Emission in Single-Crystal MAPbBr3
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: We report directional amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in a MAPbBr3 single crystal, which is produced by a single-pass excitation of femtosecond pulses at 560 nm and propagates coaxially with the pump beam during amplification interactions. The chirp in the pump pulses induces a delayed interaction between the photoluminescence (PL) produced by the shorter wavelength components and the excitation by the longer wavelength components, forming a “chasing–overlapping–leaving” process. The group velocity dispersion performance on the falling edge of the absorption spectrum of the MAPbBr3 crystal favors a large extension of the interaction length, facilitating such an ASE process along the pumping channel. The ASE interactions produce a yellow beam with a peak wavelength of 575 nm and a pulse energy of 0.47 nJ for a pump pulse energy of 1.2 μJ. The output ASE beam has the same quality as the pump in the small divergence and high-quality transverse mode.

papers.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment–protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic–vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pigment compositions of CP29 and Lhcb1, a monomeric subunit of the major LHCII trimer, reshape excitonic connectivity and energy transfer pathways in the complexes. Compared to Lhcb1, energy transfer pathways in CP29 are more spatially connected and reversible, suggesting that CP29 evolved to distribute excitation between the core and periphery of the PSII antenna. We find that small structural modifications from a common framework tune CP29 and Lhcb1 to complementary roles in the PSII supercomplex.

papers.title: Photoinduced Ligand Displacement of Semiconductor Nanomaterials
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Organic ligands at the surface of colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are usually assumed to remain anchored during optical processes. Recent time-resolved spectroscopic studies overturn this assumption: photoexcitation can displace ligands from the NC surface through photoinduced charge transfer. Because conventional ligand exchange is bound by thermodynamic equilibrium, such light-driven displacement offers on-demand, out-of-equilibrium control of the ligand shell, with implications for photocatalysis, photopatterning, and the photostability of NC-based devices. In this Perspective, we outline the fundamentals of NC–ligand surface chemistry and of the charge-transfer processes that trigger desorption, survey the growing experimental evidence─from time-resolved infrared studies of carboxylate ligands to our work using π-conjugated perylene bisimide ligands as sensitive optical reporters of desorption─and discuss the emerging quantum-chemical picture of the dissociation. We conclude with design rules and open questions toward photocontrolled NC surfaces.

papers.title: Confining Single-Atom Cobalt Sustains Singlet Oxygen-Driven Aniline Oxidative Coupling toward Azobenzene
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Direct oxidative coupling of anilines represents an atom-economical route to valuable azobenzenes, yet its practical deployment is severely restricted by the uncontrolled generation of chaotic radical species and the rapid degradation of catalysts under harsh oxidative environments. Herein, we demonstrate that a precisely tailored confining microenvironment enables selective control over reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, overriding the conventional chaotic radical pathway. With a single-atom cobalt catalyst anchored on nanodiamonds and encapsulated within a ZIF-8 derived NC overlayer (Co1/ND@NC) as a model, singlet oxygen (1O2) was identified as the predominant ROS driving the highly selective coupling of aniline with H2O2 as sustainable oxidant. Mechanistic studies reveal that 1O2 effectively accelerates the conversion of the N-phenylhydroxylamine intermediate to nitrosobenzene, a kinetically favored step that promotes subsequent condensation with aniline to yield azobenzene with exceptional selectivity. Moreover, the NC confinement effectively prevents cobalt leaching, ensuring robust structural integrity of the single-atom sites under harsh oxidative conditions. As a result, the Co1/ND@NC catalyst achieves an azobenzene production rate of ∼7.1 mmol g–1 h–1 with 97.0% selectivity and maintains stable performance over seven consecutive cycles. This work not only uncovers the critical role of the nonradical 1O2 pathway in selective aniline coupling but also establishes a new paradigm for engineering confined single-atom microenvironments for sustainable oxidation catalysis.

papers.title: Diabatic Seam Space Sampling for Hydrogen Tunneling Systems with Nuclear–Electronic Orbital Theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Hydrogen tunneling is central to many chemical and biological processes. Herein, we introduce the vibronic-SHAKE (V-SHAKE) approach to comprehensively sample energy-conserving molecular configurations enabling hydrogen tunneling. A constrained form of nuclear–electronic orbital multistate density functional theory (NEO-MSDFT) dynamics, where the tunneling hydrogen nucleus is quantized, is used to sample geometries in the diabatic seam space corresponding to the intersection of the reactant and product NEO-DFT diabatic vibronic surfaces. V-SHAKE is applied to hydrogen and deuterium tunneling in 4-cyanobutanolate and (Z)-4-hydroxybut-3-en-2-one. The vibronic coupling is found to vary significantly in the diabatic seam space, mainly due to changes in the donor–acceptor distance. The reaction coordinate and gradient of the vibronic coupling at the minimum energy crossing point are nearly orthogonal and are dominated by motions stabilizing the product relative to the reactant or decreasing the donor–acceptor distance, respectively. V-SHAKE provides fundamental insights and qualitative support for assumptions underlying rate theories.

papers.title: Role of Structural Features and Heteroatom Functionality in the Photocatalytic Selectivity of Sulfur Dots for Competitive H2 and H2O2 Production
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Sulfur dots (S-dots) have emerged as promising elemental semiconducting nanomaterials owing to their distinctive photoluminescence and photocatalytic properties. However, the influence of structural features on their fundamental photophysical and optoelectronic properties remains largely unexplored. Herein, oxygen-rich S-dots (OSDs) and nitrogen-rich S-dots (NSDs) were synthesized by tuning heteroatom functionalities and investigated for selective photocatalytic H2 and H2O2 production. OSDs selectively produce H2O2 through oxygen reduction, whereas NSDs favor H2 evolution via proton reduction. Correlating structural and morphological characteristics with photophysical and optoelectronic properties revealed distinct charge-carrier dynamics governing their photocatalytic selectivity. Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy further elucidated the underlying mechanisms. The surface functionalities of NSDs induce photobasicity and promote exciplex formation with H2O, facilitating proton abstraction and H2 evolution. In contrast, the band structure and favorable energy-level alignment of OSDs enable selective H2O2 production. These findings demonstrate heteroatom engineering as an effective strategy for tuning the photocatalytic selectivity of elemental S-dots.

papers.title: Broad Infrared Absorption of Doped Tetrathiafulvalene-Derivative Monolayers on Thiolate-Covered Au(111)
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The vibronically coupled broad infrared (IR) absorption of self-assembled tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) derivative monolayers on functional alkanethiolate-covered Au(111) surfaces was studied by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The broad IR absorption band was caused by the presence of dopants during self-assembly, and was affected by the morphology of the resulting monolayer. Interestingly, the broad IR peak at 4700 cm–1 shifted to 6700 cm–1 as the temperature decreased from 296 to 90 K. These phenomena are unique to molecular monolayer films on substrates. By comparison of the IR data with the TD-DFT calculation results, we confirmed that the origin of the broad IR absorption originated from charge transfer (CT) excitation of dimer cations and revealed the absorption characteristics.
