papers.title: Soluble Complexes Destruct Metal-Alkanoate Clusters in the Mixture of Colloidal Quantum Dots
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Metal alkanoates represent the most challenging impurities in quantum dot (QD) purification. These species readily form clusters through extended metal–carboxylate coordination in common QD solvents. When present in QD dispersions, such clusters coassemble with QDs to generate insoluble and gel-like aggregates. Herein, we demonstrate that these clusters and related assemblies can be effectively disassembled via the introduction of tetramethylammonium alkanoate (NMe4Al). This strategy enables facile purification of diverse QDs through selective precipitation of the QDs within a single toluene–acetonitrile dissolution–precipitation cycle. The generalized complex-based purification protocol fully preserves the native surface ligands of QDs, thereby retaining their photoluminescence quantum yields and colloidal stability. This generalized purification protocol is expected to play a key role in fundamental research and technical applications of colloidal QDs.

papers.title: CO2 Activation on Ceria: Polarization-Resolved Infrared Identification of Surface Carbonates on CeO2(110)
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Understanding CO2 activation on ceria is central to elucidating elementary steps in catalytic CO2 conversion, yet direct vibrational identification of carbonate species on well-defined ceria single crystals has remained elusive. Here, we use polarization-resolved infrared reflection–absorption spectroscopy to identify surface carbonates formed upon CO2 adsorption on oxidized CeO2(110), with surface quality confirmed using CO as a probe molecule and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Alongside molecularly physisorbed CO2, we observe bands at 1510 and 1280 cm–1 that we assign to a monodentate carbonate on the stoichiometric surface; their distinct polarization dependence matches the adsorption geometry predicted by density functional theory, giving direct experimental validation of the proposed structure. Additional bands at 1570 and 1610 cm–1, absent from the ideal-surface picture, are tentatively assigned to carbonates at defective sites such as step edges or oxygen vacancies. By establishing definitive, structurally validated vibrational fingerprints for CO2 activation on a single-crystal ceria surface, this work provides an essential molecular-level reference for interpreting infrared spectra of ceria-based powder catalysts.

papers.title: Strain-Switchable Local Valley Splitting and Carrier-Mediated Piezomagnetism in an Altermagnetic Mn2Se2S Monolayer
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Two-dimensional altermagnetic semiconductors are promising for low-stray-field spintronic and valleytronic applications, yet Mn-based systems with strain-tunable local valley splitting and piezomagnetism are rarely studied. Using first-principles calculations, we predict a dynamically stable Mn2Se2S monolayer with an altermagnetic ground state and out-of-plane spin orientation, which remains semiconducting over the Hubbard U = 3.0–4.0 eV range. Uniaxial in-plane strain breaks the diagonal mirror symmetry, yielding a sign-reversible local piezovalley response with a local valence-band splitting varying over a range of 246.13 meV. Carrier doping induces a strain-dependent imbalance between spin-channel occupations, enabling a net magnetization and a doping-tunable piezomagnetic effect. Strain defines −1, 0, and +1 local valley-ordering states, for which the valley-contrasting Berry curvature suggests a possible electrical readout through a transverse response. This work expands Mn-based altermagnetic semiconductors and identifies Mn2Se2S as a candidate for strain-driven valleytronic and piezomagnetic devices.
papers.zh: Q-Q-Q-1-Q-Q-Q-Q-Q单层中的应变可调局部谷分裂和载流子介导的压磁性

papers.title: Phase- and Substoichiometry-Dependent Magneto-Optical Responses of Plasmonic Cu–Sn–S Ternary Semiconductor Nanodots
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Cu–Sn–S (copper–tin–sulfide; CTS) ternary semiconducting chalcogenides are composed of nontoxic and earth-abundant elements, so there has been a great deal of interest in future photovoltaic devices. In this article, we investigate optical and magneto-optical (MO) properties of CTS nanodots with different phases, Cu3SnS4 and Cu2SnS3, to better understand the influence of elemental deficiencies on their composition-dependent performance. Both Cu3SnS4 and Cu2SnS3 nanodots are successfully obtained via direct synthesis using multiple cation precursors in the presence of thiourea and found to possess isostructural orthorhombic phases. The nanodots of Cu3SnS4 exhibit optical absorption attributed to localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) with a broad peak at 1500–2000 nm, while those of Cu2SnS3 at > ∼3000 nm, depending on their substoichiometry. The p-type LSPR mode of the Cu3SnS4 nanodots is rationalized by magnetic circular dichroism (MCD), and the surface Cu-deficiency rather than the donor defects (S-deficiency and/or Sn-excess) significantly contributes to the free carrier (hole) generation. The value of effective hole mass is estimated by the MCD spectral simulation. As for the Cu2SnS3 nanodots, in addition to the LSPR band in the IR region, two distinct optical transitions near the bandgap region (∼500–800 nm) are unveiled by strong MCD responses with the same signs, stemming from two noninteracting Faraday B-terms, and then the origin of these transitions is discussed.
papers.zh: 等离子体Cu–Sn–S三元半导体纳米点的相依赖性和亚化学计量依赖性磁光响应

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Study of the Interfacial Mechanical Behavior and CO2 Adsorption Characteristics of MgO-Reinforced Expansive Soil
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Reactive magnesium oxide (MgO) is an increasingly attractive low-carbon binder for expansive soil stabilization, yet the molecular mechanisms coupling MgO hydration products with clay minerals and CO2 retention remain unclear. Using molecular dynamics simulations, this study examines the interfacial mechanical behavior and CO2 adsorption characteristics of brucite-montmorillonite systems representing MgO-reinforced expansive soil, across five montmorillonite models with cation exchange capacity (CEC) values from 18.43 to 178.20 cmol·kg–1. Increasing CEC markedly strengthens the brucite-montmorillonite interface, with a more than threefold increase in interfacial interaction energy and a more than 50% increase in interfacial hydrogen bonds, raising the peak tensile stress from approximately 0.7 to more than 2.0 GPa and the energy absorption capacity from approximately 30 to 400 MJ·m–3. CO2 preferentially accumulates near both mineral surfaces, but the montmorillonite interface becomes increasingly dominant at higher CEC values. The montmorillonite-CO2 interaction energy decreases from approximately −45 to −65 kcal·mol–1, and the CO2 diffusion coefficient decreases from approximately 17.5 × 10–9 to 12.0 × 10–9 m2·s–1, confirming stronger interfacial confinement. An overall response desirability (Ddes) increases monotonically with CEC and enters the good response regime at approximately 99.38 cmol·kg–1, establishing CEC as a governing molecular-scale descriptor for low-carbon, MgO-based stabilization of expansive soil.

papers.title: Multiagent Optimization and Multiphysics Investigation of Lead-Free CsBi3I10 Photodetectors
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The practical development of perovskite photodetectors is restricted by lead toxicity and the limited performance of many lead-free alternatives. This study investigates an all-inorganic CsBi3I10 photodetector through a comprehensive device-to-circuit simulation framework, integrating one-dimensional device modeling, multiagent optimization, multiphysics analysis, and circuit-level readout. A multiagent strategy is employed to cooperatively optimize interfacial and bulk parameters, overcoming the limitations of conventional single-parameter scanning. The optimized device achieves a responsivity of 0.484 A/W at 640 nm and an estimated detectivity of 1012–1013 Jones after including Johnson noise. Multiphysics evaluations reveal that mechanical bending effectively modulates the absorber bandgap, while the device maintains excellent thermal stability (280–360 K) and exhibits fast, reversible transient responses under pulsed illumination. Furthermore, transimpedance amplifier modeling demonstrates reliable photocurrent-to-voltage conversion under both flat and deformed states. This work establishes a systematic pathway for the application-oriented design of environmentally benign, flexible, and robust optoelectronic systems.
papers.zh: 无铅CsBi3I10光电探测器的多智能体优化和多物理场研究

papers.title: A Potential-Gated Molecular Circuit with Frictionless Hydride Transfer for Formic Acid Oxidation
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Direct formic acid fuel cells represent a cornerstone of the clean energy transition, yet their efficiency remains tethered to the rigid scaling relations of the formic acid oxidation reaction. Here, we demonstrate that a heteronuclear Rh–Cr dual-atom catalyst can bypass these traditional limits by operating as a potential-gated molecular circuit. Using grand-canonical ab initio molecular dynamics at the explicit aqueous interface, we observe the reaction in real time under constant-potential conditions. Our simulations reveal a remarkable division of responsibility between the two metal centers. The Cr site acts as a static anchor, spontaneously deprotonating formic acid and pinning the formate anion in a geometry that prevents the formation of carbon monoxide (CO). Meanwhile, the Rh center acts as a potential-controlled relay. It remains a spectator during initial absorption but switches on at a critical potential threshold, facilitating a near-frictionless hydride transfer with a negligible barrier of just 0.04 eV. This synergistic handshake effectively decouples intermediate stability from reaction kinetics─a feat impossible for single-site catalysts. We observe a synergetic migratory oxidation pathway, in which the Rh center, once activated, facilitates near-frictionless C–H activation and a hydride transfer. Crucially, we show that traditional constant-charge models fail to capture this circuit-like behavior, leading to artificially high barriers and a misidentification of the rate-determining step. By framing the Rh–Cr pair as a stereoselective electronic filter, this work provides a new blueprint for designing catalysts that do not just speed up reactions but also electronically steer them toward high-flux and poison-resistant pathways.
papers.zh: 具有无摩擦氢化物转移的用于甲酸氧化的电位门控分子电路

papers.title: Predicting Defect States: A Quick Screening Protocol for Substitutional Point Defect Engineering
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Point defects in crystalline materials play a central role in determining electronic, optical, and magnetic properties. However, systematic exploration of defect configurations remains computationally expensive because large supercell calculations are required to approximate isolated defects under periodic boundary conditions. We present a unit-cell-based tight-binding protocol that enables rapid prescreening of substitutional defects. The protocol extracts Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians from small, fully relaxed unit cells of the host and defect-like systems, replicates the host Hamiltonian to construct a supercell model, and introduces the defect by modifying only the on-site energies at the substitution site while leaving the hopping parameters unchanged. We validate the protocol across three diverse systems: isostructural substitutional defects in transition-metal dichalcogenides (MMo MoS2, M = Ce, Zr, Nb, Tc, and Ru), symmetry-breaking carbon substitutions in hexagonal boron nitride (CBCN h-BN), and nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. These case studies span two-dimensional and three-dimensional hosts, simple substitutions, and substitution-vacancy complexes. In all cases, the protocol successfully captures the number of in-gap states, their degeneracies, and their shallow or deep character relative to host band edges, despite some quantitative deviations in absolute energy positions. We further identify limitations for vacancies of highly electronegative atoms and for charge-state or spin-polarization effects, both of which involve self-consistent charge redistribution not captured by the protocol.
papers.zh: 缺陷态预测：用于取代型点缺陷工程的快速筛选方案

papers.title: Prediction of MAX-to-Mxene Convertibility Using Constrained Clustering
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Since 2011, MXenes have emerged as promising materials with diverse applications. However, their synthesis through selective etching of recurring layers in MAX phases remains challenging to predict due to a lack of comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing the synthesis protocol. This work seeks to accelerate the discovery of promising MAX phases for conversion to MXenes by employing machine learning. Inspired by previous work using positive–unlabeled learning for this problem, we employed a combination of a constrained clustering algorithm for identifying convertible materials with a classifier for scoring their convertibility. Our proposed algorithm learns to weigh multiple kernels projecting elemental and calculated properties of MAX phases, thus leveraging clusters that respect constraints holding convertible MAX phases together. We score the convertibility of the identified clusters using a support vector classifier with the previously learned kernel, and retain samples with high convertibility scores. To validate the model, we developed a specific timeline validation that incorporates the time of discovery of each MAX-to-MXene conversion, and show that the proposed pipeline is able to correctly suggest convertible MAX phases before their discovery at a given time. Our results suggest Ta3AlC2, and Ti4GaC3 as notable materials for synthesizing novel MXenes. The model also validates the successful conversions of Nb2GaC to NbC and Zr2AlC to Zr2C despite these not being labeled as positive. Moreover, we also identified 4 MAX phases as alternative candidates to synthesize already discovered MXenes: Ta2GaC, Ti2GaN, Ti3GaC2, and Nb2InC.
papers.zh: 使用受限聚类预测MAX到MXene的可转化性

papers.title: Regulating the Density of State of Co3O4 Enables Electrocatalysts in Li–O2 Batteries
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Regulating the electronic states of catalysts for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalytic activity is crucial yet challenging in lithium–oxygen (Li–O2) batteries. In this study, we synthesized Co3O4 as a model system to explore the correlation between the density of states (DOSs) of Co3O4 and OER catalytic activities in Li–O2 batteries. Compared to the original Co3O4, as well as the single-element doped P–Co3O4 and Pt–Co3O4, the Pt and P codoped Co3O4 (Pt/P–Co3O4) demonstrate enhanced DOSs across the entire range near the Fermi level due to the misaligned distribution of electronic states between Pt and P. The significant increase in the DOSs of Pt/P–Co3O4 results in a high donor energy level, which enhances the adsorption strength with intermediate states, thereby significantly reducing the charge activation energy and overpotentials. Establishing the relationship between the DOSs of the catalyst and the charging overpotential provides important guidance for designing high-performance cathode catalysts for Li–O2 batteries.
papers.zh: 调节Co3O4的状态密度使电催化剂在锂-O2电池中发挥作用

papers.title: Molecular Thermodynamics of Lower Critical Solution Temperature Ionic Liquid/Water Mixtures: Tetrabutylphosphonium Trifluoroacetate
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Lower critical solution temperature (LCST) ionic liquids (ILs) are thermoresponsive materials that undergo liquid–liquid demixing with water into water-rich (WR) and IL-rich (ILR) phases upon heating. Despite the vast combinatorial space of cation–anion pairings, LCST behavior is observed in only a handful of aqueous ILs. To uncover the enthalpic and entropic driving forces that govern this unique phase behavior among molecular liquids, we investigate an exemplary LCST IL, tetrabutylphosphonium trifluoroacetate ([P4444][TFA]), by pairing equilibrium molecular dynamics and finite-concentration thermodynamic integration with chilled-mirror dew point water activity experimental measurements. Computationally predicted excess chemical potentials of water (μH2OE) show excellent agreement with experimental measurements over IL weight fractions wIL = 85–95% at T = 300 and 323 K, with absolute deviations ranging from 0.04 to 1.2 kJ mol–1, establishing accurate resolution of the non-ideal solvation contribution. μH2OE is counterbalanced by a strongly favorable ideal entropy of mixing, governed by the large (∼19:1) IL/water molar volume ratio, and a uniformly unfavorable solvation free energy (relative to bulk water). The excess partial molar enthalpy of water (hH2OE) is marked by strong temperature sensitivity, undergoing an exothermic to endothermic shift of ∼5–6 kJ mol–1 from 300–373 K. On the other hand, the non-ideal entropy of solvation (sH2OE,n.id.) is uniformly unfavorable. Mechanistically, this enthalpy/entropy temperature dependence is traced to electrostatic screening probed by the charge–correlation structure factor SZZ(k)/k2, the competing water–water and water–anion interactions, and the structural organization of water imposed by the hydrophobic P4444+ cation.
papers.zh: 离子液体/水混合物下临界溶液温度的分子热力学：三氟乙酸四丁基磷

papers.title: The NPC1L1 Sterol Transporter: A Molecular Dynamics Study on the Influence of Cholesterol Binding on Intradomain and Interdomain Motions
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1) transmembrane protein, localized on the apical membrane of enterocytes, is a key player in cholesterol metabolism and homeostasis, whose proper regulation is essential to avoid the development of cardiovascular diseases. The cryo-EM resolution of its structure in two distinct conformations provided a possible explanation of the mechanism which allows cholesterol to be transported from the lumen to the cytoplasm. This mechanism likely exploits the high mobility of the luminal N-terminal domain (NTD), which first binds the cholesterol molecule─although this was not resolved in the cryo-EM structures─ and whose spatial disposition with respect to the other extracellular domains is what most distinguishes the two conformations. In this work, we performed extensive all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the NPC1L1 protein, embedded in a membrane model, in four functional states: open apo, open bound, closed bound, and closed apo. Briefly, the analyses of the MD trajectories showed that the wide motions of NTD observed in the open apo state are partially restrained in the open bound state. Moreover, cholesterol binding to the NTD also makes this domain dynamically coupled to the collective rearrangements of the middle luminal domain (MLD) and the C-terminal domain (CTD). In the closed bound state, a new NTD-cholesterol hydrogen bond is observed, which could represent the first step for cholesterol delivery. Finally, the closed apo state is characterized by an increased MLD flexibility which may destabilize extracellular domain interfaces, preparing the NPC1L1 transporter to return to the open apo state. Ultimately, our protocol provides a robust framework that can be used to analyze novel NPC1L1 inhibitors.
papers.zh: NPC1L1甾醇转运蛋白：胆固醇结合对域内和域间运动影响的分子动力学研究

papers.title: The Effect of Side-Chain Length and Grafting Density on the Rheological Behavior of Branched Polymers
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Branched structures play a key role in determining the physical properties of molecular brushes, but it remains unclear how this molecular factor governs their conformational dynamics and rheological behavior. Here, we employed molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the influence of side-chain length and grafting density on the rheological behavior of branched polymers with a fixed backbone length. All systems exhibit shear-thinning behavior consistent with theoretical and experimental results. Branched polymers with high grafting density and short side chains exhibit lower viscosity at the same molecular weight. We characterized the shape and orientation of bottle-brush polymers in steady-state flow and developed a structure-performance relationship by combining Spearman correlation analysis with explainable machine learning (SHAP). Chain orientation is shown to be the dominant structural mechanism leading to viscosity reduction. The side-chain length plays a more pronounced role in dictating the trends in shear thinning; long side chains promote molecular orientation and main-chain stretching, leading to enhanced thinning effects. At high grafting density, side-chain crowding prevents alignment with the flow field, leading to a diminished thinning effect. These molecular-level insights facilitate the adjustment of the branching structure of bottlebrush polymers to regulate their rheological properties, enabling the customized design of complex branched polymers.
papers.zh: 侧链长度和接枝密度对支化聚合物流变行为的影响

papers.title: Different Generation and Ionization Methods Reveal Naphthalene–Water Interaction in Clusters
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The interactions between naphthalene (Np) and water molecules play a role in astrochemistry and atmospheric chemistry. Mixed naphthalene–water clusters allow investigation of these interactions at the molecular level. We use different generation and ionization methods to study (Np)m(H2O)n clusters: (I) They are formed in charged (both positively and negatively) He nanodroplets (HND) after uptake of naphthalene and water molecules. (II) Free clusters are formed by supersonic expansions either (A) directly in coexpansion of naphthalene and water in Ar buffer gas, or (B) large naphthalene clusters are formed in supersonic expansion and they pick up individual water molecules. In experiment (II), the clusters are charged positively by electron impact ionization at 70 eV or negatively by electron attachment at ≈2 eV. All mass spectra, independent of cluster generation and ionization technique, show cluster ion series [(Np)m(H2O)n]± with a strong propensity for the magic n = 4 mass peak. The negative ion [(Np)m(H2O)n]− spectra of the clusters generated in HND (I) and in coexpansion (II.A) exhibit striking similarity, with n = 4 and 8 magic clusters. These findings are substantiated by theoretical calculations of the [(Np)m(H2O)n]+/0/– clusters. Complex information revealed by the experiment and calculations offers detailed insight into the naphthalene–water interaction.
papers.zh: 不同的生成和电离方法揭示了团簇中萘与水的相互作用

papers.title: VPT2 Meets MLPs: IR and Raman Spectroscopy of Eight Molecules, Including 74-Atom Cholesterol, Using MACE-OFF and MACE-MDP
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Vibrational second-order perturbation theory is a widely used method to perform postharmonic calculations of vibrational energies and infrared (IR) and Raman spectroscopy. We recently reported an application of this approach for vibrational energies using Fortran and Python software with machine-learned potentials (MLPs), with an application to 21-atom aspirin. Here, the software reported previously is extended to perform calculations of IR and Raman spectroscopy. Applications are made to six molecules, with up to 31 atoms, considered in a recent paper by Kapil and co-workers using MACE-based software for the MLP (MACE-OFF) and dipole moment/polarizability (MACE-MDP) to perform harmonic calculations of IR and Raman spectra with a linear approximation for the dipole and polarizability. Large differences are seen between those and the vibrational second-order perturbation theory (VPT2) spectra for XH-stretch fundamentals, and comparisons with experimental IR spectra for three of these molecules plus cholesterol show significant improvement of the VPT2 spectra over the harmonic ones. The extendability of the new software is demonstrated for 74-atom cholesterol using MACE software. The weakness of the VPT2 approach is shown for the IR spectrum of the formic acid dimer, using our PIP potential and dipole moment surface.
papers.zh: VPT2与MLPs相遇：使用MACE-OFF和MACE-MDP对包括74原子胆固醇在内的八种分子的IR和拉曼光谱分析

papers.title: Physical Origins of Anion Recognition in Rationally Designed Receptors: Balancing Interaction Energy and Drug Score
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The rational design of synthetic anion receptors requires a detailed understanding of how different noncovalent interactions govern molecular recognition while maintaining physicochemical properties compatible with biological applications. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to investigate the recognition of biologically relevant anions (acetate, chloride, and dihydrogen phosphate) by seven structurally distinct receptors. The analyses reveal that classical N–H···anion hydrogen bonds constitute the dominant contribution to the calculated interaction energy, whereas halogen bonding, C–H···anion contacts, and anion−π interactions provide secondary or cooperative stabilization depending on the receptor architecture. Complementary in silico ADMET, drug score, and toxicity analyses, integrated through a composite multicriteria ranking, identify receptor 7 as the system that best combines strong anion-binding affinities, predominantly arising from classical N–H···anion hydrogen bonding, with an excellent pharmacokinetic profile, full compliance with Lipinski’s criteria, and the absence of predicted mutagenic, tumorigenic, irritant, or reproductive risks. These findings establish quantitative relationships linking electronic structure, noncovalent interaction mechanisms, and pharmacological descriptors, providing mechanistic principles for the rational design of supramolecular receptors for biologically relevant anions. The transport ability of these receptors was not evaluated and would require experimental validation.
papers.zh: 合理设计的受体中阴离子识别的物理起源：平衡相互作用能和药物评分

papers.title: Solvent Effects on the Photophysical Mechanism of a 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone Derivative with TICT Characteristics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: 2’-Hydroxybenzochalcone derivatives serve as solid-state laser materials and promising high-sensitivity fluorescent probes with TICT and ESIPT dual photophysical pathways, yet their solvent-dependent mechanisms remain ambiguous. Herein, synthesized 2’-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzochalcone (HMBC) was systematically explored via spectroscopic characterization and theoretical calculations in three aprotic solvents of varied polarity. Increasing solvent polarity induces a gradual red shift in the absorption peaks, and dual fluorescence emission is observed with a significantly large Stokes shift for the long-wavelength band. DFT and TD-DFT results reveal that the initial hydroxyl proton configuration plays a critical role in directing the excited-state relaxation of HMBC. In combination with the extremely low fluorescence quantum yields measured in dilute solution, the excited-state behavior of HMBC was shown to be predominantly governed by TICT rather than ESIPT. Moreover, a clear correlation among solvent polarity, excited-state molecular torsion, charge-transfer character, and luminescence behavior was established. This work offers guidance for the rational design of advanced fluorescent probes toward environmental and biomedical detection based on 2’-hydroxylchalcone template.
papers.zh: 溶剂对具有TICT特性的2’-羟基苯甲酮衍生物光物理机制的影响

papers.title: Charge-Transfer Complexation and Electron Donor–Acceptor Interaction between 4-Aminoantipyrene as a Donor and 3,5-Dinitrobenzoic Acid as a π-Acceptor: A Combined Experimental and DFT Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Due to a hybrid electronic state at the interface of charge-donor and charge-acceptor molecules, the charge-transfer state influences a wide variety of physical processes that occur in organic semiconductor devices. This work describes the formation of a novel charge-transfer complex in solution at room temperature, employing 3,5-dinitrobenzoic acid as the acceptor and 4-aminoantipyrine as the electron donor. The charge-transfer study was carried out by UV–vis and fluorescence spectroscopy. Further, the ground-state electronic transfer was confirmed by cyclic voltammetry. In addition, density functional theory calculations indicate the limits of the highest occupied molecular orbital and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital to optimize the ground-state geometry and visually verify charge localization along the intricate interface. Strong intermolecular forces, such as hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions, are confirmed by both theoretical and experimental analyses. These forces play a major role in the thermodynamic stability and electron delocalization of the charge-transfer complex. The study highlights the critical importance of noncovalent interactions in stabilizing donor–acceptor systems. The study also highlights that intermolecular interactions and π–π stacking contribute to the formation and stability of donor–acceptor complexes, which have potential applications in molecular electronics.

papers.title: Smoothed Truncated Coulomb Potential for Periodic Gaussian-Basis Hartree–Fock Exchange
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Truncated Coulomb (TC) potentials reduce finite-size errors and accelerate thermodynamic-limit convergence in periodic Hartree–Fock (HF) calculations, but their use with Gaussian basis sets is complicated by the evaluation of electron repulsion integrals (ERIs), particularly for nonspherical truncation domains and all-electron calculations. We introduce the smoothed truncated Coulomb (sTC) potential as a systematically improvable approximation to a parent TC potential. A real-space Gaussian convolution smooths the sharp truncation boundary, and a single dimensionless parameter, η, controls the width of the smoothing window, which can be tightened to systematically approach the TC reference. The smoothing by sTC enables a dual-space algorithm for evaluating periodic Gaussian-basis ERIs that requires neither a large plane-wave basis nor new molecular integral kernels and is applicable to both pseudopotential and all-electron calculations, including the important Wigner–Seitz-cell truncation boundaries. Benchmarks spanning insulating, semiconducting, layered, metallic, and molecular-crystal systems show that sTC-based HF closely reproduces TC results in pseudopotential calculations and extends TC-quality calculations to all-electron settings. Across these systems, sTC substantially improves thermodynamic-limit convergence relative to the probe-charge Ewald method while remaining practical for all-electron calculations in which direct TC-based calculations are computationally challenging.

papers.title: The Stress Localization Function─A Stress-Derived Real-Space Descriptor for Chemical Bonding Analysis
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Existing quantum-chemical topology descriptors, including the Laplacian of the electron density, the Electron Localization Function (ELF), and the Localized Orbital Locator (LOL), characterize bonding through the density and its low-order derivatives, but they trace the localization of electrons rather than the local balance between the kinetic and potential energy densities and sometimes fail in cases such as heavy atoms, hypervalent centers, and bonds of intermediate character. To address these deficiencies, we introduce the Stress Localization Function (SLF), a real-space bonding descriptor constructed from the quantum-mechanical stress tensor. The trace of the stress tensor is the local virial field, which connects the kinetic and potential energy at each point in space. The SLF is obtained by taking its magnitude, comparing it to the value for a uniform electron gas of the same local density, and mapping the result onto a bounded scale, in analogy to the ELF or LOL. Applied to atoms across the periodic table, the SLF resolves the complete electronic shell structure, including the outermost shells of heavy atoms that the Laplacian fails to recover and that stress-based indicators have not resolved with any single choice of parameter. For the 4d elements, the SLF recovers the full complement of shells with no adjustable parameter. It registers the number of occupied shells rather than the nominal period, as shown by palladium’s anomalous 4d105s0 configuration. The core value is essentially universal (≈0.578), transferable from free atoms to bonded environments. Across a benchmark set of single, double, and triple bonds, the SLF decreases monotonically with bond order while simultaneously tracking bond polarity through the electronegativity of the bonding partner, separating two distinct chemical effects within a single scalar field. The descriptor further characterizes nonprototypical bonding, including three-center bonds, as in the textbook example of H3+ and boranes, the hypervalent center in BrF3, and the σ-donation and π-back-donation of metal carbonyls. The SLF thus provides a stress-derived, energetic view of electron organization that complements existing density-based descriptors.

papers.title: Capturing Transient Polaron Formation Dynamics: A Time-Dependent Polaron Transformation Approach
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Static polaron transformations impose an equilibrium environmental displacement at the initial time and can therefore misrepresent transient polaron formation. We introduce a time-dependent (TD) polaron transformation that describes the dynamical formation of polarons. We first present the TD polaron transformation for the spin–boson model via an infinite sequence of interaction-picture transformations. Each transformation in the sequence cancels the residual term generated by its predecessor; the ordered transformation sequence combines exactly into a displacement operator whose amplitude is zero at the initial time. We then generalize this recursive elimination to any suitably partitioned Hamiltonian. When the generated operator algebra closes, the ordered sequence of transformations reduces to an exact closed form; otherwise, a truncated sequence provides a systematic short-time approximation. For the transformed spin–boson Hamiltonian, we derive a second-order Nakajima–Zwanzig quantum master equation with two-time bath correlation functions. We benchmark this quantum master equation against numerically exact matrix-product-state dynamics and hierarchical equations of motion using Landau–Zener sweeps coupled to a thermal bath, whose tunable crossing time acts as a clock for polaron formation. We find that the TD-polaron quantum master equation outperforms the static formulation in regimes where transient polaron formation competes with the system evolution. The TD-polaron transformation is therefore applicable to nonequilibrium processes such as sudden charge injection, while the underlying sequential elimination scheme extends to other suitably partitioned Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Adaptive Substructure Sampling for Molecules with Flexible Alkyl Substituents
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: The exponential growth of conformational space in molecules with flexible side chains presents a fundamental bottleneck for atomistic sampling methods. A large fraction of this complexity arises from weakly coupled, quasi-degenerate torsional degrees of freedom that contribute little to chemically meaningful structural diversity while dramatically increasing computational cost. We present a substructure-based conformational sampling framework that separates flexible side chains from the molecular core at the graph level. Detached substituents are replaced by capped surrogate groups, enabling independent sampling of subsystems and systematic reconstruction of approximate full-molecule ensembles. A limiting variant neglects explicit sampling of the side chains and assumes extended reference conformations. This approximation is rationalized using high-level electronic-structure data for linear alkyl chains, which show that folded conformations become thermodynamically competitive only beyond well-defined lengths, particularly in solution. The approach is implemented within CREST and reduces the effective dimensionality of conformational sampling for molecules with extended flexible substituents.

papers.title: AdaptivePy: A Unified Python Framework for Adaptive Sampling in Molecular Dynamics
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Adaptive sampling accelerates the exploration of conformational space in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by repeatedly analyzing the accumulated trajectories and seeding a new round of simulations from informative configurations. A growing collection of adaptive sampling policies has been proposed, each built around a particular notion of what makes a configuration informative, yet these methods are scattered across separate and often incompatible implementations, which complicates their systematic comparison and their combined use in meta-adaptive sampling schemes. Here, we present AdaptivePy, a compact and extensible Python framework that implements nine seed-selection policies behind a single configuration-driven interface, spanning simple population-based baselines, several established machine-learning and geometry-based methods, and two ensemble or meta-sampling policies introduced in this work. We show that the shared implementation reproduces the characteristic selection behavior of each policy on a series of analytic benchmark landscapes. We also introduce a new adaptive sampling scheme that employs TS-DAR, a deep learning framework originally designed to identify transition states, as an acquisition criterion that drives the discovery of an entire multibasin landscape starting from a single basin. We further demonstrate that the common interface enables meta-adaptive sampling policies, which aggregate the rankings of several policies into a single set of seeds. We apply all nine policies to explicit-solvent simulations of alanine dipeptide and the miniprotein chignolin. The policy that performs best depends on the system, on the performance metric, and on the amount of accumulated sampling, justifying the use of meta-policies that combine different algorithms. AdaptivePy thereby provides a unified testbed for the adoption, benchmarking, and continued development of adaptive sampling methods for biomolecular MD simulations.

papers.title: Systematic Correction of Kohn–Sham-Derived Excitation Energies via a Quantum Monte Carlo Approach
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Developing and applying accurate methods for the calculation of excitation spectra remains an outstanding problem in electronic structure. Here, we present the first application of auxiliary boson-corrected diffusion Monte Carlo (ABCDMC) to ab initio systems of atoms and ions in the second row of the periodic table and molecules. In ABCDMC, the many-body electron–electron correction to the density functional theory (DFT) exchange-correlation energy is captured statistically via an auxiliary boson ground state obtained with diffusion Monte Carlo. Moreover, the kinetic-energy contribution to correlation is included up to the limit of a finite active-space expansion. The excitations are described as a product of a linear combination of Fermionic functions derived from DFT and the auxiliary boson state. The corrections to the DFT-derived excitation spectra are obtained by statistically sampling an observable on the auxiliary boson state. We benchmark ABCDMC on the experimental excitation spectra of second-row neutral atoms (Li–F), cations (Be+–Ne+), dications (B2+–Na2+), and the carbon dimer against full configuration interaction (FCI). For the atomic set (96 excitations), ABCDMC improves local density approximation excitation energies for low-lying single excitations up to the n = 3 shell, reducing the mean signed error from −0.059 to less than 0.001 Ha and the root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) from 0.102 to 0.037 Ha using at most 25 determinants per species. An O+ convergence study shows systematic improvement as the determinant space is enlarged and double excitations are included. For the carbon dimer, ABCDMC matches FCI within 9 mHa RMSD for 11 low-lying excitations using 16 determinants. Overall, these results indicate that ABCDMC is particularly promising for the calculation of low-energy excitations with very small active spaces. However, the method is not designed to correct basis-set errors associated with diffuse wave functions and the cusp condition errors at the core in atomic systems using Gaussian bases which are also present in the underlying DFT. The compact determinant expansions used here suggest that ABCDMC may be useful for larger systems and, in future work, for correcting DFT band structures of solids, provided a sparse multireference basis can be constructed.

papers.title: A Two-Bead-Per-Amino Acid Coarse-Grained MD Model with Hydrogen Bonding (2BPA-HB) to Probe DNAJB6b-Mediated Suppression of Polyglutamine Aggregation in Huntington’s Disease
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Polyglutamine (polyQ) aggregation plays a central role in several neurodegenerative diseases, including Huntington’s disease. DNAJB6b, a molecular chaperone involved in protein quality control, is known to efficiently suppress polyQ aggregation, but its antiaggregation mechanism remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the interaction between DNAJB6b and the polyQ region (Q48) of mutant Huntingtin Exon 1 (mHttEx1) using a custom-built coarse-grained molecular dynamics model. The model incorporates a two-bead-per-amino-acid representation with hydrogen bonding (termed 2BPA-HB) and is calibrated against all-atom molecular dynamics data in terms of geometry, hydrophobicity, and hydrogen bonding. The model reproduces the tertiary structure of DNAJB6b and its interactions with Q48 and reveals an inverse correlation between DNAJB6b concentration and Q48 aggregation propensity. Our simulations show that DNAJB6b undergoes cocondensation with polyQ molecules, thereby shielding the polyQ from forming the intermolecular hydrogen bonds necessary for amyloid formation. The 2BPA-HB CGMD model enables efficient exploration of DNAJB6b conformations, supporting future studies of chaperone-mediated aggregation suppression and therapeutic development.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Computationally Efficient Prediction of State-to-State Transition Cross Sections for Molecular Collision Processes
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: A neural network model is adopted to develop a machine learning approach for the prediction of rotational state-to-state transition cross sections for inelastic molecule + molecule collisions. This method is applied to H2O + H2 system that includes 200 rotational states of the water molecule as a target and all states of H2 projectile up to j = 8. It is shown that with a relatively small subset of transitions used for training and validation of the neural network, one can have a fast and reliable prediction of cross sections and rate coefficients with a mean relative error of ∼7%, which is comparable to the accuracy of the method used to generate the original dataset. This demonstrates that the calculation of rate coefficients based on cross sections predicted by the machine learning approach may dramatically reduce the CPU effort associated with numerical solution of the molecular scattering problem, which opens ample opportunities for accelerating the generation of collisional databases for astrochemical and other applications.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

papers.title: BlindDDG: A Blind Evaluation-Based Method for Protein Mutation Stability Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Protein thermodynamic stability changes upon mutation profoundly affect protein structure and biological function. Recent advances in deep learning and protein language models have provided powerful tools for computational analysis of mutation-induced stability changes. However, most existing methods focus on quantitative regression of free-energy changes, which places strong dependence on precise experimentally measured ΔΔG values, although reliably determining the direction of stability change is itself an important objective in many practical applications. Here, we propose BlindDDG, a novel framework that reformulates protein mutation stability prediction from quantitative ΔΔG estimation to direction-oriented stability change classification. First, we introduce a blind-evaluation strategy that models mutation-induced changes by learning the representation difference between wild-type and mutant proteins, rather than relying solely on their individual intrinsic properties. This formulation focuses on the direction of stability changes and reduces the dependence on precise quantitative ΔΔG measurements. Second, a Siamese architecture with shared parameters is employed to encode the wild-type and mutant states and capture subtle mutation-associated differences. Third, a local structure-aware cross-attention mechanism is developed to integrate mutation-centered structural information with global protein language model representations, enabling effective multimodal feature interaction. Experimental results on the independent S669 benchmark demonstrate that BlindDDG achieves strong classification performance, obtaining an F1 score of 0.5449, an MCC of 0.3929, an accuracy of 0.7721, and a recall of 0.5417 for stabilizing mutation identification. BlindDDG outperforms all evaluated methods in F1 score, MCC, accuracy, and recall, highlighting its effectiveness in capturing mutation-induced stability changes, particularly for imbalanced stability classification.

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. Here we benchmark three ML-based structure prediction models, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold3 (AF3), against a curated data set of viral antigen-nanobody complexes deposited after the AF3 training cutoff. AF3 outperformed the other models: success (interface DockQ > 0.23) rose from 33% with a single seed to 50% and 65% with 10 and 100 seeds-per-target, respectively, compared with 18% for Boltz-2 and 30% for Chai-1. Using an expanded data set, we evaluated confidence metrics and found that a strict ipTM cutoff of 0.8, or a combination of ipTM ≥ 0.6 with a CDR3 loop pLDDT ≥ 60, reliably excluded incorrect predictions while retaining most successful ones. We further establish best practices for two AF3-specific capabilities, the choice of antigen multimeric state and the inclusion of N-glycosylation, both of which can be decisive for epitope success depending on the target. Finally, we apply these guidelines to two design problems: ranking a library of VEEV-neutralizing nanobodies and mapping the epitope of the broadly neutralizing nanobody CC3 across homologous alphavirus antigens. These results provide a practical framework for ML-based viral nanobody epitope prediction and design.

papers.title: Predicting Chemical Roles from Database Descriptions Using Natural Language Processing
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: In recent years, the use of document information to predict compound activity has gained attention. However, existing methods face challenges in applying these predictions to compounds not included in the training data because of the shortage and insufficient applicability of chemical knowledge as well as in interpreting the basis for predictions. Therefore, this study developed an approach to classifying the chemical roles of these compounds. By analyzing the descriptions of compounds registered in databases using Doc2Vec, we obtained the embeddings. Specifically, by setting the tag portion of Doc2Vec to the substructures of compounds, we acquired embeddings corresponding to the substructures and summed them to represent the compounds. We predicted the presence or absence of 10 chemical roles for the compounds; compared to predictions using chemical descriptors, our predictions had higher F1 scores for many chemical roles. Additionally, by applying Shapley additive explanations, we visualized the substructures likely to influence the prediction of the presence or absence of each role, confirming that their interpretation was consistent with the findings of the previous research. This paper suggests that the obtained embeddings, which combine the structural information and annotations of compounds, are useful descriptors for classifying the chemical roles of the compounds.

papers.title: A Real‐Space Force Analysis of Chemical Bonding and SN2 Reactivity From Exchange‐Correlation Potentials
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: The nature of chemical bonding and chemical reactivity can be described from the spatial organization of electronic forces acting in real space. Here, the force‐field framework based on one‐electron potentials is extended to molecular bonding and to the evolution of an SN2 reaction. Exchange, correlation, electrostatic, and PAEM potentials, together with their associated force fields, were analyzed for reference diatomic systems, a H n Y–F series (Y = Li, Be, B, C, N, O; n = 0–3) spanning different bonding regimes, and the F − + CH 3 Cl → FCH 3 + Cl − reaction along the intrinsic reaction coordinate. The results show that exchange dominates large regions of interatomic space, whereas correlation is especially sensitive to electronic reorganization in bonding regions. The corresponding force fields reveal the ionic‐to‐covalent transition and the concerted reorganization around forming FC and breaking CCl bonds, providing a physically grounded real‐space route to interpret bonding and reactivity.

papers.title: Theoretical Study on the Continuous Reaction Mechanism of OUCH + With CS 2
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: Understanding the reaction mechanisms of the atypical uranium species OUCH + provides insight into the intrinsic reactivity of uranium ions in the gas phase. Based on thermodynamic and kinetic calculations, this study investigates the continuous reactions of OUCH + with CS 2 , including the three processes: OUCH + + CS 2 → OUS + , OUS + + O 2 → UO 2 + and OUS + + H 2 O → UO 2 + . The reaction mechanisms between OUCH + and CS 2 , OUS + and O 2 , H 2 O were explored by using density functional theory. Reaction pathways were proposed from the calculated potential energy profiles, and the competitive mechanisms for the reactions of OUS + with O 2 and H 2 O were analyzed. Additionally, reaction rate constants were calculated by using variational transition state theory including one‐dimensional tunneling effects, and the concentration evolution of the continuous reaction was simulated. The results provide an important theoretical basis for advancing research on the chemistry of actinide elements.

papers.title: Computational Insights Into Marine Red Algae‐Derived Bromophenols as Dual‐Action Antioxidants and Cholinesterase Inhibitors Targeting ROS in Alzheimer's Disease
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: Marine red algae‐derived bromophenols are promising multifunctional candidates for Alzheimer's disease (AD) owing to their antioxidant and neuroprotective potential. In this work, an integrated computational approach was employed to evaluate their radical‐scavenging activity, Alzheimer's‐related targets, drug‐likeness, and binding stability. DFT analysis identified C4 [3‐(2,3‐dibromo‐4,5‐dihydroxyphenyl)‐2‐phenylpropanoic acid] as the most favorable antioxidant, particularly toward ROO • , with an interaction energy of −6.89 kcal/mol. The SET‐PT pathway was the most favorable mechanism, supported by its lower ionization potential (542.76 kcal/mol) and favorable proton dissociation energy (612.54 kcal/mol). NBO, NCI‐RDG, ELF, and QTAIM analyses further supported the stability of the C4–ROO • complex. Network pharmacology identified AChE and BuChE as key Alzheimer's‐related targets, while molecular docking showed favorable C4 binding affinities of −9.5 to −8.3 kcal/mol. ADMET profiling indicated favorable drug‐likeness and pharmacokinetic characteristics with comparatively low toxicity. MD and MM‐GBSA analyses further supported stable C4–AChE binding, with a predicted Δ G _bind of −40.32 kcal/mol. Overall, C4 emerges as a promising multifunctional bromophenol with antioxidant and cholinesterase‐targeting potential for AD, warranting experimental validation.

papers.title: Theoretical Investigation of Ethane‐to‐Aromatics Conversion Over [ GaH 2 ]‐ ZSM ‐5
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: Gallium‐modified ZSM‐5 (Ga‐ZSM‐5) zeolites are highly effective catalysts for the ethane‐to‐aromatics (ETA) process. In this work, the catalytic role of the Ga + , [GaO] + and [GaH 2 ] + species in Ga–ZSM‐5 is investigated using a cluster model and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, focusing on ethane dehydrogenation (EDH) and subsequent ethene aromatization steps. Anharmonic vibrational analysis reveals that the H–Ga–H asymmetric stretching vibration corresponds to the experimentally observed band. Moreover, the Interaction Region Indicator (IRI) analysis shows that the ethane‐zeolite interaction is dominated by van der Waals forces. Although ethane activation over [GaH 2 ] + remains energetically demanding during the EDH stage, with an activation free energy of 68.7 kcal mol −1 , the subsequent steps are comparatively more accessible, and the active site can be regenerated without the severe energetic penalty observed for the Ga + and [GaO] + pathways. Finally, C 6 ring closure is identified as the turnover frequency‐determining transition state species for the ETA process. These results provide detailed mechanistic insight into the role of [GaH 2 ] + in the ETA process and support the use of cluster models as reliable and efficient alternatives for investigating metal‐modified zeolite catalysis.

papers.title: LTVAE : Hybrid LSTM –Transformer VAE Architecture for Molecular SMILES Representation
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: A hybrid LSTM–Transformer Variational Autoencoder (LTVAE) framework is introduced in this paper for learning compact and chemically meaningful latent representations from SMILES strings, providing a SMILES‐to‐latent‐to‐SMILES representation model trained on ZINC15 and evaluated on ZINC15 and an out‐of‐distribution dye dataset. In the proposed model, sequential and structural dependencies in molecular strings are encoded using a bidirectional LSTM, while a Transformer‐based decoder is employed to reconstruct valid molecular structures in the evaluated settings. When trained on a curated ZINC15 dataset, the framework achieves reasonable reconstruction performance, with 98.58% token‐level accuracy, 92.19% string‐level accuracy, a 99.30% chemical validity ratio, and an average Levenshtein distance of 0.29 using a 64‐dimensional latent space. Reconstruction under an out‐of‐distribution evaluation setting is evaluated on a structurally distinct dye dataset, where 95.56% token‐level accuracy and 85.30% validity are achieved. The learned latent space preserves trends aligned with both general molecular descriptors and dye‐relevant structural descriptors, particularly conjugation length and aromatic surface fraction, with Fsp providing complementary information on molecular saturation. Controlled perturbations in the latent space suggest smooth and chemically consistent structural variations, illustrating the continuity and interpretability of the learned latent manifold.

papers.title: Accurate ab initio structure and vibration–rotation dynamics of the beryllium dimer
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The accurate potential energy function of the beryllium dimer in its ground electronic state has been obtained. The valence-electron correlation energy was calculated using the coupled-cluster approach, up to the CCSDTQ level of approximation (equivalent in this case to the full-configuration-interaction level of theory) with the augmented correlation-consistent basis sets as large as aug-cc-pV10Z. The core-electron correlation effects were estimated up to the CCSDTQ level using the core–valence basis sets as large as aug-cc-pCV7Z. The scalar relativistic, adiabatic, and non-adiabatic effects on spectroscopic constants of Be2 were also discussed. In particular, the adiabatic binding energy De of Be2 was predicted without invoking any extrapolation procedures to be 935 cm−1, with an uncertainty of ±2 cm−1. The vibrational term values and the effective rotational constants of Be2 were predicted to be within the corresponding experimental error bars.
papers.zh: 铍二聚体的精确从头算结构和振转动力学

papers.title: Local alternatives to Becke weights for molecular quadrature
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Most density functional theory (DFT) calculations employ Becke’s methodology to partition the space in and around an n-atom molecule into n overlapping quasi-atomic regions. In this way, a single molecular integral for the energy (or other property) is reduced to a sum of n atomic integrals, each of which can then be approximated using a local grid in spherical polar coordinates. Unfortunately, the formal cost of Becke’s partition is O(n2N), where N is the total number of grid points, and this can become a computational bottleneck when applied to large molecules. We propose two modifications of Becke’s approach, each of which is formally exact and depends only on knowledge of the Delaunay neighbors of each nucleus. The two modifications can be used separately to produce schemes whose costs are O(nN) or together to produce a scheme whose cost is only O(N). Numerical tests for a variety of molecules and atomic grids suggest that the O(N) scheme should be implemented in all DFT software packages.
papers.zh: 用于分子求积的贝克权重局部替代方案

papers.title: NEVPT2 multiple spawning molecular dynamics simulations for uracil
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation of the initially excited bright ππ* state through the S2/S1 conical intersection, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling. These results highlight the effectiveness of this QD-NEVPT2 implementation for studying excited-state dynamics.

papers.title: Möbius-inspired signed inverse-power representations for pair-potential reconstruction, design, and RDF-driven inversion
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Analytic pair potentials provide microscopic models for classical liquids, soft matter, and coarse-grained simulations. We develop a Möbius-inspired signed inverse-power representation for pair-potential reconstruction, potential-shape design, and radial distribution function (RDF)-driven inversion. The strict form uses the Möbius sequence as an arithmetic baseline. The extended form is a general signed integer inverse-power expansion with a continuous overall amplitude. It exactly represents the Lennard-Jones interaction and approximates attractive Yukawa and Morse potentials over specified radial intervals. Potential and force diagnostics establish the limits of short-range and long-range extrapolation. The same representation generates several prescribed interaction shapes and supports discrete inversion searches using shell-averaged force responses with a coordinate-derived finite-box boundary contribution. Six benchmarks span dilute and dense Lennard-Jones states and two temperatures of a repulsive Yukawa system. Independent Monte Carlo simulations reproduce their principal RDF features and selected local structural distributions, while resolving energy and pressure differences. Joint block resampling quantifies competition between nearby analytic forms. A frozen Yukawa approximation also retains close pair structure in one cross-temperature test, with measurable thermodynamic discrepancies. The results support explicit analytic pair models within stated radial and thermodynamic domains and identify the sampling and physical limitations of their structural interpretation.

papers.title: Dual-channel range-separated local hybrid functionals beyond the zero-sum game
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: A dual-channel range-separated local hybrid (RS2LH) framework has been developed. It uses two local mixing functions (LMFs) for the coordinate-space mixing of short- and long-range semi-local and exact exchange-energy densities. Previous range-separated local hybrids with strong-correlation corrections (scRSLH) can be reformulated as RS2LH. We start from an existing scRSLH, retain the human-designed Padé-form sc-contributions, but replace a t-LMF by a neural network (n-LMF). This gives the ωLH26nP composite model which, in contrast to previous scRSLH functionals, does not require a calibration function to deal with the gauge issue. We then proceed to the first explicit RS2LH, ωLH26n, where two n-LMFs are explicitly trained on weak- and strong-correlation as well as fractional-charge training data. ωLH26nP and ωLH26n are evaluated on a wide range of data, including GMTKN55 and W4-17RE main-group energetics, organometallic transition-metal test sets, spin-restricted covalent bond dissociation as a measure for strong correlation, but also on diverse quasiparticle energies. Both functionals perform excellently for main-group energy benchmarks but show limited transferability to transition-metal energetics. While ωLH26nP also performs excellently for molecular quasiparticle energies comparable to previous RSLH functionals, and also for spin-restricted bond dissociation, the explicit ωLH26n RS2LH shows larger deviations. It is shown that the available training energy data are adequate for the SR-LMF but insufficient to give the correct asymptotic potential via the LR-LMF. The composite approach of ωLH26nP benefits from the pre-designed strong-correlation features and the resulting excellent quasiparticle energies. The deep-neural-network DM21 functional performs worse than ωLH26n; its fractional-charge training data alone are clearly insufficient to obtain accurate quasiparticle energies.

papers.title: Spin controlled transport switching with negative differential resistance in a chiral molecular device
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Manipulating electron transport through spin control is fundamental to molecular spintronics. We show that adjusting the crystal field and oxidation state of a magnetic center embedded in a chiral framework allows accurate regulation of transport across spin states ranging from S = 0 to 2. Our results reveal pronounced current drops (up to 70%) during spin transitions and the appearance of negative differential resistance (NDR), arising from bias-driven realignment of the highest occupied molecular orbitals and accompanying shifts in the transmission spectrum. We further show that asymmetric coupling to the environment, in particular through a CO axial ligand, leads to current rectification and robust NDR under reverse bias. In addition, Fe(III) junctions exhibit remarkable spin-filtering capabilities, with the S = 3/2 state achieving a spin polarization exceeding 0.95 at low bias, highlighting a versatile strategy for molecular spin-state engineering.

papers.title: Delocalized relativistic effects: Unraveling cooperative and anticooperative mechanisms
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The term “relativistic effects” originates from the history of quantum mechanics and refers to the discrepancies between values calculated by models that consider relativity and those that do not. We introduce a methodology that opens up the possibility of analyzing the mechanisms by which relativistic effects combine in molecular structures containing multiple heavy elements. Through an n-body decomposition of relativistic effects, the individual contributions of each heavy element are revealed, along with collective contributions that can be either cooperative or anticooperative. Illustrations are given of the effects of spin–orbit coupling on total energy, electron density, and the intricate mechanisms by which these effects are transferred through space to the molecular electrostatic potential or the strength of intermolecular interactions. Near a heavy atom, such properties can be significantly more affected by the spin–orbit coupling effects produced by other distant heavy atoms, not bonded to the atom of interest or to each other. For molecular properties, it is shown that the influence of collective components (two-body, three-body, etc.) account for about one-tenth of the total effect of spin–orbit coupling.

papers.title: On-surface regioselective cyclodehydrogenation of 1,3,6,8-tetra-o-tolylpyrene on Au(111)
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: On-surface reactions have emerged as a powerful strategy for engineering covalent nanoarchitectures with potential applications in electronics, optoelectronics, spintronics, and photovoltaics. Despite their expansion into various product categories, reactions involving methyl-phenyl functional groups remain limited due to cyclization competition between the methyl and benzene groups. Here, we investigate the regioselective cyclodehydrogenation of a pyrene core decorated with methyl-phenyl on an Au(111) substrate. Using bond-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, we identify four cyclization pathways originating from the external methyl-phenyl groups in combination with the internal aryl group, yielding five products with diverse magnetic ground states. Statistical analysis indicates that closed-shell structures with methyl groups distributed clockwise or anticlockwise dominate (>60%), revealing a preferred configuration on the Au(111) surface. This selectivity is attributed to the cooperative influence of the underlying Au(111) template, which directs the cyclization pathways. Our study promotes the development of on-surface synthesis by elucidating substrate-templated regioselective behavior during competitive methyl–phenyl cyclodehydrogenation and establishing an atomically precise approach for fabricating non-benzenoid carbon nanostructures.

papers.title: The associative ionization of N(2P) + O(3P) revisited
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The room temperature rate constant for the reaction of N(2P) + O(3P) has been measured using a flow tube apparatus by monitoring the concentrations of both reactants via absorption spectroscopy and simultaneously monitoring the associative ionization product, NO+, using time-of-flight mass spectrometry. A value of 2.5 ± 1.3 × 10−11 cm3 s−1 is reported along with a lower limit on the product branching fraction for associative ionization (as opposed to quenching) of 0.5 and likely much larger, >0.9.

papers.title: Two-state resonance narrowing model and verification of organic molecule emission spectra
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Electron–vibrational coupling theory quantitatively describes organic molecular spectra and is key to understanding spectral broadening. However, organic molecular vibrational modes are discrete, high-frequency, and multimode-coupled; a unified framework that condenses mode-resolved information into a single, physically meaningful descriptor remains lacking. To this end, we employ the two-state resonance (TSR) model to construct a unified framework in which the resonance coefficient c2 is a core descriptor for the charge-reorganization response of a molecule along the neutral–zwitterionic coordinate; in the presence of an external polarizing field such as a solvent field, it also reflects sensitivity to solvation perturbations. For typical heteroatom narrowband emitters, fitting FWHM against TSR parameters enables estimation of the limit and guides the design of high-color-purity emitters.

papers.title: TPPS4 nanotube molecular structure and linear spectra: Matching theory and experiment
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Extended organic molecular aggregates are promising materials for nonlinear optics, photodynamic therapy, and other photonic applications. Meso-tetra(4-sulfonatophenyl) porphine (TPPS4) molecules form two zwitterionic species (Z1 and Z2) at solution pH = 1, which self-assemble into chiral molecular nanotubes exhibiting strong optical activity. While the macroscopic structure of these nanotubes is well characterized experimentally, their atomistic organization remains unresolved. A theoretical model of TPPS4 nanotubes based on the Frenkel exciton model is constructed to determine molecular packing characteristics that reproduce experimental spectra. Matching calculated and experimental absorption and circular dichroism spectra allows determining the orientation of the molecular plane within the nanotube.

papers.title: Millimeter-wave spectroscopy of vdW bands of He–HCN near the dissociation limit and the determination of the intermolecular potential
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Transitions to the internal rotation second excited state (j = 2) and the intermolecular stretching first excited state (vs = 1) of He–HCN, located close to the dissociation limit (by 0.2633 and 0.1759 cm−1 lower than the limit, respectively), were observed by millimeter-wave spectroscopy using the supersonic jet technique. The observed transition frequencies were fitted, together with those of the internal rotation fundamental band (j = 1 − 0), to the effective Hamiltonian with the intermolecular potential V(R, θ) expanded with the asymptotic long-range potential coefficients cn,l. The potential energy surface has a global minimum at the linear configuration (He⋯H–C–N) with a depth (De) of 30.150 cm−1 and a saddle point at the anti-linear configuration (He⋯N–C–H) located 9.014 cm−1 higher than the global minimum. The predissociation lifetimes of the quasi-bound states (τ = 0.16–0.29 μs) were derived from the line broadening of the observed transitions and agreed well with the calculated results with the radial probability density outside the centrifugal barrier.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of the validity of Janak path integral and Slater–Janak theorem
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Janak’s theorem states that the derivative of the total energy with respect to an orbital occupation number equals the corresponding orbital energy. Integration of the Janak relation is referred to as the Janak path integral, and it connects the total energies of the N- and N−1- electron systems, yielding the ΔSCF ionization energy. We numerically assess the validity of the Janak path integral for ionization processes using both Hartree–Fock (HF) and Kohn–Sham (KS) methods. Although convergence of the Janak path integral to the exact value becomes slower as the curvature of the Janak path increases, it nonetheless exactly reproduces the ΔSCF result—even for nonlinear Janak paths and regardless of the approximate functional employed. Furthermore, the total electronic energy can be expressed in terms of highest occupied molecular orbital energies. It is known as the Slater–Janak theorem. We examine this relation using a range of numerical integration schemes. While systematic refinement of the integration yields convergence to the exact result, convergence is rapid for HF but markedly slower for KS. The KS exchange–correlation functional is expressed in terms of the electron density and introduces spurious electron–electron interactions in one-electron systems. Consequently, the Janak path for a one-electron system exhibits anomalous behavior near the cationic limit. This results in slow convergence of the Janak path integral for systems with few electrons and, correspondingly, slow convergence of the KS Slater–Janak relation.
papers.zh: Janak路径积分和Slater–Janak定理有效性的数值研究

papers.title: Spectroscopic and Computational Insights into Different Binding with Bovine Serum Albumin and Esterase-Like Activity Tuning: Echinatin versus Licochalcone B
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The interactions of two chalcones, echinatin (ECN) and licochalcone B (LCB), differing by a single B ring phenolic–OH, with bovine serum albumin (BSA) and their modulation of BSA esterase-like activity were investigated spectroscopically and via molecular docking under physiological conditions. UV–vis absorption, fluorescence, and competitive displacement assays revealed both ligands form ground-state complexes with BSA at Sudlow Site I. Thermodynamics showed spontaneous, exothermic binding driven by hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces. Raman and docking indicated ECN binds via its A ring and carbonyl, whereas LCB binds via its B ring and carbonyl. This subtle structural difference yields distinct binding modes, underlying their differing modulation of BSA esterase-like activity, with LCB being a stronger enhancer. These findings reveal how a single hydroxyl difference tunes albumin recognition and activity regulation, shedding light on their pharmacological and pharmacokinetic divergence while guiding the design of licorice-derived chalcones.

papers.title: Dielectric Solvation-Regulated Excited-State Energetics Dictate Reverse Intersystem Crossing Dynamics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: The efficiency of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) is fundamentally governed by the rate of the reverse intersystem crossing process (krISC), which depends exponentially on the singlet–triplet activation energy barrier (ΔEST) according to the Arrhenius relationship. This work demonstrates that dielectric solvation provides an effective means of modulating the energetic landscape governing rISC. By systematically probing the dielectric response of the 1CT, 3CT, and 3LE states, we reveal how the local environmental polarity alters both ΔEST and the 1CT–3LE energy separation. Moreover, we explored the crucial role of the medium’s rigidity in maximizing the radiative properties of TADF emitters by suppressing excessive molecular motions. The photophysical properties from solution to solid-state films further establish that the dielectric characteristics of the host matrix exert a decisive influence on excited-state energetics and delayed fluorescence performance. These findings identify solid-state solvation as a previously underappreciated strategy for controlling excited-state energetics and establish host dielectric engineering as a powerful strategy for maximizing TADF efficiency while simultaneously mitigating dipole–dipole interaction-induced photoluminescence (PL) quenching.
