papers.title: Origin of Divergent H/D Isotope Effects on 31P NMR Chemical Shifts in Ferrocene Derivatives: A Multicomponent DFT Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: The hydrogen-bonded neutral ferrocene-1,1′-diyl-bis(methylphosphinic acid) (FcPMe) and its monoanion (FcPMe(−)) exhibit divergent H/D isotope effects on their 31P NMR chemical shifts (δP). The previous quasi-adiabatic Born–Oppenheimer-based treatment failed to predict even the correct sign of the isotope effect for the monoanion. Herein, we elucidate the origin of this phenomenon using a multicomponent quantum mechanical (MC_QM) approach, which directly incorporates nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) into the electronic structure. Our results reveal that NQEs induce significant changes in the molecular geometry and the associated electronic structure, leading to a qualitative reshaping of the δP profile and a reversal in the sign of the H/D isotope effect. In neutral FcPMe, this coupling reduces the proton-transfer barrier. In FcPMe(−), NQEs eliminate the barrier for the proton, transforming a classical transition state into a stable, symmetric equilibrium structure in which the optimized protonic Gaussian center lies at the O···O midpoint, whereas a residual barrier persists for the heavier deuteron. Crucially, we demonstrate that the structural relaxation induced by NQEs, together with the associated changes in the electronic structure, qualitatively alters the highly nonlinear geometric dependence of the 31P NMR chemical shift. The curvature of the δP profile changes from a classical ″M-shape″ to a nearly quadratic form. Because the proton resides exactly at the minimum of this quadratic curve while the deuteron slightly deviates from it, this qualitative transformation provides the clear mechanistic explanation for the reversed sign of the isotope effect. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating NQE-induced structural changes into electronic structure calculations when analyzing isotope effects on highly nonlinear spectroscopic properties and provide a framework for understanding proton quantum dynamics in complex hydrogen-bonded systems.
papers.zh: 二茂铁衍生物中对31P NMR化学位移的不同H/D同位素效应的起源：一项多组分DFT研究

papers.title: Deciphering the Filamentous Organization of Human Liver Phosphofructokinase-1 through Highly-Coarse-Grained Modeling
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Enzyme filamentation is an increasingly recognized mode of metabolic regulation and spatial organization, yet the relationship between filament-forming interactions, assembly morphology, and potential function remains insufficiently understood. Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK1), a key glycolytic enzyme, provides a prominent example: its liver isoform, PFKL, forms higher-order filamentous assemblies with distinct experimentally resolved interaction modes. Here, we develop a shape-based rigid-body model of human PFKL tetramers with explicit interaction sites derived from these filament-forming interfaces. The model preserves the overall tetramer geometry while remaining sufficiently coarse-grained to simulate the collective assembly and organization of many PFKL tetramers. We use this framework to determine how the relative strengths of the Interface 1–Interface 1 and Interface 1–Interface 2 interaction modes influence filament formation and emergent assembly morphology. We further examine how an attractive membrane-like surface alters PFKL organization and how filament formation affects the spatial colocalization of generic client proteins representing potential components of glycolytic assemblies. The simulations reveal how protein shape, interface specificity, surface association, client size, and interaction strength influence higher-order organization. Together, these results establish a structure-informed framework for connecting experimentally defined enzyme interfaces to mesoscale assembly. This framework provides a computationally tractable approach for investigating enzyme filament formation and membrane-associated protein organization.

papers.title: Electronic Structure and Electric Dipole Properties of the AgK Molecule: An Adiabatic and Diabatic Study
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: An ab initio investigation of the AgK molecule is carried out within both the adiabatic and diabatic representations for low‐lying electronic states of ∑ + , Π and Δ symmetries below the ionic dissociation limit . Potential energy curves, spectroscopic constants, vibrational properties, and permanent and transition electric dipole moments were computed using a pseudopotential approach combined with full configuration interaction calculations. The calculated spectroscopic constants for the X 1 ∑ + , D 1 ∑ + , a 3 ∑ + and (2) 1 Π states show good agreement with the available theoretical and experimental data, supporting the reliability of the adopted methodology. The adiabatic potential energy curves exhibit numerous avoided crossings that govern the redistribution of ionic character and induce strong non‐adiabatic interactions between neighboring electronic states. To describe these interactions consistently, a diabatization procedure based on the variational effective Hamiltonian formalism was implemented, yielding diabatic potential energy curves and dipole moment functions. The resulting diabatic permanent dipole moment of the ionic state exhibits the expected linear dependence on the internuclear distance, providing a clear signature of its charge‐transfer character. These results provide useful theoretical data for future spectroscopic and quantum dynamical studies of cold and ultracold AgK molecules.

papers.title: Solvent dependency of the free energy landscape of a protein translocating graphene nanopores
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The translocation of (bio)polymers through nanometer-sized openings in solid-state materials is a key process that allows us to identify the identity, length, and sequence of the biopolymer. The efficiency and speed of this process, however, are influenced by the local environment and the interatomic interactions among all components: the biopolymer, pore material, and solvent environment. In order to quantify and understand this influence, we perform all-atom molecular dynamics and enhanced sampling, implementing metadynamics. For this, we use a model biomolecule, part of the H4 histone protein, and a two-dimensional graphene nanopore. To assess the translocation process and the underlying free-energy landscape of the protein, we model the process within a simple monovalent solution, as well as in a molecular denaturant. Using different collective variables, we calculate the respective free energy profiles of the protein translocation and analyze the influence of the different solvents. Our results enable a fundamental understanding of biopolymer translocation through material openings and the key energetic components that can be evaluated in order to understand and optimize the process in view of nanopore-based biosensing.

papers.title: Boltzmann generators for amorphous particle systems
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Sampling configurations in thermodynamic equilibrium is a long-standing challenge in statistical physics. Boltzmann generators address this problem by employing generative models to propose independent configurations, which are then reweighted via importance sampling using exact likelihood evaluations. Recent Boltzmann generators based on continuous normalizing flows and flow matching have achieved significant success for particle systems and biomolecules. However, these approaches have not been extended to amorphous materials (glasses), for which equilibrium sampling is notoriously slow. Because of their disordered structure, the invariances and geometrical constraints of amorphous materials differ from those of crystals and biomolecules, preventing the direct use of existing generative models. Here, we develop Boltzmann generators tailored to amorphous materials by building the required equivariances directly into Riemannian stochastic interpolants. Our framework incorporates periodic boundary conditions and particle symmetries using equivariant graph neural networks. Numerical experiments demonstrate that enforcing physical symmetries significantly improves the accuracy of Boltzmann generators but also reveal an intrinsic limitation of the continuous-flow formulation: accumulated numerical errors during likelihood integration break time-reversibility, compromising exact thermodynamic reweighting. These results reveal a fundamental challenge for continuous-flow generative models in statistical mechanics and call for alternative approaches that preserve exact thermodynamic consistency.
papers.zh: 用于非晶态粒子系统的玻尔兹曼生成器

papers.title: Ab initio investigation of excited states and absorption spectra of small mercury clusters (Hg2–5)
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We report a systematic ab initio investigation of the excited states and absorption spectra of small mercury clusters (Hg2–5). Benchmarking multi-reference configuration interaction (MR-CISD) and equation-of-motion coupled-cluster (EOM-CCSD) methods shows that EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-PVTZ-PP reproduces atomic excitation energies within ±500 cm−1 of experiment, whereas MR-CISD deviates by about ±1100 cm−1. For the mercury dimer, EOM-CCSD potential energy curves yield absorption bands in excellent agreement with experimental transitions, while asymptotic excitation energies closely match atomic references. Extending this methodology, we present the first systematic ab initio study of absorption spectra of Hg3, Hg4, and Hg5, which display broad bands in the range of 37 000–60 000 cm−1. The consistent agreement with experimental benchmarks and diagnostics confirming single-reference character validates EOM-CCSD as a robust approach for describing excited states and optical spectra of mercury clusters.

papers.title: How do interacting quantum atoms energy components depend on the choice of partitioning method? Disentangling the effects of atomic weights and populations
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Interacting Quantum Atoms (IQA) is a real-space energy decomposition framework that reveals how individual atoms and their pairwise interactions contribute to the stabilization of molecules, yet its application has been dominated by the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM). Although fuzzy partitioning schemes offer smoother atomic densities, reduce numerical costs, and avoid complications associated with non-nuclear attractors, their influence on IQA energy components has not been systematically assessed. We investigate how the choice of atomic partitioning affects IQA energy components by comparing QTAIM with several variational Hirshfeld-based schemes. To enable direct comparisons between QTAIM- and fuzzy-partitioned IQA energy components, we integrate charge-constrained variational Hirshfeld partitioning with the IQA framework, generating fuzzy analogs of QTAIM atoms with identical atomic charges. Across a diverse set of diatomic and polyatomic molecules, we observe that fuzzy partitioning consistently results in less negative intra-atomic energies and more stabilizing interatomic interactions than QTAIM. These differences are traced to changes in the underlying electron–nuclear attraction and electron–electron repulsion terms. The proposed methodology provides a rigorous basis for comparing QTAIM and fuzzy atoms in IQA, enabling the effects of atomic populations and partitioning schemes to be disentangled for the first time.

papers.title: TRAILS-MD: Mapping complex conformational landscapes and transition pathways via lightweight lineage-aware adaptive sampling
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are fundamentally limited by the timescale gap between rapid atomic fluctuations and slow, activated conformational transitions. While adaptive sampling accelerates the exploration of metastable states, conventional implementations often obscure the dynamical connectivity between discovered basins, confusing broad configurational coverage with the sampling of physically viable transition pathways. Here, we present a lightweight, engine-agnostic adaptive sampling framework (TRAILS-MD) that iteratively launches short trajectory ensembles across either fixed or on-the-fly machine-learned (ML) collective-variable (CV) spaces. A defining feature of our approach is explicit trajectory lineage preservation, which allows for the rigorous reconstruction of connected pathways from highly parallelized, disjointed exploration stages. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework across a hierarchy of molecular challenges: overcoming low-dimensional barriers in peptide isomerization, navigating entropic bottlenecks in protein folding (Trp-cage and WW domain), mapping transient exit tunnels during ligand unbinding (HSP90), and exploring large conformational changes in adenylate kinase. Finally, we show how lineage-aware exploratory ensembles can seamlessly seed unbiased production trajectories for the construction of Markov state models (MSMs). By bridging the gap between deep-learning-driven coordinate discovery and strict parent–child trajectory tracking, this framework democratizes advanced data-driven sampling for routine computational biophysics workflows.

papers.title: Dynamics and branch-point motion in entangled symmetric star polymers examined via slip-spring and molecular dynamics simulations of rheology, diffusion, and scattering functions
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: This study examines the dynamics of entangled star polymers using the slip-spring (SS) model, comparing its predictions quantitatively with molecular dynamics simulations of the Kremer–Grest (KG) model and qualitatively with experimental data. We demonstrate that branch-point (BP) diffusion in the SS model is only modestly inhibited by increasing the functionality (f) or by suppressing constraint release. This cannot be explained by the naïve picture in which hopping motion is induced by the loss of entanglements on f − 2 arms, suggesting diffusive mechanisms that require escape from entanglements only on fewer arms. After confirming that the SS model qualitatively reproduces experimental results for linear rheology, BP-to-arm-end vector relaxation, and diffusion, we examine the mean-squared displacements (MSDs) and intermediate scattering functions (ISFs) computed by both models. While linear viscoelastic behavior is known to be almost independent of f, the KG model shows clear f-dependence of MSD and ISF. With an appropriately determined number of entanglements, the SS model reproduces the KG results well at long times, the regime that a coarse-grained model is expected to describe. Deviations appear at short times, possibly because, unlike the KG model, the SS model assumes Gaussian statistics at all length scales. To discuss the differences between the SS and KG models, we examined the radial distribution functions between BPs in the KG model, which show that close approach between two BPs becomes increasingly unlikely as f increases, and this can be interpreted as an effective repulsion between BPs. We discussed how this observation may inform possible future extensions of the SS model.

papers.title: Reaching the thermodynamic limit of periodic CCSD cohesive energies and band gaps
papers.jname: npj Computational Materials
papers.abs: The high computational cost of periodic coupled-cluster theory has limited the density of Brillouin zone sampling, yielding finite-size errors that need to be removed by extrapolation. Here we report the development and application of a distributed-memory software implementation of periodic coupled-cluster theory with single and double excitations (CCSD) that runs efficiently on up to 12 nodes with 96 cores each. This new implementation allows ground-state and excited-state calculations in which the Brillouin zone is sampled with up to 6 3 = 216 k -points, allowing us to reliably extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit. For eight simple semiconductors and insulators, we report the cohesive energy and band gap, which are converged to 0.1 eV, providing definitive benchmark numbers for the CCSD level of theory. Compared to experimental values, average errors for the cohesive energy are 0.1–0.2 eV (typically an underestimate), and average errors for the band gap are about 0.4 eV (typically an overestimate).

papers.title: Luminescence Modulation by Confined Ferromagnetic Polaron formation in Zn2+ Doped MnSb2O3(OH)Cl
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Transition metal and rare earth metal ternary compounds often exhibit semiconducting luminescence properties, magnetic characters of ferromagnetic (FM) and/or antiferromagnetic (AFM) phases, but which phase contributes to luminescence is still in controversy. To elucidate this relationship, we investigate the layered antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductor MnSb2O3(OH)Cl (θ = −8.5 K, PLQY < 0.1%) as a model platform. Partial substitution of Mn2+ by Zn2+ disrupts the interdimer AFM coupling. This disruption attenuates the luminescence quenching and liberates the intrinsic short-range FM coupling within the confined [Mn2O8Cl2] dimers across the Mn1–xZnxSb2O3(OH)Cl series. Consequently, the as-synthesized Mn1–xZnxSb2O3(OH)Cl series achieves activated photoluminescence, delivering an optimal PLQY of 30% at x = 0.7 dominated by intense 660 nm red emission from localized FM-coupled Mn–Mn pairs. Under extreme dilution (x = 0.995), where intersite energy transfer is thoroughly suppressed, the characteristic 575 nm yellow emission of isolated single Mn2+ octahedra emerges. This is accompanied also by the weak 490 nm emission band from the confined excitons around single Zn sites and Zn–Zn pairs. In contrast, pristine MnSb2O3(OH)Cl exhibits negligible emission due to severe nonradiative quenching induced by interdimer AFM coupling. This work demonstrates, for the first time for magnetic multielement semiconductors, that significant d-d transition emission can be enhanced by localized ferromagnetic Mn–Mn coupling in confined (MnX)n clusters via confinement effects, thereby clarifying the controversy concerning the emission origins of AFM clusters in TM compounds.

papers.title: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome: Potential Role in Magnetoreception
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Radical-pair-based magnetic compass mechanisms are believed to depend on spin-selective reaction pathways modulated by the Earth’s magnetic field. However, the influence of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) on the magnetic compass function at the molecular level remains largely unknown. In this study, we address this question by monitoring the electron spin polarization of long-range charge-separated (CS) states in cryptochromes using time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Our results reveal a measurable, albeit modest, 8% contribution of CISS to the observed spin polarization in the secondary CS state, while the CISS contribution is less than 6% in the tertiary CS state. We propose that the CISS polarization originates from the twisting rearrangement of an oxidized tryptophan residue. This is consistent with previously reported light-induced conformational changes between the inactive and active states of cryptochromes. Furthermore, model calculations predict that even a minor CISS can generate pronounced anisotropy in the signaling-state yield and impact a preferred yield directionality by breaking the magnetic-field inversion symmetry. Together, these findings suggest that CISS may provide an additional mechanism for directional sensitivity in radical pair-based chemical magnetoreception.

papers.title: Terahertz-Driven Conformational Remodeling of Filamentous Actin: Insights into Intense Terahertz-Field-Mediated Biopolymer Responses
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: We demonstrate the precise, noninvasive control of filamentous actin (F-actin) conformations using high-intensity terahertz (THz) pulses via a dominantly nonthermal mechanism. By combining femtosecond time-resolved mid-infrared spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, super-resolution confocal imaging, and a data-driven machine learning pipeline (CNN–UMAP–K-means), we show that 0.4 THz pulses selectively weaken intermolecular β-sheet structures (1615 cm–1) while enhancing α-helical content (1650 cm–1) in F-actin, driving a dynamical shift toward monomer-like (G-actin) vibrational energy relaxation (VER) with up to 95% spectral similarity. In A549 cells, THz irradiation systematically reduces F-actin aggregation, as evidenced by fluorescence imaging. The spectral and dynamical changes induced by THz differ distinctly from thermal denaturation, with no characteristic peak shift observed under heating, supporting a dominantly nonthermal mechanism; our observations are consistent with coupling between intense terahertz fields and collective low-frequency intermonomer vibrational motions within F-actin filaments. The machine learning framework enables unbiased clustering and quantitative similarity analysis to identify optimal irradiation parameters (70 μJ, 10 min) that maximize selective F-actin remodeling without perturbing G-actin integrity. This work establishes intense THz as a powerful photonic tool for manipulating protein assemblies at molecular and cellular levels, advancing our fundamental understanding of THz–biopolymer interactions for biophotonic applications.

papers.title: Intrinsic Descriptors Guide the Design of Stable Metal-Doped RuO2 Electrocatalysts for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: RuO2 is a benchmark anode catalyst for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), but rapid dissolution severely limits its practical application. Although heteroatom doping can improve RuO2 durability, the intrinsic dopant properties governing individual dissolution steps remain poorly understood. Here, we combine density functional theory calculations (DFT) with surface Pourbaix analysis to investigate metal doped RuO2 (M-RuO2) under acidic OER conditions. The calculations reveal a cluster-like RuOxHy pathway governed by two key steps: Ru–O bond cleavage to form *RuO and subsequent hydroxylation to form *RuOOH. We identify the oxide formation energy (Eform) of the dopant oxide and dopant ionic electronegativity (χi) as intrinsic descriptors for these two steps, respectively. The former exhibits a volcano relationship with *RuO formation energy, whereas the latter shows an inverted-volcano relationship with *RuOOH formation energy. Together, these descriptors identify Mo, W, Ta, Nb, and Al as promising stabilizing dopants. Calculated OER activities for Ta, Nb, and Al-doped RuO2 further indicate that improved dissolution resistance can coexist with appreciable catalytic activity. For the dual-dopant systems examined, Ru–O bond cleavage is governed primarily by the stronger oxygen-binding dopant, whereas hydroxylation follows the average ionic electronegativity of the dopant pair. These findings link readily accessible dopant properties to elementary dissolution thermodynamics, providing a general strategy for screening and designing durable RuO2-based catalysts for acidic OER.

papers.title: Exploring the Isotropic to Nematic Phase Transition in a Liquid Crystal under Vibrational Strong Coupling
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: We investigate how vibrational strong coupling (VSC) between a mid-infrared cavity mode and selected molecular vibrational transitions influences the isotropic-to-nematic phase transition of the prototypical liquid crystal 4-cyano-4′-pentylbiphenyl (5CB). Using a tunable Fabry–Pérot microcavity, we achieve VSC with prominent stretching and bending vibrational modes of 5CB mesogens in the isotropic phase. Through temperature-dependent optical birefringence, Fourier-transform infrared, and UV–visible spectroscopic measurements, we directly compare cavity-coupled and control samples. Surprisingly, we find that the isotropic-to-nematic phase transition is robust against VSC, indicating that the formation of vibro-polaritonic states does not appreciably perturb the isotropic phase of 5CB. More broadly, our results show that VSC of the studied vibrational modes of 5CB (-C≡N, -C═C-, −C-H) does not produce a measurable change in the I → N transition under the experimental conditions investigated.

papers.title: Selecting Ion Beam Energy for Defect Engineering in h -BN and Graphene
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Computational guidance for selective defect engineering in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) and graphene by ion implantation is essential for the development of single-atom catalysts, single-photon emitters, and quantum sensors based on these two-dimensional materials. We use spin-polarized ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to predict the minimum energy of ion irradiation leading to atom ejection from h-BN and graphene. The study spans 64 elements of the Periodic Table from He to Hg, excluding lanthanides, and it investigates the irradiation conditions for direct single-step implantation. We show that in the low ion energy regime (tens of electronvolts), the implantation outcome is determined by chemical interactions between an incident ion and the target atom in a monolayer. Our results are aimed at guiding experiments on the controlled generation of vacancies and dopant centers in h-BN and graphene by choosing an appropriate ion for irradiation and tuning its kinetic energy.

papers.title: First-Principles Descriptors of Heteroanion Effects on Early-Stage Ni Segregation in SrTiO3
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Exsolution of Ni nanoparticles from SrTiO3-based perovskites is a promising route to thermally stable solid oxide fuel cell anodes. A-site deficiency and B-site cation substitution are widely used to promote exsolution, but the effect of heteroanionic substitution in the oxygen sublattice remains less well understood. Here, we use first-principles density functional theory to examine how N, S, F, and Cl substitution modifies descriptors associated with early-stage Ni surface segregation energetics in a SrTiO3-derived model. The calculations show that heteroanion substitution alters Ni segregation by changing local lattice distortion, defect electrostatics, Ni–anion bonding, oxygen-vacancy formation, migration barriers, and electronic structure. However, each calculation is restricted by its probing intentions and the models used. Within the model set, F gives the most favorable O-site substitution formation energy in the bulk model and Ni segregation energy at the surface site. N gives the most favorable Ni segregation energy in the bulk site and oxygen-vacancy formation energy at the selected site. Cl gives the lowest barrier along the sampled Ni-migration pathway, and S gives the smallest computed Kohn–Sham gap, which does not reflect enhanced conductivity. Rather than identifying a single optimal dopant, these results reveal how different heteroanions tune distinct descriptors relevant to early-stage Ni segregation. The descriptor set provides a comparative theoretical basis for using oxygen-sublattice chemistry to guide the design of heteroanionic SrTiO3-based anodes.

papers.title: Dual Roles of Nickel in Key Components of Fuel Cells: Sintering Aid and Electrocatalytic Modifier
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The differential effect of nickel doping in perovskite-type energy materials is a focus of SOFC. In this study, the systematic investigation of Sm3+/Ho3+-codoped BaCeO3–BaZrO3 (BaCe0.7Zr0.1Sm0.1Ho0.1O3−δ, BCZSH) revealed the dual-action mechanism of NiO as an electrolyte sintering aid and a cathode active component. In the electrolyte, the doping of 2 mol % NiO can increase the concentration of oxygen vacancies while decreasing ion conduction at grain boundaries in a reducing atmosphere. The symmetrical cell tests show that Ni doping significantly reduces the polarization resistance and activation energy of the Ba0.5Sr0.5Co0.8Fe0.1Ni0.1O3−δ (BSCFN) cathode. DRT analysis confirmed that all dynamic processes were improved. In single cells, internal Ni doping reduced Rp by 44–63% and increased PPD by 54–87% at 600–700 °C. All these indicate that Ni doping can enhance the inherent catalytic activity of the cathode, which accelerates the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) kinetics.

papers.title: The Regulatory Mechanisms of Molecular Chirality to the Androgen Receptor
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Chirality is a fundamental characteristic of biological systems and underpins the structural architecture of key biomolecules such as amino acids and sugars. Molecular chirality can profoundly influence drug efficacy, often diminishing activity or even eliciting toxic effects. The androgen receptor (AR), a member of the nuclear receptor superfamily, plays a pivotal role in prostate cancer progression. Its ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD) exhibits pronounced chiral discrimination, resulting in marked stereoselectivity among enantiomeric ligands in modulating AR activity. However, the atomic-level mechanisms by which chirality governs AR conformation and function remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed funnel metadynamics simulations to investigate the binding pathways and free energy landscapes of the (R)- and (S)-enantiomers with AR-LBD. Our results reveal that the (S)-enantiomer stabilizes a conformation highly similar to the DHT-bound active state of AR through hydrophobic packing and cooperative polar interactions, facilitating optimal positioning of H12 and maintaining a complete interface for coactivator binding. Conversely, the (R)-enantiomer with a bulky C-5 substituent disrupts the hydrophobic core of the ligand-binding pocket and induces abnormal polar interactions. Such structural perturbation destabilizes the H11–H12 loop and distorts the activation function-2 (AF2) interface, which weakens the binding capacity of coactivator peptides. These findings elucidate the atomistic basis of chiral-specific regulation of AR and offer mechanistic insights that could inform the rational design of enantiopure therapeutics and strategies to overcome resistance in AR-targeted prostate cancer treatments.

papers.title: Modulating Squaraine Fluorescence via Hydrogen Bonding: A Selective Turn-Off Sensor for Thioglycolic Acid
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Thioglycolic acid (TGA), a common ingredient in hair removal creams and other industrial formulations, owing to its hazardous nature, necessitates sensitive and selective analytical detection. Herein, we report a symmetrical squaraine-based fluorescent probe for the selective detection of TGA, investigated employing fluorescence spectroscopy, NMR, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The probe upon interaction with TGA, undergoes pronounced fluorescence quenching arising from hydrogen-bonding interaction, which perturbs the intramolecular charge-transfer (ICT) excited state. The probe exhibits a linear response over the 23.8–77.4 nM concentration range with a detection limit of approximately 4 nM and demonstrates excellent selectivity toward TGA. Practical applicability was validated by the quantification of TGA in commercial hair removal cream samples. In addition, the probe functions as a molecular logic gate based on its fluorescence response, highlighting its potential for intelligent molecular sensing.

papers.title: Anomalous Reversal of CO2-Induced Viscosity/Diffusivity Trends in Water: A Molecular Dynamics Study
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Experimental viscosity data for dilute, water-rich aqueous CO2 are available only up to moderate temperatures, with reported measurements up to 449 K, leaving the temperature regime relevant to geothermal and carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) applications largely unexplored. Here, equilibrium molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to compute viscosity, self-diffusion coefficients, and density of CO2–H2O mixtures over 278–900 K and 10–30 MPa using multiple combinations of force fields for water and CO2. At 278–443 K, increasing the CO2 fraction increased viscosity and decreased molecular mobility, consistent with available low-temperature measurements. At 573 K, however, the trend reversed: at xCO2 = 5 mol %, the viscosity decreased by about 10% relative to pure water at 25 MPa, whereas the diffusivity increased by about 8% at 20 MPa. Above 700 K, composition effects became weaker and often comparable to the associated uncertainties. Analyses of number density, CO2 hydration, hydrogen bonding, tetrahedral order, and rotational relaxation show that the reversal behavior originates from the temperature-dependent volumetric and structural response of the water network to CO2 dissolution. The results identify a transport anomaly near 573 K that should be considered in modeling water-rich CO2-bearing fluids.

papers.title: Unveiling Cation–Polymer Coordination: A Reverse Approach from Neutron Scattering in Dilute Acetonitrile Solutions
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Quantifying cation coordination is essential for understanding ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes, yet reliable experimental determination of coordination numbers remains challenging. Here, we establish a calibrated framework that integrates Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy with neutron total scattering data to quantify cation coordination environments relevant to polymer electrolytes. Building on FTIR measurements using acetonitrile as a vibrational probe, apparent cation–acetonitrile coordination numbers can be extracted but are systematically overestimated due to coordination-dependent absorbance effects. Here, neutron total scattering provides an independent structural reference that enables correction of these biases. The corrected coordination numbers are subsequently converted to cation–polymer coordination numbers through a competitive coordination framework based on a site-balance assumption. Using this approach, quantitative coordination numbers for Li+, Na+, and Mg2+ are determined for poly(ethylene oxide) in acetonitrile solution across a range of compositions. This approach yields quantitatively reliable coordination numbers across multiple cation chemistries and polymer concentrations, providing a robust and experimentally accessible basis for interpreting spectroscopic coordination data in polymer electrolyte-relevant environments.

papers.title: Molecular Insights into the Aβ-42 Tetramer-Induced Disruptive Effects on a Model Phospholipid Membrane
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Formation of pores in neuronal membranes by amyloid-β (Aβ) oligomers is believed to be the origin behind neurotoxicity in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, despite significant efforts, high-resolution characterizations of the pore-forming Aβ oligomers from experimental studies have been hindered due to structural heterogeneity of such aggregated oligomers. Consequently, efforts have been made to characterize the aggregated oligomers that develop within a membrane environment. Attempts have been made in this study to probe the microscopic properties of the three-dimensional structure of an Aβ oligomer, specifically an Aβ-42 tetramer present in a membrane-mimicking environment. The tetramer comprises of eight antiparallel β strands forming an Aβ-42 barrel. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations at constant temperature and pressure (NPT) have been carried out on a fully hydrated liquid-crystalline lamellar phase of dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC) lipid bilayer with an Aβ-42 tetramer embedded into it forming a pore. The results were compared with that of a fully hydrated pure DPPC bilayer system. Based on the calculations, we have been able to successfully quantify the disruptions in the bilayer structure caused by the peptide tetramer through conformational rearrangements of the lipid hydrocarbon chains. We believe that the results presented can quantitatively provide fundamental molecular-level insights into the detrimental effects of pore-forming Aβ-42 on membrane environment, which in turn, may have important implications on Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Single-Probe Operator-Defect Control of ACE Reuse in Plane-Wave Hybrid DFT
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Hybrid density functional theory is limited by the repeated cost of exact exchange (EXX). Adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) reduces this cost, but repeated ACE use still requires a decision on when the compressed operator should be reconstructed. We introduce adaptiveEXX, an a posteriori controller for gamma-point plane-wave hybrid DFT that uses one Rademacher probe in the occupied subspace to monitor an EXX operator-defect indicator. The cached ACE operator is rebuilt when the monitored defect exceeds a prescribed threshold, while a deterministic five-call safety horizon limits the maximum reuse age. The one-probe indicator gives the same threshold classification as the full occupied-space defect at all 69 calibration points, and an independent random seed gives the same 69 classifications. For Si (8 atoms) and MgO (2 atoms), increasing the monitor from one to three or five probes increases stochastic work without changing SCF evaluation or ACE action counts. Across five PBE0 benchmarks, the geometric-mean occupied-ACE to adaptiveEXX wall-time ratio is 1.15, and the Si size series reaches 1.67 for the 16-atom cell. HSE06 calculations confirm numerical compatibility with screened exchange but do not show an acceleration relative to that of occupied-subspace ACE. The method is therefore an online operator-quality control layer for bounded ACE reuse rather than a replacement for a fixed rebuild period that is already known to be favorable.

papers.title: Algorithm for Locating SCF Solutions Reveals Conceptual Limitations of the Broken-Symmetry Approach Applied to the Oxygen-Evolving Complex
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Broken-symmetry (BS) calculations of polynuclear open-shell transition-metal complexes are widely used but rely on critical assumptions including the existence and stability of the self-consistent-field (SCF) solutions and the Heisenberg structure of magnetic interactions. We develop a new algorithm for systematic generation and analyses of SCF solutions and apply it to the oxygen-evolving complex (OEC). Several of these solutions are either electronically unstable or exhibit non-Heisenberg character, challenging the conventional interpretation of BS calculations. With homotopy continuation, the DFT solutions continuously transform into the Hartree–Fock solutions through an electron transfer in metal–oxo fragments, explaining a strong functional dependence of BS calculations. The Brueckner coupled-cluster method with double excitations establishes which SCF solutions provide the best reference determinant for correlated wave function treatments. Expansion of the developed methodology further strengthen the understanding of electronic structure in the Kok cycle of the OEC.

papers.title: A Machine-Learned Symbolic Committor for a Chemical Reaction: Isomerization in Retinal and p -Coumaric Acid
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: The thermal cis-trans isomerization of C═C double bonds in chromophores is a prototypical high-barrier reaction whose mechanism hinges on subtle out-of-plane bending motions. Combining machine-learning-guided path sampling (AIMMD) with symbolic regression, we learn an interpretable committor for two chemically distinct chromophores, N-retinylidene-lysine and p-coumaric acid anion, in vacuo from unbiased molecular dynamics trajectories generated by two-way shooting. Parametrizing the committor with a neural network and sampling it uniformly across the full range allows the model to resolve the reaction coordinate across the full transition region, not only at the isocommittor surface pB(x) = 0.5. A feature-attribution analysis identifies four proper dihedrals around the reactive bond as the informative coordinates, while the improper dihedrals at the sp2-hybridized carbon atoms prove unsuitable because reactant, transition, and product states share the same values. Symbolic regression then distills the committor into compact analytical expressions─to our knowledge the first committor both learned and distilled into closed form for a chemical reaction─and shows that a coupling of all four dihedrals is required to reproduce the S-shaped, stepwise pathway seen in the transition-path ensemble. This S-shape is absent from the minimum free-energy path: it arises from the dynamics of the short transition events combined with the mass asymmetry between heavy-atom and hydrogen-bearing dihedrals, and the larger asymmetry of p-coumaric acid yields the more pronounced S-shape this picture predicts. An interpretable, machine-learned committor, though a function of configuration alone, thus exposes dynamical features of the mechanism to which the free-energy surface is blind. The workflow requires no prior assumptions about the reaction coordinate and extends naturally to other high-barrier isomerizations and, combined with a reactive potential, opens a path toward bond-breaking chemical reactions.

papers.title: Global Potential Energy Surface Exploration Using Generative Stochastic Surface Walking (Gen-SSW)
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Global potential energy surface (PES) exploration offers a unique way to predict the structure of material from first principles. Here, we develop Gen-SSW method to enable autonomous and fast global PES exploration, which combines a general-purpose SE(3)-equivariant 3D diffusion model, LASP-Gen, with stochastic surface walking (SSW) global optimization. Contrary to the conventional SSW global PES exploration that requires a long serial trajectory to overcome high barriers between large structural basins, Gen-SSW establishes an autonomous, massively parallel global optimization framework, which realizes global PES exploration via divide-and-conquer: many short SSW trajectories are performed based on the seed structures batch-generated from LASP-Gen. By applying Gen-SSW across complex materials, we show that (i) LASP-Gen can efficiently yield a structural pool with huge structure diversity and reasonable local chemical bonding patterns, and (ii) By docking LASP-Gen with SSW, Gen-SSW can identify efficiently low-energy polymorphs of materials, as exampled by ionic materials (TiO2, LiFePO4), amorphous alloys (Ge2Sb2Te5), strong covalent materials (boron) and molecular crystals (phenol crystal). In particular, we find a new boron allotropy, namely α̃-B, that is only 6 meV/atom above α-boron but 17 meV/atom more stable than γ-boron, and suggest a synthetical route for making this new phase via solid–solid phase transition.

papers.title: A Quantum-HPC Hybrid Workflow for Reaction-Center Electronic Dynamics: Application to a Cytochrome P450-Inspired Iron-Complex Model
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: We introduce population-transfer dynamics as a practical validation observable for active-state-derived reduced Hamiltonians in multistate reaction-center chemistry. In transition-metal systems, missing couplings or configurations can compromise the reliability of reduced active space models along a reaction coordinate, even when the overall spectrum is reproduced reasonably well. Using a cytochrome P450-inspired Fe-complex model, we construct a reaction-coordinate-dependent effective Hamiltonian from state-averaged complete active-space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF) calculations, map it to a quantum circuit representation suitable for current hardware, and propagate the dynamics from the reactant-side ground state. At the spectrum level, the reduced Hamiltonian reproduces the SA-CASSCF reference with an RMS deviation of 0.030 eV and a maximum absolute deviation of 0.143 eV. As a dynamics-based diagnostic, the product-manifold population pP(t) identifies a pronounced near-degeneracy window around x ≈ 0.3, where state mixing is strongest; specifically, computed from classical exact time evolution reaches 0.488 at x = 0.3 after 10 fs, compared with 7.26 × 10–2 at x = 0.2 and 5.90 × 10–3 at x = 0.0. To render the workflow executable on current trapped-ion hardware, we quantify the NISQ-relevant trade-off between dynamical fidelity and circuit resources through coupling pruning and first-order Trotterization. A coupling cutoff of ε = 0.02 eV reduces the nonzero coupling set from 32 to 7 while preserving the dominant transfer pathways, and a Trotter step number of M = 30 provides the best practical operating point among the tested values. Finally, we demonstrate the end-to-end workflow on Quantinuum’s trapped-ion quantum computer Reimei. The hardware reproduces the key reaction-coordinate trend identified by the classical reduced model, including the pronounced maximum at x = 0.3, where the measured product population is 0.42 on hardware and 0.43 on the matched emulator. Overall, this work establishes a dynamics-based diagnostic route for assessing the adequacy of active-space-derived reduced Hamiltonians and shows that chemically interpretable multistate electronic dynamics can already be executed on current trapped-ion hardware under realistic device constraints.

papers.title: An Efficient Neural Network Architecture for Molecular Vibrational States: From Rigid Molecules to Molecular Complexes
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Accurately solving the nuclear Schrödinger equation for molecular complexes exhibiting noncovalent interactions remains a challenge due to the exponential scaling of basis sets and the presence of strongly anharmonic, large-amplitude motions. Recently, we proposed a neural network (NN) method to tackle high-dimensional vibrational problems and successfully applied it to C3H8 in full dimensionality; however, applying the method to molecular complexes has been hindered by difficulties in representing delocalized wave functions across multiple minima. In this work, we present a substantially improved NN-based methodology that overcomes these limitations through two key developments: (i) a novel NN architecture specifically designed to capture the asymptotic behavior and delocalization characteristics of weakly bound complexes, and (ii) an efficient training protocol that optimizes the variance of local energies. We demonstrate that this approach achieves subcm–1 accuracy for the vibrational ground and excited states of CH4 with substantially fewer parameters than the previous method requires. Crucially, for the prototypical water dimer (H2O)2, the new method successfully computes both ground state and intramolecular excited states with ∼1 cm–1 accuracy using ∼6000 NN parameters. This work establishes a robust and scalable framework for performing full-dimensional, fully coupled vibrational calculations on molecular complexes, providing an efficient approach for accurate spectroscopic predictions of such systems.

papers.title: Predicting CYP450 Induction and PXR Activation with Machine Learning Approaches: Challenges and Opportunities
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Many drugs increase the activity of cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes, an effect known as induction, which is a major cause of harmful drug–drug interactions (DDIs). Predicting induction from chemical structure would help identify DDI risks early in compound development. Yet, unlike many other drug properties, CYP450 induction is rarely modeled, because the data needed to train models are scarce and expensive to produce. Using an industry-scale data set covering induction of three CYP450 enzymes (CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP1A2) and PXR activation, we benchmark four machine learning models across six molecular representations and compare performance against models trained on a curated public data set. On the internal data, the best models separated inducers from noninducers moderately well (MCC 0.35–0.46) but could not predict the magnitude of induction. Almost no model or representation performed significantly better than the others, pointing to the data rather than the method as the limiting factor. The same pattern was observed for public data, where a large public PXR set reached this range, whereas a small, heterogeneous public CYP3A4 set failed where the data are scarcer and noisier. We then show that the shared biology of these end points carries a usable signal. A model trained on one end point partly predicted the others, and this transfer followed the known regulatory relationships between PXR and the CYP450 enzymes. Hence, these biological links can serve as useful inductive biases for future models. Finally, we found that the models we trained are already reasonably well calibrated, which, combined with their classification performance, makes them useful for prioritizing compounds that are within the applicability domain of the models.
papers.zh: 利用机器学习方法预测CYP450诱导和PXR激活：挑战与机遇

papers.title: RAVEN: Frozen Random Graph Reservoirs with Physics-Informed Interaction Fingerprints for Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Predicting protein–ligand binding affinity directly from three-dimensional complex structures remains challenging because available structure–affinity data are limited, heterogeneous, and highly susceptible to similarity-driven data set bias. Most graph-learning approaches address this problem by optimizing molecular representations end-to-end against affinity labels, potentially coupling representation learning to data set-specific correlations. Here, we introduce RAVEN (Randomized Atomistic Views with Ensemble Neural Reservoirs), a different learning paradigm in which multiple independently initialized atomistic graph neural networks are used as fully frozen reservoirs of nonlinear structural representations. Rather than adapting the graph encoders to affinity labels, RAVEN samples multiple independently initialized structural views from the initialization-induced representation space and integrates them with deterministic, physics-informed interaction fingerprints. Heterogeneous neural and tree-based readers then exploit these representations, followed by validation-based nonnegative fusion. On a similarity-isolated PDBbind 2020R1 benchmark reconstructed using GEMS similarity criteria, RAVEN achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.8005 and an RMSE of 1.2346 pK units on the held-out test set, and a Pearson correlation of 0.8415 on the protected CASF-2016 subset. Ablation analyses further show that increasing the number of frozen graph views generally improves the predictive utility of the structure-only representation, whereas physics-informed tree-based readers exhibit distinct residual patterns that enhance heterogeneous model fusion. These results demonstrate that competitive protein–ligand affinity prediction does not require end-to-end optimization of every representation component and establish frozen randomized graph reservoirs as a modular strategy for combining structural diversity, physical priors, and complementary inductive biases in molecular prediction.

papers.title: Instance-Wise Contrastive Graph Neural Network Enables the Discovery of Novel Aedes aegypti Larvicidal Compounds
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Aedes aegypti remains a major arboviral vector, making larval control a critical strategy to reduce mosquito populations. However, resistance to commercial larvicides has reduced the long-term effectiveness of current interventions, reinforcing the need for new compounds with improved potency and selectivity. Here, we present an instance-wise contrastive graph neural network (GNN) framework to accelerate the discovery of novel larvicidal compounds. The model was trained on a curated data set of 556 organic compounds organized into LC50-derived multitask classification thresholds and integrated Transformer-inspired graph learning with whole-molecule and fragment-level contrastive regularization. This model achieved strong held-out performance, with global AUC = 0.95 ± 0.01, PR-AUC = 0.93 ± 0.01, MCC = 0.77 ± 0.03, and G-mean = 0.88 ± 0.02, outperforming conventional machine learning and graph-based baselines. Predictive uncertainty analysis and counterfactual maps further supported the interpretation of threshold-sensitive predictions and substructural contribution patterns. The model was applied to screen 1.3 million compounds, resulting in 10 candidates for experimental validation. Three compounds showed measurable larvicidal activity against A. aegypti larvae. Among them, LC-79 emerged as the most promising hit, with 2-day and 5-day LC50 values of 0.24 μg/mL (0.66 μM) and 0.05 μg/mL (0.13 μM), respectively, an IE50 of 0.06 μg/mL (0.16 μM), and rapid larval mortality (LT50 = 1.10 days at 1 μg/mL). LC-79 also showed no measurable acute toxicity to Daphnia magna at the highest tested concentration [EC50–48h > 43 μg/mL (> 119 μM)], resulting in selectivity indices > 180 and > 860 relative to its 2-day and 5-day LC50 values. Overall, this study demonstrates that contrastive graph learning can move beyond retrospective larvicide modeling to experimentally validated hit discovery, identifying LC-79 as a potent and preliminarily selective acylthiourea larvicide candidate for further mechanism-of-action, resistance, and semifield evaluation.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction for Photoresist Materials
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Vast knowledge dispersed across the unstructured literature remains an indispensable complement to photoresist development. However, the intricate relationships among formulation, processing, and performance are not only scattered throughout publications but also complicated by semantic heterogeneity and contextual ambiguity, hindering knowledge management that extends beyond simple retrieval. To address these issues, we employed large language models (LLMs) to construct a photoresist material knowledge graph (KG) covering synthesis, properties, and applications. From nearly 12,000 full-text documents, we extracted 320,000 entities, 178,000 relationships, and 1,172,000 attribute entries. By integrating this KG with an LLM via a dual-path retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) strategy, we achieved 95.33% accuracy on a domain-specific question-answering task, substantially outperforming the standalone LLM (76.67%). This work offers a reference framework for knowledge management and intelligent reasoning in the photoresist field.
papers.zh: 基于大语言模型的感光材料知识图谱构建

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.
papers.zh: 用于将基于结构的分子生成与按需化学空间相匹配的强化学习

papers.title: Enabling Computational Exploration of an Expanding Academic Chemistry Space
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Ultralarge virtual libraries have become a cornerstone of modern early stage drug discovery, enabling the rapid exploration of billions of compounds. The chemical space accessible to most screening campaigns, however, remains constrained not by the availability of building blocks, which are broadly shared across vendor catalogs, but by the narrow set of well-established reaction chemistries used to combine them. To address this limitation, we present the continued development of the Pan-Canadian Chemical Library (PCCL), a community-driven effort to expand the accessible chemical space beyond commercial libraries by incorporating synthetic reactions developed across academic laboratories in Canada. The current release of the PCCL is contributed by seven Canadian academic groups. Using broadly available commercial building blocks, the resulting reaction space spans on the order of 1017 theoretically reachable drug-like compounds. Moreover, using cheap building blocks from ChemSpace (≤\$100/100 mg), an explicitly enumerated and experimentally actionable sublibrary of approximately 77 M compounds suitable for high-throughput virtual screening was generated. Comparison with the Enamine REAL library reveals that PCCL occupies a largely orthogonal chemical space, with fewer than 0.1% Bemis–Murcko scaffolds shared between the two libraries. Rather than explicitly enumerating the full 1017 compound space, we introduce a PostgreSQL/RDKit-backed hit-expansion framework that enables targeted enumeration and analog retrieval directly within the reaction space. The expanded PCCL demonstrates how a community-sourced initiative can provide a scalable mechanism to access novel chemical space and support early stage drug discovery against challenging and underexplored biological targets.
papers.zh: 助力对不断扩大的学术化学领域的计算探索

papers.title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this limitation, we developed a spatially resolved computational framework that integrates spatial transcriptomics to improve the prediction of anticancer drugs. Using a data set of 1291 diverse compounds, we compared the predictive performance of conventional disease-specific bulk signatures with that of localized spatial gene expression signatures. Whereas bulk signatures yielded insufficient predictive performance, incorporating spatial information improved prediction accuracy. Analysis of the predicted drug rankings further demonstrated that the spatial layer substantially improved the prioritization of known anticancer drugs while also identifying unclassified and nononcology compounds with potential anticancer effects. These findings indicate that the predicted therapeutic relevance of a compound depends on localized transcriptomic states rather than representing a static property across an entire heterogeneous tumor section. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a robust, region-aware computational framework for accurately characterizing the anticancer properties of compounds and offers a more nuanced paradigm for transcriptomics-based drug evaluation.

papers.title: DeepMolVir: Learning Virtual Virus Representations for Sequence-Aware Virus–Inhibitor Activity Prediction
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus–inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound–virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound–virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.

papers.title: Rovibrational cross sections for the CO2 0000, 0110, 0220, and Fermi resonance states 1000(1) and 1000(2) in collisions with He atoms
authors: Floris F. S. van der Tak
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We present quantum scattering calculations of CO2–He state-to-state integral cross sections for 25 transition sets, covering pure rotational transitions within and rovibrational transitions between: the ground state 0000, the bend fundamental 0110, the bending overtone 0220, and the Fermi doublet states 1000(1) and 1000(2). Exact coupled-channel (CC) and coupled-states approximation (CSA) calculations are performed using a new five-dimensional potential energy surface. The calculations cover collision energies from 20 to 5220 cm−1, sufficient to obtain converged rate coefficients over 100–800 K, and include initial rotational states for each transition up to at least j = 35. We present an energy-grid algorithm for rovibrational quantum scattering calculations that minimizes the number of separate calculations required. The resulting cross sections exhibit a dominant Δj = 0 propensity and parity-dependent patterns. For the benchmark 0000, j′ ← 0110, j transition, thermally averaged rate coefficients reproduce available experimental data. A comparison between the CC and CSA cross sections shows that for vibrational quenching transitions, the CSA cross sections increasingly deviate from the CC results with increasing initial rotational state j. Calculated integral cross sections cover collision energies and rotational states needed to derive rate coefficients for radiative transfer modeling of mid-infrared CO2 spectra from environments that are not in local thermal equilibrium. The computationally simpler CO2–He system allows the methodology and approximations to be tested at high collision energies and rotational states, helping assess their suitability for the more complex and astrochemically important CO2–H2 system.

papers.title: Observable-specific kinetic-domain hierarchies in Markovian population dynamics
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Markovian population dynamics on a network are commonly formulated through a master equation for site populations and analyzed either in the site representation or in terms of independently evolving eigenmodes. Neither description directly resolves the relaxation of a selected observable into kinetically interpretable stages. We develop an observable-specific kinetic-domain (KD) representation that recasts this relaxation as a kinetic hierarchy. The resulting basis is algebraically equivalent to that obtained by Arnoldi orthogonalization of an observable-seeded Krylov sequence. This hierarchy describes the multidimensional population dynamics as a funnel-like sequence of kinetic stages with collective site-space structures and interstage transition rates. Generalized survival functions (GSFs) on nested kinetic subspaces then yield an exact stagewise decomposition of the time-dependent observable relaxation and, upon time integration, a characteristic passage time for each stage, thereby identifying the rate-determining stage and revealing the underlying relaxation mechanism. Applications to analytically solvable networks and extended two-dimensional lattices demonstrate how the KD/GSF framework resolves complex relaxation into interpretable collective stages and show that similar global relaxation time scales can conceal markedly different underlying sequences of kinetic steps. By extracting the collective kinetic pathway relevant to the selected observable, the KD representation complements site- and eigenmode-based descriptions and can enable dimensional reduction in large stochastic networks.

papers.title: Real-space vs interelectronic exchange mixing for the prediction of low-lying Rydberg excitations within time-dependent density functional theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Low-lying Rydberg excitations are a challenge for linear-response time-dependent density functional theory because many functionals substantially underestimate their energies due to self-interaction error. The established remedy is range separation, which switches to full exact exchange (EXX) at large interelectronic distances. Local hybrid functionals instead control the EXX admixture through a real-space local mixing function (LMF), and range-separated local hybrids (RSLHs) combine both mixing schemes. Here, we analyze the two mixing coordinates by evaluating 87 Rydberg (3s and 3p) and 75 valence excitation energies from the QUEST database. A benchmark of 18 functionals shows that range-separated hybrids, some local hybrids, and RSLHs describe these states with comparable accuracy, with the best of each class reaching Rydberg mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.14–0.20 eV, but differences in their other ingredients prevent attributing this accuracy to either scheme. We therefore scan the LMF prefactor b and the range-separation parameter ω for a curated subset. A full-range EXX admixture, supplied through the LMF or a global fraction, describes these states more accurately than pure range separation (best Rydberg MAEs of 0.12 vs 0.20 eV). For RSLHs, the global Rydberg optimum lies at ω = 0, so range separation offers no further gain once real-space mixing is optimized. Real-space mixing incurs smaller barrier-height penalties when Rydberg-optimal parameters are transferred to ground-state properties, and a small ω can reconcile Rydberg and atomization-energy accuracy in LSDA-based RSLHs. For future RSLHs, we recommend encoding low-lying Rydberg states in the LMF, leaving the range-separation parameter for properties requiring long-range EXX, notably charge-transfer excitations.

papers.title: Position-and conformation-dependent effects of fluorination on the structure and methyl internal rotation of methyl benzoates
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The effects of fluorination on molecular structure and internal dynamics were investigated in monofluorinated methyl benzoates (methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, methyl 3-fluorobenzoate, and methyl 4-fluorobenzoate) using high-resolution rotational spectroscopy in combination with quantum-chemical calculations. Two conformers were identified for methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, whereas only one conformer each was observed for the 3- and 4-fluorinated species. All observed conformers exhibited A/E torsional splittings arising from internal rotation of the ester methyl rotor and were analyzed using the XIAM code. The experimentally derived barriers V3 lie in the range of 425–460 cm−1, exhibiting both position- and conformation-dependent behavior. The syn conformer of methyl 2-fluorobenzoate exhibits the largest barrier, whereas the barriers for anti-methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, anti-methyl 3-fluorobenzoate, and methyl 4-fluorobenzoate are close to that of methyl benzoate. Quantum-chemically predicted equilibrium structures indicate that the structural perturbations induced by fluorination are primarily localized near the substitution site. In the syn conformer of methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, the shorter F⋯HCH3 distance places the negative electrostatic region around fluorine closer to the positively polarized methyl hydrogen atoms. This proximity is consistent with enhanced local interactions that may contribute to its larger torsional barrier. These results demonstrate that the effect of fluorination on methyl internal rotation depends not only on the substitution position but also on the conformer-specific spatial arrangement of fluorine relative to the ester methyl rotor.
papers.zh: 氟化对甲基苯甲酸酯结构和甲基内部旋转的位置和构象依赖性影响

papers.title: Signatures of auxeticity in microgels at low and ultralow crosslinker concentration
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Auxetic behavior, characterized by a negative Poisson’s ratio, is a counterintuitive mechanical response exhibited, among other systems, by certain polymer networks. Here, through in silico simulations, we investigate the mechanical response of thermoresponsive microgels across the volume phase transition upon varying crosslinker concentration down to ultralow crosslinker (ULC) conditions, a regime so far unexplored. After refining the method to estimate the elastic moduli based on equilibrium shape fluctuations for the challenging case of ULCs, which are very sparse networks with rather anisotropic shapes, we are able to show signatures of the onset of auxetic behavior near the volume phase transition for microgels with crosslinker concentration of ∼1%. In addition, we find that ULC microgels exhibit a tendency toward negative Poisson’s ratio across the entire swollen regime. Further examining the auxetic response within the inner region of the network, we also demonstrate that, for ULC microgels, this extends across all length scales, suggesting that it is an intrinsic property of the weakly connected polymer network. The present findings should likely stimulate novel experimental investigations, aiming to measure the Poisson’s ratio of individual low and ultralow crosslinked microgels, to verify these intriguing numerical predictions.

papers.title: Origin of long-lived nuclear spin states and coherences in aliphatic chains revealed by relaxation theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Delocalized long-lived states (LLSs) and collective zero-quantum long-lived coherences (LLCs) in aliphatic chains provide a promising route for preserving nuclear spin order on timescales exceeding conventional longitudinal and transverse relaxation times, respectively. Their extended lifetimes make them attractive for applications including hyperpolarization storage, ligand-observed drug screening based on the loss of longevity upon binding to a target protein, and quantum information processing exploiting collective properties of many-body spin systems. Although LLSs and LLCs have been observed experimentally in methylene networks, their origin and general structure in chains of arbitrary length have remained unclear. Here we show that these relaxation-protected modes follow directly from Redfield relaxation theory by constructing the null space of the dominant intra-pair dipole–dipole relaxation superoperator. For a chain containing N methylene groups, this subspace contains 2N − 1 independent non-trivial operators, excluding the identity operator. When the two geminal protons are chemically equivalent within each methylene group, global intra-pair parity restricts experimental access to at most 2N − 2 of these operators. We develop a general framework for constructing the corresponding long-lived operators for chains of arbitrary length and illustrate it explicitly for N = 2, 3, and 4. Numerical simulations that explicitly account for coherent evolution and inter-pair dipole–dipole relaxation closely reproduce the experimentally observed decay dynamics and further demonstrate that the resulting LLSs and LLCs exhibit lifetimes substantially longer than the corresponding T1 and T2 relaxation times, respectively.

papers.title: Dipole moment of the YbOH molecule
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The YbOH molecule is a sensitive system to use in searches for fundamental symmetry violations. Its molecular-frame permanent and transition dipole moments are of key importance for preparing and interpreting experiments. We calculate these quantities for the lowest bending vibrational modes of the ground electronic state. A high-level coupled cluster method for electronic structure calculations, together with averaging over vibrational states, was employed to obtain accurate values.

papers.title: Generalized vibrational perturbation theory in curvilinear internal coordinates: Theory and applications
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Second-order vibrational perturbation theory (VPT2) is widely employed for the calculation of anharmonic vibrational properties thanks to its favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost. However, the presence of strong vibrational resonances requires dedicated treatments beyond standard perturbative approaches. In this work, a generalized VPT2 framework based on curvilinear internal coordinates is developed. Closed-form expressions are derived for the interaction terms associated with Fermi and Darling–Dennison resonances, including 1–1, 2–2, and 1–3 couplings. In contrast to conventional Cartesian-coordinate formulations, the present treatment accounts for additional kinetic-energy contributions arising from the non-diagonal form of the vibrational kinetic-energy operator. The resulting methodology has been implemented in a general computational engine and has been validated through applications to representative molecular systems. The importance of the variational treatment of resonances is highlighted through the investigation of selected case studies, while the flexibility of the proposed framework is demonstrated through its combination with dual-level schemes employing different electronic-structure methods for harmonic and anharmonic contributions. The present work extends the applicability of perturb-then-diagonalize approaches in curvilinear coordinates and provides an efficient route toward accurate anharmonic calculations for medium- and large-sized molecular systems.
papers.zh: 曲线内部坐标的广义振动摄动理论：理论与应用

papers.title: Nonlinear canonical transformations for studying spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories offer promising avenues, they are not yet black-box methods and often require substantial system-specific development. Spin Hamiltonians such as the XXZ and J1–J2 models provide compact but demanding benchmarks for these challenges. In particular, spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. In this work, we introduce a nonlinear spin–fermion–spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian to a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and J1–J2 Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions because nonlocal strings appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.
