papers.title: Composition-dependent thermal and ionic conduction in NASICONs: Insights from molecular dynamics simulations
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The ongoing quest to optimize solid-state batteries in terms of sustainability, cost, and efficiency has shifted the focus to sodium-based battery materials. This study investigates the thermal and ionic conductivities of crystalline sodium superionic conductors of the type Na1+xZr2SixP3−xO12 (x = 0, 1.5, 1.6, 2.0, 2.4, 2.5, 2.8, 3.0) using molecular dynamics simulations. Thermal conductivities are calculated using the Green–Kubo approach at temperatures of 150, 300, 623, and 900 K. Furthermore, sodium ion diffusion constants are derived from mean-square displacements. The highest thermal conductivity is obtained for x = 0 at all temperatures. For all stoichiometries, thermal conductivity decreases with increasing temperature. Among all fractional stoichiometries, the activation barrier for ion diffusion is found to be lowest for x = 2.8. The influence of ion diffusion on thermal conductivity is shown to be negligible by artificially altering the activation barrier. However, we demonstrate that the standard Green–Kubo method strongly overestimates thermal conductivity in stoichiometries with high ionic diffusivity because of spurious convective heat flux contributions. Taking into account only the conductive part of the heat flux yields reliable results that match those from nonequilibrium simulations, cepstral analysis accounting for sodium ion mass flux, and experiments. The underlying thermal transport mechanism is analyzed using the theory of Allen and Feldman for disordered solids. The dominant transport mechanism across all investigated temperatures and stoichiometries is found to be the diffusive propagation of delocalized, non-plane-wave-like vibrational modes called diffusons. However, in the end members at 150 K, competing mechanisms are also likely to occur.
papers.zh: NASICONs中成分依赖的热导和离子导电：分子动力学模拟的见解

papers.title: Chiral vibrational modes and vibrational circular dichroism
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: The recent interest in chiral phonons in a variety of physical phenomena and their hypothesized role in the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect [Fransson, Phys. Rev. Res. 5, L022039 (2023)] call for further investigation into the chirality of molecular vibrations. Although molecular chirality has conventionally been quantified using structural properties, recent work has highlighted the role of dynamical response properties as chirality metrics. In this work, we examine an inter-atom helicity pseudoscalar as a complementary measure of vibrational chirality, associated with the vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) intensity in the fixed partial charge (FPC) approximation. This pseudoscalar is translationally and rotationally invariant, can distinguish between opposite enantiomers and, unlike the atomic pseudoscalar measure considered in our earlier work [Abraham and Nitzan, Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 268001 (2024)], does not rely on a predefined symmetry axis. For a twisted ethane model as well as several small molecules, this pseudoscalar correlates well with structural descriptors based on the continuous chirality measure. Overall, our results support response-based metrics as a physically meaningful and practically useful characterization of vibrational chirality. Importantly, while the FPC-based VCD estimate provides a useful quantifier of vibrational chirality, we show that it is a rather poor predictor of the actual molecular VCD response because the latter is strongly influenced by the (vibrational configuration-dependent) molecular electronic response.
papers.zh: 手性振动模式和振动圆二色性

papers.title: Simple algorithm for evaluating SU(2) non-abelian geometric phase in the vicinity of molecular conical intersection of odd electron number
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Molecular conical intersection of odd-electron number are known to give arise to non-abelian geometric phases. In this work, we present a simple algorithm for evaluating the SU(2) geometric phases given a trajectory represented as a discrete set of coordinates in the five-dimensional branching space. Motivated by the special property that such conical intersection behaves as abelian ones in three-dimensional subspace, we take two steps to establish the algorithm. We first prove that it is possible to construct an augmented trajectory consisting of spherical triangles that has the same geometric phases as the original trajectory. We then prove that the geometric phase contribution from each spherical triangle can be evaluated from its properties using Stokes’ theorem in a way that closely resembles abelian conical intersections. The total geometric phases are thus evaluated by path-ordered products of contributions from each spherical triangle. Based on the augmented trajectory, we further show that the geometric phases of the upper and lower states will switch under inversion transformation of the trajectory. This relation is further generalized to show that the Wilson loop, defined as the trace of the geometric phases, will switch between the two states under any five-dimensional improper isometric transformation. Example calculations of geometric phases for trajectories generated on five-dimensional polytopes are also presented and discussed.
papers.zh: 用于评估奇电子数分子锥形交叉点附近SU(2)非阿贝尔几何相的简单算法

papers.title: Third-order size-consistent Brillouin–Wigner perturbation theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Low-order Rayleigh–Schrödinger perturbation theory with Møller–Plesset partitioning is size-consistent but not regular, and for this reason, the third-order variant, MP3, is not commonly used in computational quantum chemistry. Recently, it has become clear how to modify Brillouin–Wigner perturbation theory at second order to be both size-consistent and regular, by using a non-Møller–Plesset partitioning to define BWs2. In this work, a solution is presented for the problem of defining an iterative third-order generalization, iBWs3, that is, size-consistent, regular, and exact for the electron correlation of two electrons in two orbitals. iBWs3 can be seen as a scaled symmetrized version of coupled cluster theory with doubles including only the linear and the mosaic quadratic terms, thus with the same compute scaling. An implementation and a series of tests on restricted orbital dissociations and relative energies are reported.
papers.zh: 三阶大小一致的布里渊-维格纳微扰理论

papers.title: Recent developments in TURBOMOLE
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: TURBOMOLE is a general-purpose quantum-chemical and materials science program suite for large-scale and high-throughput simulations of molecules and periodic systems of arbitrary dimensionality. The primary focus is on robust and highly efficient methods from first principles. Applications range from the interpretation or even prediction of various spectroscopic results to the elucidation of catalytic or reaction mechanisms. In this review, we summarize the latest developments between 2020 and 2026, consisting of substantial advances in density functional theory and coupled-cluster methods of ground and excited states, relativistic approaches for magnetic properties, and embedding or multiscale frameworks. In addition, the introduction of a new complete active space and configuration interaction module extends the capabilities of the program suite to multireference systems with strong static correlation. Finally, the user-friendliness was greatly improved with TURBOMOLE version 8.0 (2025) by new input formats and default settings making simulations easily possible for expert and non-expert users with a diverse chemical, physical, materials science, or biochemical education and training.
papers.zh: TURBOMOLE的最新动态

papers.title: Structure–flexibility relationships at low dielectric dialkyl ester liquid surfaces of DES, DEO, DEA, and DBS: A vibrational spectroscopy and MD simulations study
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: Dialkyl esters, such as dibutyl sebacate (DBS), diethyl sebacate (DES), and diethyl adipate (DEA), are attractive, less-toxic alternatives to phthalate plasticizers, yet a mechanistic understanding of their behavior at soft interfaces, where wetting, adhesion, and physicochemical interactions are governed, remains limited. Resolving molecular orientation and organization at liquid–air interfaces is challenging with conventional techniques. Here, we combine sum frequency generation (SFG) vibrational spectroscopy with complementary infrared, Raman measurements, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the interfacial structure of low-dielectric esters [DBS, DES, DEA, and diethyl oxalate (DEO)]. SFG reveals that terminal methyl group orientations vary substantially across the series, with DES exhibiting a pronounced tilt toward the surface plane relative to DBS, DEA, and DEO. The analysis of CH2/CH3 symmetric stretching intensity ratios indicates a higher population of gauche conformations and increased conformational disorder at the DES interface despite its shared sebacate backbone with DBS. MD simulations support these observations, showing differences in alkyl chain ordering, flexibility, and carbonyl–carbonyl separation, and yielding tilt angles broadly consistent with experiment for DES while highlighting sensitivity in SFG-derived values to optical and hyperpolarizability assumptions. Notably, the CH3 Fermi resonance ratio and surface tension follow similar trends (DES > DEA > DBS ≈ DEO) across the dialkyl ester series, linking enhanced conformational flexibility and intermolecular packing heterogeneity at the molecular scale to macroscopic interfacial properties. These results enhance our understanding of soft low-dielectric liquid interfaces more broadly.
papers.zh: DES、DEO、DEA和DBS的低介电常数二烷基酯液体表面的结构-柔性关系：振动光谱和MD模拟研究

papers.title: Hybrid mechanics of coupled qubits
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: We find that a technique analogous to hybrid mechanics previously developed for Gaussian coherent states and molecular vibrations, can be extended to SU(2) coherent states describing coupled qubits. This formulation reveals a sparse structure of the propagator, leading to a computationally efficient scheme while maintaining numerical accuracy. As a result, the method enables simulations of larger qubit systems on classical computers. In particular, we demonstrate accurate real-time propagation for systems of up to 21 qubits, which would be computationally demanding using straightforward quantum-dynamics approaches.

papers.title: Symmetry adapted auxiliary density perturbation theory
papers.jname: The Journal of Chemical Physics
papers.abs: It is shown that the linear response equations of auxiliary density perturbation theory take a block diagonal form when symmetry adapted auxiliary functions are employed. Symmetry adapted linear combinations of primary and auxiliary functions were prepared by diagonalizing a nuclear attraction matrix and explicitly building real irreducible representations. Numerical results are provided as a proof of concept showing that all matrices required as building blocks of the response matrix take block diagonal form, together with the response matrix itself. Ionization energies and analytic Fukui functions are calculated to show the applicability on a small set of highly symmetric molecules.

papers.title: Polymorph-Dependent Reconstruction of Excitonic Coupling under Pressure Regulates Room Temperature Phosphorescence
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Pressure-responsive organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) offers a promising platform for optical sensing, information encryption, and anticounterfeiting. Understanding how external mechanical perturbations regulate triplet exciton dynamics in organic crystals remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state photochemistry. Here, density functional theory (DFT) and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) excited-state calculations are combined to compare the pressure-dependent RTP behavior of ToMoT-α and ToMoT-β. Despite nearly identical emission at ambient pressure, ToMoT-α exhibits a strongly nonmonotonic spectral excursion of 102 nm (449–551 nm), whereas ToMoT-β varies by only 10 nm. This divergence originates from their contrasting anisotropic compressibility and pressure adaptability. Under compression, ToMoT-α undergoes directional lattice relaxation and molecular reorganization, reconstructing intermolecular excitonic coupling and modulating triplet-state decay kinetics, whereas ToMoT-β largely preserves its structure and photophysical properties. These complementary responses support a conceptual dual-polymorph platform for self-referenced pressure readout and recovery-state discrimination. Ambient-pressure reoptimization further suggests that the relative crystal-energy difference can serve as a qualitative descriptor of structural recovery tendency. This work establishes a structure-packing and excited-state relationship for pressure-responsive organic phosphorescence and identifies polymorphism as a strategy for programming RTP responses.
papers.zh: 压力下激子耦合的多晶型物依赖性重构调节室温磷光

papers.title: Regulation of Amplified Spontaneous Emission Dynamics in Quasi-Two-Dimensional Perovskites via the Energy-Funneling Effect
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Quasi-two-dimensional perovskites with mixed-phase multiple-quantum-well distributions are promising gain media for amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), but the regulatory role of phase distribution in ASE behavior remains unclear. Here, quasi-two-dimensional (BA)2(MA)n−1PbnBr3n+1 films with different phase distributions were investigated using steady-state optical spectroscopy, femtosecond Kerr-gated time-resolved ASE measurements, and transient absorption spectroscopy. Compared with large-n-dominated films, those with a more balanced phase distribution exhibit a lower ASE threshold, smaller emission-peak shift, and weaker line width broadening. Time-resolved ASE and transient absorption analyses further indicate that small-n phases buffer photoexcited carriers and delay their transfer into large-n emissive phases, thereby moderating carrier accumulation in the emissive phase and yielding a more stable emission wavelength and narrower line width. These findings clarify how phase distribution regulates ASE through carrier buffering and redistribution, demonstrating phase engineering as an effective strategy for stable perovskite gain media.
papers.zh: 通过能量漏斗效应调控准二维钙钛矿中的放大自发辐射动力学

papers.title: Mechanistic Origin of the 2e– CO2 Reduction Selectivity of Single-Atom Catalysts via Kinetic Bifurcation of *COOH
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Electrochemical two-electron CO2 reduction (2e– CO2RR) to carbon monoxide (CO) and formic acid (HCOOH) on single-atom catalysts (SACs) has long been rationalized by independent reaction pathways initiated from distinct CO2 adsorption modes. Here, employing constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations combined with the slow-growth enhanced sampling, we demonstrate that product selectivity across diverse SACs is governed by the kinetic bifurcation of a common *COOH intermediate. We uncover that the initial CO2 activation proceeds via cation-assisted chemisorption even on electron-deficient metal centers such as Sb and Sn. The downstream product branching originates from a kinetic competition between CO and HCOOH formation, which effectively explains experimental selectivity. Beyond reproducing empirical trends, our findings establish *COOH bifurcation kinetics as a key governing principle for 2e– CO2RR, providing mechanistic insights for the rational design of selective SACs.
papers.zh: 通过*COOH的动力学分叉实现单原子催化剂2e– CO2还原选择性的机理起源

papers.title: Polar Heterolayered Oxychalcogenides Enable Strong Nonlinear Optical Effect and Dual Midinfrared Transparent Windows
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Midinfrared (mid-IR) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals are essential for laser and photonic technologies, yet existing materials frequently suffer from either weak NLO response or narrow IR transparency. Herein, we propose a polar heterolayered design strategy to overcome this limitation in oxychalcogenides by integrating cooperative layer polarization, optical anisotropy, and phonon decoupling. Guided by this approach, we identify LaGaOSe2, which features a polar heterolayered structure. This material exhibits a strong NLO response comparable to that of AgGaS2, a large birefringence of 0.2, and a bandgap of 2.36 eV. Remarkably, vibrational decoupling between the heterogeneous sublayers produces a pronounced phonon gap in LaGaOSe2, giving rise to predicted dual IR transparent windows within the one-phonon approximation. This work identifies LaGaOSe2 as a promising mid-IR NLO crystal and provides an intriguing structural strategy for designing high-performance IR-NLO materials through cooperative polarization and vibrational engineering in heterolayered systems.
papers.zh: 极性异层氧硫族化物实现强非线性光学效应和双中红外透明窗口

papers.title: Enhancing Predictive Simulations of Conjugated Polymers through Exciton-Coupled Dynamics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abs: Among the semiconducting conjugated polymers (CPs), cis-polyacetylene (cis-PA) has recently received attention due to its advances in organic electronics applications. Excitonic effects and energy dissipation affect the critical properties of these materials. Here, cis-PA oligomers are studied in two different forms: (a) pristine cis-PA (undoped) and (b) cis-PA codoped with sodium and phosphorus fluoride. We introduce the Bethe–Salpeter equation (BSE) + Redfield framework for converting nonradiative energy dissipation channels from an independent orbital approximation (IOA) framework to an excitonic basis. The excitonic nonradiative and radiative channels are used to calculate rates for photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Excitonic effects produce system-dependent changes in phonon-mediated relaxation. They accelerate relaxation and reduce the PLQY in undoped cis-PA, while slowing relaxation and increasing the PLQY relative to the IOA description in codoped cis-PA. These findings emphasize the influence of state degeneracy and electron–hole (e–h) interactions, which are inherently captured within the exciton framework.
papers.zh: 通过激子耦合动力学增强共轭聚合物的预测模拟

papers.title: Photoresponsive Selenium Nanoparticle Colloids: A Pathway toward Chalcogen-Based Liquid Semiconducting Materials
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Conventional semiconductor technologies rely on pure, highly ordered crystalline solids in which electronic coherence and minimal defect densities enable band-like charge transport. Liquids, in contrast, generally lack long-range structural order and conduct electricity (if at all) through ionic motion or hopping mechanisms. The development of liquid materials exhibiting semiconducting behavior could therefore offer substantial advantages, including compositional versatility, tolerance to defects and impurities, environmental stability, and compatibility with scalable deposition techniques. In this work, we demonstrate that elemental selenium can be incorporated into systems based on the organic superbase 1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) to form stable colloids of amorphous selenium nanoparticles at room temperature, as confirmed with a selection of characterization techniques. Electrochemical and optical experiments reveal reversible photoresponsive behavior and most likely mixed ionic-electronic transport. While illumination induces a pronounced decrease in impedance and an increase in current response, consistent with photogenerated charge carriers within the bulk selenium phase. Although the system remains structurally disordered and colloidal in nature, it poses several characteristics commonly associated with semiconducting materials. Consequently, these DBU-stabilized colloids present a promising, synthetically simple platform for liquid semiconducting media that could offer a pathway toward defect-tolerant soft materials. The results from this study form a foundation that can inspire an interest in a research area involving liquid semiconductors, soft electronics, adaptive materials, ionic-electronic coupling, and photodoped fluids.
papers.zh: 光敏硒纳米颗粒胶体：通往基于硫族元素的液体半导体材料的途径

papers.title: Ionization Energies, Electron Affinities, Bandgaps, Exciton Binding Energies, and Polarization Energies of Orientation-Controlled Picene, [6]-Phenacene, and [7]-Phenacene Thin Films
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Phenacenes, in which benzene rings are fused in a zigzag manner, are chemically robust π-conjugated hydrocarbons of interest for organic electronic applications and superconductivity. However, quantitative electronic parameters of phenacene thin films remain limited compared with those of acenes. Here, we determine the ionization energies (IEs), electron affinities (EAs), bandgaps, exciton binding energies, and polarization energies of orientation-controlled thin films of picene, [6]-phenacene, and [7]-phenacene using ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy and low-energy inverse photoelectron spectroscopy. The energy parameters depend only weakly on molecular size. In contrast, both IE and EA exhibit large orientation-dependent shifts of approximately 1 eV: lying films show IEs of 6.28–6.42 eV and EAs of 2.20–2.39 eV, whereas standing films show IEs of 5.54–5.74 eV and EAs of 1.46–1.73 eV. Nevertheless, the bandgaps of approximately 4 eV and exciton binding energies of approximately 1 eV remain nearly independent of molecular size and orientation. Analysis of polarization energies shows that the induction term is nearly orientation independent, whereas the electrostatic term strongly depends on orientation and originates primarily from molecular quadrupole moments. These results identify molecular orientation as a key factor governing frontier energy levels in phenacene thin films.
papers.zh: 取向受控肟、[6]-菲并苯和[7]-菲并苯薄膜的电离能、电子亲和能、带隙、激子结合能和极化能

papers.title: Li/Na Mixed Metal Nitride as a Protective Layer for Na Metal Anodes
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Artificial interphases are essential for stabilizing the highly reactive alkali-metal anode/solid-electrolyte interface in solid-state batteries, yet identifying materials that simultaneously possess high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability remains a major challenge. Here, we propose mixed alkali-metal nitride Li2NaN as a protective interlayer for sodium–metal solid-state batteries. Density functional theory optimization and 10 ps ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the Li2NaN interlayer suppresses the decomposition of Na6PS5Cl over the simulated time window, preventing the formation of detrimental phosphorus sulfide species at the protected interface. To further investigate ion transport, molecular dynamics simulations based on a modified universal force field were performed for pristine and vacancy-engineered Li2NaN. While the pristine structure exhibits poor ionic diffusion, introducing Li/Na/N vacancies dramatically enhances alkali-ion transport. The optimized 2.5% vacancy structure achieves Na-ion and Li-ion conductivities of 10.78 and 1.50 mS/cm, respectively, exceeding those of most reported inorganic interphase materials. In particular, Na-ion transport is intrinsically faster than Li-ion transport in the mixed alkali-metal nitride framework. These results identify vacancy-engineered Li2NaN as a fast ion-conducting candidate interphase that is dynamically stable in the simulated interface, providing a rational strategy for designing protective layers for next-generation sodium–metal solid-state batteries.
papers.zh: 锂/钠混合金属氮化物作为钠金属阳极的保护层

papers.title: Increasing Surface-Exposed Lattice Oxygen in Medium-Entropy CoCrMOx Matrix for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: The rational design of promising non-noble-metal electrocatalysts with medium-entropy compositions for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains challenging. Herein, we report a sheet-like amorphous ternary Co–Cr–Fe oxide (CoCrFeOx) catalyst, whose overpotential requires merely 280 mV and 347 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm–2 in alkaline medium, respectively. Moreover, its specific activity at η400 reaches 25.9 mA cm–2, which is 3.1 times that observed for CoCrNiOx, and it demonstrates excellent stability over 50 h. Comprehensive XPS, XAS, methanol molecule probe, quasi-in situ EPR, and online DEMS experiments reveal that Fe incorporation not only increases the proportion of exposed lattice oxygen, reducing steric hindrance from hydroxyl-covered oxygen vacancies, but also slightly lowers the average Co valence, which facilitates the formation of high-valent Co3+ active sites under anodic polarization and the occurrence of the LOM. This work highlights the critical role of lattice oxygen and the Co electronic environment in boosting alkaline OER performance, offering a new avenue for designing multicomponent amorphous oxides as efficient electrocatalysts.
papers.zh: 在中熵CoCrMOx基体中增加表面暴露的晶格氧以实现高效析氧

papers.title: Boosted Energy Extraction from the CapMix Process by Grafting with Titratable Polymers
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Salinity gradient energy offers a sustainable route to convert ionic chemical potential differences into usable power. Capacitive mixing enables this conversion without membranes, but suffers from limited ion regulation at electrode interfaces. Here we show that, by grafting electrode surfaces with titrating polymers, the performance can be substantially improved. Using Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations with exact image-charge Ewald summations, we demonstrate how the coupled effects of ion adsorption and charge regulation in response to an external potential can be harnessed. Grafted electrodes are shown to deliver substantially more energy relative to bare surfaces, driven by charge regulation effects that exploit the pH difference that typically exists between rivers and the ocean. While the effect is in principle maximized at high grafting densities and moderate chain lengths, the performance is fairly robust to variations in these parameters, within reasonable bounds. Complementary classical polymer Density Functional Theory calculations confirm these trends, validating the mechanistic framework. This work also establishes a practical approach to harvest electrical energy during wastewater neutralization, where acidic (or alkaline) effluents serve as complementary reservoirs, and offers a promising strategy to couple environmental remediation with renewable energy recovery.
papers.zh: 通过与可滴定聚合物接枝来提高CapMix工艺的能量提取

papers.title: Confinement of Mononuclear Iron Hydroxides within CHA-Type Zeolite Cages for Stable Methane Oxidation Catalysis
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Mononuclear metal centers offer molecularly defined catalytic active sites but readily aggregate under reaction conditions. Here we show that a simple post-treatment for Fe-containing CHA-type zeolite produces cha-cage-confined mononuclear Fe hydroxides. Acid treatment removes external hematite while preserving the CHA topology. UV–vis and NH3-TPD indicate highly dispersed residual Fe species in the micropores after the acid treatment. Fe K-edge XANES exhibits an enhanced pre-edge peak, and FT/WT-EXAFS shows Fe–O coordination with no significant Fe–Fe scattering; curve fitting gives a short Fe–O distance of 1.87 Å, consistent with four-coordinate Fe3+. In addition, 57Fe Mössbauer spectra are dominated by quadrupole-split absorption from high-spin Fe3+, and the magnetically split components of hematite present in the parent material disappear after acid treatment. XANES spectra simulated for the density functional theory (DFT)-optimized Fe(OH)3(H2O) model reproduce the measured increase in pre-edge intensity relative to hematite. Automated reaction route mapping with periodic DFT identifies Fe(OH)3(H2O) as the most plausible cage-confined species. Such confined mononuclear Fe hydroxides catalyze the oxidation of methane with H2O2, while maintaining both catalytic activity and their local Fe structure during recycling, without detectable Fe leaching. Transition-state calculations reveal a possibility of concerted H atom transfer from CH4 to H2O2 assisted by a proton relay around an Fe(OH)4 intermediate. This work establishes a simple route to robust, cage-confined mononuclear Fe hydroxides that couple molecular-level definition with solid-state stability for the liquid-phase methane oxidation.
papers.zh: 将单核氢氧化铁限制在CHA型沸石笼中以实现稳定的甲烷氧化催化

papers.title: Chemical Interface Damping Controlled by Interfacial Linkers in Plasmonic Nanoparticle-Polyaniline Hybrids
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Metal nanoparticle-conductive polymer hybrids combine strong light absorption, functional tunability, and pathways for energy and charge transfer, yet linker-specific plasmon damping remains poorly understood. Here, single-particle hyperspectral imaging quantifies plasmon resonance energies and homogeneous line widths in gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), AuNP-polyaniline (PANI), AuNP-4-aminothiophenol (ATP)-PANI, and AuNP-N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-PANI hybrids. PANI produces the plasmon red-shift, whereas chemisorbed ATP and NHC linkers induce further red-shifts and pronounced chemical interface damping (CID). AuNP-PANI establishes a CID baseline dominated by plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer (PIRET) to PANI, a contribution also present in both linked hybrids. Beyond the PIRET contributions, the additional damping is assigned to linker-specific plasmon-induced interfacial charge transfer: resonant electron transfer from Au into unoccupied ATP-derived states and resonant hole transfer involving occupied NHC-derived states near the Au Fermi level. Favorable hole transfer alignment and conductive Au–C bridging are consistent with the slightly larger CID of NHC-linked hybrids. These results connect interfacial bonding motifs to distinct plasmon damping pathways and identify interfacial chemistry as a design parameter for plasmon energy extraction.
papers.zh: 由等离激元纳米颗粒-聚苯胺杂化材料中界面连接体控制的化学界面阻尼

papers.title: Phonon Spectral Characteristics Outweigh Bonding Hierarchy in MSe0.5Te0.5/MSe Thermoelectrics
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
papers.abs: Low lattice thermal conductivity (κl) in crystalline solids is often attributed to bonding hierarchy arising from the coexistence of weak and strong chemical bonds. However, the extent to which the bonding hierarchy alone can dictates the intrinsic heat transport remains unclear. Here, using first-principles calculations combined with density functional theory, we investigate the lattice dynamics and carrier transport properties of MSe0.5Te0.5/MSe (M = Ga, In, and Tl) bilayer heterostructures with broken out-of-plane mirror symmetry. The interfacing of Janus MSe0.5Te0.5 layer onto a pristine MSe monolayer provides an ideal platform to disentangle the relative roles of bonding hierarchy and phonon spectral characteristics in determining κl. All the studied heterostructures are found to be energetically and dynamically stable. TlSe0.5Te0.5/TlSe exhibits an ultralow κl of 0.76 W/mK at 300 K, originating from strong phonon softening and bunching together with enhanced Tl rattling vibrations induced by localized charge accumulation that weakens Tl-centered bonds. More importantly, despite possessing a weaker bonding environment, InSe0.5Te0.5/InSe exhibits a higher κl than GaSe0.5Te0.5/GaSe BH. This anomalous trend is attributed to pronounced phonon branching and the absence of a phonon band gap in the intermediate optical range of Ga-based heterostructure, which activate additional three-phonon scattering channels and substantially reduce phonon lifetimes. These findings demonstrate that phonon spectral characteristics can outweigh conventional bonding hierarchy effects in governing lattice thermal transport. Furthermore, the Janus interface preserves favorable carrier transport while suppressing the Mexican-hat-like valence-band dispersion. Consequently, maximum thermoelectric figures of merit of 2.08 (p– type), 2.82 (n– type), and 0.38 (p– type) are achieved for GaSe0.5Te0.5/GaSe, InSe0.5Te0.5/InSe, and TlSe0.5Te0.5/TlSe, respectively, at 800 K.
papers.zh: 在MSe0.5Te0.5/MSe热电材料中，声子谱特性比键合层次更重要

papers.title: Amyloid versus Hydrogel Fibrillar Architectures in Short Amyloidogenic Peptides: Structural Insights at Amino Acid Resolution
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Amyloid peptides self-assemble into either pathogenic insoluble fibrils or functional hydrogel networks, yet their molecular-level structural differences remain poorly understood. This study utilized isotope-edited Infrared (IR) and vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) spectroscopies to compare the residue-level structures of amyloid and hydrogel fibrils formed by short peptide fragments from α-synuclein (SYN), human islet amyloid polypeptide (hIAPP), and Lactoferrin (LAN). Results showed that structural differences depend heavily on the peptide sequence. For SYN, short, bundled amyloid fibrils form in-registry parallel β-sheets, whereas long hydrogel networks contain parallel β-sheets with a minor C-terminal helical turn, exhibiting opposite supramolecular chirality. Similarly, IAP assemblies display opposite chirality and parallel β-sheets, but distinct coupling interactions reveal different local packing arrangements. Conversely, both LAN fibril types show identical long morphologies, matching supramolecular chirality, and parallel β-sheets mixed with N-terminal β-turn/loop involvement. Overall, isotope-edited IR and VCD analysis confirm that amyloid and hydrogel fibrils possess distinct molecular arrangements, twists, and morphologies dictated by their secondary structure in the corresponding fibril forms. By linking macroscopic morphology to residue-level structure and supramolecular organization, these findings provide critical insights for designing targeted amyloidosis therapies and functional biomaterials.

papers.title: Hydration Layers on Nanoparticles Regulate Ice Growth
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: Nanoparticle hydrophilicity plays an important role in regulating ice growth in supercooled water. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to systematically investigate how particle–water interactions affect both the pushing–engulfment transition and ice-growth kinetics. Increasing hydrophilicity progressively enhances the hydration structure around the nanoparticle, increasing its effective excluded size and narrowing the gap available for ice-front propagation. This enhanced geometric confinement requires larger supercooling for particle engulfment, resulting in a nonlinear decrease in the pushing–engulfment transition temperature. The ice-growth rate shows a nonmonotonic dependence on hydrophilicity, arising from a crossover between interfacial deformation and particle embedding at low hydrophilicity and reduced nanoparticle mobility at high hydrophilicity. The growth rate reaches a maximum at intermediate hydrophilicity. These results reveal how nanoscale hydration structures regulate ice growth through coupled geometric and kinetic effects. These findings provide a molecular-level framework for understanding and controlling ice growth in nanoparticle-containing systems and may aid the design of nanostructured materials for anti-icing and ice regulation.
papers.zh: 纳米颗粒上的水合层调节冰的生长

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abs: The incredible diversity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) creates a difficult challenge for predicting the steady-state partition ratios indicative of cellular health and function. Many PFAS are amphiphilic surfactants, often with ionic or polar headgroups driving their aqueous solubility and nonpolar tails driving the molecules to interfacial environments. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations generate potential of mean force (PMF) curves that integrate the energy of molecular interactions along a defined pathway, offering a means to understand how PFAS interact with and pass through structured phospholipid bilayer environments. However, it is unclear whether MD results calculated over such short time scales (∼ns) can be extrapolated to inform the steady-state conditions relevant to metrics of phase partitioning. Here we propose that PFAS water-bilayer partition ratios can be extrapolated from MD-derived PMF parameters derived from DOPC and POPC phospholipid bilayers via models of damped Brownian motion. Predictions of this approach are consistent with observations that PFAS become rapidly absorbed into bilayers yet are slow to emerge, resulting in large partition ratios that we validate against existing measurements. This model predicts that although water-bilayer partition ratios depend exponentially on the number of fluorinated carbons in the alkyl tail, the exponent differs based on the headgroup between either sulfonate or carboxylate PFAS. We find that MD-derived energy profiles accurately inform tail group contributions to water-bilayer partition ratios, whereas PFAS headgroup chemistry regulates the extent of intrabilayer binding, which, taken together, creates a rich and complex bilayer partitioning profile.
papers.zh: 基于分子动力学的全氟和多氟烷基物质(PFAS)在磷脂双层环境中的分配预测

papers.title: Portable GPU Acceleration of snMECP+COSx via Algorithm–Architecture Codesign
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Efficient construction of Coulomb and exact-exchange matrices remains a major computational bottleneck in large-scale hybrid density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here we present a portable GPU implementation of the multipole expansion of Coulomb potential, its seminumerical variant, and COSx, a revised COSX-type chain-of-spheres exact-exchange treatment implemented in the BDF quantum chemistry package, through an algorithm–architecture codesign strategy. The implementation establishes a unified heterogeneous CPU–GPU execution framework for energy and analytical nuclear-gradient evaluations while introducing method-specific optimizations for different computational kernels. For the fully numerical MECP Coulomb kernel, grid-centric accumulation, Morton (Z-order) spatial batching, and batch-level screening improve memory locality and reduce redundant memory traffic. For the snMECP Coulomb and COSx exact-exchange kernels, angular-momentum-aware on-the-fly contraction eliminates large intermediate integral storage and significantly increases arithmetic intensity. Benchmarks on diverse molecular systems and basis sets demonstrate speedups of up to 34.6× for the seminumerical Coulomb kernels and 11.3× for the COSx kernels relative to the corresponding optimized CPU implementations using the corresponding benchmark CPU allocations, while multi-GPU calculations achieve parallel efficiencies approaching 99% for the dominant seminumerical Coulomb workload. As a chemically realistic application, single-GPU B3LYP-D3(BJ)/6-31G(d,p) geometry optimizations of ZnPc dimers and trimers reproduce the reference electronic-structure and conformational-energy trends with CPU–GPU total-energy differences below 5 × 10–8Eh, while reducing the complete optimization wall time by 1.53×–1.80×. The portable HIP implementation supports both AMD and NVIDIA GPU platforms and establishes an efficient and scalable computational framework for large-scale hybrid DFT calculations within the BDF quantum chemistry package.
papers.zh: 通过算法-架构协同设计实现便携式 GPU 加速 snMECP+COSx

papers.title: Planar Pentacoordinate Fluorine Embedded in the Aromatic [FCu5(C10H10)2] Sandwich
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Designing an experimentally viable planar pentacoordinate fluorine (ppF) species remains challenging, although planar F©Li5F5– and F©Zn5O5– stars have recently been predicted. Here, using the stable [Cu5(C10H10)2]+ sandwich as the ligand cage, we have broken through the limitation of planar ligand rings and designed the first triple-layered ppF [FCu5(C10H10)2] sandwich complex. The ppF [FCu5(C10H10)2] sandwich possesses perfect D5h symmetry, with a FCu5 pentagon sandwiched by two large π-coordinating C10H10 rings. It exhibits good thermodynamic and kinetic stability. Chemical bonding analysis reveals that the stability of the ppF center is dominated by multicenter ionic bonding, while the ligand cage is guarded by the d−π bonding between Cu and C atoms, as well as the localized C–C, C–H, and delocalized π bonds on the C10H10 rings. Magnetic response and adaptive natural density partitioning (AdNDP) analyses reveal a unique global cylindrical aromatic character sustained by robust multicenter interlayer bonding. The current contribution not only introduced a new member to the ppF family but also provided a new “sandwich strategy” for designing planar hypercoordinate fluorine atoms.

papers.title: TD-DFT-Validated Guidelines for BOPHY Molecular Rotors as Fluorescent Viscosity Sensors
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: Fluorescent molecular rotors (FMRs) based on BOPHY (a boron bis(pyrrolyl-methylene)hydrazine chelate) platforms are emerging as promising viscosity sensors for biological imaging, yet the rational design of new derivatives lacks reliable computational guidelines. We present a systematic TD-DFT study of 30 derivatives of BOPHY and its five-membered-ring diphenylboron isomer, PYDBO, in two stages. First, benchmarking four exchange-correlation functionals against experiment identifies TPSSh/6-31+G** for absorption and PBE0/LR/6-31+G** for emission as optimal levels of theory; crucially, the linear-response solvation formalism outperforms the more rigorous state-specific approach for emission in these rigid, low-polarity boron platforms, a result with broad implications for TD-DFT studies of BODIPY-related fluorophores. Second, each derivative is multiparametrically screened against six rational design indicators spanning conformational, spectral, and dynamic properties (Förster–Hoffmann criterion). This screening identifies six viscosity-sensing candidates─3a, 5a, 6a, 1b, 4b (BOPHY 1), and 1f (PYDBO 3)─and reveals a counterintuitive platform–rotor compatibility: xylyl rotors are far less hindered on BOPHY 2/PYDBO 3 than on BOPHY 1. Among the candidates, 5a shows the lowest excited-state barrier, 4b the highest oscillator strength, and 1f the most red-shifted emission─priority targets for experimental synthesis and cellular viscosity imaging.
papers.zh: TD-DFT-用于BOPHY分子转子作为荧光粘度传感器的经验证指南

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Theory of Stark Shift in Optical Transitions of Organic Molecules under Inhomogeneous Electric Fields
papers.jname: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.abs: When molecules are exposed to external static electric fields, their optical transitions shift in energy, which is a phenomenon known as the DC Stark effect. Conventionally, the Stark effect is treated under the assumption of field homogeneity at the molecular scale, allowing for interpretations of the energy shifts based on the changes of the molecular dipole moment and polarizability. However, in realistic environments featuring defects and nanoscale heterogeneities, molecules experience strongly inhomogeneous electric fields that vary on the submolecular scale, rendering standard selection rules and dipole-based models inadequate. Here, we develop a generalized theory of the Stark effect that accounts for such atomic-scale field inhomogeneities. We demonstrate that the total Stark shift can be decomposed into linear and quadratic contributions, which, when treated locally, break the conventional dipolar selection rules and are sensitive to specific microscopic molecular properties. Furthermore, we show that these effects should be accessible in a well-controlled manner in the current experimental setups. Specifically, we consider a realistic configuration in which the atomically sharp tip of a light-assisted scanning-tunneling microscope (STM) generates highly localized electric fields. We show that spatial variations in the linear Stark shift provide maps with subnanometric spatial resolution of photoinduced charge redistribution for representative molecular dyes, exhibiting high sensitivity to molecular composition and chemical functionalization. Additionally, the quadratic contribution probes the spatial distribution of the changes in the polarizability upon excitation. These results establish nanoscale Stark shift spectroscopy as a robust method for studying excited-state properties in strongly inhomogeneous electric fields characteristic of STM, defects, interfaces, and molecular nanostructures.
papers.zh: 非均匀电场下有机分子光学跃迁斯塔克位移的原子尺度理论

papers.title: Data-Driven Approach for Predicting Long-Time Anomalous Transport from Short Trajectories
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Molecular simulations provide detailed microscopic trajectories but often do not reach the long-time transport regime. Predicting long-time transport from ensembles of short trajectories is particularly challenging in heterogeneous materials, where static spatial disorder and viscoelastic memory can produce similar transient dynamics while leading to different behaviors at longer times. We introduce the spatial-disorder generalized Langevin equation (SD-GLE), a likelihood-based generative framework that represents local effective potential landscapes as realizations of a Gaussian random field and temporal correlations through a memory kernel; variational Bayesian inference jointly learns both components from short trajectory ensembles and uses them to generate long trajectories in statistically equivalent environments. In controlled benchmarks, SD-GLE recovers the prescribed disorder covariance and memory kernel, while application to randomly cross-linked polymer networks demonstrates an accurate prediction of size-dependent long-time and non-Gaussian tracer transport, including the crossover to hopping-dominated motion. By linking short-time microscopic motion that departs from simple diffusion to long-time transport behavior, SD-GLE provides a bottom-up modeling strategy that is applicable to a broad range of molecular systems with complex transport dynamics.
papers.zh: 基于数据的短期轨迹预测长期异常输运的方法

papers.title: Paired-Isotopologue Hessian Benchmarking for Second-Order Validation of Machine-Learned Water Potentials
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are commonly validated against energies and forces, yet vibrational predictions depend on the curvature and mode information encoded in the Hessian of the potential-energy surface. Here, we introduce a paired-isotopologue Hessian benchmark for MLIPs using hydrogen-bonded water as a test system. For each MD-sampled water-cluster geometry, a common electronic Hessian is combined with matched HH, DH, and DD mass patterns, enabling the controlled evaluation of vibrational frequencies, normal modes, and isotope responses across nine universal, molecular, and water-specific potentials. Model rankings differ across force-, Hessian-, and vibration-based evaluations, while the paired isotopologue response follows the broad vibrational ordering and remains consistent across structural sources. Beyond global error measures, local coordinate analysis distinguishes Hessian errors with markedly different relevance to specific vibrational observables. Along isotope paths, near-degenerate modes can lose individual mode overlap without a corresponding loss of the vibrational subspace. Together, these results establish Hessian and mode-space validation as necessary complements to energy- and force-based evaluations of MLIPs intended for vibrational calculations.
papers.zh: 用于机器学习水势二阶验证的配对同位素异形体Hessian基准

papers.title: Unraveling the Ultrafast Photodynamics of Molecular Photoswitches in β-Adrenergic Receptors by First-Principles Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: Understanding how protein environments regulate the photodynamics of chromophores is a central task in quantum biology and remains a major challenge. This challenge is particularly significant for G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), which are natively nonphotochromic but can be optically controlled via synthetic photoswitchable ligands. Such artificial photoreceptors are new and important because they not only enable the photocontrol of signaling processes beyond those regulated by rhodopsins but also deepen our fundamental understanding of quantum effects in light-protein interactions. However, the ultrafast nonadiabatic dynamics of these ligands in GPCRs remain difficult to resolve experimentally, while traditional computational approaches fail to describe these processes accurately and efficiently. Here, we employed a multiscale framework to comprehensively characterize how receptor binding, mutations, receptor subtype, chemical substitution, and binding pocket electrostatics regulate the photodynamics of photoswitchable antagonists (OPs) of β-adrenergic receptors (β-ARs). This framework integrates extensive first-principles ground-state conformational sampling, absorption-spectra calculations, and nonadiabatic dynamics simulations. Chemical substitutions influence how excitation energy, excited-state lifetimes, and quantum yields (QY) respond to receptor binding, subtype changes, and binding-pocket mutations. The F289A and Y199A mutants generally accelerate excited-state dynamics by reducing local contacts, whereas the D113E mutation slows the dynamics of OP2 in β2-ΑR by reducing the excited-state driving force. Neutralizing the charge of the counterion D113 residue via protonation increases the QY of OP2 in β2-ΑR by altering the local electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding environment. The ultrafast photoisomerization of the ligands does not require large binding-pocket expansion. Overall, this work provides new insights into how binding-pocket environments regulate the photochemical properties of photoswitchable ligands targeting GPCRs.
papers.zh: 通过第一性原理非绝热动力学模拟揭示β-肾上腺素受体中分子光开关的超快光动力学

papers.title: Rule-Defined Multitopology PEG Ligand Library for Virtual Screening
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) is widely used in drug delivery, primarily as a passive protective component, whereas active targeting typically relies on additional, structurally complex ligands. Developing PEG as a ligand with targeting potential could simplify the architecture of targeted nanomedicines; realizing this concept first requires treating PEG topology as a ligand-scaffold design variable and establishing a unified multitopology structural resource. Using a shared local assembly grammar and topology-specific rules, we constructed a rule-defined PEG ligand 2D master library spanning seven topology classes; the generated view contains approximately 123 million unique structures, and the default-retained view contains approximately 50 million unique structures. The library extends the represented PEG ligand space beyond linear chains to include branched, multiarm, ring-constrained, and multicyclic regions, thereby providing a traceable 2D structural basis for downstream virtual screening.
papers.zh: 用于虚拟筛选的规则定义多拓扑PEG配体库

papers.title: The Delta-ML IR Spectroscopist: Structured Delta-Learning between Harmonic DFT Infrared Spectra
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Accurate theoretical infrared spectra support molecular identification and high-throughput screening, but higher-level harmonic density functional theory (DFT) calculations are costly at scale; we therefore test whether a low-cost PBEh-3c harmonic spectrum can serve as a physical prior for predicting an ωB97X-D3/def2-TZVPD target using a bounded frequency-axis warp, broad-intensity adjustment, and local peak refinement. On 494 held-out test molecules, Delta-ML reaches a mean Spectral Information Similarity (SIS; 1 for identical spectra) of 0.7800 against the target, up from 0.3290 for the uncorrected PBEh-3c spectrum; a direct model given the same structure and PBEh-3c spectrum reaches 0.5759, indicating that most of the gain comes from the structured correction rather than from access to the PBEh-3c spectrum. In a learning-curve experiment, 3,000 training molecules (22% of the training set) reach a mean SIS of 0.7301, 94% of the value obtained with all 13,338 molecules, with a corresponding 10th-percentile SIS of 0.4736 compared with 0.5473 for the full-data controlled benchmark; at this training size, the estimated number of new molecules that must be screened before Delta-ML recovers the cost of generating its training data falls from about 19,400 to 5,100. The model reproduces a harmonic computational target, not experimental or anharmonic spectra.
papers.zh: Delta-ML IR光谱学家：谐波DFT红外光谱之间的结构化Delta学习

papers.title: An Informatics Approach to Recommender Systems for PFAS Molecule Replacement
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants used across an enormous range of industrial and consumer applications, and identifying safe, nonfluorinated replacements remains a slow, largely trial-and-error process. In this work, we construct a recommender engine for suggesting PFAS alternative chemistries based on past replacements. We present a data-driven recommender framework that learns molecular substitution relationships from experimentally documented PFAS-to-non-PFAS pairings, and we demonstrate its viability through two case studies. In the first, a recommender approach grounded in known substitution chemistry and validated by first-principles physics is shown to accelerate the identification of over 500 potential nonregrettable PFAS alternatives across diverse application domains. In the second, we consider substitutions with silicone molecules, performing ab initio calculations on 95 unique PFAS molecules that have been replaced by silicones and 12 unique silicone molecules that have served as replacements, and we then use our recommender engine to identify chemistries that are prime candidates for replacement. Together, these results demonstrate that a data-driven recommender approach can meaningfully navigate the vast space of possible PFAS replacements and surface chemically plausible, synthesizable candidates for experimental evaluation.
papers.zh: 用于PFAS分子替换的推荐系统信息学方法

papers.title: Multistate-Averaged Kohn–Sham ΔSCF Method for Excitation Energies, Transition Properties, and Absorption Spectra and Its Relation to Ensemble Density Functional Theory
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abs: The ΔSCF (Δ-Self-Consistent-Field) approach is an attractive alternative to time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) for excited-state calculations, particularly for Rydberg, charge-transfer, and doubly excited states, for which conventional linear-response TDDFT performs poorly. However, conventional ΔSCF methods based on the unrestricted Kohn–Sham formalism suffer from spin- and spatial-symmetry breaking, optimize the ground- and excited-state determinants independently, leading to nonorthogonal Kohn–Sham determinants that complicate the calculation of transition properties, and require a separate SCF procedure for each excited state of interest. In order to address these limitations, we present a potential-averaged multistate-averaged Kohn–Sham (pa-MSTA-KS) method, which averages the Hartree-exchange-correlation potential of the ground state with state-averaged Hartree-exchange-correlation potentials of one or several excited states during a single SCF procedure. Unlike restricted open-shell Kohn–Sham (ROKS) approaches, pa-MSTA-KS yields canonical SCF equations and can be implemented in any standard KS code with minimal effort. The pa-MSTA-KS method avoids spin-symmetry breaking by construction, yields orbitals that describe ground and excited states simultaneously, and enables the direct evaluation of transition dipole moments and the simulation of full UV/vis absorption spectra based on a single SCF calculation. For excitation energies of the QUEST1 data set and for absorption spectra of water, ethylene, and ammonia, pa-MSTA-KS outperforms TDDFT in accuracy. By combining the generalized-adiabatic-connection Kohn–Sham formalism with ensemble density-functional theory, we provide a formal basis for the pa-MSTA-KS method and derive a new decomposition of the ensemble correlation energy into state- and density-driven contributions.
papers.zh: 用于激发能、跃迁性质和吸收光谱的多态平均Kohn–Sham ΔSCF方法及其与系综密度泛函理论的关系

papers.title: Machine Learning Predictions of Experimental Mössbauer Properties of Fe-Containing Molecular Complexes and Protein Models
papers.jname: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
papers.abs: Mössbauer spectroscopy is among the best techniques for probing molecular structures of iron complexes and proteins. Extracting structural insights from experimental spectra often necessitates accurate DFT predictions of isomer shift (IS) and quadrupole splitting (QS) parameters. However, substantial computational cost and sensitivity to the choice of functional and basis set limit their utility for high-throughput structural screening. To address this gap, various traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models were investigated, using a curated experimental data set of 522 diverse compounds. After engineering models and descriptors, the DL model Chemprop has the highest coefficient of determination (R2) for the test data set (0.92 for IS; 0.73 for QS), with R2 = 0.98/0.91 for IS/QS in the overall data set. Validation of this model corroborates its high, close-to-DFT accuracy for IS predictions, and also shows a significant improvement room for QS predictions. Its predictions of several iron sites in both heme and nonheme proteins and both first- and second-coordination sphere models with challenging and/or unique novel structural features replicated previous DFT structural predictions that are in excellent agreement with experiment, which is a significant application given that no protein data was used to train the ML model. This approach achieved a 218-fold reduction in computational time compared to DFT calculations with same geometries. Results from this first ML work on Mössbauer data of molecular iron complexes will facilitate rapid structural screening previously impractical for large sets of iron complexes and iron-protein binding site structures.
papers.zh: 含铁分子络合物和蛋白质模型实验Mössbauer性质的机器学习预测

papers.title: Euler–Lagrange Equations: Kohn–Sham Energy and X‐Ray Density Matrix
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: The Kohn–Sham equations and the one‐body equations associated with X‐ray density‐matrix refinement arise from different constrained variational problems but have parallel Euler–Lagrange structure. On the Kohn–Sham side, stationarity of the electronic energy gives the one‐electron Hamiltonian eigenvalue equations. On the X‐ray side, stationarity of a constrained residual functional gives a one‐body eigenvalue equation involving a constrained Euler–Lagrange operator, denoted here by D . The practical construction of the X‐ray projector, however, is carried out by the Clinton equations, which iteratively enforce projector admissibility and experimental constraints. We make explicit the mathematical relationship between these two descriptions: the Clinton iteration constructs the projector , while the constrained Euler–Lagrange equation characterizes the same stationary projector through the condition D p = 0, or equivalently, for Hermitian D , = 0. Consequently, the occupied subspace of the converged Clinton projector can be represented by orbitals satisfying D = . For exact data, both the X‐ray and Kohn–Sham developments yield the same exact density; under the stated finite‐basis uniqueness conditions they yield the same occupied projector, although D and the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian remain physically distinct operators.
papers.zh: 欧拉-拉格朗日方程：科恩-沙姆能量和X射线密度矩阵

papers.title: Electronic Band Structure, Bonding, and Optical Properties of Yb 2 Cd 2 Pn 3 (Pn = P, As, Sb, Bi) Compounds: A DFT Investigation
papers.jname: International Journal of Quantum Chemistry
papers.abs: The physical characteristics of four Zintl compounds Yb 2 Cd 2 Pn 3 (Pn = P, As, Sb, Bi) have been thoroughly examined using first‐principles calculations. The density functional theory based Vienna ab initio simulation package has been employed. These Zintl phases demonstrate a monoclinic crystal arrangement characterized with space group C2/m (No. 12). The computed band gap values using GGA (meta‐GGA) 0.5327 (0.8302), 0.3061 (0.5934), and 0.2891 (0.3597) eV indicate the semiconducting nature of all studied compounds except Yb 2 Cd 2 Bi 3 which exhibits semimetallic nature, with valence band dominated by p‐orbital of pnictogen atom and conduction band by Yb‐d states. The effect of SOC has been further investigated to account for relativistic effects, yielding band gap values of 0.5266, 0.2927, and 0.1345 eV for Yb 2 Cd 2 P 3 , Yb 2 Cd 2 As 3 , and Yb 2 Cd 2 Sb 3 , respectively. The –COHP spectra reveal that the Pn–Cd atomic pair plays an appreciable role in stabilizing the crystalline structures. The optical parameters have been analyzed upon incident radiation along the X , Y , and Z directions. The titled compounds exhibit strong absorption in the ultraviolet and unique plasmonic attributes, emphasizing their potential for use in plasmonic and optoelectronic applications. Moreover, the reflectivity and energy‐loss spectra suggest that Yb 2 Cd 2 Pn 3 compounds hold strong potential for use in optical coatings and advanced photonic devices. Further, the bonding characteristics of all Zintl phases have been observed from charge transfer analysis.
papers.zh: Yb 2 Cd 2 Pn 3 （Pn = P、As、Sb、Bi）化合物的电子能带结构、键合和光学性质：一项DFT研究

papers.title: Relativistic Effects on Bond Critical Points and Basin Population on Heavy‐Atom‐Containing Molecules With the Modified Dirac Equation
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: In this work, the topology of the scalar field at four‐component (4c) level, including bond critical points (BCPs) and basin populations, is studied for SnH 4– n I n ( n = 0, …, 4) and UF 6 molecular systems. The basin population of the 4c scalar fields is calculated for the first time using the near‐grid method combined with the Lebedev and Chebyshev quadratures, which improves the efficiency of the methodology applied in our previous work [A. D. Zapata‐Escobar, A. F. Maldonado. Definitions of atoms in molecules with the modified Dirac equations. J. Chem. Phys. 164, 024114 (2026)]. The scalar fields used are the Dirac electron density () and the modified Dirac scalar field (). In Sn‐containing molecules, it was found that the Sn–BCP distance in the Sn–H bond increases when relativistic effects are included, and there is also an increase in the electron density at the BCPs, indicating that the covalent character of the Sn–H bond is enhanced. In the case of the Sn–I bond, the Sn–BCP distance also increases with relativistic effects, but a decrease in the covalent character is observed as the electron density decreases. For the UF 6 molecule, relativistic effects move the BCPs closer to the uranium (central) atom and far away to the fluorine atoms, and this behavior is opposite to that obtained for the tin (central) atom in Sn‐containing systems. Furthermore, relativistic effects produce changes in the electronic populations, with respect to the nonrelativistic values, exceeding 10% when heavy atoms are involved. In summary, it is observed that the basin associated with the heaviest atom in the studied systems is contracted by relativistic effects.
papers.zh: 修正狄拉克方程对含重原子分子的键临界点和盆地布居的相对论效应

papers.title: Assessing Structural, Thermal, and Mechanical Properties of Zirconium‐Based Metal‐Organic Frameworks via DFTB3 / 3OB MD Simulations: A Benchmark Beyond UiO Frameworks
papers.jname: Journal of Computational Chemistry
papers.abs: The exceptional stability and broad application potential of zirconium‐based metal‐organic frameworks call for reliable atomistic methods capable of describing their structural, thermal, and mechanical properties. In this work, we benchmark the recently introduced extension of the DFTB3/3OB parameter set for the transition metal zirconium by evaluating a representative set of Zr‐containing metal‐organic frameworks spanning different secondary building units and topologies, namely UiO‐66, UiO‐67, MOF‐801, MIL‐140A, and MIL‐163. Equilibrium lattice parameters, X‐ray diffraction patterns, thermal expansion coefficients, and volumetric stiffness measures have been computed from DFTB3/3OB molecular dynamics simulations and compared to literature reference data. The results have been further assessed using hybrid DFT (HSEsol) reference calculations and contextualized through an independent comparison with neural‐network‐based MACE‐DAC‐1 simulations. Across the benchmark set, DFTB3/3OB provides a consistent structural description and reproduces the dominant experimental diffraction features, while the deviations of the lattice parameters remain small. DFTB3/3OB correctly reproduces the negative thermal expansion behavior of the UiO frameworks and predicts positive thermal expansion for MOF‐801; for the investigated MIL‐type systems, the observed anisotropic expansion highlights a stronger method dependence. For the cubic frameworks UiO‐66 and UiO‐67, the bulk moduli obtained via DFTB3/3OB fall within reported reference ranges and generally indicate intermediate stiffness relative to MACE‐DAC‐1 and HSEsol. For the non‐cubic MIL‐140A and MIL‐163, the corresponding MD‐derived fixed‐shape isotropic volumetric moduli provide a consistent basis for comparison between DFTB3/3OB and MACE‐DAC‐1. Overall, the presented results support the applicability and transferability of DFTB3/3OB to molecular dynamics simulations of zirconium‐based MOFs beyond the prototypical UiO frameworks.
papers.zh: 通过DFTB3/3OB MD模拟评估锆基金属-有机框架的结构、热学和力学性能：超越UiO框架的基准
